speaker: Abelone
dialogue: Thoring runs the inn. Speak to him.

speaker: Acolyte Jenssen
dialogue: Patience. The body needs time to mend.

speaker: Adara
dialogue: I'm going to be a silversmith one day, like my mother and father.

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: What am I supposed to do? Never leave the house? You want that, Endon?

speaker: Endon
dialogue: You're closing the stall, and that's final.

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: You want to give up now? Out of fear? Is that what we're teaching our daughter?

speaker: Adara
dialogue: Mama, why are you and papa fighting?

speaker: Endon
dialogue: We're not fighting, we're just...Why don't I get you something to eat? Mama and papa will talk later.

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: What should we have tonight?

speaker: Endon
dialogue: Something simple, a stew perhaps.

speaker: Adara
dialogue: Stew again, papa? I want steak.

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: Maybe we could spend a litle bit more and buy some meat, Endon.

speaker: Endon
dialogue: Maybe. Let me think about it.

speaker: Adara
dialogue: Mama, when is Cade coming home?

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: He's off fighting, Adara, with the Stormcloaks. He'll return when the war is over.

speaker: Endon
dialogue: Our son joining the Stormcloaks. If this war had never happened, Cade would have joined the Imperial Legion, like grandfather.

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: Endon, we talked about this... Are you still disappointed in Cade's choice?

speaker: Endon
dialogue: No. I think if I was a young man, I would have done the same.

speaker: Adara
dialogue: Can I join the Legion when I grow up?

speaker: Endon
dialogue: If there's still a Legion left, Adara. I'm sure you'd make a great soldier. Just like your brother.

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: We sold all those lovely little necklaces you brought me today. Did you make them yourself?

speaker: Adara
dialogue: That's right! Papa helped me with the clasps, but I did all the links on my own.

speaker: Endon
dialogue: Adara bends the silver so naturally. Grandmother would have cried if she saw how deft our daughter has become.

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: Well, I'm proud of both of you. I haven't been so busy since those nobles from Solitude come into the city three years ago.

speaker: Endon
dialogue: I miss those days, before the Forsworn took up arms again, when you could walk the roads in peace.

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: Endon, dear, please don't.... Save your frustrations for work.

speaker: Endon
dialogue: You're right, dear. I'm sorry to worry you.

speaker: Addvar
dialogue: You shouldn't leave Solitude without trying our fish. Best in Skyrim.

speaker: Svari
dialogue: They can't hurt uncle Roggvir. Tell them he didn't do it.

speaker: Addvar
dialogue: Svari, you need to go home. Go home and stay there until your mother comes.

speaker: Aldis
dialogue: Lock the city gate.

speaker: Vivienne
dialogue: You should tell her that her uncle is scum that betrayed his High King. Best she know now, Addvar.

speaker: Addvar
dialogue: You're all heart, Vivienne.

speaker: Aldis
dialogue: Roggvir. You helped Ulfric Stormcloak escape this city after he murdered High King Torygg. By opening that gate for Ulfric you betrayed the people of Solitude.

speaker: Sorex
dialogue: He doesn't deserve to speak!

speaker: Roggvir
dialogue: There was no murder! Ulfric challenged Torygg. He beat the High King in fair combat.

speaker: Roggvir
dialogue: Such as our way! Such as the ancient custom of Skyrim, and all Nords!

speaker: Vivienne
dialogue: Cut 'em down!

speaker: Aldis
dialogue: Guard. Prepare the prisoner.

speaker: Roggvir
dialogue: I don't need your help.

speaker: Aldis
dialogue: Very well, Roggvir. Bow your head.

speaker: Roggvir
dialogue: On this day... I go to Sovngarde.

speaker: Addvar
dialogue: Svari, Jala said you stole an apple from her cart yesterday. Is this true?

speaker: Svari
dialogue: Just a little one! I was hungry!

speaker: Greta
dialogue: I'll talk with Jala, dear. I'm sure she'll accept a potato as repayment.

speaker: Addvar
dialogue: I suppose. But Svari, we don't steal. We're better than that. Understand?

speaker: Svari
dialogue: Yes, papa.

speaker: Greta
dialogue: Eat up, Svari.

speaker: Addvar
dialogue: It's all we've got for today. Don't be greedy.

speaker: Greta
dialogue: Maybe we'll have better luck tomorrow.

speaker: Addvar
dialogue: We'll make it, Greta. We always have so far...

speaker: Addvild
dialogue: If you're looking to purchase goods, I have none to sale. You should head into Riften instead.

speaker: Leonara
dialogue: My darling, you've made me the happiest woman in all Skyrim.

speaker: Addvild
dialogue: It brings me joy to hear that, but what possessed you to say that so suddenly?

speaker: Leonara
dialogue: I've already lost a family, and we're about to start a new one. I don't want that to happen again.

speaker: Addvild
dialogue: My sweet {{Hide|Leanora|Leonara}}, I will never let anything happen to us. I promise.

speaker: Leonara
dialogue: I'm not so sure the few guards they've assigned to the farm are enough.

speaker: Addvild
dialogue: It will have to do. Besides, if it came to blows, I'm sure the {{Hide|Snow-Shod's|Snow-Shods|description=extra apostrophe}} would come out here and assist us.

speaker: Leonara
dialogue: I suppose so. I just fear they won't make it out here in time.

speaker: Addvild
dialogue: Just worry about keeping the fields tended and let the Jarl worry about the war.

speaker: Adeber
dialogue: I'm one of the miners. Plenty of ore to dig up around here.

speaker: Orthus Endario
dialogue: Just in time. This is Adelaisa, one of my superiors from the Company.

speaker: Orthus
dialogue: Adelaisa, I'm sorry.

speaker: Adelaisa
dialogue: Sorry isn't good enough, Orthus. There's a lot of gold at stake here, and sniveling isn't going to get it back.

speaker: Adisla
dialogue: Every now and then someone from the city comes by. Think they aren't used to seeing a Nord working for a Dark Elf.

speaker: Belyn
dialogue: Make sure the back fence is repaired. I swear I saw some skeevers in nibbling the leaves yesterday.

speaker: Adisla
dialogue: Oh, no skeevers out here, sir. They can't stand the cold.

speaker: Belyn
dialogue: Maybe, but the way you burn through all that wood to keep the cabin toasty, they might mistake this place for Elsweyr.

speaker: Adisla
dialogue: Sorry, sir. These old bones do like a bit of warmth in the evening. There's no need to make fun.

speaker: Belyn
dialogue: You just need to remember that there's a war on, and firewood isn't cheap these days.

speaker: Adisla
dialogue: I was wondering if you had ordered the shipment of that frostwheat, sir.

speaker: Belyn
dialogue: Yes, but that fool Endario can't get it in. I'll thrash him when I get back to the city, don't you worry.

speaker: Adisla
dialogue: I wasn't wanting to get anyone in trouble, sir. Just wanting to get the new planting started, is all.

speaker: Belyn
dialogue: Yes, wouldn't want to miss the lush summer we have ahead.

speaker: Belyn
dialogue: So, have you ever actually spoken to Captain Lonely-Gale?

speaker: Adisla
dialogue: By the gods, he's just a retired ship's captain.

speaker: Belyn
dialogue: Maybe to you, but he's just so... his story is...

speaker: Adisla
dialogue: He's just a guard captain. And not a very good one, at that.

speaker: Adonato Leotelli
dialogue: I'm a writer by trade. Not that the people of Skyrim do much reading.

speaker: Adrianne Avenicci
dialogue: I don't claim to be the best blacksmith in Whiterun. Eorlund Gray-Mane's got that honor. The man's steel is legendary. All I ask is a fair chance.

speaker: Adrianne
dialogue: I just can't fill an order that size on my own. Why don't you swallow that stubborn pride of yours and ask Eorlund Gray-Mane for help?

speaker: Idolaf
dialogue: Ha! I'd sooner bend my knee to Ulfric Stormcloak. Besides, Gray-Mane would never make steel for the Legion.

speaker: Adrianne
dialogue: Have it your way. I'll take the job, but don't expect a miracle.

speaker: Aduri Sarethi
dialogue: This place is boring. Nothing but the same thing every day.

speaker: Avrusa
dialogue: Aduri, how come the fields haven't been tilled like I asked?

speaker: Aduri
dialogue: Because it's boring. The fields are going to do fine... you don't have to dote over them so much.

speaker: Avrusa
dialogue: Boring? That food is paying for everything. If we lose even a single crop, we could starve or be forced to beg. I won't have it!

speaker: Aduri
dialogue: All right, I understand. I'll do it tomorrow, okay? Just get off my back.

speaker: Aduri
dialogue: Have you decided if I can head up to Solitude yet? I hear it's the best place to meet someone who may be willing to teach me to paint.

speaker: Avrusa
dialogue: I'm sorry, Aduri, not this year. Perhaps next year after the harvest, I don't know. There's so much to do.

speaker: Aduri
dialogue: It's not going to be next year, nor the year after that! You just care about this farm more than you care about me!

speaker: Avrusa
dialogue: Painting won't put food on the table, but our crops will. Be patient Aduri... it will happen someday, I promise.

speaker: Aduri
dialogue: Where did all these pretty red plants come from?

speaker: Avrusa
dialogue: Remember Uncle Sinderion? These are the plants he was searching for... the Crimson Nirnroot.

speaker: Aduri
dialogue: They're beautiful. I can see why he wanted to find them.

speaker: Avrusa
dialogue: One day, these beautiful plants will make us famous and we can finally move off of this farm... thanks to Sinderion.

speaker: Aela the Huntress
dialogue: Something has shifted in the moons, brother.

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: I told you, this is the whelp that Vilkas mentioned.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: Ah, yes. I heard you gave him quite a thrashing.

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: Don't let Vilkas catch you saying that.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: Did you call me?

speaker: Aela
dialogue: Of course we did, icebrain. Show this newblood where the rest of the whelps sleep.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: New blood? Oh, hello. I'm Farkas. Come, follow me.

speaker: Eorlund
dialogue: Who will start?

speaker: Aela
dialogue: I'll do it. Before the ancient flame... We grieve.

speaker: Eorlund
dialogue: We grieve.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: We grieve.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: We grieve.

speaker: Eorlund
dialogue: At this loss... We weep.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: We weep.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: We weep.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: We weep.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: For the fallen... We shout.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: We shout.

speaker: Eorlund
dialogue: We shout.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: We shout.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: And for ourselves... We take our leave.

speaker: Eorlund
dialogue: We take our leave.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: We take our leave.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: We take our leave.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: His spirit is departed. Members of the Circle, let us withdraw to the Underforge, to grieve our last together.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: The old man had one wish before he died. And he didn't get it. It's as simple as that.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: Being moon-born is not so much of a curse as you might think, Vilkas.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: That's fine for you. But he wanted to be clean. He wanted to meet Ysgramor and know the glories of Sovngarde. But all that was taken from him.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: And you avenged him.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: Kodlak did not care for vengeance.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: No, Farkas, he didn't. And that's not what this is about. We should be honoring Kodlak, no matter our own thoughts on the blood.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: You're right. It's what he wanted, and he deserved to have it.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: Kodlak used to speak of a way to cleanse his soul, even in death. You know the legends of the Tomb of Ysgramor.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: There the souls of Harbingers will heed the call of northern steel. We can't even enter the tomb without Wuuthrad, and it's in pieces, like it has been for a thousand years.

speaker: Eorlund
dialogue: And dragons were just stories. And the elves once ruled Skyrim. Just because something is, doesn't mean it must be. The blade is a weapon. A tool. Tools are meant to be broken. And repaired.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: Is that? Did you repair the blade?

speaker: Aela
dialogue: You wanted to see me?

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: I worry that you've been spending too many nights out.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: Where I go is my business. If you have a concern about my honor, bring it before the Circle.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: You forget yourself, young one.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: I'm sorry. I didn't mean to snap. Just... these hunters. We're all on edge.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: That's why it's best to not mistake foolhardiness for bravery.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: How goes the hunt?

speaker: Aela
dialogue: Skjor's heard rumors of a bear the size of a mammoth in Hammerfell. We're going to seek it out.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: What glorious prey. Come back alive, and with stories to tell!

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: All these younglings scampering around.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: Worried one of them is going to take your place?

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: Some of them might try. But that's not what I'm worried about.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: What then?

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: That they might get themselves killed.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: By you?

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: They should be so lucky.

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: Are you prepared for tonight's hunt?

speaker: Aela
dialogue: I've been thinking we need to be more... discreet.

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: There's nothing wrong with what we're doing.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: You know the old man doesn't like it. Let's just not be too obvious.

speaker: Njada
dialogue: I've heard some rumors... about you and Skjor.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: And if you want to keep having ears, you'll pretend you didn't.

speaker: Njada
dialogue: Is it not allowed?

speaker: Aela
dialogue: It's not exactly forbidden, but even so... it's not true. So that's that.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: How do you manage to hold your ground like that?

speaker: Njada
dialogue: You have to remember, it's not about strength. It's about leverage.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: But strength doesn't hurt.

speaker: Njada
dialogue: Well, no. I'm just saying there's more to defense than muscle.

speaker: Aerin
dialogue: I've never seen Mjoll this upset about anything. The city really gets to her.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: I had another run-in with the Thieves Guild.

speaker: Aerin
dialogue: Be careful, Mjoll. The Thieves Guild has Maven Black-Briar at her back. One snap of her fingers, and you could end up in Riften Jail... or worse.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: They represent the reason I'm here. I can't just ignore them, Aerin.

speaker: Aerin
dialogue: I know. I just don't want you to leave; you're the only good thing that's happened to this city in a long time.

speaker: Aerin
dialogue: Well, you were right. These so called 'Gutter Saints' live in the sewers beneath.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: I suspected as much. The real question now is do we do something about it ourselves or do we speak to the Jarl?

speaker: Aerin
dialogue: I say we go down there and clear the place out, just like old times.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: No, my friend. That would be reckless. We have to help, but help in a way that doesn't directly place anyone in harm's way. For now, give this 'Ratway' a wide berth.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: Sometimes I'm not certain that the people of Riften want to be helped.

speaker: Aerin
dialogue: I think some of them do, Lady Mjoll. They're just too frightened to step up and do something about it like you are.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: Aerin, you never cease to amaze me. You always see the good in everything.

speaker: Aerin
dialogue: It's only because I've had an excellent teacher.

speaker: Aerin
dialogue: You've been in Riften for quite some time now, Lady Mjoll. I fear that you soon may leave us.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: Riften has problems of its own. Now is not the time for exploration and discovery.

speaker: Aerin
dialogue: I'm relieved to hear you say that. If you were to leave, I'd miss you terribly.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: Aerin, I owe you my life. It would take a threat to all of Skyrim for me to depart.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: Aerin, have you seen my ring? The one with the inscription?

speaker: Aerin
dialogue: No, I haven't. Don't tell me you've lost it.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: I hope not. That ring is irreplaceable.

speaker: Aerin
dialogue: I'll look around the house and if I find it, I'll bring it to you right away.

speaker: Afflicted 1
dialogue: Peryite, heed our call and deem us worthy. Our leader, Orchendor, has led us here, and for that we are thankful. He has shown us that our suffering is not a punishment, but a blessing.

speaker: Afflicted 2
dialogue: Yes, a blessing. For many months we have sought your guidance, yet we have heard nothing from you. If we do not please you, give us a sign so we may understand why.

speaker: Afflicted 1
dialogue: Yes, a sign. We are lost without your guidance. On the ninth of Rain's Hand, our prayers went unanswered, yet here we stand unfaltering in our belief that you will soon show yourself to us.

speaker: Afflicted 2
dialogue: Yes, show yourself to us. Until that day, we will continue to devote our lives to you and suffer for you.

speaker: Afflicted 1
dialogue: Yes, suffer for you.

speaker: Afflicted 1
dialogue: I'm sorry to wake you, my brother, but I have a request from Orchendor.

speaker: Afflicted 2
dialogue: Yes, what is it?

speaker: Afflicted 1
dialogue: He requests more barrels of ichor to be delivered to the Arcanex tonight.

speaker: Afflicted 2
dialogue: This is the reason you wake me? I already have Orchendor's request taken care of.

speaker: Afflicted 1
dialogue: I'm sorry, my brother.

speaker: Afflicted 2
dialogue: Now, leave me to my sleep. My strength and patience are waning.

speaker: Afflicted 1
dialogue: Yes, my brother. Forgive me. May the blessing of Peryite be with you.

speaker: Afflicted 2
dialogue: Yes, yes. As with you. Now, off with you.

speaker: Afflicted Refugee
dialogue: Are you finished ogling the grotesque? I suppose I should be grateful you didn't simply attack me.

speaker: Agni
dialogue: My mother and father died years ago. Falion takes care of me now.

speaker: Falion
dialogue: Have you been working on your concentration?

speaker: Agni
dialogue: Yes sir, I have.

speaker: Falion
dialogue: Good, good. Concentration is paramount when dealing with magic forces.

speaker: Falion
dialogue: Because an unfocused mind will almost certainly be obliterated. Destroyed by the forces you attempt to control and wield.

speaker: Falion
dialogue: Have no fear. I believe its within you to excel in your studies. But you must learn to concentrate!

speaker: Agni
dialogue: Yes, sir!

speaker: Agni
dialogue: When I grow up, will I go to the College in Winterhold?

speaker: Falion
dialogue: No, I don't think that will be necessary.

speaker: Agni
dialogue: But I'm learning about magic, and that's what they do there. Shouldn't I go?

speaker: Falion
dialogue: The College is not the only place to learn about magic.

speaker: Agni
dialogue: But you went there, didn't you? Isn't that where you learned?

speaker: Falion
dialogue: I was there only for a short time. Much of what I have learned has been on my own. And I will teach you. You have no reason to go there.

speaker: Falion
dialogue: That is enough.

speaker: Agni
dialogue: I had a bad dream again last night.

speaker: Agni
dialogue: I dreamt that you went away. You made monsters.

speaker: Falion
dialogue: It's just a dream, child. Nothing more.

speaker: Agni
dialogue: It was scary. It was like it was real!

speaker: Falion
dialogue: Hush now. Think no more of it.

speaker: Agni
dialogue: Is it true that you kill deer and eat their hearts?

speaker: Falion
dialogue: What? Where did you hear such a thing?

speaker: Agni
dialogue: I don't know. Someone in town said it.

speaker: Falion
dialogue: It's not true, I assure you.

speaker: Falion
dialogue: Don't believe everything you hear, child.

speaker: Ahkari
dialogue: I seem to have an unfortunate talent for getting myself involved in misunderstandings with the law.

speaker: Ahlam
dialogue: Men are all alike, from Skyrim to Hammerfell. They care only for war and politics, and treat their women like cattle.

speaker: Ahtar, checking Roggvir's body.
dialogue: That makes Twenty-Three.

speaker: Ahtar
dialogue: Rest up, scum. Probably getting executed tomorrow.

speaker: Bjartur
dialogue: Yeah, you said that yesterday.

speaker: Ahtar
dialogue: Come now, you'll want to show up in Sovngarde refreshed. You got an eternity of merrymaking ahead of you.

speaker: Bjartur
dialogue: Hey, jailor! What I don't understand is why you're siding with the Imperials.

speaker: Ahtar
dialogue: Shut up, scum.

speaker: Bjartur
dialogue: I mean, the Redguards fought off the Aldmeri and the Empire, and now Hammerfell is an independent state. That's all we Nords want for Skyrim!

speaker: Ahtar
dialogue: I said shut up, scum!

speaker: Bjartur
dialogue: So it's okay if your people rebel against the Empire, but not mine?

speaker: Ahtar
dialogue: They aren't my 'people'. I'm with the Empire because they pay me; and that means I'm out here, and you're in there. So shut up, scum!

speaker: Aia
dialogue: Few can resist my charms. Even fewer are worthy of them.

speaker: Pantea
dialogue: Passably. Aia is my star pupil; none of the others can hold a candle to her, especially not that wretched Illdi.

speaker: Viarmo
dialogue: Try not to play favorites, Lady Ateia. It does a disservice to the whole class.

speaker: Pantea
dialogue: Yes, Headmaster.

speaker: Aia
dialogue: You know, my father collected exotic alcohols.

speaker: Aia
dialogue: Rum from Hammerfell, mulled wine from Daggerfall, and the like.

speaker: or
dialogue: I'm still finding your Spiced Wine to be the best drink I've ever tasted.

speaker: Evette
dialogue: Thanks, Aia. That means a lot.

speaker: Aia
dialogue: Must it be written? Poetry is so dull when it isn't set to music.

speaker: Giraud
dialogue: I'm sure it will be fine, just don't be late.

speaker: Aia
dialogue: Lady Ateia has already arranged for me to perform in the court of the Jarl of Falkreath.

speaker: Jorn
dialogue: You'd better hope the war's over by then. The Stormcloaks would eat you alive!

speaker: Aia
dialogue: Hmph. Music tames the most savage beasts. Even Nords.

speaker: Illdi
dialogue: Ataf keeps making eyes at me.

speaker: Aia
dialogue: You should tell him to mind his own business.

speaker: Illdi
dialogue: Aia. You're so mean. I don't think he means anything by it.

speaker: Aia
dialogue: Have it your way, then.

speaker: Aia
dialogue: At this point, I hardly see how your advice would improve it; it's flawless.

speaker: Inge
dialogue: I'll be the judge of that. Now, back to your practice.

speaker: Pantea
dialogue: You there, have you performed your voice exercises today?

speaker: Aia
dialogue: Always! Perfection takes dedication, after all!

speaker: Pantea
dialogue: Yes, well, see that you keep at it. That is all.

speaker: Pantea
dialogue: Your performance has been excellent lately Aia. You still need training but one day you will make an adequate singer.

speaker: Aia
dialogue: Yes, Dean. Thank you.

speaker: Aicantar
dialogue: Don't let my uncle go on about his theories. You'll be here all night.

speaker: Aicantar
dialogue: Uncle Calcelmo...

speaker: Calcelmo
dialogue: What is it, nephew? Can't you see I'm trying to think here?

speaker: Aicantar
dialogue: I just wanted to know if you needed anything.

speaker: Calcelmo
dialogue: Um, no. Nothing. Nothing at all.

speaker: Aicantar
dialogue: Are you sure?

speaker: Calcelmo
dialogue: Stop bothering me, Aicantar!

speaker: Calcelmo
dialogue: Next season, nephew. Next season for sure...

speaker: Aicantar
dialogue: 'Next season for sure...' What? Uncle Calcelmo, I don't understand what you mean.

speaker: Calcelmo
dialogue: The excavation, Aicantar! Right after I finish my book. We'll start excavating Nchuand-Zel again.

speaker: Aicantar
dialogue: Could I maybe skip the excavation, Uncle Calcelmo? I, uh, just don't think you won't need me.

speaker: Calcelmo
dialogue: Nonsense, you're a vital part of my research team. You'll be there, have no fear! Now, I don't want to hear another word of protest.

speaker: Aicantar
dialogue: You heard me, captain- our work must not be disturbed. Kill any intruders on sight. Call for backup if you need it. But let no one through.

speaker: Aicantar
dialogue: Accidents like this just don't happen. Someone is trying to sabotage my uncle's research.

speaker: Aquilius
dialogue: I...all right. If there is a thief, he won't leave this tower alive. But shouldn't we inform Master Calcelmo?

speaker: Aicantar
dialogue: I'll deal with my uncle. Just...go! Scour this place from top to bottom!

speaker: Aquilius
dialogue: All right men, spread out and search the tower. No telling who - or what - we're dealing with here.

speaker: Ainethach
dialogue: If the Forsworn aren't attacking my town, the Nords are trying to force me off it.

speaker: Ainethach
dialogue: I want you sellswords out of my mine.

speaker: Atar
dialogue: Watch your tongue, native. We'll leave when we're sure there are no Forsworn here.

speaker: Ainethach
dialogue: Oh, and when would that be, I wonder? When I sell my land to the Silver-Bloods?

speaker: Atar
dialogue: The Silver-Bloods have made you a very generous offer for this pile of dirt. I suggest you take it.

speaker: Alain Dufont
dialogue: Well, you must have all of those annoying gods on your side to have made it this far, whoever you are. Even I have to admit that's pretty impressive.

speaker: Stig Salt-Plank
dialogue: Come now, dearie, surely we aren't all that bad.

speaker: Karita
dialogue: Just... leave me alone! I've brought your mead, now drink it and shut your filthy mouths.

speaker: Alding
dialogue: Oh, we've got other things in mind for our mouths, sweetie.

speaker: Alduin to the Last Dragonborn
dialogue: You do not even know our tongue, do you? Such arrogance, to dare take for yourself the name of Dovah!

speaker: Alduin
dialogue: {{hide|Sahloknir, ziil gro dovah ulse! Slen Tiid Vo!|Sahloknir, I bind your dragon spirit for eternity! Flesh Time Undo!}}

speaker: Sahloknir
dialogue: {{hide|Alduin, thuri! Boaan tiid vokriiha suleyksejun kruziik?|Alduin, my king (overlord)! Has the time arrived (flown) to restore (unkill) your ancient dominion (power-of-king)?}}

speaker: Hakon
dialogue: Gormlaith! We're running out of time! The battle...

speaker: Dragon
dialogue: Daar sul thur se Alduin vakrii. Today Alduin's lordship will be restored. But I honor your courage. Krif voth ahkrin. Die now, in vain.

speaker: Hakon
dialogue: For Skyrim!

speaker: Gormlaith
dialogue: Hyah! Know that Gormlaith sent you down to death! Hakon! A glorious day, is it not?

speaker: Hakon
dialogue: Have you no thought beyond the blooding of your blade?

speaker: Gormlaith
dialogue: What else is there?

speaker: Hakon
dialogue: The battle below goes ill. If Alduin does not rise to our challenge, I fear all may be lost.

speaker: Gormlaith
dialogue: You worry too much, brother. Victory will be ours.

speaker: Hakon
dialogue: Why does Alduin hang back? We've staked everything on this plan of yours, old man.

speaker: Felldir
dialogue: He will come. He cannot ignore our defiance. And why should he fear us, even now?

speaker: Gormlaith
dialogue: We've bloodied him well. Four of his kin have fallen to my blade alone this day.

speaker: Felldir
dialogue: But none have yet stood against Alduin himself. Galthor, Sorri, Birkir...

speaker: Gormlaith
dialogue: They did not have Dragonrend. Once we bring him down, I promise I will have his head.

speaker: Felldir
dialogue: You do not understand. Alduin cannot be slain like a lesser dragon. He is beyond our strength. Which is why I brought the Elder Scroll.

speaker: Hakon
dialogue: Felldir! We agreed not to use it!

speaker: Felldir
dialogue: I never agreed. And if you are right, I will not need it.

speaker: Hakon
dialogue: No. We will deal with Alduin ourselves, here and now.

speaker: Gormlaith
dialogue: We shall see soon enough. Alduin approaches!

speaker: Hakon
dialogue: So be it.

speaker: Alduin
dialogue: Meyye! Tahrodiis aanne! Him hinde pah liiv! Zu'u hin daan!

speaker: Gormlaith
dialogue: Let those that watch from Sovngarde envy us this day! Joor... Zah...Frul!

speaker: Alduin
dialogue: Nivahriin joorre! What have you done? What twisted Words have you created?! Tahrodiis Paarthurnax! My teeth to his neck! But first... dir ko maar. You will die in terror, knowing your final fate... To feed my power when I come for you in Sovngarde!

speaker: Gormlaith
dialogue: If I die today, it will not be in terror! You feel fear for the first time, worm. I see it in your eyes.

speaker: Felldir
dialogue: Fo... Krah Diin!

speaker: Gormlaith
dialogue: Skyrim will be free!

speaker: Hakon
dialogue: No, damn you! It's no use! Use the Scroll, Felldir! Now!

speaker: Felldir
dialogue: Hold, Alduin on the Wing! Sister Hawk, grant us your sacred breath to make this contract heard! Begone, World-Eater! By words with older bones than your own we break your perch on this age and send you out! You are banished! Alduin, we shout you out from all our endings unto the last!

speaker: Felldir
dialogue: You are banished!

speaker: Hakon
dialogue: It worked... you did it...

speaker: Felldir
dialogue: Yes, the World-Eater is gone... may the spirits have mercy on our souls.

speaker: Alduin
dialogue: Bahloki nahkip sillesejoor. My belly is full of the souls of your fellow mortals, Dovahkiin. Die now and await your fate in Sovngarde!

speaker: Paarthurnax
dialogue: Lost funt. You are too late, Alduin!

speaker: Alduin
dialogue: Suleyki mulaag, Paarthurnax. My power has waxed, while yours has waned. Aav uv dir. Join me or perish with your mortal friends.

speaker: Paarthurnax
dialogue: Unslaad hokoron! Never again!

speaker: Alea Quintus
dialogue: None of your damned business who I am! If you're going to kill me, just do it already!

speaker: Alessandra
dialogue: I can see that disapproving look in your eye.

speaker: Alexia Vici
dialogue: Oh I know enough. I know those trouble-making Stormcloaks refuse to submit to Imperial authority. Such seditious behavior. Why, it's treason!

speaker: Vulwulf
dialogue: Typical Imperial rot. You speak of Skyrim like you know the land, know its people. You're from Cyrodiil! You know nothing about us! Nothing!

speaker: Alexia
dialogue: Oh, I know enough. I know those trouble-making Stormcloaks refuse to submit to Imperial authority. Such seditious behavior. Why it's treason!

speaker: Vulwulf
dialogue: And when the elves marched into your beloved Cyrodiil, and everyone took up arms against them, wasn't that treason? Against the Dominion? Huh?

speaker: Alexia
dialogue: Why that's not the same thing at all. The Dominion were invaders. Conquerors. We had to fight them, to preserve our own way of life.

speaker: Vulwulf
dialogue: My point exactly.

speaker: Alfhild Battle-Born
dialogue: Need something? Unlike the rest of my family, I've got work to do.

speaker: Alfhild
dialogue: So, what book should I read to you tonight?

speaker: Bergritte
dialogue: How about The Lusty Argonian Maid?

speaker: Bergritte
dialogue: You've got no sense of humor, you know that? Why don't you pick up where you left off with The Real Barenziah.

speaker: Alik'r Prisoner
dialogue: My life with the Alik'r is over now, but I have no wish to die in this gods-forsaken land. If I can be released from prison I may start over.

speaker: Prisoner
dialogue: Guard! My fine's been paid, now set me free!

speaker: Guard
dialogue: Sorry, my ears aren't so good. You say something?

speaker: Prisoner
dialogue: I said my fine has been paid! Now let me out!

speaker: Guard
dialogue: Right, right... Oh, look at that. I seem to have lost my keys. Might take me a while to find them. You just sit tight, I'll get around to it eventually.

speaker: Prisoner
dialogue: Curse you!

speaker: Hold Guards
dialogue: Have you seen those warriors from Hammerfell? They've got curved swords. Curved. Swords.

speaker: Whiterun Guard
dialogue: Look, you've already been told you're not allowed here. Turn around and go back the way you came.

speaker: Whiterun Guard
dialogue: I don't care what you're doing, after what happened you're lucky I don't toss you in jail. Now get lost.

speaker: Redguard woman
dialogue: I don't know who you think I am, and I don't care. Leave me alone!

speaker: Redguard woman
dialogue: I'm not going anywhere. Now back off before I do something drastic.

speaker: Redguard woman
dialogue: Next time you're looking to pester someone, make sure it's the right person!

speaker: Alva
dialogue: I hear you put Laelette out of her misery.

speaker: Hroggar
dialogue: How are you feeling?

speaker: Alva
dialogue: I feel wonderful, just like every night.

speaker: Hroggar
dialogue: Do you need anything? Are you hungry?

speaker: Alva
dialogue: Oh Hroggar, you know I'm always hungry. Don't worry, I'll eat when I need to. Oh, look! We have company!

speaker: Alva
dialogue: Why, good evening Jonna!

speaker: Alva
dialogue: What can't you get me, sweetie?

speaker: Jonna
dialogue: Umm... Did you want somethin' to eat?

speaker: Alva
dialogue: Eat? No, I don't think I'm... hungry. Not now, at least.

speaker: Jonna
dialogue: Right. Okay, tell me if you change yer mind.

speaker: Alva
dialogue: I'm bored, Benor. Nobody wants to have any fun with me.

speaker: Alva
dialogue: Hroggar doesn't have to know if we sit together. Or drink together. I doubt he would even care.

speaker: Benor
dialogue: You tempt me mightily, Alva. But I won't cuckhold another man, even on murderer like Hroggar.

speaker: Alva
dialogue: Would you like to buy a lady a drink?

speaker: Alva
dialogue: Forget about Hroggar. He's always so tired lately. I need someone with a little fire in their blood.

speaker: Gorm
dialogue: After all you've put that man through. You should be more loyal to him.

speaker: Alvor
dialogue: I could forge you a warhammer that would crush a giant's head like a walnut.

speaker: Alvor
dialogue: Sigrid! We have company!

speaker: Sigrid
dialogue: Hadvar! We've been so worried about you! Come, you two must be hungry. Sit down and I'll get you something to eat.

speaker: Alvor
dialogue: Now then, boy, what's the big mystery? What are you doing here looking like you lost an argument with a cave bear?

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: I don't know where to start. You know I was assigned to General Tullius's guard. We were stopped in Helgen when we were attacked by...a dragon.

speaker: Alvor
dialogue: A dragon? That's ridiculous. You aren't drunk, are you boy?

speaker: Sigrid
dialogue: Husband. Let him tell his story.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Not much more to tell. The dragon flew over and just wrecked the whole place. Mass confusion. I don't know if anyone else got out alive. I doubt I'd have made it out if not for my friend here. I need to get back to Solitude and let them know what's happened. I thought you could help us out. Food, supplies, a place to stay.

speaker: Dorthe
dialogue: Hadvar, did you really see a dragon? What did it look like? Did it have big teeth?

speaker: Sigrid
dialogue: Hush, child. Don't pester your cousin.

speaker: Alvor
dialogue: Well, I'd better get back to work. You two make yourselves at home.

speaker: or
dialogue: I'm bored standing around, papa. I could take over for you...

speaker: or
dialogue: Patience, Dorthe. You'll get some time at the forge, I promise you. But not right now. You need to keep watching me. That's how you'll learn.

speaker: or
dialogue: Yes, sir.

speaker: Dorthe
dialogue: You really think I can be a blacksmith someday, papa? As good as Eorlund Gray-Mane? Or maybe... even as good as you?

speaker: Alvor
dialogue: Oh, I know it! You keep working hard, like you been doing, and you could be the greatest blacksmith Skyrim has ever seen.

speaker: Dorthe
dialogue: He he. Thanks, papa.

speaker: Alvor
dialogue: I can only hammer so fast, Gerdur.

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: They don't have to be perfect. Just send them over when they're ready.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Uncle Alvor! Hello!

speaker: Alvor
dialogue: Hadvar? What are you doing here? Are you on leave from...Shor's bones, what happened to you, boy? Are you in some kind of trouble?

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Shh. Uncle, please. Keep your voice down. I'm fine. But we should go inside to talk.

speaker: Alvor
dialogue: What's going on? [looks at Dragonborn] And who's this?

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: He's/She's a friend. Saved my life, in fact. Come on, I'll explain everything but we need to go inside.

speaker: Alvor
dialogue: Okay, okay. Come inside, then. Sigrid will get you something to eat, and you can tell me all about it.

speaker: Alvor
dialogue: I got a new order in for shields. I'm gonna need some hardwood planks. None of that soft pine this time.

speaker: Alvor
dialogue: War may be good for business, but it's hard on families.

speaker: Hod
dialogue: A hard truth, that is. Let's drink to the fallen ones.

speaker: Alvor
dialogue: Sigrid! Love of my life! When you get a spare moment, I could use some water.

speaker: Sigrid
dialogue: Don't you sweet talk me, Alvor. Not after last night. I'll bring you water when I'm done with my other chores.

speaker: Alvor
dialogue: Woman, you'll be the death of me yet. Fine, take your time. I'll just die of thirst in the heat of this forge.

speaker: Alvor
dialogue: Good morning, wife.

speaker: Alvor
dialogue: Well, I'd better get to work. I have to fix another saw blade for Gerdur's mill.

speaker: Sigrid
dialogue: Take care, husband.

speaker: Amaund Motierre
dialogue: Don't you have all the information you need? Please, the Emperor isn't going to kill himself. Hmph. Now wouldn't that be a blessing...

speaker: Ambarys Rendar
dialogue: It's not the cold of Skyrim that gets me. It's the stink from the people.

speaker: Ambarys
dialogue: Don't you ever find it demeaning, working for that Nord family?

speaker: Ambarys
dialogue: Fine, then. I guess some Dunmer are content to be their pets.

speaker: Suvaris
dialogue: Here's what's going to happen. I'm going to pretend I didn't hear that, and you're going to leave me alone. Deal?

speaker: Ambarys
dialogue: What's new with the {{Sic|Cruel-Seas|Shatter-Shields}} Suvaris? Have they given you one of those helmets with the horns on them yet?

speaker: Suvaris
dialogue: What do you want from me? I work for them, okay? We're not friends. They pay me, and I get the job done. That's it.

speaker: Ambarys
dialogue: Touchy. Maybe some Dunmer lives in you yet.

speaker: Suvaris
dialogue: Either pour another drink or keep moving, Ambarys.

speaker: Ambarys
dialogue: Why do you even need to ask? They treat your people as bad as they do mine.

speaker: Scouts
dialogue: I think that's just their way. The Nords don't like anybody who's not a Nord, but they're not bad people, deep down.

speaker: Ambarys
dialogue: Look around you. Don't you know what their little war is about? They want all non-Nords out of Skyrim. That means you and me.

speaker: Scouts
dialogue: Oh, I doubt that very much. Who would load their ships, then?

speaker: Ambarys
dialogue: Just you wait and see.

speaker: Ambarys
dialogue: How much do they pay you per day?

speaker: Scouts
dialogue: That's really none of your business...

speaker: Ambarys
dialogue: How much?

speaker: Scouts
dialogue: Eight septims per day, plus lodging.

speaker: Ambarys
dialogue: Eight septims for breaking your back, and then you live in squalor. How much is your dignity worth?

speaker: Scouts
dialogue: If it's all the same to you, Scouts-Many-Marshes prefers to eat and drink in peace.

speaker: Ambarys
dialogue: Sorry, my scaly friend, you've come to the wrong place. Around here we don't ignore what's happening in the world.

speaker: Amren
dialogue: Sometimes I miss the soldier's life, but when I hold my daughter in my arms, I know I made the right choice.

speaker: Braith
dialogue: Papa, the next time you go away, I want to come with you.

speaker: Amren
dialogue: When I go away, I go to war. That's no place for a little girl.

speaker: Braith
dialogue: Every knight needs a squire. I could help you with your sword, things like that.

speaker: Amren
dialogue: Nice try, blossom, but I'm not a knight, I'm a mercenary. The answer's still no. Besides, your mother would miss you too much.

speaker: Braith
dialogue: Yeah. Right.

speaker: Braith
dialogue: Papa, I want to talk to you...

speaker: Amren
dialogue: Hmm? What about?

speaker: Braith
dialogue: Well, there's this boy, and...

speaker: Amren
dialogue: Listen, Braith... Why don't you talk to your mother about this, okay? There's a good girl.

speaker: or
dialogue: I wish your mother were still alive. She could answer you much better. Let me think on it and we'll talk later.

speaker: Saffir
dialogue: I know your family's honor is important to you, but we can't afford it!

speaker: Amren
dialogue: It took me weeks to find that thieves' den. I can't stop now, and I can't get the sword on my own.

speaker: Saffir
dialogue: So you're willing to starve your wife and daughter to reclaim some rusty old sword?

speaker: Amren
dialogue: I just need to hire one, maybe two good men. You won't starve.

speaker: Saffir
dialogue: I'll put it plainly. You can claim your sword, or you can keep your wife. If you set foot outside the gate, I won't be here when you return.

speaker: Amren
dialogue: Saffir! Wait... I....

speaker: Ancano
dialogue: I had hoped your scholars would be on a level comparable with my own colleagues. They are not.

speaker: Mirabelle
dialogue: I believe I made myself rather clear.

speaker: Ancano
dialogue: Yes, of course. I'm simply trying to understand the reasoning behind the decision.

speaker: Mirabelle
dialogue: You may be used to the Empire bowing to your every whim, but you will find the Thalmor find no such treatment here. You are here at the pleasure of the Arch-Mage. I hope you appreciate the opportunity.

speaker: Ancano
dialogue: Yes, of course. The Arch-Mage has my thanks.

speaker: Mirabelle
dialogue: Very good. Then we're done here.

speaker: Savos
dialogue: I'm sorry, were you about to say something?

speaker: Ancano
dialogue: Well, what is the meaning of this?

speaker: Quaranir
dialogue: I'm sorry, I'm afraid I don't understand.

speaker: Ancano
dialogue: Don't play coy. You asked to see a specific member of the College. Here he/she is. Now what is it that you want?

speaker: Quaranir
dialogue: There's been a misunderstanding. Clearly I should not be here. I shall simply take my leave.

speaker: Ancano
dialogue: What? What trickery is this? You're not going anywhere until I find out what you're up to.

speaker: Quaranir
dialogue: I'm not 'up to' anything. I apologize if I have offended you in any way.

speaker: Ancano
dialogue: We shall see about this...

speaker: Ancano
dialogue: I'm afraid I must intrude. I need to speak to your associate immediately.

speaker: Tolfdir
dialogue: This is most inappropriate! We are involved in serious research here!

speaker: Ancano
dialogue: Yes, I've no doubt of its gravity. This, however, is a matter that cannot wait.

speaker: Tolfdir
dialogue: Well, I'm quite sure I've never been interrupted like this before...the audacity!...[to player] I suppose we'll have to continue this at some later time, when we can avoid interruptions.

speaker: Ancano
dialogue: You've come for me, have you? You think I don't know what you're up to? You think I can't destroy you? The power to unmake the world at my fingertips, and you think you can do anything about it?

speaker: Tolfdir
dialogue: Spells have no effect!

speaker: Ancano
dialogue: I am beyond your pathetic attempts at magic. You cannot touch me.

speaker: Tolfdir
dialogue: The staff! Use it on the Eye!

speaker: Ancano
dialogue: Enough! Still you persist? Very well. Come then. See what I can do now.

speaker: Andurs
dialogue: I spend so much time among the dead, I sometimes forget how much I miss the company of the living.

speaker: Angeline Morrard
dialogue: Ah, welcome to Angela's Aromatics. Can I help with some herbal needs?

speaker: Angeline
dialogue: Vivienne, could you check out supplies of mandrake root?

speaker: Vivienne
dialogue: Which one is that again?

speaker: Angeline
dialogue: It's the root that looks like an ugly little man.

speaker: Vivienne
dialogue: In that case, I'm pretty sure it tried to buy me a drink last night.

speaker: in
dialogue: Name's Angi and if you try anything stupid I won't hesitate to put ''{{sic

speaker: Rolff
dialogue: You come here where you're not wanted, you eat our food, you pollute our city with your stink, and you refuse to help the Stormcloaks.

speaker: Suvaris
dialogue: But we haven't taken a side because it's not our fight.

speaker: Angrenor
dialogue: Hey, maybe the reason these gray-skins don't help in the war is because they're Imperial spies!

speaker: Suvaris
dialogue: Imperial spies? You can't be serious!

speaker: Rolff
dialogue: Maybe we'll pay you a visit tonight, little spy. We got ways of finding out what you really are.

speaker: Angvild
dialogue: We were supposed to be rich by now, you know. Thorgar insisted we'd be swimming in gold.

speaker: Anise
dialogue: I'm just a poor old woman, dear. No need to trouble yourself with me.

speaker: Verner
dialogue: Ever think about spending more time around town?

speaker: Annekke
dialogue: Not when there's so much to see!

speaker: Verner
dialogue: I guess I should join you more often.

speaker: Annekke
dialogue: You should. I miss you.

context: You used to love finding new places
speaker: Annekke
dialogue: Verner, you should have come out with me yesterday. I found the most amazing tree growing right out of a cave.

context: You used to love finding new places
speaker: Verner
dialogue: And I found a new deposit of amber. Would have been nice to have some help pulling it out.

context: You used to love finding new places
speaker: Annekke
dialogue: You used to love finding new places.

context: You used to love finding new places
speaker: Verner
dialogue: I still do. I just like to have food waiting for me when I come home.

speaker: Verner
dialogue: Sweetheart, did you move my pickaxe?

speaker: Annekke
dialogue: It's at the south end near that loose rockpile.

speaker: Verner
dialogue: So you can be helpful sometimes.

speaker: Annekke
dialogue: No need to get snippy.

speaker: Anoriath
dialogue: Do you hunt? The plains outside Whiterun are ripe with game.

speaker: Anoriath
dialogue: I don't suppose you're going to buy something this time?

speaker: Brenuin
dialogue: Just browsin' today. If the gods be kind, someone will take mercy on me and spare a few Septims.

speaker: Anoriath
dialogue: If they do, promise you'll actually purchase something for once.

speaker: Brenuin
dialogue: By Ysmir, I will. Gods know it's been too long since I tasted real meat.

speaker: Anoriath
dialogue: I've been thinking of hunting out beyond the boundaries of Whiterun Hold.

speaker: Elrindir
dialogue: Again? You just had an 'extended hunt' last month. To the pine forest, wasn't it?

speaker: Anoriath
dialogue: That was three days. I'm thinking more like three weeks.

speaker: Elrindir
dialogue: Three weeks? You're mad! You can't keep the stand closed for that long!

speaker: Anoriath
dialogue: Why not? Business has been terrible. Most folk would rather hunt their own meat than buy ours.

speaker: Elrindir
dialogue: Nonsense. That's just an excuse for you to avoid working, and 'commune with the greenwood like our fathers of old' and blah blah.

speaker: Anoriath
dialogue: Congratulations, brother. You've been living in Skyrim so long, you've become a Nord.

speaker: Elrindir
dialogue: At least the Nords don't shirk their responsibilities.

speaker: Elrindir
dialogue: Our stock of arrows is running a bit low.

speaker: Anoriath
dialogue: All right. I'll fletch some more when I get the time.

speaker: Elrindir
dialogue: Good. I'll do the same. We've still got plenty of shafts from that Riverwood shipment.

speaker: Anoriath
dialogue: It's been two months, and no word from father.

speaker: Elrindir
dialogue: Don't worry, brother. I'm sure he's fine. We've waited longer before receiving a letter.

speaker: Anoriath
dialogue: Might be worth riding out to Solitude, see if a messenger ship's come in.

speaker: Elrindir
dialogue: If it'll put your mind at ease, then I agree. But not now, all right? We need the business from the stand.

speaker: Nazeem
dialogue: Do you have anything even remotely fresh?

speaker: Anoriath
dialogue: I can assure you, it's all fresh. I hunt the game myself, every day.

speaker: Nazeem
dialogue: Hmm. As you say.

speaker: Anoriath
dialogue: Maybe you'd like to try the horker? Or some beef?

speaker: Nazeem
dialogue: You don't prepare the meat with any of those strange Elven spices, do you?

speaker: Anoriath
dialogue: Ahhhh... No, no Elven spices; just some salt, to preserve it. You're not afraid of salt, are you?

speaker: Nazeem
dialogue: I'm not 'afraid' of anything. I simply prefer quality merchandise. No, no this meat won't do at all. Too much fat, and it all smells... wrong.

speaker: Anoriath
dialogue: Suit yourself, then. The woods are that way. Outside the walls, walk straight ahead. Can't miss them. Good luck on your hunt.

speaker: Nazeem
dialogue: Good day.

speaker: Anoriath
dialogue: Ah, Olfina. How may I help you?

speaker: Olfina
dialogue: Got any sausages? I'm cooking a special breakfast for a friend, and they're his favorite.

speaker: Anoriath
dialogue: Would your good friend be named Jon, by any chance? I've spied the two of you talking quite intimately.

speaker: Olfina
dialogue: Best you forget whatever you think you saw, elf. Such idle talk can prove hazardous to one's health.

speaker: Ysolda
dialogue: I've got a recipe for venison stew that I want to try out. Will you have venison anytime soon?

speaker: Anoriath
dialogue: Certainly. I'll be sure to bring some back for you the next time I go hunting.

speaker: Ysolda
dialogue: Make it quick, and there might be a bowl of hot stew in it for you.

speaker: Anton Virane
dialogue: What have I done for the gods to take me so far from my beloved Daggerfall?

speaker: Anton
dialogue: Voada, you spilled laundry water in the soup pot again! Do I need to cut off your fingers to teach you a lesson?

speaker: Anton
dialogue: What was that?

speaker: Voada
dialogue: Now, now, brother, Rondach was just being his usual gloomy self, he didn't mean it, did you Rondach? You're just being silly again.

speaker: Anton
dialogue: Whatever. Just get back to work. Now.

speaker: Anton
dialogue: Filthy natives. Get to work. We have meals to prepare and no time to prepare them!

speaker: Voada
dialogue: Right away, sir!

speaker: Rondach
dialogue: Always another big meal to cook. Figures.

speaker: Anton
dialogue: Move it. Get to work. Get to work!

speaker: Anuriel
dialogue: As Riften's Steward I'm afraid I can provide only limited assistance, but speak your mind.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: Have our scouts come up with any information on these reports of dragons?

speaker: Anuriel
dialogue: Yes, milady. That unpleasantness at Helgen supposedly involved a dragon. It killed several soldiers before it departed.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: I want you to speak to the city guard. Make sure there's a contingency plan in effect in case Riften falls under attack.

speaker: Anuriel
dialogue: Yes, milady. I've also taken the liberty in preparing a private carriage... just in case.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: Good. If Riften should fall, it's only right that its leader be spared.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: Anuriel, a word please.

speaker: Anuriel
dialogue: Yes, my lady?

speaker: Laila
dialogue: It's been brought to my attention that the poison known as skooma may be present in our city. What do you know of this?

speaker: Anuriel
dialogue: I believe it to be a falsehood perpetrated by the Empire in order to weaken the {{Sicquote|citizen's|citizens'}} confidence in your ability to rule.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: Excellent, then they'll be no need to devote any resources to stopping it. Thank you, Anuriel. That will be all.

speaker: Anuriel
dialogue: My lady, Maven Black-Briar has sent word that she requires your seal in order to expand her shipments into Morrowind.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: But of course! Tell her she'll have it. Maven is one of the few people I can trust and I'd be delighted to give her my blessing.

speaker: Anuriel
dialogue: Yes, my lady. I will pass the good news on to her.

speaker: Unmid
dialogue: Anuriel, would you please stop declaring that the city is safe for the Jarl to roam? You and I both know that isn't true.

speaker: Anuriel
dialogue: I would never knowingly place Laila in danger, you know that too. Why do you always question my judgment? You don't trust me.

speaker: Unmid
dialogue: I trust you, I'm just concerned about her safety. That's all. Don't be angry with me.

speaker: Anuriel
dialogue: I'm not angry with you. Tell you what, lover. Meet me in my chambers later and we can discuss the situation in private.

speaker: Anuriel
dialogue: Unmid, my sweet. Are we still meeting later for... combat training?

speaker: Unmid
dialogue: Of course. Your training isn't complete yet.

speaker: Anuriel
dialogue: I look forward to it then.

speaker: Anwen
dialogue: Yes, yes. I haven't got all day...

speaker: Aquillius Aeresius
dialogue: Good business for the East Empire Company means all the more gold for the Empire.

speaker: Aranea Ienith
dialogue: We are children of the Twilight. Beings who are to be guided from the darkness into the light. And from the light into darkness.

speaker: Arcadia
dialogue: I offer remedies for ailments both common and rare. Do let me know if I can be of service.

speaker: Ardwen
dialogue: We are traveling to the Shrine of Kynareth in Whiterun. I hear the Gildergreen is more beautiful than ever since it's been restored.

speaker: Arivanya
dialogue: Horses. All day long. Do you have any idea how dull horses are?

speaker: Arnbjorn
dialogue: Here's all you need to know: I'm a werewolf. I like killing things. I love Astrid. I hate annoying people. And the color blue gives me a headache.

speaker: Arnbjorn
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Veezara
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha! Again! Again! Do the part where he tries to buy you some candy.

speaker: Gabriella
dialogue: Oh Babette, but you are so wicked.

speaker: Nazir
dialogue: What about you, Festus? How did that last contract turn out?

speaker: Arnbjorn
dialogue: Oh, yes, please, old man. Regale us with your tales of wizardry...

speaker: Gabriella
dialogue: And what of your latest, Arnbjorn. Something about a Khajiit? Merchant was it?

speaker: Babette
dialogue: Oh, a big doggy chasing a little kitty! How adorable!

speaker: Nazir
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Festus
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Veezara
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Arnbjorn
dialogue: I am not adorable, it was not funny, and he wasn't a merchant. He was a Khajiit monk, a master of the Whispering Fang style. But now he's dead... and I have a new loincloth.

speaker: Nazir
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Festus
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Veezara
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Babette
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Cicero
dialogue: But the Night Mother is mother to all! It is her voice we follow! Her will! Would you dare risk disobedience? And surely... punishment?

speaker: Festus Krex
dialogue: Oh, be quiet you great lumbering lapdog. The man has had a long journey. You can at least be civil. Mister Cicero, I for one am delighted you and the Night Mother have arrived. Your presence here signals a welcome return to tradition.

speaker: Cicero
dialogue: Oh, what a kind and wise wizard you are. Sure to earn our Lady's favor.

speaker: Astrid
dialogue: You and the Night Mother are of course welcome here, Cicero. And you will be afforded the respect deserving of your position as Keeper. Understood... husband?

speaker: Cicero
dialogue: Oh, yes yes yes! Thank you, thank you, thank you!

speaker: Astrid
dialogue: But make no mistake. I am the leader of this Sanctuary. My word is law. Are we clear on that point?

speaker: Cicero
dialogue: Oh yes, mistress. Perfectly! You're the boss.

speaker: Arngeir
dialogue: Sky above, Voice within.

speaker: Borri
dialogue: Fiik... Lo...Sah!

speaker: Einarth
dialogue: Fiik... Lo...Sah!

speaker: Wulfgar
dialogue: Fiik... Lo...Sah!

speaker: Wulfgar
dialogue: Wuld... Nah...Kest!

speaker: Einarth
dialogue: Arngeir, Rok/Rek los Dovahkiin, Strundu'ul. Rok/Rek fen tinvaak Paarthurnax.

speaker: Delphine
dialogue: So. Arngeir, is it? You know why we're here. Are you going to let us in or not?

speaker: Arngeir
dialogue: You were not invited here. You are not welcome here.

speaker: Delphine
dialogue: We have as much right to be at this council as all of you. More, actually, since we were the ones that put the Dragonborn on this path.

speaker: Arngeir
dialogue: Were you? The hubris of the Blades truly knows no bounds.

speaker: Esbern
dialogue: Delphine, we're not here to rehearse old grudges. The matter at hand is urgent. Alduin must be stopped. You wouldn't have called this council if you didn't agree. We know a great deal about the situation and the threat that Alduin poses to us all. You need us here if you want this council to succeed.

speaker: Arngeir
dialogue: Very well. You may enter.

speaker: Arngeir
dialogue: Now that everyone is here, please take your seats so we can begin. I hope that we have all come here in the spirit of...

speaker: Jarl Ulfric Stormcloak
dialogue: No. You insult us by bringing her to this negotiation? Your chief Talos-hunter?

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: That didn't take long.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Hear, hear!

speaker: Elenwen
dialogue: I have every right to be at this negotiation. I need to ensure that nothing is agreed to here that violates the terms of the White-Gold Concordat.

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: She's part of the Imperial delegation. You can't dictate who I bring to this council.

speaker: Arngeir
dialogue: Please. If we have to negotiate the terms of the negotiation, we will never get anywhere. Perhaps this would be a good time to get the Dragonborn's input on this matter.

speaker: Jarl Ulfric Stormcloak
dialogue: But she is to observe, nothing more. We are not negotiating with her, is that clear?

speaker: Elenwen
dialogue: Ulfric, why so hostile? After all, it's not the Thalmor that's burning your farms and killing your sons.

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: She's supposed to be on our side?

speaker: Jarl Ulfric Stormcloak
dialogue: You know exactly... no. Not this time.

speaker: Arngeir
dialogue: Now that that's settled, may we proceed?

speaker: Jarl Ulfric Stormcloak
dialogue: I have something to say first.

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: Here we go.

speaker: Jarl Ulfric Stormcloak
dialogue: The only reason I agreed to attend this council was to deal with the dragon menace. There's nothing else to talk about, unless the Empire is finally ready to renounce its unjust claim over the free people of Skyrim.

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: I knew he wouldn't be able to resist.

speaker: Jarl Ulfric Stormcloak
dialogue: We're here to arrange a temporary truce to allow the Dragonborn here to deal with the dragons. Nothing more. I consider even talking to the Empire a generous gesture.

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Are you done? Did you just come here to make speeches? Or can we get down to business?

speaker: Jarl Ulfric Stormcloak
dialogue: Yes, let's get this over with.

speaker: Arngeir
dialogue: Are we ready to proceed? Jarl Ulfric. General Tullius. This council is unprecedented. We are gathered here at the Dragonborn's request. I ask that you all respect the spirit of High Hrothgar, and do your best to begin the process of achieving a lasting peace in Skyrim. Who would like to open the negotiations?

speaker: Jarl Ulfric Stormcloak
dialogue: Yes, let's get down to it. We want control of Markarth. That's our price for agreeing to a truce.

speaker: Jarl Elisif the Fair
dialogue: So that's why you're here, Ulfric? You dare to insult the Greybeards by using this council to advance your own position?

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Jarl Elisif, I'll handle this.

speaker: Jarl Elisif the Fair
dialogue: General, this is outrageous! You can't be taking this demand seriously! I thought we were here to discuss a truce!

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Elisif! I said I'd handle it. Ulfric, you can't seriously expect us to give up Markarth at the negotiating table. You hope to gain in council what you've been unable to take in battle, is that it?

speaker: Arngeir
dialogue: I'm sure Jarl Ulfric does not expect something for nothing.

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: Yes, that'd be entirely out of character.

speaker: Arngeir
dialogue: What would the Empire want in return?

speaker: Jarl Elisif the Fair
dialogue: Wait. General, you don't intend to just hand over Markarth to that... traitor!

speaker: Jarl Balgruuf the Greater
dialogue: This is how the Empire repays us for our loyalty?

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Enough! First, let's be clear. This council wasn't my idea. I think it's a waste of time. You are a traitor to the Empire, and deserve a traitor's death. But I at least will negotiate in good faith.

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: You heard the man, Ulfric. We've made you a fair offer. Are you serious about these talks, or are you just here to posture?

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: You always were a fool, Ulfric. You're no better at diplomacy than you are on the battlefield.

speaker: Esbern
dialogue: Stop! Are you so blind to our danger that you can't see past your petty disagreements? Here you sit arguing about... nothing! While the fate of the land hangs in the balance!

speaker: Jarl Ulfric Stormcloak
dialogue: Is he with you, Delphine? If so, I advise you to tell him to watch his tongue.

speaker: Delphine
dialogue: He is with me. And I advise you both to listen to what he has to say, before you do anything rash.

speaker: Esbern
dialogue: Don't you understand the danger? Don't you understand what the return of the dragons means? Alduin has returned! The World-Eater! Even now, he devours the souls of your fallen comrades! He grows more powerful with every soldier slain in your pointless war! Can you not put aside your hatred for even one moment in the face of this mortal danger?

speaker: Elenwen
dialogue: A very pretty speech, but what does it have to do with...

speaker: Jarl Ulfric Stormcloak
dialogue: Shut up. If he's right about Alduin... we both have just as much to lose here, Tullius, remember that. Now, back to the matter at hand. Don't hand me a mug of sheep's piss and call it mead. These terms are still not acceptable.

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: I'm sure you have something in mind.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Damn right we do.

speaker: Jarl Ulfric Stormcloak
dialogue: You surrender Falkreath to us. Siddgeir steps down, and Dengeir of Stuhn resumes the Jarlship.

speaker: Jarl Ulfric Stormcloak
dialogue: It seems I have no other choice but to let the Dragonborn decide. Although I'm starting to doubt your fairness.

speaker: Jarl Ulfric Stormcloak
dialogue: These terms are not acceptable. You know that.

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: I'm listening.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Don't play dumb, Tullius!

speaker: Jarl Ulfric Stormcloak
dialogue: Bah! This is a waste of time. I can see that we won't get better terms from this council. So be it. The sons of Skyrim at least put the greater good above our own interests.

speaker: Jarl Elisif the Fair
dialogue: I have nothing to say to that murderer. General, you've proven yourself a good friend to Skyrim. I continue to trust that you will do your utmost to safeguard our interests.

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Thank you, Jarl Elisif. I appreciate your loyalty. The Empire can live with these terms, yes. For a temporary truce, until the dragon menace is dealt with. After that, Ulfric... there will be a reckoning. Count on it.

speaker: Jarl Ulfric Stormcloak
dialogue: Come on Galmar. We have a lot of work to do.

speaker: Jarl Balgruuf the Greater
dialogue: Giving up Markarth is a heavy price for this truce, Dragonborn. I hope it was worth it.

speaker: Arngeir
dialogue: Jarl Balgruuf, I assume you are familiar with the Dragonborn's plan?

speaker: Jarl Balgruuf the Greater
dialogue: Yes, I'm ready to do my part. Just say the word, and my men will help you spring this trap.

speaker: Arngeir
dialogue: But the difficulty remains - how to lure a dragon to Dragonsreach at all?

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Well that's an excellent question. You haven't overlooked that little detail, have you?

speaker: Esbern
dialogue: Ah. I believe I can be of help here.

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: I'd give a week's pay to see the look on Ulfric's face again, when he had to swallow the terms of the truce.

speaker: Arniel Gane
dialogue: I don't think anyone here truly understands how useful my work will be.

speaker: Faralda
dialogue: Come on, Arniel. Let's go.

speaker: Arniel
dialogue: Do we have to? They'd never lift a finger to help us.

speaker: Arnskar Ember-Master
dialogue: They don't call me the Ember-Master for nothing. What do you need?

speaker: Arob
dialogue: The air has the smell of beasts. The hunt is good today.

speaker: Nagrub
dialogue: Ah, the air is good today. I welcome the smell of blood from all the kills I will make.

speaker: Arob
dialogue: Patience, my son. The hunter {{sic|days|does}} not welcome the blood of his prey, he waits for it.

speaker: Arob
dialogue: The air has the smell of beasts. The hunt is good today.

speaker: Nagrub
dialogue: Yes, mother. I'm eager to prove my skills today.

speaker: Arvel the Swift
dialogue: Yes, the claw. I know how it works. The claw, the markings, the door in the Hall of Stories. I know how they all fit together!

speaker: Asbjorn Fire-Tamer
dialogue: I used to live at the orphanage here in Riften. Grelod said my ma and da left me there when I was a baby... that they didn't want me.

speaker: Asgeir Snow-Shod
dialogue: Sorry, I'm afraid I can't help you much right now... I'm currently in mourning.

speaker: Vulwulf
dialogue: Drink up, my boy! Drink to those who have fallen! May their souls find their way to Sovngarde!

speaker: Asgeir
dialogue: Take it easy, father. You're making a scene.

speaker: Vulwulf
dialogue: I'll rest easy when we've driven every last Imperial pig back across the Jerall Mountains!

speaker: Vulwulf
dialogue: Now, do me the honor I deserve as your father and drink up!

speaker: Asgeir
dialogue: Yes... father.

speaker: Asgeir
dialogue: I'm sorry you disapprove, father. But I've made up my mind. I'm not a warrior, I'm a businessman.

speaker: Vulwulf
dialogue: The only reason you have the gold for your 'business' is because I gave it to you.

speaker: Asgeir
dialogue: I'll pay you back, if it means that much.

speaker: Vulwulf
dialogue: It's not about the coin, it's about honoring your legacy by picking up arms and keeping this land free. The sooner you remember that, the better.

speaker: Nura
dialogue: How are things at the Meadery, my dear?

speaker: Vulwulf
dialogue: Not this again...

speaker: Nura
dialogue: Hush, Vulwulf... let the boy speak.

speaker: Asgeir
dialogue: It's going very well, actually. The war hasn't even slowed down our production or shipping at all.

speaker: Vulwulf
dialogue: Of course it is. That's what happens when you're partners with a corrupt Imperial whore like Maven.

speaker: Nura
dialogue: Vulwulf! The Empire may be our enemy, but Asgeir is still our son and we're a long way from Cyrodiil.

speaker: Asgeir
dialogue: Father, I promise you, this has nothing to do with Empires or politics. It's just business.

speaker: Vulwulf
dialogue: It has everything to do with politics. Asgeir my son, you have so much to learn.

speaker: Jorgen
dialogue: What's the Jarl going to do about it?

speaker: Thonnir
dialogue: How are we supposed to feel safe in our own homes?

speaker: Aslfur
dialogue: Please, enough already! I have told Jarl {{sicblock|Igrod|Idgrod}} of your concerns. She'll look after you all. Please, go back to your business.

speaker: Jorgen
dialogue: We have no need for wizards in our midst!

speaker: Thonnir
dialogue: Morthal has enough problems as it is!

speaker: Jorgen
dialogue: Bah, its no use. Let's get back to it then.

speaker: Idgrod Ravencrone
dialogue: It does not surprise me. They do not share in what I see, and I cannot explain it to them.

speaker: Aslfur
dialogue: Just guide them well, and all will work out.

speaker: Idgrod Ravencrone
dialogue: I have never doubted that, husband.

speaker: Aslfur
dialogue: Have you made a decision about Falion?

speaker: Idgrod Ravencrone
dialogue: What decision is there to be made? I allowed him to live here. I stand by that.

speaker: Aslfur
dialogue: Yes, but there are concerns. Rumors that he's up to something.

speaker: Idgrod Ravencrone
dialogue: We are all up to something, my dear. All is as it should be.

speaker: Idgrod Ravencrone
dialogue: What troubles you, husband?

speaker: Aslfur
dialogue: What? Oh, nothing. All is well.

speaker: Idgrod Ravencrone
dialogue: What troubles you, husband?

speaker: Aslfur
dialogue: It's Joric. I fear his condition is worse. He calls out in his sleep sometimes. I've heard Falion's name. What does it mean?

speaker: Idgrod Ravencrone
dialogue: Joric will be what Joric will be. Give it time.

speaker: Aslfur
dialogue: You have to understand, his presence here has caused... Well, it's difficult for the people to get used to.

speaker: Jonna
dialogue: They got used to Idgrod just fine, didn't they? So what's the difference?

speaker: Aslfur
dialogue: Yes, well. Perhaps you're right.

speaker: Aslfur
dialogue: How's business?

speaker: Jonna
dialogue: Very funny.

speaker: Aslfur
dialogue: No, I... I was just asking.

speaker: Jonna
dialogue: It's as bad as ever.

speaker: Assur
dialogue: Pa says the Empire made us leave, but the Empire just does whatever the elves tell them to.

speaker: Astrid
dialogue: This Sanctuary has been my entire life since I was a young woman. That's when I first discovered my, shall we call it 'aptitude,' for elimination.

speaker: Cicero
dialogue: But the Night Mother is mother to all! It is her voice we follow! Her will! Would you dare risk disobedience? And surely... punishment?

speaker: Festus Krex
dialogue: Oh, be quiet you great lumbering lapdog. The man has had a long journey. You can at least be civil. Mister Cicero, I for one am delighted you and the Night Mother have arrived. Your presence here signals a welcome return to tradition.

speaker: Cicero
dialogue: Oh, what a kind and wise wizard you are. Sure to earn our Lady's favor.

speaker: Astrid
dialogue: You and the Night Mother are of course welcome here, Cicero. And you will be afforded the respect deserving of your position as Keeper. Understood... husband?

speaker: Cicero
dialogue: Oh, yes yes yes! Thank you, thank you, thank you!

speaker: Astrid
dialogue: But make no mistake. I am the leader of this Sanctuary. My word is law. Are we clear on that point?

speaker: Cicero
dialogue: Oh yes, mistress. Perfectly! You're the boss.

speaker: Astrid
dialogue: By Sithis, this ends now! Back away, fool! Whatever you've been planning is over! Are you all right? I heard the commotion. Who was Cicero talking to? Where's the accomplice? Reveal yourself, traitor!

speaker: Cicero
dialogue: I spoke only to the Night Mother! I spoke to the Night Mother, but she didn't speak to me. Oh no. She spoke only to him/her! To the listener!

speaker: Astrid
dialogue: What? The Listener? What are you going on about? What is this lunacy?

speaker: Cicero
dialogue: It's true, it's true! The Night Mother has spoken! The silence has been broken! The Listener has been chosen!

speaker: Babette
dialogue: Just try to relax, Veezara. Let the elixir do its work. You'll feel better, shortly.

speaker: Veezara
dialogue: Achh... Thank you, dear. You are most kind. The jester's cut feels as bad as it looks, I'm afraid.

speaker: Astrid
dialogue: Damn it, this never should have happened! We knew better. We knew better, and still we let our guards down. Agh!

speaker: Festus Krex
dialogue: It's true, I'm afraid, Cicero was a little whirlwind, slashing this way and all that. It would have been funny, if he weren't trying to murder us all.

speaker: Veezara
dialogue: Bested by a fool. Who's the fool now, hmm?

speaker: Babette
dialogue: Hush, Veezara. You were very brave. Astrid may well be dead if not for you.

speaker: Astrid
dialogue: She's right. I'll be forever in your debt, dearest brother. Now be quiet. Just... just rest.

speaker: Ataf
dialogue: Youngest bard at the Bards College, at your service.

speaker: Jala
dialogue: Well, keep at it. The fish have to get to know you before they're willing to bite.

speaker: Ataf
dialogue: My mother always used to say that too.

context: A bottle of Spiced Wine for ya?
speaker: Ataf
dialogue: Viarmo is trying to get Elisif to allow the Burning of King Olaf. I don't want to look like I don't know how to drink in front of the other bards.

speaker: Ataf
dialogue: No thank you. I'm still feeling sick from the festival.

speaker: Jorn
dialogue: I think someone has a crush on Illdi.

speaker: Atahbah
dialogue: Please, come and browse our goods.

speaker: Atahbah
dialogue: My bones ache for the Moon Sugar. It has been too long since I tasted it.

speaker: Atahbah
dialogue: My ears hear the truth in your words, and yet my body shakes with the need.

speaker: Atahbah
dialogue: Yes, of course, your are right. Still, I would give much for even a few grains of moonsugar.

speaker: Atahbah
dialogue: We have been in this land for so long, I have forgotten what it feels like to walk on warm sand.

speaker: Atahbah
dialogue: Do you ever find that you regret making this journey?

speaker: Atahbah
dialogue: That is true. Perhaps I should be more grateful for this opportunity. Not many Khajiit can say that they have visited Skyrim.

speaker: Atar
dialogue: The Silver-Bloods have made you a very generous offer for this pile of dirt. I suggest you take it.

speaker: Ainethach
dialogue: I want you sellswords out of my mine.

speaker: Atar
dialogue: Watch your tongue, native. We'll leave when we're sure there are no Forsworn here.

speaker: Ainethach
dialogue: Oh, and when would that be, I wonder? When I sell my land to the Silver-Bloods?

speaker: Atar
dialogue: The Silver-Bloods have made you a very generous offer for this pile of dirt. I suggest you take it.

speaker: Athis
dialogue: This is not play-acting, here. We are the true spirit of Skyrim. Honor is in our blood, death in our hearts.

speaker: Athis
dialogue: What kind of weapon do you prefer? I like the smaller, quicker blades.

speaker: Athis
dialogue: Aren't they slow? I can get in and out before you can have one swing.

speaker: Torvar
dialogue: Let's test that out some time.

speaker: Athis
dialogue: You might do well to learn a new weapon. Vary your style a bit.

speaker: Athis
dialogue: But ten little cuts...

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: All I need is one to cut you in half.

speaker: Athis
dialogue: Well, when you put it that way...

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: You only use the little swords.

speaker: Athis
dialogue: It's called a shortsword, you oaf. Its quicker. Sharper. And it can cut through a whale like a razor.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: But whales eat razorfish.

speaker: Athis
dialogue: And they always come to regret it.

speaker: Torvar
dialogue: One day, when you and I are on the Circle, we can change the way things are run around here.

speaker: Athis
dialogue: I don't think that's how the Circle works.

speaker: Torvar
dialogue: They're lording it over us all the time, though.

speaker: Athis
dialogue: Young warriors are smart to listen to older ones. They've lived.

speaker: Savos
dialogue: Come on, we're finally here! Let's not waste any more time!

speaker: Takes-In-Light
dialogue: Are we truly sure this is a good idea?

speaker: Atmah
dialogue: We'll be back at the College before anyone even knows we're gone.

speaker: Girduin
dialogue: You would care about that, since you're the Arch-Mage's favorite!

speaker: Savos
dialogue: Don't forget, this whole idea was Atmah's to begin with.

speaker: Hafnar
dialogue: Let's just get inside, see what's in there.

speaker: Elvali
dialogue: I can't believe we're doing this.

speaker: Savos
dialogue: Can you imagine the looks on their faces when we come back?

speaker: Hafnar
dialogue: You keep talking like you're sure we'll find something useful in here.

speaker: Girduin
dialogue: Given the history of this place, it's more than likely there's still some amount of power here.

speaker: Savos
dialogue: Enchanted weapons, tomes of ancient knowledge, Shalidor's secrets themselves -- who knows what we could find!

speaker: Takes-In-Light
dialogue: And what if... What if there are things guarding this place?

speaker: Atmah
dialogue: Against six College-trained mages? I think we'll be fine.

speaker: Elvali
dialogue: We... we have to go back. We can't leave Girduin...

speaker: Hafnar
dialogue: We barely made it out alive, and you want to go back in?

speaker: Atmah
dialogue: It's too late. There isn't enough of him left to go back in after.

speaker: Takes-In-Light
dialogue: Gods, what have we done?

speaker: Savos
dialogue: We can't go back. Might as well go forward. We can still do this.

speaker: Atmah
dialogue: Savos is right. We can make it if we just stay alert.

speaker: Savos
dialogue: Come on, we can't stop now. We have to keep moving!

speaker: Atmah
dialogue: Where's Elvali? She was right behind me.

speaker: Hafnar
dialogue: Dead. Something grabbed her from behind. Gone before I could do anything.

speaker: Takes-In-Light
dialogue: This is insanity. We never should've come here.

speaker: Atmah
dialogue: You're right. This is all my fault. Should we turn around, head back?

speaker: Hafnar
dialogue: I don't think going back is a good idea.

speaker: Savos
dialogue: Going back would be the end of all of us. We keep pushing forward, and we'll make it. We will!

speaker: Atmah
dialogue: Come on, you can make it. Let's go.

speaker: Atmah
dialogue: We shouldn't have left her there to die!

speaker: Savos
dialogue: What else could we do? Stay there and die with her? She refused to go on, we didn't have a choice!

speaker: Hafnar
dialogue: This is it, you know. Through this door. Can you feel it?

speaker: Atmah
dialogue: We're not going to make it, are we?

speaker: Hafnar
dialogue: We stay together, no matter what. Agreed?

speaker: Atmah
dialogue: I'll be right with you.

speaker: Savos
dialogue: Agreed. We all stay together.

speaker: Atub
dialogue: Ugor, no! This may be the one we need.

speaker: Ugor
dialogue: We need nothing from outsiders! Yamarz will provide for us.

speaker: Atub
dialogue: We cannot carry on this way! You know we are doomed if we do not do something!

speaker: Ugor
dialogue: Yamarz charged me with keeping outsiders away from Largashbur. You would have me disobey him?

speaker: Atub
