dialogue: You were charged with keeping us inside the walls. Have faith, Ugor. I only wish the best for our tribe.

speaker: Ugor
dialogue: Fine, it's your neck.

speaker: Atub
dialogue: It is time, Yamarz.

speaker: Yamarz
dialogue: You bring an outsider here, and now insist I call on Malacath for help, when he has clearly forsaken me? You try my patience, Atub.

speaker: Atub
dialogue: Doing nothing will not grant our tribe relief from this curse. We must try.

speaker: Yamarz
dialogue: Grrr. Fine, let's get this over with.

speaker: Atub
dialogue: Now, we begin the ritual... Great Malacath, we beseech you, aid us in our time of need...

speaker: Yamarz
dialogue: Why are we bothering with this?

speaker: Malacath
dialogue: You pathetic weakling!

speaker: Yamarz
dialogue: What's that?

speaker: Atub
dialogue: Malacath has heard my pleas! He speaks to us!

speaker: Malacath
dialogue: You dare summon me, Yamarz?

speaker: Yamarz
dialogue: What? What is this?

speaker: Malacath
dialogue: You don't deserve to call yourself an Orc! You're weak, you're small, and you're an embarrassment! You let giants... Giants!... overrun my shrine. Bring me their leader's club as an offering, and I might release you from this curse!

speaker: Atub
dialogue: So it will be. Malacath has spoken, Yamarz. Your path is clear.

speaker: Yamarz
dialogue: Very well. {{Hide|You|Referring to the Dragonborn}}, outsider, come here! I want a word.

speaker: Malacath
dialogue: Yamarz was a coward and a weakling. His deceitful ways have cost you all greatly.

speaker: Atub
dialogue: So he has been punished? And what of us? What fate shall we suffer?

speaker: Malacath
dialogue: You'll have to prove yourselves, but I'm willing to give you a chance. Gularzob's in charge now. Let's hope he's a better chief. {{Hide|You|Referring to the Dragonborn}}, place that hammer on the shrine. You're the only one who's proven worthy in all of this...

speaker: Augur of Dunlain
dialogue: You seek meaning, shelter in Knowledge. You will not find it.

speaker: Aval Atheron
dialogue: You need anything, come see me. I'm as resourceful as I am discreet.

speaker: Aval
dialogue: Friend Brunwulf, how good to see you! If you see anything you like, just let me know and I'll glad offer you a discount.

speaker: Brunwulf
dialogue: That's not necessary. I'll pay the same price as anyone else.

speaker: Aval
dialogue: But I insist. And with good reason; Malthyr told me that you've been speaking to Ulfric about our situation. He said you're going to help us. So few Nords have ever offered to help us, a discount is the least I can do.

speaker: Brunwulf
dialogue: I'm not looking for special treatment, Aval. All I did was talk to Ulfric. For all I know, he's already forgotten the conversation. I wouldn't get your hopes up.

speaker: Aval
dialogue: Oh, I see. Well, I'm sorry to have troubled you about it. Just... know that your efforts are appreciated.

speaker: Tova
dialogue: I understand you purchase used goods, as well as sell them?

speaker: Aval
dialogue: Yes, that's right. Whether or not I'm interested depends on what you've got, of course.

speaker: Tova
dialogue: I have some things that belonged to my daughter, Friga. She... she won't be needing them any more.

speaker: Aval
dialogue: Oh, I see. Yes, yes of course I'll take a look. Just bring them by whenever it's convenient for you.

speaker: Aventus Aretino
dialogue: When I grow up, I'm going to be an assassin. That way I can help lots of children, just like you!

speaker: Grimvar
dialogue: Then it's true, what everyone is saying? That Aventus Aretino is doing the Black Sacrament? Trying to summon the Dark Brotherhood?

speaker: Idesa
dialogue: Oh, Grimvar... always with the nonsense. No, no, of course not. Those are just tales...

speaker: Grimvar
dialogue: Fine. Then I'll invite him out to play. He lives right there. I'm going to knock on his door...

speaker: Idesa
dialogue: No, child! Wait! That boy, that house - they're cursed.

speaker: Grimvar
dialogue: Ha! Then I'm right. I knew it. He's trying to have somebody killed!

speaker: Idesa
dialogue: All right. I won't deny it, child. What you heard is true. But Aventus Aretino walks a dark path. His actions can lead only to ruin. Now, enough. We will speak no more of this. I am the only friend you need.

speaker: Avursa Sarethi
dialogue: Between the farm chores, cultivating my supply of Nirnroot and keeping a tight rein on my sister Aduri, there's little time for rest.

speaker: Avrusa
dialogue: Aduri, how come the fields haven't been tilled like I asked?

speaker: Aduri
dialogue: Because it's boring. The fields are going to do fine... you don't have to dote over them so much.

speaker: Avrusa
dialogue: Boring? That food is paying for everything. If we lose even a single crop, we could starve or be forced to beg. I won't have it!

speaker: Aduri
dialogue: All right, I understand. I'll do it tomorrow, okay? Just get off my back.

speaker: Aduri
dialogue: Have you decided if I can head up to Solitude yet? I hear it's the best place to meet someone who may be willing to teach me to paint.

speaker: Avrusa
dialogue: I'm sorry, Aduri, not this year. Perhaps next year after the harvest, I don't know. There's so much to do.

speaker: Aduri
dialogue: It's not going to be next year, nor the year after that! You just care about this farm more than you care about me!

speaker: Avrusa
dialogue: Painting won't put food on the table, but our crops will. Be patient Aduri... it will happen someday, I promise.

speaker: Aduri
dialogue: Where did all these pretty red plants come from?

speaker: Avrusa
dialogue: Remember Uncle Sinderion? These are the plants he was searching for... the Crimson Nirnroot.

speaker: Aduri
dialogue: They're beautiful. I can see why he wanted to find them.

speaker: Avrusa
dialogue: One day, these beautiful plants will make us famous and we can finally move off of this farm... thanks to Sinderion.

speaker: Avulstein Gray-Mane
dialogue: This was such a glorious city. But then everything had to change. The Empire came... and my brother was lost...

speaker: Fralia
dialogue: Welcome to our home.

speaker: Avulstein
dialogue: Mother, what's the meaning of this? Who have you brought into our home?

speaker: Fralia
dialogue: I can't take any more of this. No weapons, please. Let's just talk.

speaker: Avulstein
dialogue: All right, mother.

speaker: Azura
dialogue: You no longer bear the burden of prophecy. You have achieved your destiny. You are free. The doomed Dwemer's folly, Lord Dagoth's temptation, the Tribunal's seduction, the god's heart freed, the prophecy fulfilled. All fates sealed and sins redeemed. If you have pity, mourn the lost, but let the weeping cease. The Blight is gone, and the sun's golden honey gilds the land. Hail savior, Hortator, and Nerevarine. Your people look to you for protection. Monster and villains great and small still threaten the people of Vvardenfell. Enemies and evils abound, yet indomitable will might rid Morrowind of all its ills. For you, our thanks and blessings; our gift and token given. Come; take this thing from the hand of god.

speaker: Azzada Lylvieve
dialogue: Got a loving wife, a healthy son, and a patch of land to call my own. What more could a man ask for?

speaker: Babette
dialogue: It's been quite a boon looking like a child. No one ever suspects a thing.

speaker: Arnbjorn
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Veezara
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha! Again! Again! Do the part where he tries to buy you some candy.

speaker: Gabriella
dialogue: Oh Babette, but you are so wicked.

speaker: Nazir
dialogue: What about you, Festus? How did that last contract turn out?

speaker: Arnbjorn
dialogue: Oh, yes, please, old man. Regale us with your tales of wizardry...

speaker: Gabriella
dialogue: And what of your latest, Arnbjorn. Something about a Khajiit? Merchant was it?

speaker: Babette
dialogue: Oh, a big doggy chasing a little kitty! How adorable!

speaker: Nazir
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Festus
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Veezara
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Arnbjorn
dialogue: I am not adorable, it was not funny, and he wasn't a merchant. He was a Khajiit monk, a master of the Whispering Fang style. But now he's dead... and I have a new loincloth.

speaker: Nazir
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Festus
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Veezara
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Babette
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Veezara
dialogue: Tell me, sister. Are the stories true?

speaker: Babette
dialogue: You must be talking about the caravan job...

speaker: Veezara
dialogue: You infiltrated the position, eliminated the target, and made it look like an accident. Impressive. I'd say you earned your bonus on that one!

speaker: Babette
dialogue: In truth? It was so easy, I feel a bit guilty. Once again, the sweet, innocent child earned more trust than was wise.

speaker: Babette
dialogue: Just try to relax, Veezara. Let the elixir do its work. You'll feel better, shortly.

speaker: Veezara
dialogue: Achh... Thank you, dear. You are most kind. The jester's cut feels as bad as it looks, I'm afraid.

speaker: Astrid
dialogue: Damn it, this never should have happened! We knew better. We knew better, and still we let our guards down. Agh!

speaker: Festus Krex
dialogue: It's true, I'm afraid, Cicero was a little whirlwind, slashing this way and all that. It would have been funny, if he weren't trying to murder us all.

speaker: Veezara
dialogue: Bested by a fool. Who's the fool now, hmm?

speaker: Babette
dialogue: Hush, Veezara. You were very brave. Astrid may well be dead if not for you.

speaker: Astrid
dialogue: She's right. I'll be forever in your debt, dearest brother. Now be quiet. Just... just rest.

speaker: Nazir
dialogue: I'm going... as fast... as I can, you stupid she-devil. I don't see you... helping...

speaker: Babette
dialogue: I'm not exactly built for manual labor. Now come on, you've almost got it.

speaker: Nazir
dialogue: One more... pull... Yeeaahh! There.

speaker: Babette
dialogue: Can you get it open?

speaker: Nazir
dialogue: I think so. Just hold on a moment.

speaker: Nazir
dialogue: Babette, my girl - pack your things. We're moving.

speaker: Babette
dialogue: I was hoping you'd say that.

speaker: Bagrak
dialogue: You have returned with the gauntlets! Enter. Speak to our chief right away.

speaker: Hadring
dialogue: Him? Oh... Ah, name's Balablob or Malaclob, one of them funny Orc names. Talks real good, though. Not a savage at all.

speaker: Balgruuf the Greater
dialogue: If it's the war you're referring to, I'm on the side of Whiterun.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: My lord. Please. You have to listen. I only counsel caution. We cannot afford to act rashly in times like these. If the news from Helgen is true... well, there's no telling what it means.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: What would you have me do, then? Nothing?

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: My lord. Please. This is no time for rash action. I just think we need more information before we act. I just...

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Who's {{Hide|this|referring to the Dragonborn}}, then?

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: What do you say now, Proventus? Shall we continue to trust in the strength of our walls? Against a dragon?

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: My lord, we should send troops to Riverwood at once. It's in the most immediate danger, if that dragon is lurking in the mountains...

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: The Jarl of Falkreath will view that as a provocation! He'll assume we're preparing to join Ulfric's side and attack him.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Enough! Irileth, send a detachment to Riverwood at once.

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: Yes, my Jarl.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: We should not...

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: I'll not stand idly by while a dragon burns my hold and slaughters my people!

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: If you'll excuse me, I'll return to my duties.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: That would be best.

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: Farengar! Farengar, you need to come at once. A dragon's been sighted nearby. {{Hide|You|Referring to the Dragonborn}} should come, too.

speaker: Farengar
dialogue: A dragon! How exciting! Where was it seen? What was it doing?

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: I'd take this a bit more seriously if I were you. If a dragon decides to attack Whiterun, I don't know if we can stop it. Let's go.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: So, Irileth tells me you came from the western watchtower?

speaker: Whiterun Guard
dialogue: Yes, my lord.

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: Tell him what you told me. About the dragon.

speaker: Whiterun Guard
dialogue: Uh... that's right. We saw it coming from the south. It was fast... faster than anything I've ever seen.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: What did it do? Is it attacking the watchtower?

speaker: Whiterun Guard
dialogue: No, my lord. It was just circling overhead when I left. I never ran so fast in my life... I thought it would come after me for sure.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Good work, son. We'll take it from here. Head down to the barracks for some food and rest. You've earned it. Irileth, you'd better gather some guardsmen and get down there.

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: I've already ordered my men to muster near the main gate.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Good. Don't fail me.

speaker: Farengar
dialogue: I should come along. I would very much like to see this dragon.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: No. I can't afford to risk both of you. I need you here working on ways to defend the city against these dragons.

speaker: Farengar
dialogue: As you command.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: One last thing, Irileth. This isn't a death or glory mission. I need to know what we're dealing with.

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: Don't worry, my lord. I'm the very soul of caution.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: Good. You're finally here. The Jarl's been waiting for you.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: You heard the summons. What else could it mean? The Greybeards...

speaker: Hrongar
dialogue: We were just talking about you. My brother needs a word with you.

speaker: Hrongar
dialogue: That was the voice of the Greybeards, summoning you to High Hrothgar! This hasn't happened in ... centuries, at least. Not since Tiber Septim himself was summoned when he was still Talos of Atmora!

speaker: Hrongar
dialogue: Nord nonsense?! Why you puffed-up ignorant... these are our sacred traditions that go back to the founding of the First Empire!

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Hrongar. Don't be so hard on Avenicci.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Back to business, Proventus. We still have a city to defend.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: Yes, my lord.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Proventus, what do you make of all this? If Ulfric were to attack Whiterun...

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: As in all things, lord, caution... I urge us to wait and see.

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: Prey waits.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: I'm of a mind with Irileth. It's time to act.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: You plan to march on Windhelm?

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: I'm not a fool, Proventus. I mean it's time to challenge Ulfric to face me as a man, or march his Stormcloaks up to the gates.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: He'll do no such thing! A dagger in the back is all you could expect!

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: He was rather straightforward with Torygg.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: Torygg? He simply walked up to the boy and murdered him!

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: True. He's already proven his personal strength. Now he seeks to prove his army's.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: Then might I urge you to consider General Tullius' request? I mean, if you are bent on offending Jarl Ulfric...

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: Ulfric is the one who has offended. But, Proventus has a point. Ulfric has made it clear; in his mind, to refuse his claim is to side with the Empire.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: And what harm is there in letting a few Legionnaires die in place of your own men?

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: It seems cowardly.

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: Was it cowardly then to accept the White-Gold Concordat?

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: This again? That was different. Was I given a chance to object to the terms of the treaty? No. The Jarls weren't asked. We were told. And we had to like it.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: The chests of gold didn't hurt.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Damnit! This isn't about gold!

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: It's time to decide.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: Lord, wait. Let us see if Ulfric is serious.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Oh, he's serious. But so am I.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Proventus. Bring me my pen. And the good parchment.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: Are we writing a letter, Lord?

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Yes, to General Tullius. I need to make a few things clear before I accept these Legionnaires of his.

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: Halt! In the name of the Jarl, Balgruuf the Greater.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: It's a little late for that, don't you think?

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: Stay back, lord!

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: I'll be damned if I let this rabble take my city without raising my own sword.

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: Protect the Jarl with your lives!

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Enough! That's enough. I surrender... I surrender. Peace! Everyone stand down. That's an order. Stand down!

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Vignar Gray-Mane! Your family was noticeably absent from the walls. Now I know why. Wouldn't a dagger in the back have sufficed?

speaker: Vignar
dialogue: You think this is personal? The Empire has no place in Skyrim... not any more. And you? You have no place in Whiterun anymore.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: A convenient position to hold now. But mark my words, old man, in the days to come, Ulfric will spread his rebellion thin. And what then? We need the Empire, as much as it needs us. We Nords are the Empire! Our blood built it. Our blood sustains it! You of all people should know that.

speaker: Vignar
dialogue: If this was my Empire, I'd be able to worship whoever I damned well pleased. You wish to see an Empire without Talos? Without its soul? We should be fighting those witch-elves, not bending knee to them. The Emperor is nothing more than a puppet of the Thalmor. Skyrim needs a High King who will fight for her, and Whiterun needs a Jarl who will do the same.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Tell me, Vignar. Was all this worth it? How many of those corpses lining our streets wear the faces of men who once called you friend? What about their families?

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Enough! Both of you! There is a burning city out there that needs a government.

speaker: Vignar
dialogue: He's right. Galmar, come, let us restore order.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: This isn't over. You hear me you old fool! This isn't over! {{hide|And you. A Stormcloak? I'd thought better of you.|Referring to the Dragonborn.}} You'll all come to regret this day.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: It's all for a good cause, old chap. Ulfric Stormcloak? The rightful High King? That's bordering on treason, man! Stand up. Stand up, I say!

speaker: Razelan
dialogue: I don't understand... did you say Ulfric Stormcloak? Fine fellow, although a bit too fond of... I mean, no, of course, I condemn him in the most...

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: You take it back then? You retract your statement? Well?

speaker: Elenwen
dialogue: Razelan. And you promised to behave yourself this time. Remove him. He's disturbing the other guests.

speaker: Razelan
dialogue: I protest! This is an insult to the dignity of my person! This time I'm completely innocent!

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Tell your men to stand down. I don't need any help dealing with this kind of fool. He isn't worth the trouble. I apologize for the disruption to such a festive occasion.

speaker: Razelan
dialogue: Absolutely not! I protest... uh, that is, yes, of course. I still don't understand what just... oh never mind.

speaker: Whiterun Guard
dialogue: Hear that?

speaker: Whiterun Guard 2
dialogue: Shor's bones, here he comes!

speaker: Jarl Balgruuf the Greater
dialogue: Steady! Steady, now! Keep under cover until it's down!

speaker: Jarl Balgruuf the Greater
dialogue: Get back! Get back! We need to trap it, not kill it!

speaker: Jarl Balgruuf the Greater
dialogue: That's it! Now, wait until he's inside!

speaker: Jarl Balgruuf the Greater
dialogue: Got him!

speaker: Whiterun Guard 3
dialogue: I think it's holding!

speaker: Odahviing
dialogue: Horvutah med kodaav. Caught like a bear in a trap... Zok frini grind ko grah drun viiki, Dovahkiin. Ah. I forget. You do not have the dovah speech. My... eagerness to meet you in battle was my... undoing, Dovahkiin. I salut your, hmm, low cunning in devising such a grahmindol - strategem.

speaker: Farengar
dialogue: Incredible! Uh... sir, you have no idea how long I have waited for such an opportunity! I would be most appreciative if you would permit me to perform some, ah, tests on you. Purely in the interests of the advancement of knowledge.

speaker: Odahviing
dialogue: Begone, mage. Do not test my promise to the Dovahkiin.

speaker: Farengar
dialogue: I assure you, you will not even notice me. Most of them are hardly painful at all to a large dragon such as yourself.

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: Farengar, very bad idea. Even for you.

speaker: Farengar
dialogue: Surely you won't miss a few scales... or a small amount of blood...

speaker: Odahviing
dialogue: Joor mey! What are you doing back there? Yol... Toor...Shul!

speaker: Jarl Balgruuf the Greater
dialogue: Farengar! Enough, fool!

speaker: Whiterun Guard
dialogue: Get ready to open the trap! This seems like a really bad idea to me.

speaker: Jarl Balgruuf the Greater
dialogue: Carry on, soldier. This is all part of the Dragonborn's plan.

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: By all the gods...

speaker: Odahviing
dialogue: Faas nu, zini dein ruthi ahst vaal.

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: You're either the bravest person I've ever met or the biggest fool.

speaker: Jarl Balgruuf the Greater
dialogue: May Kynareth guard you while you pass through her realm!

speaker: Hrongar
dialogue: Have you reconsidered my idea?

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: I haven't changed my mind, if that's what you're asking. I won't leave Whiterun defenseless, even for a day.

speaker: Hrongar
dialogue: If we send half our guards to aid the Legion, just for a few days, it could tip the scales in the Empire's favor. The Companions can help protect the city, and the Emperor will be in our debt.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Have you lost all sense? We are short on guards as it is! If we lose half our men, the Dark Brotherhood and Thieves Guild will have the run of the city. The Stormcloaks will be the least of our worries! The answer is no, I tell you! Now stop pestering me with your war-mongering!

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: Balgruuf, did you slip out again last night for a drink at the Bannered Mare?

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Heard about that, did you? Yes, I went out for a pint or two. What of it?

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: These secret visits to the tavern will make you an easy target for an enemy assassin. You should have told me first.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Damn it, woman, I'm the Jarl of Whiterun! I won't apologize for talking to my people. You can't protect me every moment of the day.

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: That might be so, but it will never stop me from trying.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: My lord, our provisions are running dangerously low. Our stores of meat, wine, and grain are all but depleted.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Purchase more supplies, then. That's your job as Steward, isn't it? Why do you trouble me with these details?

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: My lord, since Ulfric Stormcloak's uprising, the cost of goods has doubled. I'll need more coin if I'm to provision us properly.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Our coffers are nearly empty. I can scarcely afford to pay the guards, and we need every one of them in these troubled times. You'll have to make do with what we have, Proventus.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: Yes, my lord.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: I won't say it again, Vignar; Talos worship is forbidden. It's the Empire's law, and we're still a part of the Empire.

speaker: Vignar
dialogue: A law made at the tip of an Aldmeri sword, aye. A sword stained red with Nord blood. Is this what our people fought and died for? To forsake our most beloved ancestor and divine?

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: I'm no happier about this than you are, but I don't want the see the Thalmor rounding up people in the streets and throwing them in prison.

speaker: Vignar
dialogue: Do your loyalties lie with the Thalmor, then?

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: I warn you, Gray-Mane, you are treading on dangerous ground.

speaker: Vignar
dialogue: Don't threaten me, boy. You're either a Nord who respects our traditions, or you're not. If not, it isn't me you'll have to answer to, but the people of this city and this Hold.

speaker: Balimund
dialogue: Come to see Balimund perform miracles with steel, eh?

speaker: Banning
dialogue: I like the loyalty of a dog. Not as fickle as a wolf.

speaker: Eola
dialogue: Not too full on bread and wine, I hope?

speaker: Banning
dialogue: I always leave room for the main course, Eola.

speaker: Hogni
dialogue: When was your first meal, Banning?

speaker: Banning
dialogue: Do dogs count?

speaker: Hogni
dialogue: Of course they don't count!

speaker: Banning
dialogue: My friend Marex. We were hunting, and I thought he was an elk.

speaker: Hogni
dialogue: That must have been quite a surprise.

speaker: Banning
dialogue: Either way, I came back with meat for the table.

speaker: Barbas
dialogue: Skyrim is now host to giant, flying lizards and two-legged cat-men... and you're surprised by me? Yes. I just talked. And am continuing to do so.

speaker: Barbas
dialogue: I knew I could trust you!

speaker: Shrine to Clavicus Vile
dialogue: Yeah, yeah, dog gets master, master gets cosmic axe, everyone's happy. Just get over here, mutt.

speaker: Shrine to Clavicus Vile
dialogue: Ah, that feels so much better! You forget how nice supreme power feels until you've been stuck in a cave for a few years. Now, as for your wish... Power, was it? You can be a part of a tremendous power - all you have to do is let your soul be absorbed by this axe. I never said it would be your power... Oh, fine. Have my boon and be done with it. Got more interesting deals to make, anyway.

speaker: Barknar
dialogue: Enjoying the hospitalities of the inn. Suggest you do the same.

speaker: Bassianus Axius
dialogue: Hmph. What a boring conversation.

speaker: Beem-Ja
dialogue: Don't rush ahead. This is a trap if I ever saw one.

speaker: Salma
dialogue: Would you look at that!

speaker: Beem-Ja
dialogue: This is it! Gathrik awaits us!

speaker: Salma
dialogue: What are you on about? Let's just get the treasure here and go.

speaker: Beirand
dialogue: Seems there's no end to the needs of the Imperials. But what can I help you with?

speaker: Svari
dialogue: They can't hurt uncle Roggvir. Tell them he didn't do it.

speaker: Addvar
dialogue: Svari, you need to go home. Go home and stay there until your mother comes.

speaker: Aldis
dialogue: Lock the city gate.

speaker: Vivienne
dialogue: You should tell her that her uncle is scum that betrayed his High King. Best she know now, Addvar.

speaker: Addvar
dialogue: You're all heart, Vivienne.

speaker: Aldis
dialogue: Roggvir. You helped Ulfric Stormcloak escape this city after he murdered High King Torygg. By opening that gate for Ulfric you betrayed the people of Solitude.

speaker: Sorex
dialogue: He doesn't deserve to speak!

speaker: Roggvir
dialogue: There was no murder! Ulfric challenged Torygg. He beat the High King in fair combat.

speaker: Roggvir
dialogue: Such as our way! Such as the ancient custom of Skyrim, and all Nords!

speaker: Vivienne
dialogue: Cut 'em down!

speaker: Aldis
dialogue: Guard. Prepare the prisoner.

speaker: Roggvir
dialogue: I don't need your help.

speaker: Aldis
dialogue: Very well, Roggvir. Bow your head.

speaker: Roggvir
dialogue: On this day... I go to Sovngarde.

speaker: Beitild
dialogue: My miners are as dumb as rocks are grey.

speaker: Beitild
dialogue: Keep at it. We need to work twice as hard now that fat-headed Leigelf has declared war!

speaker: Beitild
dialogue: No he isn't! He's the enemy, and we are going to crush him.

speaker: Karl
dialogue: Drafted into a war, how could my life get worse?

speaker: Belethor
dialogue: Everything's for sale, my friend. Everything. If I had a sister, I'd sell her in a second.

speaker: Belrand
dialogue: Versatility is the key to survival. Hire me, and you'll well-prepared to face threats both magical and mundane.

speaker: Belyn
dialogue: Make sure the back fence is repaired. I swear I saw some skeevers in nibbling the leaves yesterday.

speaker: Adisla
dialogue: Oh, no skeevers out here, sir. They can't stand the cold.

speaker: Belyn
dialogue: Maybe, but the way you burn through all that wood to keep the cabin toasty, they might mistake this place for Elsweyr.

speaker: Adisla
dialogue: Sorry, sir. These old bones do like a bit of warmth in the evening. There's no need to make fun.

speaker: Belyn
dialogue: You just need to remember that there's a war on, and firewood isn't cheap these days.

speaker: Adisla
dialogue: I was wondering if you had ordered the shipment of that frostwheat, sir.

speaker: Belyn
dialogue: Yes, but that fool Endario can't get it in. I'll thrash him when I get back to the city, don't you worry.

speaker: Adisla
dialogue: I wasn't wanting to get anyone in trouble, sir. Just wanting to get the new planting started, is all.

speaker: Belyn
dialogue: Yes, wouldn't want to miss the lush summer we have ahead.

speaker: Belyn
dialogue: So, have you ever actually spoken to Captain Lonely-Gale?

speaker: Adisla
dialogue: By the gods, he's just a retired ship's captain.

speaker: Belyn
dialogue: Maybe to you, but he's just so... his story is...

speaker: Adisla
dialogue: He's just a guard captain. And not a very good one, at that.

speaker: Bendt
dialogue: Meals are served to bards at designated times. Find an inn if you want to make requests.

speaker: Benkum
dialogue: Hello, hello, hello. Interested in fighting in the Pit? The rules are strict, but if I don't see it, it didn't happen, know what I mean?

speaker: Benor
dialogue: I'm the best warrior in Morthal, and that's no boast.

speaker: Benor
dialogue: If you leave that kinslayer Hroggar, I would be happy to keep your company.

speaker: Alva
dialogue: Hroggar doesn't have to know if we sit together. Or drink together. I doubt he would even care.

speaker: Benor
dialogue: You tempt me mightily, Alva. But I won't cuckhold another man, even on murderer like Hroggar.

speaker: Benor
dialogue: Ho, Gorm.

speaker: Benor
dialogue: Not right now. Anything new?

speaker: Gorm
dialogue: Still the same. I tell you, something's got to be done.

speaker: Benor
dialogue: When the time is right, friend. When we're sure.

speaker: Gorm
dialogue: The longer we wait, the worse it gets.

speaker: Benor
dialogue: Let's talk about it some other time.

speaker: Benor
dialogue: And it's full of vampires?

speaker: Bergritte Battle-Born
dialogue: There's a rift here in Skyrim, and can't neither magic nor the passin' of time make it right.

speaker: Bergritte
dialogue: How about The Lusty Argonian Maid?

speaker: Bergritte
dialogue: You've got no sense of humor, you know that? Why don't you pick up where you left off with The Real Barenziah.

speaker: Bergritte
dialogue: Lars, dear, why don't you go outside and play? It's a beautiful day.

speaker: Lars
dialogue: That's all right, grandmother. I like staying home with you.

speaker: Bergritte
dialogue: It's that Braith girl again, isn't it? Has she been bothering you again? I've a mind to speak with her mother.

speaker: Lars
dialogue: No! Please, grandmother, don't do that. I'm fine. Really. Can we just... not talk about this anymore?

speaker: Bergritte
dialogue: All right, dear.

speaker: Bersi Honey-Hand
dialogue: Welcome to the Pawned Prawn. What can I do for you?

speaker: Drifa
dialogue: Spices? I'm certain I have no idea what you're talking about.

speaker: Bersi
dialogue: You sure? It was in your hand writing. If you can't keep the books straight then let me do them.

speaker: Drifa
dialogue: You keep giving and giving Bersi, and they'll keep taking and taking. When is it going to end?

speaker: Bersi
dialogue: What would you have me do, woman? Cross the Guild? Take them all on one by one?

speaker: Drifa
dialogue: You know I don't mean that. We need to find a way out of this. Perhaps talk to Laila...

speaker: Bersi
dialogue: Laila is as clueless as she is stupid. No. If anything's to be done about this, we have to deal with it ourselves.

speaker: Betrid Silver-Blood
dialogue: My dear vagrant, we're the only family worth knowing in Markarth. We own everything in this city, even the jail.

speaker: Betrid
dialogue: Rhiada, did you clean the tables today? They're filthy!

speaker: Rhiada
dialogue: I'm sorry, Betrid. I'll clean them right away.

speaker: Betrid
dialogue: No, don't bother. You're useless, as always. I'll get Ildene to do it.

speaker: Rhiada
dialogue: I'm sorry, Betrid. I thought I had cleaned the tables properly.

speaker: Betrid
dialogue: Oh, stop apologizing. It makes you look like an idiot. Learn to talk back a bit, girl! Why, when I was in the temple....

speaker: Rhiada
dialogue: The temple, Betrid? You were one of Dibella's faithful?

speaker: Betrid
dialogue: I misspoke. Never mind what I said. Now get back to work.

speaker: Betrid
dialogue: Where were you last night, Thonar? Busy with work or have you found some other woman who's willing to tolerate your lack of ambition?

speaker: Thonar
dialogue: I am busy keeping this family in coin and your pretty little head adorned with jewels, so I'll thank you not to question where I go at night, wife.

speaker: Betrid
dialogue: Well maybe if you would finally convince Thongvor to put you in charge of the family, I wouldn't need to question you anymore.

speaker: Thonar
dialogue: I'll take control of the family on my own time, Betrid. Until then, my brother remains in charge and you'll keep your mouth shut.

speaker: Betrid
dialogue: Oh dear, whatever is a girl to do with such fearful brutes about her?

speaker: Betrid
dialogue: Did I hear correctly, Thonar? Is your brother really asking you to settle another dispute between Mulush and Nepos?

speaker: Thonar
dialogue: Someone has to keep the silver production running, Betrid, and that means keeping Mulush and Nepos in line once in a while.

speaker: Betrid
dialogue: Humph. Who's running the Silver-Bloods? You or your brother? You need to tell Thongvor that he should settle this himself or step down.

speaker: Thonar
dialogue: The only thing I need to do, dear wife, is make sure profits are up, no matter what. If Thongvor won't do the dirty work, I will.

speaker: Betrid
dialogue: You'll never be in charge of this family with that attitude, loving husband.

speaker: Birna
dialogue: I'll sell just about anything, if it's worth my time. Keep that in mind, will you?

speaker: Bjartur
dialogue: You here for my next interrogation? I got nothing but time.

speaker: Bjorlam
dialogue: Need a ride?

speaker: Bodil
dialogue: Here to dig. That's all.

speaker: Priestess of Boethiah
dialogue: The Lord of Plots, Deceiver of Nations, Devourer of Trinimac. The Queen of Shadows, Goddess of Destruction, He-Who-Destroys and She-Who-Erases...

speaker: Cultist 1
dialogue: Our Lord! She has come!

speaker: Cultist 3
dialogue: She is here, among us.

speaker: Cultist 1
dialogue: Shhh! Be still. Beware her anger!

speaker: Boethiah
dialogue: Listen. All of you! Hear me! I have need of a warrior. Only the most ruthless, cunning, and agile will do. You have gathered here night after night, sacrificing fools upon my shrine, and sparring aimlessly with yourselves. But which among you truly exceeds the rest? Prove yourselves to me! I have a special task for whichever of you is left standing.

speaker: Bolar
dialogue: I've read the entrails many times, but can't fathom why Mauhulakh's wives keep finding tragedy.

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: Are the gods angry with me?

speaker: Bolar
dialogue: Why do you ask me that?

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: Why else have they cursed me? Killed all my wives?

speaker: Bolar
dialogue: Perhaps it's actually a sign of their love for you. They don't want to see you with unworthy mates.

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: Then they should send one they consider worthy.

speaker: Bolar
dialogue: Patience, boy.

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: Bolar, I must ask you something.

speaker: Bolar
dialogue: Yes, child?

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: Have the spirits told you where I may find a wife? One who will be safe from this curse?

speaker: Bolar
dialogue: Oh, all things in time, my boy. All things in time. What more do you need that Yatul and I cannot provide?

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: I need more children.

speaker: Bolar
dialogue: Well, that's a different matter...

speaker: Bolar
dialogue: He's lonely. What do you expect?

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: No matter. You'll take care of things like you always have.

speaker: Bolar
dialogue: Please, let's not have it come to that.

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: True... we could simply make sure she never reaches Narzulbur.

speaker: Bolar
dialogue: That wasn't what I meant.

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: If he does show up with a bride, we'll have to move quickly.

speaker: Bolar
dialogue: Once she's with child, I will not harm her.

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: Yes, you've made that quite clear in the past. And now we have Urog and Dushnamub because of your weakness.

speaker: Bolar
dialogue: They are good, loyal children.

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: They squander their father's love. We can't dally this time.

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: Have you scried anything new in the entrails?

speaker: Bolar
dialogue: Very little. It's an uncertain time.

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: Not for us, it isn't.

speaker: Bolar
dialogue: For all of us.

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: Come back to me when you have something useful.

speaker: Bolar
dialogue: He's been spending a lot of time at the graves again.

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: Good. The more time he pines for the dead wives, the less time he spends finding a new one.

speaker: Bolar
dialogue: Be careful. The spirits can speak to the living if there's a strong connection.

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: Bah. He never had a connection with any of them beyond what his loins told him.

speaker: Bolar
dialogue: Maybe, but...

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: We're the ones he loves. Me, and you.

speaker: Bolfrida Brandy-Mug
dialogue: The weather's harsh, but I like to think my sunny personality is what helps the grain grow.

speaker: Bolfrida
dialogue: Oh dear, I hadn't thought of that.

speaker: Bolfrida
dialogue: Come on, we just need a little elbow grease.

speaker: Faryl
dialogue: There are places in the world that aren't wrapped in ice, you know.

speaker: Bolgeir Bearclaw
dialogue: My duty is to keep the Jarl safe. Not play nursemaid to you sycophants.

speaker: Bolgeir
dialogue: We lost another five guardsmen, my Jarl. If General Tullius continues to conscript our men and send them off to battle, we'll have none left to protect the city.

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: Yes, I know. The general acted with my blessing. It is vital that we bring Ulfric to justice, but that cannot happen until his army of Stormcloaks is defeated utterly.

speaker: Bolgier
dialogue: Told you that, did he? I'm sworn to protect you, my Jarl, but I'm the last line of defense. The first line is the walls around this city and the men who patrol them. Men whom, I might add, we're precious short on.

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: I'm aware of that, Bolgeir, and I appreciate your dedication. However, if we lose the war, the guardsmen of Solitude will make little difference in the end.

speaker: Bolgeir
dialogue: No disrespect toward the general, but sometimes I wonder if he's got your best interests at heart. In any case he won't be turnin' me into no Imperial soldier. I know my place, and it's at your side.

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: It comforts me to know that, Bolgeir.

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: Steward, I have an idea that might help to bolster the morale of our people in this difficult time. I think we shall have a grand parade, and let General Tullius march his troops from the Blue Palace to Castle Dour in all their finery.

speaker: Bolgeir
dialogue: I must protest, my Jarl. A parade would make you an easy target for a Stormcloak assassin. You're safer here in the palace.

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: Oh, very well. I can see there's no changing your stubborn Nord minds. But when this war is won, I will have my parade!

speaker: Falk
dialogue: Yes, my Jarl.

speaker: Bolli
dialogue: Started out with a single fishing pole and now I have an entire building and two boats to my name. Not bad for a middle-aged Nord, eh?

speaker: Bolli
dialogue: So while I was in Ivarstead, I heard news that something terrible happened at Helgen.

speaker: Bolli
dialogue: If that's true, then we have much more to fear than the Thieves Guild.

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: I'd still keep an eye on my purse if I was you.

speaker: Bolli
dialogue: Grelka, I wanted to talk about that suit of leather armor you sold me. The fasteners are already coming loose.

speaker: Bolli
dialogue: Why should I pay for a repair on something I just bought?

speaker: Grelka
dialogue: All right, all right. Just bring it to me tomorrow and I'll fix it for you.

speaker: Bolli
dialogue: Haelga, we need to stop seeing each other.

speaker: Haelga
dialogue: Oh, Bolli you silly man. You weren't saying that when you were licking that honey off my...

speaker: Bolli
dialogue: Haelga! That's just it. I can't keep up with you. Your Dibellan techniques... they're exhausting.

speaker: Haelga
dialogue: Is it really me, or is it your wife? You need to make a choice Bolli. The honey or her.

speaker: Haelga
dialogue: When are you going to take me away from here Bolli?

speaker: Bolli
dialogue: I told you, I can't just pick up and leave. I have my wife, my business... not to mention you have the Bunkhouse.

speaker: Haelga
dialogue: That old place? I could care less about it. Its you I want, Bolli.

speaker: Bolli
dialogue: I... I'm sorry Haelga, I can't. Not yet.

speaker: Bolli
dialogue: Madesi, what's this bill for 300 septims!

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: Begging your pardon, milord. Your wife has run up quite an account in the last few months.

speaker: Bolli
dialogue: Outrageous! Who does she think she is?!

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: I believe she's trying to look as ravishing as possible for you, milord.

speaker: Bolli
dialogue: Oh, well... I suppose that's a noble cause. I'll settle this bill at the end of the day. Thank you.

speaker: Bolli
dialogue: I have two more bushels for you, Marise. That should keep you well-stocked.

speaker: Marise
dialogue: Sounds good. May I owe you for them?

speaker: Bolli
dialogue: Of course. Say, how are you going to sell all those fish before they spoil?

speaker: Marise
dialogue: You know I can't tell you that. As soon as I do, and you have a few meads in you, everyone will know.

speaker: Bolli
dialogue: Decided to show up for work today, eh?

speaker: Bolli
dialogue: It means I have a business to run, I need to have the books straight and you're barely ever here!

speaker: Nivenor
dialogue: For goodness sake, Bolli! You barely lift a finger yourself when you're here except to point at things for your workers to do. Let them do the work, that's what you pay them for!

speaker: Nivenor
dialogue: Bolli, I was looking at the finances and I noticed you've been donating gold to the Temple of Mara. Are you out of your mind?

speaker: Bolli
dialogue: Maramal's been helping me through a rough patch. I just wanted to pay him back. It's not like he's keeping it!

speaker: Nivenor
dialogue: Uh huh. I'm sure he runs outside with the coin and throws it up in the air so Mara herself can catch it. Come off of it, Bolli.

speaker: Bolli
dialogue: You may be my wife, but this is my business, so just do your job. Don't worry, you'll still have plenty of gold left over to waste on trinkets.

speaker: Bolli
dialogue: Talen my friend, up for some fishing this week?

speaker: Bolli
dialogue: Oh come now, what's a dragon or two compared to a day full of fishing!

speaker: Talen-Jei
dialogue: That's not funny, Bolli. People are scared.

speaker: Bolli
dialogue: Wujeeta, we need to talk.

speaker: Bolli
dialogue: I don't know what I'm going to do with you. I can't just let this go unpunished.

speaker: Wujeeta
dialogue: Please, don't get rid of me! I need the coin. I... I'll work for free for the rest of this week. Please!

speaker: Bolli
dialogue: Sigh. Very well. You're lucky Maramal has placed me in a very forgiving mood.

speaker: Bolund
dialogue: That Valga Vinicia is a gossip and a troublemaker.

speaker: Bor
dialogue: I'm here to mine, outlander. So unless you want to dig, get out.

speaker: Borgakh the Steel heart
dialogue: Soon, I will be of age. The taste is bitter.

speaker: Borgny
dialogue: Mining is an honest trade. No real tricks to it.

speaker: Uraccen
dialogue: Madanach's guard. Big, even for an Orc. Heard he ripped a man's arm off and beat him to death with it. He's old-fashioned like that.

speaker: Phinis Gestor
dialogue: And then there's Borvir and Rundi. Twins, though they rarely agreed on anything.

speaker: Bothela
dialogue: The Hag's Cure is here for all your discreet needs...

speaker: Bothela
dialogue: No, no girl. It's the picked spider tongue and then the decayed taproot. Do it the other way, and your cure turns into a poison.

speaker: Bothela
dialogue: You will. Until then, you'll taste every potion you make before you sell it.

speaker: Muiri
dialogue: Bothela, I have a question....

speaker: Bothela
dialogue: You want to know a secret of mine, young girl? The most effective poison to kill a man? A potion to make others fall in love, perhaps?

speaker: Muiri
dialogue: I was actually just wondering if you had any family....

speaker: Bothela
dialogue: Oh. Oh, I see....

speaker: Muiri
dialogue: I'm sorry. You don't have to tell me if you don't....

speaker: Bothela
dialogue: I have one. A nephew. He's in prison for being a member of the Forsworn.

speaker: Muiri
dialogue: I'm sorry, I didn't realize.

speaker: Bothela
dialogue: Don't be. We all make mistakes.

speaker: Bothela
dialogue: You should be more careful with the man you pick, dear.

speaker: Muiri
dialogue: He said he loved me...

speaker: Bothela
dialogue: Real men prove their love. Words are as empty as the air they run through.

speaker: Bothela
dialogue: Stop moping about, girl. Tears won't change what you've done.

speaker: Muiri
dialogue: I was such a fool. How could I let him use me like that?

speaker: Bothela
dialogue: We all get used, dear. It's living with it that makes you a woman.

speaker: Braith
dialogue: What're you lookin' at? I'm not afraid of you, ya know. Even if you are my elder.

speaker: Braith
dialogue: Battle-Born! Give me your money!

speaker: Lars
dialogue: I... I don't have any money.

speaker: Braith
dialogue: You'd better give me five Septims, right now, or I'm going to bloody your nose...

speaker: Lars
dialogue: No! Please! I really don't have any money, Braith! I'll give you ten septims tomorrow. Just don't hit me.

speaker: Braith
dialogue: Ten Septims tomorrow, baby Battle-Born. Or I'm gonna bloody your nose and your lip.

speaker: Braith
dialogue: Oh look, it's little baby Battle-Born.

speaker: Lars
dialogue: Leave me alone, Braith...

speaker: Braith
dialogue: What are you gonna do if I don't? Huh? Gonna cry to your papa?

speaker: Lars
dialogue: Just go away!

speaker: Lars
dialogue: Braith. I.... I've come to tell you that I'm not afraid of you anymore.

speaker: Braith
dialogue: Don't make me laugh, baby Battle-Born. You'll be afraid of me till the day I kill you.

speaker: Lars
dialogue: You... You're wrong! You can't hurt me anymore...

speaker: Braith
dialogue: Oh no? So you're gonna fight back if I punch you? Huh? You're gonna hit a girl?

speaker: Lars
dialogue: Well, no... I... I mean...

speaker: Braith
dialogue: That's what I thought. Now get out of my way, baby. I got things to do.

speaker: Braith
dialogue: Mother? Can I talk to you?

speaker: Saffir
dialogue: Not now, Braith.

speaker: Saffir
dialogue: Not now, Braith.

speaker: Braith
dialogue: I wanted to ask you something. It's about a boy...

speaker: Saffir
dialogue: Not now, Braith. Go... go ask your father.

speaker: Braith
dialogue: Papa, the next time you go away, I want to come with you.

speaker: Amren
dialogue: When I go away, I go to war. That's no place for a little girl.

speaker: Braith
dialogue: Every knight needs a squire. I could help you with your sword, things like that.

speaker: Amren
dialogue: Nice try, blossom, but I'm not a knight, I'm a mercenary. The answer's still no. Besides, your mother would miss you too much.

speaker: Braith
dialogue: Yeah. Right.

speaker: Braith
dialogue: Papa, I want to talk to you...

speaker: Amren
dialogue: Hmm? What about?

speaker: Braith
dialogue: Well, there's this boy, and...

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: If there's anything you wish to purchase, just let me know.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Everyone! Everyone! Gather 'round! I have something amazing to show you that demands your attention! Gather 'round all! No pushing, no shoving. Plenty of room!

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: Come on, Brynjolf... what is it this time?

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Patience, Brand-Shei. This is a rare opportunity, and I wouldn't want you to get left out.

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: That's what you said about the Wisp Essence and it turned out to be crushed nirnroot mixed with water!

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: That was a simple misunderstanding, but this item is the real thing. Lads and lasses I give you, Falmerblood Elixir!

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: Oh come on, are you talking about the Snow Elves?

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: The one and only. Mystical beings who live in legends and were masters of great magic. Imagine the power that coursed through their veins!

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: How did you get that, then? No one's seen them in years!

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: My sources must remain a secret for their own protection but I can promise that the contents are genuine. One sip of the elixir and your wishes will be granted. Great wealth, everlasting life or perhaps limitless power could be yours!

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: How much does it cost?

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Only twenty gold septims! Hurry before my supply is gone.

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: Don't listen to him, he's making this up.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Please hurry, I have only a few bottles left!

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: That Wisp Essence didn't help, but maybe this will.

speaker: Riften Guard
dialogue: All right Brand-Shei. Turn out your pockets, we know you have it.

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: Have what? What in blazes are you talking about?

speaker: Riften Guard
dialogue: Don't play stupid. I said turn out your pockets... now!

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: I'm telling you, I don't... wait, what's this ring? This isn't mine!

speaker: Riften Guard
dialogue: That's right. It isn't yours. You're under arrest, Brand-Shei.

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: This is insane! I didn't steal anything! I never saw this ring before in my entire life!

speaker: Riften Guard
dialogue: We can do this one of two ways. You walk with me up to the keep, or I can drag your lifeless body. Your choice.

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: But... I... very well.

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: You've heard too? They say the town was completely destroyed by a dragon.

speaker: Bolli
dialogue: If that's true, then we have much more to fear than the Thieves Guild.

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: I'd still keep an eye on my purse if I was you.

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: Dinya, about that incense you requested? Its not arriving anytime soon. The Khajiit caravans are having tough times getting through.

speaker: Dinya
dialogue: That's a shame. What's causing them all the trouble?

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: There's the stories about Helgen, bandits, skirmishes between the Stormcloaks and the Imperials... it almost seems endless.

speaker: Dinya
dialogue: Chin up, Brand-Shei. Lady Mara will provide us strength and guidance through these difficult times.

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: Worse. The Khajiit Caravans are the only way to get supplies into the city, and even those are becoming more infrequent.

speaker: Grelka
dialogue: Well, let's all raise a flagon to Ulfric; future King of Skyrim and bringer of poverty to the working class!

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: Grelka! Lower your voice before you get us both in trouble.

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: Maven, please. I didn't know it was your man. Had I known, I would have looked the other way, I swear.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Turning him in to the guards? Have you joined Mjoll as official peacekeepers of Riften? You cost me a lot of coin.

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: Maven, I... please, don't hurt me.

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: Is it true you chased a thief from your home? I overheard Aerin mentioning it.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: It's true. Wasn't much of a thief though. Made enough noise to wake the Red Mountain.

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: Good. Maybe that will teach them to leave honest citizens alone.

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: I'm afraid not. I don't deal in stolen goods.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: Stolen? How can you be certain? I may have just misplaced it somewhere in the city.

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: Lady Mjoll, if you lost a gold ring anywhere in this city I'm afraid it's likely never to be seen again. I'm sorry.

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: The Argonian sugar-cane wine? It's pretty hard to get around here. Very expensive.

speaker: Nivenor
dialogue: That's fine. I have a special occasion coming up, and I'd like to have it.

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: I'll see what I can do.

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: Yes, I heard. I think all of Skyrim knows by know.

speaker: Shadr
dialogue: Do you... do you think that could happen here? I mean, could a dragon come here and burn the city down?

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: I don't know. All we can do is hope the Eight will favor us and have these creatures stay far away from Riften.

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: Svana, I heard that Sibbi was put in jail. What happened?

speaker: Svana
dialogue: They say...well, they say he murdered someone. Something to do with Svidi.

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: Come to think of it, I haven't seen Svidi in a while. Wait...he didn't...

speaker: Svana
dialogue: No, it was Svidi's brother, Wulfur. She's in hiding, now. Somewhere far from here, I'd suspect.

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: If he wasn't a Black-Briar, I'd march right over to the jail and teach Sibbi some manners...but then I'd suspect that I'd end up like Wulfur.

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: What's with all the boots and shoes you keep buying? You must have bought twenty pairs in the last two years.

speaker: Tythis
dialogue: Always be prepared. You never know if you might get a split in one, or lose one, then where would you be? No sir, that's not happening to me.

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: Um... okay. Well, the boots aren't here yet. Hopefully on the next Khajiit caravan.

speaker: Brelyna Maryon
dialogue: Before you even ask, yes I have an ancestry steeped in magic, and no I don't want to talk about it.

speaker: Tolfdir
dialogue: Welcome, welcome! We were just beginning. Please, stay and listen. So, as I was saying, the first thing to understand is that magic is, by its very nature, volatile and dangerous. Unless you can control it, it can and will destroy you.

speaker: Brelyna
dialogue: Sir, I think we all understand that fairly well. We wouldn't be here if we couldn't control magic!

speaker: Tolfdir
dialogue: Of course, my dear. Of course. You all certainly possess some inherent natural ability. That much is not being questioned. What I'm talking about is true control, mastery of magic. It takes years, if not decades, of practice and study.

speaker: Tolfdir
dialogue: Please, please! This is exactly what I'm talking about. Eagerness must be tempered with caution, or else disaster is inevitable.

speaker: Onmund
dialogue: But we've only just arrived here -- you've no idea what any of us are capable of. Why not give use a chance to show you what we can do?

speaker: Onmund
dialogue: We're all pretty new to this, right? Let's just give it a chance. What's the worst that could happen?

speaker: Tolfdir
dialogue: All right, let's settle down. I suppose we can try something practical... In continueing with out theme of safety, we'll start with Wards. Wards are protective spells that block magic. I'll teach you all a ward, and we'll see if you can succesfully use it to block spells, all right?

speaker: Brelyna
dialogue: See? He agrees with us too! Why don't you actually show us something?

speaker: Tolfdir
dialogue: All right, let's settle down. I suppose we can try something practical... In continueing with out theme of safety, we'll start with Wards. Wards are protective spells that block magic. I'll teach you all a ward, and we'll see if you can succesfully use it to block spells, all right?

speaker: Tolfdir
dialogue: All right, let's settle down. I suppose we can try something practical... In continueing with out theme of safety, we'll start with Wards. Wards are protective spells that block magic. I'll teach you all a ward, and we'll see if you can succesfully use it to block spells, all right?

speaker: Brenuin
dialogue: My favorite drinking buddy! Let's get some mead.

speaker: Carlotta
dialogue: How goes the begging today, Brenuin?

speaker: Brenuin
dialogue: That's right, mock the town beggar like everyone else. But I've got a right to browse, don't I? I ain't hurtin' anyone.

speaker: Carlotta
dialogue: Make it quick, then. I don't want your stink driving my customers away.

speaker: Brenuin
dialogue: The gods smile on them who show charity. Best you remember that.

speaker: Carlotta
dialogue: And what might you be looking at?

speaker: Brenuin
dialogue: Oh, the fruit looks so good. So juicy.

speaker: Carlotta
dialogue: No handouts today, Brenuin. Now scat. You'll scare off my paying customers.

speaker: Brenuin
dialogue: Oh, just one apple, Carlotta? Just one tiny apple. I'll pay you tomorrow, I swear it.

speaker: Carlotta
dialogue: That's what you said last week, and the week before that. Now go, before I call a guard.

speaker: Brenuin
dialogue: No, no! Don't do that. No need to do that. I'm going. See? I'm leaving. No guards, please.

speaker: Carlotta
dialogue: Look, come back tomorrow, okay? If I have anything left that's not sold or spoiled, you can have it.

speaker: Brenuin
dialogue: You've got the heart of Mara herself, you know that? Thank you, Carlotta. Thank you.

speaker: Anoriath
dialogue: I don't suppose you're going to buy something this time?

speaker: Brenuin
dialogue: Just browsin' today. If the gods be kind, someone will take mercy on me and spare a few Septims.

speaker: Anoriath
dialogue: If they do, promise you'll actually purchase something for once.

speaker: Brenuin
dialogue: By Ysmir, I will. Gods know it's been too long since I tasted real meat.

speaker: Brenuin
dialogue: Spare a coin for a fellow Nord who's down on his luck?

speaker: Ysolda
dialogue: So you can spend it on drinks at the Bannered Mare? If it's food you need, ask for that instead.

speaker: Brenuin
dialogue: Never you mind, then. I'll find a more charitable soul.

speaker: Ysolda
dialogue: That's what I thought.

speaker: Drennen
dialogue: I don't like this place. It feels like we're being...watched.

speaker: Breya
dialogue: Its a simple job, Drennen. We get in, we steal the Lexicon, we leave. Don't get jumpy.

speaker: Fathoms
dialogue: If you two cannot handle this, we can find others to hire.

speaker: Roots
dialogue: Enough. Their services will be more than adequate. Let us continue.

speaker: Breya
dialogue: Why are all these...things...ignoring us?

speaker: Roots
dialogue: Avanchnzel is waiting.

speaker: Breya
dialogue: Waiting for what?

speaker: Roots
dialogue: No one seems to know. Perhaps the return of the Dwemer. Perhaps the ending of the world.

speaker: Breya
dialogue: Best get rid of the ones we see. Just in case.

speaker: Breya
dialogue: I told you we should have hired a thief.

speaker: Fathoms
dialogue: We are thieves, you fool. We're stealing the cube.

speaker: Breya
dialogue: [heh] And yet none of us can pick a damned lock.

speaker: Drennen
dialogue: This place is huge.

speaker: Roots
dialogue: It is large, indeed. I did not anticipate Avanchnzel's size or the time needed to uncover the entrance. A few hours sleep and we should be ready to continue through.

speaker: Drennen
dialogue: Maybe we should turn back. I don't want to sleep here.

speaker: Roots
dialogue: Drennen, do you understand that the Lexicon at the bottom of this place holds the accumulated memories of centuries of Dwemer.

speaker: Breya
dialogue: Not to mention our pay.

speaker: Fathoms
dialogue: So we're not turning back, you fool.

speaker: Breya
dialogue: Besides, you're not afraid of a few sleeping metal men. Are you, Drennen?

speaker: Breya
dialogue: I thought you said these things were 'sleeping'?

speaker: Roots
dialogue: You said they were sleeping. I said they were waiting. It seems a few of them were 'waiting' for someone to try and take the Lexicon.

speaker: Drennen
dialogue: I can't do this. We shouldn't be here. I'm sorry.

speaker: Fathoms
dialogue: Let the field mouse run. Your pay will be double.

speaker: Breya
dialogue: My pay will be nothing if we die in here!

speaker: Roots
dialogue: Calm yourself, Breya. We are close to the Lexicon. I can feel it calling. We can do it without Drennen.

speaker: Roots
dialogue: We are close now. Can you feel the Lexicon calling out?

speaker: Fathoms
dialogue: [sarcastic] Sure.

speaker: Breya
dialogue: So we get it and get out, right?

speaker: Roots
dialogue: Once we have the Lexicon, we need to take it to its podium. I know what to do from there. Soon the Lexicon's knowledge will be mine.

speaker: Fathoms
dialogue: Ours. Soon the Lexicon's knowledge will be ours.

speaker: Roots
dialogue: Of course.

speaker: Roots
dialogue: We're almost there. I can hear the Lexicon. Come on, quickly!

speaker: Breya
dialogue: Something doesn't feel right. [pause] Wait!

speaker: Brill
dialogue: Ah, hello, my good friend. Would you do me a kindness? I seem to be down to my last drop of spirits; let me tell ya, sobriety is highly overrated.

speaker: Vignar
dialogue: There's a chill in the air. Ysmir's beard, it gets colder in here every day.

speaker: Brill
dialogue: That's just you getting skinnier every day, old man. You're losing your padding. You need to eat more.

speaker: Vignar
dialogue: Well, if my layabout manservant fed me more, that wouldn't be a problem.

speaker: Brill
dialogue: Oho! Manservant? Is that what I am now?

speaker: Vignar
dialogue: My mistake. A manservant wouldn't let me starve or freeze. I let you live here, and now I'm two steps closer to the grave.

speaker: Brill
dialogue: Old man, without me, you would have withered away a long time ago.

speaker: Vignar
dialogue: Hmph. Damn you for being right.

speaker: Vignar
dialogue: You ain't made me that stew in a long time.

speaker: Brill
dialogue: Which, the mutton or the vegetable?

speaker: Brill
dialogue: Hmm. So I haven't. All right, I'll buy the ingredients tomorrow and we can have it for dinner.

speaker: Brill
dialogue: Fancy a game of Iron Hearts later?

speaker: Vignar
dialogue: You going to lose horribly, and then say you let me win?

speaker: Vignar
dialogue: Then you're on.

speaker: Brina Merilis
dialogue: I wasn't born in Skyrim, but when I served in the Legion this land became my home.

speaker: Britte
dialogue: Sissel thinks she's so special. No way she's more special than me.

speaker: Brond
dialogue: Steel. Barehanded. Armor. Naked. It's all fighting. I can kill you with a weapon or by myself. No difference.

speaker: Brother Verulus
dialogue: New to Skyrim? I was confused at first, too. The Nords call their mausoleums the Hall of the Dead.

speaker: Thongvor
dialogue: What are you hiding, priest?

speaker: Verulus
dialogue: I'm not hiding anything. It's closed for a reason.

speaker: Thongvor
dialogue: Typical Imperial lies. First you take away Talos, and now keep us from seeing our honored dead? You and the Jarl will answer for any desecration of my ancestors' bodies!

speaker: Verulus
dialogue: That's enough, Thongvor. We're done.

speaker: Verulus
dialogue: Who... who are you? What's going on?

speaker: Eola
dialogue: Priest of Arkay. I'm your friend.

speaker: Verulus
dialogue: You're my... friend....

speaker: Eola
dialogue: Yes. I'm your friend, and I've invited you to dinner.

speaker: Verulus
dialogue: I've been invited to dinner.... I'm so hungry....

speaker: Eola
dialogue: Why don't you lay down and rest, while we get the meal ready?

speaker: Verulus
dialogue: I need to lay down. I'll just be a minute....

speaker: Eola
dialogue: Come with me. Our feast is about to begin.

speaker: Eola
dialogue: The meal is on Namira's table. Go ahead. Carve.

speaker: Brunwulf Free-Winter
dialogue: There's no glory in war. It's just something they tell soldiers so they'll risk their lives.

speaker: Brunwulf
dialogue: That's not necessary. I'll pay the same price as anyone else.

speaker: Aval
dialogue: But I insist. And with good reason; Malthyr told me that you've been speaking to Ulfric about our situation. He said you're going to help us. So few Nords have ever offered to help us, a discount is the least I can do.

speaker: Brunwulf
dialogue: I'm not looking for special treatment, Aval. All I did was talk to Ulfric. For all I know, he's already forgotten the conversation. I wouldn't get your hopes up.

speaker: Aval
dialogue: Oh, I see. Well, I'm sorry to have troubled you about it. Just... know that your efforts are appreciated.

speaker: Brunwulf
dialogue: Elda, honey, let's not talk about the war. It's in the past.

speaker: Elda
dialogue: I'm sorry. What would you like to talk about?

speaker: Brunwulf
dialogue: Hows about we figure out some way to keep warm tonight?

speaker: Elda
dialogue: Oh! You behave, now!

speaker: Brunwulf
dialogue: How long have you run this place, again?

speaker: Elda
dialogue: Nearly thirty years now.

speaker: Brunwulf
dialogue: Just wondering when you'll be ready to give it up and settle down. Seems like you're always working.

speaker: Elda
dialogue: I just feel like if I'm not here, then something could go wrong. Nils is a hard worker, but I wouldn't trust him to run things.

speaker: Brunwulf
dialogue: One of these days he'll have to learn.

speaker: Elda
dialogue: Perhaps. But not today.

speaker: Brunwulf
dialogue: I've been thinking about building that cabin we talked about.

speaker: Elda
dialogue: Oh? Where?

speaker: Brunwulf
dialogue: There's a clear spot just west of Riften. You know the area?

speaker: Elda
dialogue: I've been there before, but I don't know it well.

speaker: Brunwulf
dialogue: Well that's where I want to build. In the fall forest. Give it an easterly view. The sunrise is almost as pretty as you are.

speaker: Elda
dialogue: That sounds lovely. You're very sweet.

speaker: Brunwulf
dialogue: It's not that simple. Ulfric wants a Skyrim for the Nords. He doesn't trust what he calls 'outsiders'.

speaker: Malthyr
dialogue: You've seen how we live―cramped alleys, run-down buildings, few guard patrols. Even the name 'Gray Quarter' is an insult.

speaker: Brunwulf
dialogue: I'll speak to Ulfric soon, but I make no promises that I can change his mind.

speaker: Malthyr
dialogue: That's all I ask. With your help, we have a chance to make a better life for ourselves here. For that, I thank you.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: Bryling's obsession with honor and tradition is quaint... But politically irrelevant.

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: As you know, Solitude's coffers are much depleted by the war efforts. Thane Erikur, you have a strong head for business. What do you suggest?

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: This is an unfortunate but unavoidable ebb in revenue. But as long as we continue to support the Empire, our sacrifices will be well rewarded.

speaker: Bryling
dialogue: Listen to you, speaking of sacrifice. You've never gone hungry a day in your life, Erikur!

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: And what would my impetuous Thane Bryling suggest, instead?

speaker: Bryling
dialogue: Simple. Let the Empire fight its own war, with its own funds, and without hijacking our supplies and soldiers. Let Haafingar rebuild.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: My lady... Surely you're not that naïve. Such foolishness would only leave us defenseless. The rebels would storm the palace in an afternoon.

speaker: Bryling
dialogue: The Stormcloaks only rebel because the Empire uses Skyrim as its personal larder. The more they take, the more support the rebels gain!

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: That is quite enough. Perhaps I will raise these issues when I have an audience with General Tullius.

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: Thane Bryling, what do you have to report about the state of Haafingar's defenses?

speaker: Bryling
dialogue: The news is the same as it's been for the rest of the war, your grace. Our borders are secure, but at the cost of the guards for our towns and roads.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: I don't see any reason why we'd need them. As long as those dogs stay outside of our borders, we're fine.

speaker: Bryling
dialogue: The Stormcloaks are far from the only threat to the hold. The roads are beset by bandits and beasts... and now there's even talk of bloody dragons.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: My dear Bryling. Barring any... fancy and folly... the good people of Haafingar are surely capable of dealing with the odd highwayman or stray dog.

speaker: Bryling
dialogue: Trouble on the roads and cities means less commerce. Less commerce means less money and more starving people. And that means more crime.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: Humph. That's only a problem for people who can't afford to hire their own security.

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: That may well be our only answer. I will empower my Steward to seek out capable individuals to secure Haafingar. Thank you, my Thanes.

speaker: Bryling
dialogue: There's something that's been troubling me, Falk. I am hesitant to share it, but I feel that I must.

speaker: Falk
dialogue: Speak your mind, Bryling. You're among friends here.

speaker: Bryling
dialogue: You know that I support the Empire, as we all do. However, I fear General Tullius is underestimating the Stormcloaks. Too often the general has lost good soldiers because he did not take Ulfric and his men seriously. If this continues, and the worst comes to pass, Solitude will pay the price. The Empire is headquartered here, after all.

speaker: Falk
dialogue: We don't have the luxury of hanging back to see who wins before choosing our friends, Bryling. You know this. And besides, no Nord with a shred of honor would consider it. We're no cowards. Have faith, Bryling. When this war is over and Ulfric is dead, you'll see that you were jumping at shadows, and nothing more.

speaker: Bryling
dialogue: Falk, you shouldn't have come. You know what'd happen if people found out about us.

speaker: Falk
dialogue: I know, my lady. I just needed to see you outside of court, away from all of the politics.

speaker: Bryling
dialogue: I'm serious. If Erikur knew about us, he'd force you to resign from your position. And without you, he'd have the Jarl bent around his little finger.

speaker: Falk
dialogue: You're right, of course. But when this war is over, I'll gladly resign and we can stop sneaking around like this.

speaker: Bryling
dialogue: One more reason to pray for the fighting to end then, my love.

speaker: Falk
dialogue: It's nearly time to collect taxes on your properties here in the city, Bryling. We'll need to visit each home for an assessment.

speaker: Bryling
dialogue: Is it that time again already? Very well, let's meet this evening and make the arrangements.

speaker: Bryling
dialogue: Stop it, both of you. You're acting like children.

speaker: Bryling
dialogue: What news have you heard from the war, Irnskar?

speaker: Irnskar
dialogue: You won't like it, my lady.

speaker: Bryling
dialogue: I'm well aware that I won't like it. But it's my duty to keep my people safe. Tell me.

speaker: Irnskar
dialogue: Possession of the holds change on an almost daily basis, but I can report that Haafingar is still secure. Your people are safe.

speaker: Bryling
dialogue: I'm not just talking about my subjects. I'm talking about my people: the proud Nords of Skyrim.

speaker: Irnskar
dialogue: I told you you wouldn't like the news.

speaker: Irnskar
dialogue: My lady, I'm pleased to inform you that you have a new gown for court, specially tailored by madame Endarie.

speaker: Bryling
dialogue: Really? How did we afford that? Besides, I like the gown I already have.

speaker: Irnskar
dialogue: Madame Endarie insisted. She made it free of charge, in honor of your lenience about last month's rent discrepancies.

speaker: Bryling
dialogue: That was suspiciously nice of her. I thought she hated everyone.

speaker: Irnskar
dialogue: She does, my lady. But apparently, she hates you just a little less than the others.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: The way they walk, what they're wearing. It's a dead give-away.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Everyone! Everyone! Gather 'round! I have something amazing to show you that demands your attention! Gather 'round all! No pushing, no shoving. Plenty of room!

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: Come on, Brynjolf... what is it this time?

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Patience, Brand-Shei. This is a rare opportunity, and I wouldn't want you to get left out.

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: That's what you said about the Wisp Essence and it turned out to be crushed nirnroot mixed with water!

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: That was a simple misunderstanding, but this item is the real thing. Lads and lasses I give you, Falmerblood Elixir!

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: Oh come on, are you talking about the Snow Elves?

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: The one and only. Mystical beings who live in legends and were masters of great magic. Imagine the power that coursed through their veins!

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: How did you get that, then? No one's seen them in years!

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: My sources must remain a secret for their own protection but I can promise that the contents are genuine. One sip of the elixir and your wishes will be granted. Great wealth, everlasting life or perhaps limitless power could be yours!

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: How much does it cost?

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Only twenty gold septims! Hurry before my supply is gone.

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: Don't listen to him, he's making this up.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Please hurry, I have only a few bottles left!

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: That Wisp Essence didn't help, but maybe this will.

speaker: Vekel the Man
dialogue: Give it up, Brynjolf... those days are over.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: I'm telling you, this one is different...

speaker: Dirge
dialogue: We've all heard that one before, Bryn! Quit kidding yourself.

speaker: Vekel the Man
dialogue: It's time to face the truth, old friend. You, Vex, Mercer... you're all part of a dying breed. Things are changing!

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Dying breed, eh? Well what do you call that then!

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Mercer? This is the one I was talking about... our new recruit.

speaker: Mercer Frey
dialogue: This better not be another waste of the Guild's resources, Brynjolf. Before we continue, I want to make one thing perfectly clear. If you play by the rules, you walk away rich. You break the rules and you lose your share. No debates, no discussion... you do what we say, when we say.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Wait a moment, you're not talking about Goldenglow, are you? Even our little Vex couldn't get in.

speaker: Mercer Frey
dialogue: You claim this recruit possesses an aptitude for our line of work. If so, let him prove it. Goldenglow Estate is critically important to one of our largest clients. However, the owner has suddenly decided to take matters into his own hands and shut us out. He needs to be taught a lesson. Brynjolf will provide you with the details.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Mercer, aren't you forgetting something?

speaker: Mercer Frey
dialogue: Hmm? Oh, yes. Since Brynjolf assures me you'll be nothing but a benefit to us, then you're in. Welcome to the Thieves Guild.

speaker: Mercer Frey
dialogue: Brynjolf, have you had a chance to speak to our contact in Whiterun?

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Sorry Mercer, they no longer wish to be involved in our operation.

speaker: Mercer Frey
dialogue: I trust you've applied the appropriate pressure in order to change their mind?

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: I have. I think we may have to turn this one over to the Dark Brotherhood.

speaker: Mercer Frey
dialogue: Yes, I'm afraid you're right. Such a shame...

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: You better have a damn good reason to be here with that murderer.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: Please, lower your weapons so we can speak. I have proof that you've all been misled!

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: No tricks, Karliah or I'll cut you down where you stand. Now what's this so-called proof you speak of?

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: I have Gallus' journal. I think you'll find its contents disturbing.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Let me see. No, it... it can't be. This can't be true. I've known Mercer too long...

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: It's true, Brynjolf. Every word. Mercer's been stealing from the Guild for years, right under your noses.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: There's only one way to find out if what the lass says is true. Delvin, I'll need you to open the Vault.

speaker: Delvin
dialogue: Wait just a blessed moment, Bryn. What's in that book? What did it say?

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: It says Mercer's been stealing from our vault for years. Gallus was looking into it before he was murdered.

speaker: Delvin
dialogue: How can Mercer open up a vault that needs two keys? It's impossible. Could he pick his way in?

speaker: Vex
dialogue: That door has the best puzzle locks money can buy. There's no way it can be picked open.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: He didn't need to pick the lock.

speaker: Delvin
dialogue: What's she on about?

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Use your key on the vault, Delvin. We'll open it up and find out the truth.

speaker: Delvin
dialogue: I've used my key, but the vault's still locked up tighter than a drum. Now use yours.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: By the Eight! It's gone, everything's gone! Get in here, all of you!

speaker: Delvin
dialogue: The gold, the jewels... it's all gone.

speaker: Vex
