dialogue: That son-of-a-bitch! I'll kill him!

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Vex! Put it away... right now. We can't afford to lose our heads... we need to calm down and focus.

speaker: Delvin
dialogue: Do what he says, Vex. This isn't helpin' right now.

speaker: Vex
dialogue: Fine. We do it your way. For now.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Delvin, Vex... watch the Flagon. If you see Mercer, come tell me right away.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Delvin, please tell me you have good news.

speaker: Delvin
dialogue: If I told you that, I'd be lying. We haven't had a bit in weeks. our clients are starting to get angry.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: You tell this sorry bunch of thieves that they need to put down their flagons and get to work if they want to keep their status!

speaker: Delvin
dialogue: I will, I will...

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: Brynjolf, the time has come to decide Mercer's fate. Until a new Guild Master is chosen, the decision falls to you.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Aye, lass... and I've come to a decision. Mercer Frey tried to kill both of you, he betrayed the Guild, murdered Gallus and made us question our future. He needs to die.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: We have to be very careful, Brynjolf. Mercer is a Nightingale, an Agent of Nocturnal.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Then it's all true... everything I heard in the stories. The Nightingales, their allegiance to Nocturnal and the Twilight Sepulcher.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: Yes. That's why we need to prepare ourselves and meet Mercer on equal footing. Just outside of Riften, beyond the Southeast Gate is a small path cut up the mountainside. At the end of that path is a clearing and an old standing stone. I'd ask you both meet me there.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: So, this is Nightingale Hall. I heard about this place when I joined the Guild, but I never believed it existed.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: The assumption that the Nightingales were just a myth was seeded within the Guild on purpose. It helped avert attention from our true nature. What's wrong, Brynjolf? I can almost hear your brow furrowing.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: I'm trying to understand why I'm here, lass. I'm no priest, and I'm certainly not religious. Why pick me?

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: This isn't about religion, Brynjolf... it's business. This is Nightingale Hall. You're the first of the uninitiated to set foot inside in over a century. Now, if you'll both proceed to the armory to don your Nightingale Armor, we can begin the Oath.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Okay, lass. We've got these getups on... now what?

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: Beyond this gate is the first step in becoming a Nightingale.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Woah there, lass. I appreciate the armor, but becoming a Nightingale? That was never discussed.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: To hold any hope of defeating Mercer, we must have Nocturnal at our backs. If she's to accept you as one of her own, an arrangement must be struck.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: What sort of arrangement? I need to know the terms.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: The terms are quite simple, Brynjolf. Nocturnal will allow you to become a Nightingale and use your abilities for whatever you wish. And in return, both in life and in death, you must serve as a guardian of the Twilight Sepulcher.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Aye, there's always a catch. But at this point, I suppose there isn't much to lose. If it means the end of Mercer Frey, you can count me in.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: Wait a moment... what's that? It's Mercer! Look... down there!

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: I'm on it, lass. Damn it! There's no way through.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: He's toying with us. He wants us to follow.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Aye, lass... and we'll be ready for him. Let's keep moving.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Look at the size of this place. Have you ever seen anything like it in your life, lass?

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: Can't say that I have. Imagine the riches hidden within these walls.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: So this is what we heard. The entire tower collapsed.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: The only reason to do that would be to block pursuit. It must be Mercer. We'll have to find another way around.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Mercer was able to knock this thing down? Gods...

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: It's the Key, Brynjolf. In his hands, there's no telling what he's capable of.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: Mercer must have triggered these pistons. We're going to have to search for a way to open them.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: I'll bet my last septim that there's a mechanism around here somewhere.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Shor's Bones! Look at that monstrosity.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: It's a Dwarven Centurion. Very tough and very deadly.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: We can take the beast on or sneak around. It's your call, {{Hide|lad|or lass, referring to the Dragonborn}}. We're right behind you.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: The stench... this place reeks of Falmer.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: This must be their hive. We'll have to keep silent if we want to avoid drawing their attention.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: There's a mass of the Falmer in this chamber. We can sneak through or take them down... I don't care. As long as we get to Mercer.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Aye. Whatever {{Hide|you|referring to the Dragonbrorn}} want to do, we're with you.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: He's close. I'm certain of it. We must prepare ourselves.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Then this is it. We do this for Gallus and for the Guild.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: He's here and he hasn't seen us yet. Brynjolf, watch the door.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Aye, lass. Nothing's getting by me.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: Climb down that ledge and see if you can...

speaker: Mercer
dialogue: Karliah, when will you learn you can't get the drop on me?

speaker: Mercer
dialogue: Karliah, I'll deal with you after I rid myself of your irksome companions. In the meantime, perhaps you and Brynjolf should get better acquainted.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: What's... what's happening... I can't stop myself.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: Damn you, Mercer! Fight it, Brynjolf... he's taken control of you!

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: I'm sorry lass, I... I can't...

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: Damn! This place is coming down! Quick, get the Skeleton Key and the Eye and lets get out of here!

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: No luck there, lass. Something must have fallen on the other side of the door because it isn't moving!

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: We have to find another way out of here before the place fills with water!

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Look, I've never been good at these things, so I'm just going to keep it short. Being Guild Master means more than just getting a cut of all the loot, it's about being a leader and keeping this rabble in order. With that in mind, I propose that the position of Guild Master should be {{Hide|yours|referring to the Dragonborn}}. Delvin?

speaker: Vex
dialogue: Sure, why not.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Everyone is in agreement, so all I can do now is name {{Hide|you|referring to the Dragonborn}} Guild Master and wish you good fortune and long life. Now everyone get back to work.

speaker: Bulfrek
dialogue: There's no honor in being a Jarl's servant. No Sovngarde waits for the dust cleaners.

speaker: Cairine
dialogue: You don't want to be here. No one wants to.

speaker: Calcelmo
dialogue: You idiot. Do you even know who I am? The most recognized scholar on the Dwemer in all of Tamriel, and you people keep bothering me!

speaker: Calder
dialogue: As you will, my Thane. I will protect you with my life.

speaker: Calixto Corrium
dialogue: Welcome to the House of Curiosities! I offer a brief tour for a few coins, or you can simply browse at your leisure.

speaker: Calixto
dialogue: Of course, my dear. It may prove to be quite the curiosity! One must always be alert.

speaker: Elda
dialogue: Well, I seem to have misplaced it at the moment. But it was white, like alabaster, with three bright rubies set in it.

speaker: Calixto
dialogue: Be very careful with that. It sounds as if it may be the Death Ring of Dro'farahn. A ring of the most dangerous sort.

speaker: Elda
dialogue: Oh dear. What should I do?

speaker: Calixto
dialogue: Bring it to me straight away when you find it. Don't dally. I can keep it safe.

speaker: Elda
dialogue: Oh, thank the gods you're in Windhelm, Calixto!

speaker: Calixto
dialogue: Think nothing of it.

speaker: Elda
dialogue: Calixto, do you know if there's any truth to these rumors of dragons?

speaker: Calixto
dialogue: Eh. I try not to trouble myself with stories of the outside world. Now, if someone brings me a dragon scale, that's a different story.

speaker: Elda
dialogue: But how would you know it's real?

speaker: Calixto
dialogue: Ah, I can't reveal all my secrets to you. But rest assured, I would know.

speaker: Camilla
dialogue: Well one of us has to do something!

speaker: Lucan
dialogue: I said no! No adventures, no theatrics, no thief-chasing!

speaker: Camilla
dialogue: Well what are you going to do then, huh? Let's hear it!

speaker: Lucan
dialogue: We are done talking about this! [notices player] Oh, [clears throat] a customer. Sorry you had to hear that.

speaker: Camilla
dialogue: So, this is your plan, Lucan?

speaker: Lucan
dialogue: Yes. So now you don't have to go, do you?

speaker: Camilla
dialogue: Oh really? Well, I think your new helper here needs a guide.

speaker: Lucan
dialogue: Wh...no...I...Oh, by the Eight, fine. But only to the edge of town!

speaker: Camilla
dialogue: We don't sell silver buckles, do we? One of the customers was asking.

speaker: Lucan
dialogue: I'm afraid not.

speaker: Camilla
dialogue: Well, I was thinking...we should. We could sell all kinds of specialty items. You know, cater to some of our more...'eclectic' customers.

speaker: Lucan
dialogue: That's really not at the top of my list, no. Please, Camilla, I need you to focus.

speaker: Camilla
dialogue: Of course, Lucan. Of course. I was just, well...Never mind.

speaker: Camilla
dialogue: Lucan, I was thinking we should have a grand sale, lower the prices by half, maybe get some jugglers. We could attract lots of new customers.

speaker: Lucan
dialogue: A sale? To attract new customers? Camilla, everyone in Riverwood already shops here. There are no more customers.

speaker: Camilla
dialogue: Hmmm...Well, maybe we could go on some sort of trip. Take the wares on the road. Get some new customers.

speaker: Lucan
dialogue: Camilla, really? You don't have better things to do? Because I could certainly find a few tasks...

speaker: Camilla
dialogue: Of course, Lucan. Of course. I was just, well...Never mind.

speaker: Camilla
dialogue: It's bad enough my brother is harping on me to pick one. Don't you start too.

speaker: Hod
dialogue: I'm just sayin' you should pick one to settle down with.

speaker: Aldis
dialogue: Come on, now! I want those arrows dead center! The lives of your fellow soldiers are counting on it.

speaker: Svari
dialogue: They can't hurt uncle Roggvir. Tell them he didn't do it.

speaker: Addvar
dialogue: Svari, you need to go home. Go home and stay there until your mother comes.

speaker: Aldis
dialogue: Lock the city gate.

speaker: Vivienne
dialogue: You should tell her that her uncle is scum that betrayed his High King. Best she know now, Addvar.

speaker: Addvar
dialogue: You're all heart, Vivienne.

speaker: Aldis
dialogue: Roggvir. You helped Ulfric Stormcloak escape this city after he murdered High King Torygg. By opening that gate for Ulfric you betrayed the people of Solitude.

speaker: Sorex
dialogue: He doesn't deserve to speak!

speaker: Roggvir
dialogue: There was no murder! Ulfric challenged Torygg. He beat the High King in fair combat.

speaker: Roggvir
dialogue: Such as our way! Such as the ancient custom of Skyrim, and all Nords!

speaker: Vivienne
dialogue: Cut 'em down!

speaker: Aldis
dialogue: Guard. Prepare the prisoner.

speaker: Roggvir
dialogue: I don't need your help.

speaker: Aldis
dialogue: Very well, Roggvir. Bow your head.

speaker: Roggvir
dialogue: On this day... I go to Sovngarde.

speaker: Aicantar
dialogue: Accidents like this just don't happen. Someone is trying to sabotage my uncle's research.

speaker: Aquilius
dialogue: I...all right. If there is a thief, he won't leave this tower alive. But shouldn't we inform Master Calcelmo?

speaker: Aicantar
dialogue: I'll deal with my uncle. Just...go! Scour this place from top to bottom!

speaker: Aquilius
dialogue: All right men, spread out and search the tower. No telling who - or what - we're dealing with here.

speaker: Captain Lonely-Gale
dialogue: Fair winds and calm seas. That's an old sailor's parting.

speaker: Belyn
dialogue: So, have you ever actually spoken to Captain Lonely-Gale?

speaker: Adisla
dialogue: By the gods, he's just a retired ship's captain.

speaker: Belyn
dialogue: Maybe to you, but he's just so... his story is...

speaker: Adisla
dialogue: He's just a guard captain. And not a very good one, at that.

speaker: Lonely-Gale
dialogue: Elda, you know better than to believe every idiot traveler that wanders through.

speaker: Elda
dialogue: But they're saying that one of them freed Ulfric... that he's in league with them.

speaker: Lonely-Gale
dialogue: Think about how ridiculous that sounds. Come now.

speaker: Elda
dialogue: So what's the news on the street, Captain?

speaker: Lonely-Gale
dialogue: The dark elves are uneasy. There's a killer on the streets. And Viola Giordano won't leave me alone.

speaker: Elda
dialogue: How would you like a drink?

speaker: Lonely-Gale
dialogue: Oh, very much so.

speaker: Elda
dialogue: Coming right up.

speaker: Lonely-Gale
dialogue: A pleasure to see you as well, Niranye. What can I do for you?

speaker: Niranye
dialogue: I was wondering if you still had many associates in the shipping profession. I have a business proposition for any sailors who might be looking to make a few extra septims.

speaker: Lonely-Gale
dialogue: If that business proposition includes smuggling, forget it. The sailors I know are plenty good at finding trouble without any help from you.

speaker: Niranye
dialogue: You're such a wet blanket, captain. Can't a girl have a little fun from time to time?

speaker: Lonely-Gale
dialogue: What did you hear?

speaker: Viola
dialogue: It was an old Nord proverb. It said the best way to get over the loss of a lover is to find a new one.

speaker: Lonely-Gale
dialogue: I didn't lose a lover, Viola; I lost my wife. It's not the same thing.

speaker: Viola
dialogue: Well, if it works in the one case, why not the other? Don't you want to at least give it a try?

speaker: Viola
dialogue: Captain Lonely-Gale, I-I've been looking for you everywhere!

speaker: Lonely-Gale
dialogue: And now you've found me. Can I help you?

speaker: Viola
dialogue: Have you thought about my invitation?

speaker: Lonely-Gale
dialogue: I've thought about it, but I'm not sure it's such a good idea.

speaker: Viola
dialogue: Oh, I see. Is it still too soon?

speaker: Lonely-Gale
dialogue: Yes, I think that must be it. My wife hasn't been gone that long, after all. Ask me again on another day.

speaker: Viola
dialogue: I'm sorry to be such a bother. We'll talk another time.

speaker: Viola
dialogue: Captain. Captain!

speaker: Lonely-Gale
dialogue: What is it now, Viola?

speaker: Viola
dialogue: Did you notice that the snow settles in a different direction near the murder sites?

speaker: Lonely-Gale
dialogue: Don't you think all your tramping around there investigating might have something to do with it?

speaker: Viola
dialogue: I... well... perhaps. But still, it's curious.

speaker: Viola
dialogue: Do you think those Dark Elves had anything to do with the murders? The attacks all happened at night, after all.

speaker: Lonely-Gale
dialogue: Viola, Dark Elves sleep, just like the rest of us.

speaker: Viola
dialogue: You wouldn't think it from the racket that Cornerclub makes.

speaker: Lonely-Gale
dialogue: I'm sure the guards have the matter well in hand. Now, if you'll excuse me.

speaker: Captain Valmir
dialogue: The General has sent me to obtain a powerful weapon for the war effort.

speaker: Captain Valmir
dialogue: The research I've done seems to indicate that Skorm Snow-Strider left part of his journal here after laying siege. I believe it should indicate how to enter the blocked off sections of the stronghold. I should warn you, Forelhost is quite haunted, but I'm sure you can handle it. Return to me here once you've obtained the staff.

speaker: Imperial Soldier
dialogue: Wait it's haunted? I don't like ghosts... let me think about this for a minute... Wait... who in the blazes is this?

speaker: Captain Valmir
dialogue: Oh! Um, he he... Hold on... I... I can explain...

speaker: Imperial Soldier
dialogue: Valmir, you rat. You're not a soldier at all! Must be one of the Thalmor!

speaker: Captain Valmir
dialogue: The research I've done seems to indicate that Skorm Snow-Strider left part of his journal here after laying siege. I believe it should indicate how to enter the blocked off sections of the stronghold. I should warn you, Forelhost is quite haunted, but I'm sure you can handle it. Return to me here once you've obtained the staff.

speaker: Stormcloak Soldier
dialogue: Wait it's haunted? I don't like ghosts... let me think about this for a minute... Wait... who in the blazes is this?

speaker: Captain Valmir
dialogue: Oh! Um, he he... Hold on... I... I can explain...

speaker: Captain Wayfinder
dialogue: I don't buy all that talk about ship captains having to be stern and strict. I want my crewmen to enjoy their work.

speaker: Carlotta Valentia
dialogue: Life's hard enough with all these men propositioning me. But that bard is the worst.

speaker: Carlotta
dialogue: How goes the begging today, Brenuin?

speaker: Brenuin
dialogue: That's right, mock the town beggar like everyone else. But I've got a right to browse, don't I? I ain't hurtin' anyone.

speaker: Carlotta
dialogue: Make it quick, then. I don't want your stink driving my customers away.

speaker: Brenuin
dialogue: The gods smile on them who show charity. Best you remember that.

speaker: Carlotta
dialogue: And what might you be looking at?

speaker: Brenuin
dialogue: Oh, the fruit looks so good. So juicy.

speaker: Carlotta
dialogue: No handouts today, Brenuin. Now scat. You'll scare off my paying customers.

speaker: Brenuin
dialogue: Oh, just one apple, Carlotta? Just one tiny apple. I'll pay you tomorrow, I swear it.

speaker: Carlotta
dialogue: That's what you said last week, and the week before that. Now go, before I call a guard.

speaker: Brenuin
dialogue: No, no! Don't do that. No need to do that. I'm going. See? I'm leaving. No guards, please.

speaker: Carlotta
dialogue: Look, come back tomorrow, okay? If I have anything left that's not sold or spoiled, you can have it.

speaker: Brenuin
dialogue: You've got the heart of Mara herself, you know that? Thank you, Carlotta. Thank you.

speaker: Mila
dialogue: Can you close up the stand early today, mama?

speaker: Carlotta
dialogue: I'm afraid not, little fairy. The fruit has about another day left before it spoils. We've got to sell as much as we can, as soon as we can.

speaker: Mila
dialogue: That's what you always say.

speaker: Carlotta
dialogue: Because it's always true.

speaker: Mila
dialogue: Can we at least go to the tavern for supper?

speaker: Carlotta
dialogue: Tsk. And to think, I was going to feed you cabbages and apples again. Yes, little fairy, we can go to the tavern for supper.

speaker: Nazeem
dialogue: These fruits and vegetables are disappointing, Carlotta.

speaker: Carlotta
dialogue: I get them fresh from the farms daily, Nazeem.

speaker: Nazeem
dialogue: If you were getting them from my farm, they'd be twice as fresh.

speaker: Olfina
dialogue: Did you raise your prices, Carlotta?

speaker: Carlotta
dialogue: I had to. The farmers are charging me double for the produce I sell.

speaker: Olfina
dialogue: Let me guess, they're saying it's because of this trouble with the Stormcloaks?

speaker: Carlotta
dialogue: Exactly. Road patrols were cut in half because the Jarl needed soldiers. Now the bandits are bolder than ever. They've been raiding the farms for food, and supplies are scarcer than ever. Maybe I should sell swords and armor, instead.

speaker: Olfina
dialogue: Maybe, but they wouldn't taste as good as a loaf of fresh-baked pumpernickel.

speaker: Ysolda
dialogue: Those green apples you sold me the other day were delicious.

speaker: Carlotta
dialogue: Aren't they? I always set some aside for myself when the traders bring them up from the south.

speaker: Ysolda
dialogue: I'm sure you could charge double for those and still sell them all within a week.

speaker: Carlotta
dialogue: You're right. I'll have to remember that the next time I get a shipment in.

speaker: Cedran
dialogue: You treat a horse well, it'll take you to Oblivion and back.

speaker: Challenger
dialogue: You call yourself a wizard? I challenge you to a duel!

speaker: Burguk
dialogue: I saw you working the forge today, wife. Your muscles have grown strong from the metal shaping!

speaker: Gharol
dialogue: Do they, my chief? Am I now favored enough to replace Shel by your side at the feast? Back your words with action!

speaker: Burguk
dialogue: No more talk of Shel. As chief, I will do what I please, so point your fiery gaze to our enemies.

speaker: Burguk
dialogue: Tell me, mother, does Malacath favor our stronghold?

speaker: Shel
dialogue: My chief, Gharol threatens to have me work in the mines. You won't allow my pretty hands to dirty, will you?

speaker: Burguk
dialogue: No, my wife. You have been given other gifts to please your chief than mine work. I will talk to Gharol and all will be well.

speaker: Shel
dialogue: Oh, thank you my chief!

speaker: Larak
dialogue: The way you and your mother forge weapons is impressive.

speaker: Olur
dialogue: It's simple Orc smithing practice, my chief. Nothing that hasn't been passed down for years.

speaker: Larak
dialogue: I served in the Legion. Perhaps I'll show you some of their technique one of these days.

speaker: Larak
dialogue: I am honored.

speaker: Larak
dialogue: Your muscles ripple when you work the forge. It's pleasing.

speaker: Shuftharz
dialogue: Thank you, my chief.

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: Are the gods angry with me?

speaker: Bolar
dialogue: Why do you ask me that?

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: Why else have they cursed me? Killed all my wives?

speaker: Bolar
dialogue: Perhaps it's actually a sign of their love for you. They don't want to see you with unworthy mates.

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: Then they should send one they consider worthy.

speaker: Bolar
dialogue: Patience, boy.

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: Bolar, I must ask you something.

speaker: Bolar
dialogue: Yes, child?

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: Have the spirits told you where I may find a wife? One who will be safe from this curse?

speaker: Bolar
dialogue: Oh, all things in time, my boy. All things in time. What more do you need that Yatul and I cannot provide?

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: I need more children.

speaker: Bolar
dialogue: Well, that's a different matter...

speaker: Dushnamub
dialogue: Don't you ever wonder, father?

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: All the time.

speaker: Dushnamub
dialogue: But your aunts don't even seem to care.

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: They are good women. They love me. You will speak no more ill of them.

speaker: Dushnamub
dialogue: I've just never heard of a midwife losing all her mothers like that.

speaker: Dushnamub
dialogue: Father, I'm worried about Gadba and Mul.

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: What about them?

speaker: Dushnamub
dialogue: You don't worry about two Orc men coming into your stronghold? That they might challenge you?

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: They're miners. Harmless.

speaker: Dushnamub
dialogue: I've just learned not to trust luck around here.

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: Someday, you can have your own stronghold.

speaker: Dushnamub
dialogue: I think it may have to be far away from here.

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: Oh, if you're worried about me trying to meddle with you...

speaker: Dushnamub
dialogue: It's not you I'm worried about.

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: How is your hunting with Yatul?

speaker: Urog
dialogue: We are strong. We get the job done.

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: I'm proud of you for helping provide for us.

speaker: Urog
dialogue: Well someone has to provide around here.

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: What is that supposed to mean?

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: I don't know what your aunts told you, but...

speaker: Urog
dialogue: They're not my aunts. They're your aunts. And they told me enough.

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: What are you talking about?

speaker: Urog
dialogue: About how the Divines cursed you. What horrible thing did you do to deserve it?

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: Nothing! I... it's ill fortune. That's all.

speaker: Urog
dialogue: Well, your ill fortune means I have no mother.

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: I... I'm sorry.

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: Haven't I always been a good father? A good chief?

speaker: Urog
dialogue: Yatul and I do all the hunting. Mul and Gadba do all the mining. It seems like all you do is find more wives to get killed.

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: That's not fair, now.

speaker: Urog
dialogue: Just... try and keep out of our way.

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: You wanted to see me?

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: Bolar said you had been looking for a new wife?

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: Well, I...

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: I don't think you're quite ready yet.

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: How will I know when I'm ready?

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: Bolar and I will tell you.

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: Bolar has been in a bad mood for weeks, now.

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: Oh? I hadn't noticed.

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: Since Galka was taken from us. She's been... sad, I guess.

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: She's just worried about you. We all are. We just want you to be happy. We want to make you happy.

speaker: Atub
dialogue: It is time, Yamarz.

speaker: Yamarz
dialogue: You bring an outsider here, and now insist I call on Malacath for help, when he has clearly forsaken me? You try my patience, Atub.

speaker: Atub
dialogue: Doing nothing will not grant our tribe relief from this curse. We must try.

speaker: Yamarz
dialogue: Grrr. Fine, let's get this over with.

speaker: Atub
dialogue: Now, we begin the ritual... Great Malacath, we beseech you, aid us in our time of need...

speaker: Yamarz
dialogue: Why are we bothering with this?

speaker: Malacath
dialogue: You pathetic weakling!

speaker: Yamarz
dialogue: What's that?

speaker: Atub
dialogue: Malacath has heard my pleas! He speaks to us!

speaker: Malacath
dialogue: You dare summon me, Yamarz?

speaker: Yamarz
dialogue: What? What is this?

speaker: Malacath
dialogue: You don't deserve to call yourself an Orc! You're weak, you're small, and you're an embarrassment! You let giants... Giants!... overrun my shrine. Bring me their leader's club as an offering, and I might release you from this curse!

speaker: Atub
dialogue: So it will be. Malacath has spoken, Yamarz. Your path is clear.

speaker: Yamarz
dialogue: Very well. {{Hide|You|Referring to the Dragonborn}}, outsider, come here! I want a word.

speaker: Boy
dialogue: Well, you smell like a Hagraven. And you look like one, too!

speaker: Boy
dialogue: You... you take that back!

speaker: Girl
dialogue: Oh yeah? Well, I've seen mudcrabs that're smarter than you.

speaker: Girl
dialogue: Grr... I'm gonna get you for that!

speaker: Boy
dialogue: You can't catch me!

speaker: Cicero
dialogue: ...Is there singing in the Void? Dancing...? Surely the Dread Lord will at least allow poor Cicero to caper...

speaker: Guard
dialogue: You there! Fool! Hold fast. You've been accused of a crime against the laws of this land. What say you in your defense?

speaker: Cicero
dialogue: Wh... What? A crime? Me? Preposterous! Poor Cicero is just standing here! Cicero loves order. Oh yes! He would never disrespect the law!

speaker: Guard
dialogue: You look like a crazy man to me. And what's in that coffin, hmm? Maybe some time in a cell will help loosen that lying tongue.

speaker: Cicero
dialogue: Damn that Loreius. Oh, how he will pay for this treachery...

speaker: Guard
dialogue: You just keep quiet and stay where you are. Soon as my relief arrives, we'll all take a nice little trip.

speaker: Cicero
dialogue: But the Night Mother is mother to all! It is her voice we follow! Her will! Would you dare risk disobedience? And surely... punishment?

speaker: Festus Krex
dialogue: Oh, be quiet you great lumbering lapdog. The man has had a long journey. You can at least be civil. Mister Cicero, I for one am delighted you and the Night Mother have arrived. Your presence here signals a welcome return to tradition.

speaker: Cicero
dialogue: Oh, what a kind and wise wizard you are. Sure to earn our Lady's favor.

speaker: Astrid
dialogue: You and the Night Mother are of course welcome here, Cicero. And you will be afforded the respect deserving of your position as Keeper. Understood... husband?

speaker: Cicero
dialogue: Oh, yes yes yes! Thank you, thank you, thank you!

speaker: Astrid
dialogue: But make no mistake. I am the leader of this Sanctuary. My word is law. Are we clear on that point?

speaker: Cicero
dialogue: Oh yes, mistress. Perfectly! You're the boss.

speaker: Cicero
dialogue: Oh, but how can I defend you? How can I exert your will? If you will not speak? To anyone!

speaker: Cicero
dialogue: Poor Cicero has failed you. Poor Cicero is sorry, sweet mother. I've tried, so very hard. But I just can't find the Listener.

speaker: Astrid
dialogue: By Sithis, this ends now! Back away, fool! Whatever you've been planning is over! Are you all right? I heard the commotion. Who was Cicero talking to? Where's the accomplice? Reveal yourself, traitor!

speaker: Cicero
dialogue: I spoke only to the Night Mother! I spoke to the Night Mother, but she didn't speak to me. Oh no. She spoke only to {{Hide|him|or her if the Dragonborn is female}}! To the listener!

speaker: Astrid
dialogue: What? The Listener? What are you going on about? What is this lunacy?

speaker: Cicero
dialogue: It's true, it's true! The Night Mother has spoken! The silence has been broken! The Listener has been chosen!

speaker: Barbas
dialogue: I knew I could trust you!

speaker: Shrine to Clavicus Vile
dialogue: Yeah, yeah, dog gets master, master gets cosmic axe, everyone's happy. Just get over here, mutt.

speaker: Barbas
dialogue: Don't worry, I'll make sure he sees the light. I trusted you, now you trust me.

speaker: Shrine to Clavicus Vile
dialogue: Ah, that feels so much better! You forget how nice supreme power feels until you've been stuck in a cave for a few years. Now, as for your wish... An end to the war, was it? I'll make sure this war ends, all right. Just as soon as the dragons swarm across Skyrim and wipe out all of you puny... Oh, fine. Have my boon and be done with it. Got more interesting deals to make, anyway.

speaker: Shrine to Clavicus Vile
dialogue: Ah, that feels so much better! You forget how nice supreme power feels until you've been stuck in a cave for a few years. Now, as for your wish... Power, was it? You can be part of a tremendous power - all you have to do is let your soul be absorbed by this axe. I never said it would be your power... Oh, fine. Have my boon and be done with it. Got more interesting deals to make, anyway.

speaker: Clinton Lylvieve
dialogue: Are you a soldier? One day, I'm going to be a soldier!

speaker: Coldhearted Gravedigger
dialogue: I'm dying for a rest. I swear, I could lie down right now, and just sleep forever.

speaker: Colette Marence
dialogue: Restoration is a perfectly valid school of magic. And don't let anyone tell you otherwise!

speaker: Commander Caius
dialogue: You're not thinking of causing trouble here in this beautiful city, now are you? 'Cause I'd strongly advise against such foolishness.

speaker: Commander Caius
dialogue: Well, Sabjorn. Now that you've taken care of your little pest problem, how about I get a taste of some of your mead?

speaker: Sabjorn
dialogue: Help yourself, milord. It's my finest brew yet... I call it Honningbrew Reserve. I think you'll find it quite pleasing to your palate.

speaker: Commander Caius
dialogue: Oh come now, this is mead... not some wine to be sipped and savored.

speaker: Commander Caius
dialogue: By the Eight?! What... what's in this?

speaker: Sabjorn
dialogue: I... I don't know. What's wrong?

speaker: Commander Caius
dialogue: You assured me this place was clean! I'll see... see to it that you remain in irons for the rest of your days!

speaker: Sabjorn
dialogue: No, please! I don't understand...

speaker: Commander Caius
dialogue: Silence, idiot! I should have known better... to trust this place after it's been riddled with filth.

speaker: Sabjorn
dialogue: I beg you... please. This is not what it seems!

speaker: Commander Caius
dialogue: You... you're in charge here until I can sort this all out.

speaker: Mallus Maccius
dialogue: It will be my pleasure.

speaker: Commander Caius
dialogue: And you... you're coming with me to Dragonsreach. We'll see how quickly your memory clears in the city's prisons. Now move.

speaker: Sabjorn
dialogue: Look, I assure you, this is all just a huge misunderstanding!

speaker: Commander Caius
dialogue: I said move!

speaker: Mallus Maccius
dialogue: Farewell, Sabjorn.

speaker: Gaius
dialogue: Father, you worry too much. I'll be fine.

speaker: Commander Maro
dialogue: I know you will. But all the same, remember everything I said. Stay alert, and when you get to the cities, make your observations and move on.

speaker: Gaius
dialogue: I understand, But you're being paranoid. I'm inspecting security, not charging off into battle. There's not a lot that can go wrong.

speaker: Commander Maro
dialogue: Son, when the Emperor's safety is concerned, anything could go wrong. Off with you, now. And good travels.

speaker: Gaius
dialogue: Farewell, father. I'll return as soon as I'm able.

speaker: Faida
dialogue: Well, this is it, then. Look after yourself, Gaius. You're doing your duty, and I'm proud of you. But you'd better come back to me. You hear?

speaker: Gaius Maro
dialogue: Oh, Faida. I may travel alone, but you know I carry you always in my heart. I'll see you soon.

speaker: Penitus Oculatus Agent
dialogue: And the outpost at Dragon Bridge?

speaker: Commander Maro
dialogue: It'll be shuttered by the end of the month.

speaker: Penitus Oculatus Agent
dialogue: Very good. And you'll be returning to... Well, if you don't mind me asking, where exactly will you be going now, sir?

speaker: Commander Maro
dialogue: Hmph. Now there's an excellent question. An excellent question, indeed. Truth is, as soon as the Emperor sets sail, I'm resigning my position.

speaker: Penitus Oculatus Agent
dialogue: Oh... I see. Well then, let me be just say that it's been an honor serving under you Commander Maro.

speaker: Commander Maro
dialogue: The honor has been mine. You should be proud of what we've accomplished here. The Dark Brotherhood is no more. And the Emperor, finally, is safe.

speaker: Penitus Oculatus Agent
dialogue: Yes sir.

speaker: Constance Michel
dialogue: My only concern is for the children. The poor darlings have no one else.

speaker: Corpulus Vinius
dialogue: Welcome to the Winking Skeever, friend.

speaker: Corpulus
dialogue: It's been a good week, my boy! Loud customers mean good cheer, and good cheer means a full till! You know, I ought to retire and leave you to run the Skeever, son!

speaker: Corpulus
dialogue: Bring up some more mead, my boy. This cask's nearly tapped!

speaker: Sorex
dialogue: Yes, father. Which cask should we open?

speaker: Sorex
dialogue: Good idea, sis. Maybe you ought to be in charge!

speaker: Corpulus
dialogue: Yes, yes, fine. Just hurry! Mustn't keep the customers thirsty!

speaker: Cosnach, when asked where he works
dialogue: Arnleif and Sons Trading Company. I'm a porter. Just some muscle hired to move heavy packages.

speaker: Courier
dialogue: I've been looking for you. Got something I'm supposed to deliver - your hands only.

speaker: Curwe
dialogue: You need something talk to my husband. Vantus Loreius. Or just Loreius, if it's all the same to you.

speaker: Curwe
dialogue: I had a look at that boneyard the other day, Vantus. The one to the Northwest.

speaker: Vantus
dialogue: I told you I don't like you going there. I've seen scavengers picking at the mammoths. They could be dangerous.

speaker: Curwe
dialogue: You know, I was thinking of expanding the herb garden. Make room for some new plants I'm planning.

speaker: Vantus
dialogue: That should be all right. How much space were you planning?

speaker: Curwe
dialogue: Oh, half the field should do.

speaker: Vantus
dialogue: Half the field? What could need half the field?

speaker: Curwe
dialogue: I just think pollinating would be easier if I could do a lot of plants at once.

speaker: Vantus
dialogue: Uh... why don't we talk about this later?

speaker: Dagny
dialogue: One of the new servants? Remember that I like my meat rare.

speaker: Dagny
dialogue: I'm so angry, I can hardly stand it! Father promised me a new dress days ago, now where is it?

speaker: Frothar
dialogue: It takes a while to make a dress, Dagny. You have to be patient.

speaker: Dagny
dialogue: But I don't want to be patient! I want my dress right now! Father promised!

speaker: Frothar
dialogue: All you ever do is complain about what you want. You're a spoiled baby.

speaker: Dagny
dialogue: I'm going to tell father you said that. He'll tan your hide for sure!

speaker: Dagur
dialogue: If you've business with the College, you're welcome to stay here. It's where most of our business comes from, in fact.

speaker: Daighre
dialogue: I'm the hardest worker in Left Hand. Better than any man.

speaker: Dalan Merchad
dialogue: I'm a lot happier out here on the deck than I am wandering around in that ruin of a city.

speaker: Danica Pure-Spring
dialogue: These are trying times for us all, I know. Many come to the Temple of Kynareth to pray, and I assist them as best I'm able.

speaker: Danica
dialogue: It was taken by a lightning strike. Wish I had time to deal with it, but it's hard enough with all these wounded from the war.

speaker: Maurice
dialogue: Please, don't just let it stay like this. It's disgraceful.

speaker: Danica
dialogue: I really don't have time to deal with you right now. Please just let me get back to my work.

speaker: Maurice
dialogue: But this is supposed to be your work.

speaker: Deeja
dialogue: You want knives? You want them in your belly? No? Then you stop talking to Deeja.

speaker: Jaree-Ra
dialogue: My contact, she says Hammerfell steel is much desired by certain parties.

speaker: Deeja
dialogue: Why should we settle for half a fin when we could just take the whole whale?

speaker: Jaree-Ra
dialogue: Patience, sister. Patience.

speaker: Degaine
dialogue: Alms. I said "alms" you backbiter. Give a crippled worker a helping hand.

speaker: Degaine
dialogue: Mining accident, back when I was in prison for being a pickpocket.

speaker: Cosnach
dialogue: You’re lying. You’re not quick enough to be a pickpocket. What’s the real reason?

speaker: Degaine
dialogue: Fell off the top of the cliff after a drunken party with the priestesses of Dibella.

speaker: Cosnach
dialogue: I don’t buy that story, either.

speaker: Degaine
dialogue: Too bad. That one’s my favorite.

speaker: Delacourt
dialogue: Perhaps one day, I'll write a song about you!

speaker: Delvin Mallory
dialogue: See, that kind of attitude comes from someone who wants to get rich and stay alive long enough to enjoy it. We're goin' to get along nicely.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: You better have a damn good reason to be here with that murderer.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: Please, lower your weapons so we can speak. I have proof that you've all been misled!

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: No tricks, Karliah or I'll cut you down where you stand. Now what's this so-called proof you speak of?

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: I have Gallus' journal. I think you'll find its contents disturbing.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Let me see. No, it... it can't be. This can't be true. I've known Mercer too long...

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: It's true, Brynjolf. Every word. Mercer's been stealing from the Guild for years, right under your noses.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: There's only one way to find out if what the lass says is true. Delvin, I'll need you to open the Vault.

speaker: Delvin
dialogue: Wait just a blessed moment, Bryn. What's in that book? What did it say?

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: It says Mercer's been stealing from our vault for years. Gallus was looking into it before he was murdered.

speaker: Delvin
dialogue: How can Mercer open up a vault that needs two keys? It's impossible. Could he pick his way in?

speaker: Vex
dialogue: That door has the best puzzle locks money can buy. There's no way it can be picked open.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: He didn't need to pick the lock.

speaker: Delvin
dialogue: What's she on about?

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Use your key on the vault, Delvin. We'll open it up and find out the truth.

speaker: Delvin
dialogue: I've used my key, but the vault's still locked up tighter than a drum. Now use yours.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: By the Eight! It's gone, everything's gone! Get in here, all of you!

speaker: Delvin
dialogue: The gold, the jewels... it's all gone.

speaker: Vex
dialogue: That son-of-a-bitch! I'll kill him!

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Vex! Put it away... right now. We can't afford to lose our heads... we need to calm down and focus.

speaker: Delvin
dialogue: Do what he says, Vex. This isn't helpin' right now.

speaker: Vex
dialogue: Fine. We do it your way. For now.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Delvin, Vex... watch the Flagon. If you see Mercer, come tell me right away.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Delvin, please tell me you have good news.

speaker: Delvin
dialogue: If I told you that, I'd be lying. We haven't had a bit in weeks. our clients are starting to get angry.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: You tell this sorry bunch of thieves that they need to put down their flagons and get to work if they want to keep their status!

speaker: Delvin
dialogue: I will, I will...

speaker: Delvin
dialogue: I don't know where you find your sources, but that last shipment of skooma was some of the best quality I've seen in years.

speaker: Tonilia
dialogue: I just got luck is all. Bumped into someone who knew someone else. The rest just writes itself.

speaker: Delvin
dialogue: If you like I'd be happy to take it over the operation for you. Take the source off your hands.

speaker: Tonilia
dialogue: And lose out just when the going is getting good? No thanks.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Look, I've never been good at these things, so I'm just going to keep it short. Being Guild Master means more than just getting a cut of all the loot, it's about being a leader and keeping this rabble in order. With that in mind, I propose that the position of Guild Master should be yours. Delvin?

speaker: Vex
dialogue: Sure, why not.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Everyone is in agreement, so all I can do now is name you Guild Master and wish you good fortune and long life. Now everyone get back to work.

speaker: Dengeir of Stuhn
dialogue: My nephew has always been handed things, even the title of Jarl.

speaker: Dervenin
dialogue: My master has abandoned me! Abandoned his people. And nothing I say can change his mind.

speaker: Dervenin
dialogue: Master! You've taken me back! Does this mean we're going home? Oh, happy times! I can't wait to...

speaker: Sheogorath
dialogue: Yes, yes, that's quite enough celebration. Let's send you ahead, shall we?

speaker: Dinya Balu
dialogue: Riften is drowning in a sea of sin and wickedness and it's my personal mission to let everyone know that the warmth of Mara can see them through.

speaker: Dinya
dialogue: That's a shame. What's causing them all the trouble?

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: There's the stories about Helgen, bandits, skirmishes between the Stormcloaks and the Imperials... it almost seems endless.

speaker: Dinya
dialogue: Chin up, Brand-Shei. Lady Mara will provide us strength and guidance through these difficult times.

speaker: Dinya
dialogue: Good day, Grelka.

speaker: Grelka
dialogue: What's so good about it? I've got deadbeats who don't pay me, the city guard looking over my shoulder and Maven Black-Briar breathing down my neck.

speaker: Dinya
dialogue: You poor thing. You should come by the temple, speak to Maramal.

speaker: Grelka
dialogue: Religion isn't going to save me. So unless Mara is going to start raining coin from the heavens, why don't you mind your own business.

speaker: Dinya
dialogue: When are you going to stop by the temple, Madesi?

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: Sorry Lady Dinya, but I've been busy of late.

speaker: Dinya
dialogue: It only takes but a moment to say a silent prayer to Mara. Please come by soon; not for me, but for yourself.

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: Very well, I'll try milady.

speaker: Maramal
dialogue: They laughed at me again, Dinya. They simply don't understand.

speaker: Dinya
dialogue: I'm so sorry my husband. You must remember, they're at the Bee and Barb to drink, not to listen to a sermon.

speaker: Maramal
dialogue: Yes, yes, I know. I just wish to show them there's more to life than drowning your sorrows in a goblet of mead.

speaker: Dinya
dialogue: You're a good man, Maramal. We're lucky to have you watching over us.

speaker: Maramal
dialogue: It fills me with joy to hear you're with child, Dinya. They said it wouldn't... that it couldn't happen, but Mara has shown them they're mistaken.

speaker: Dinya
dialogue: And to think I was wandering the ash wastes only two years ago. I never knew my path would lead to you.

speaker: Maramal
dialogue: You were guided here; you were always meant to be here. That's the way of things.

speaker: Dinya
dialogue: Then I thank Lady Mara with all my heart; for you, for our child and for our love.

speaker: Dinya
dialogue: Feel free to ask me anything you like.

speaker: Marise
dialogue: There's someone I like very much in Riften. I think I'd like to marry him someday, but... well, he's not of my kind. Would Mara be angry?

speaker: Dinya
dialogue: No, no... not at all. Mara believes that the spark of a union comes from inside us, not from our appearance. Tell you what... if you still feel unsure, come by the temple sometime and we'll talk about it.

speaker: Dirge
dialogue: I don't care if you're best buddies with the Guild Master, I'll still smash in your skull if you try anything.

speaker: Dirge
dialogue: You know what I mean. Tell your boss that rough is rough, but when someone pulls a {{Sicquote|dagger fun|dagger, fun}} time is over.

speaker: Delvin
dialogue: I'll pass it along.

speaker: Dirge
dialogue: You did? Thanks. {{sicquote|I|I'll}} get you the rest of your coin by tomorrow.

speaker: Delvin
dialogue: Yeah, funny think about that. The price was a hundred higher than I expected.

speaker: Dirge
dialogue: {{sicquote|Vekel|Delvin}}, you have no shame. I'll get you the rest like I said. I want that hammer.

speaker: Vekel
dialogue: Dirge! Did you take out the trash like I asked?

speaker: Dirge
dialogue: Yeah. Threw it in the lake like you said.

speaker: Vekel
dialogue: Tell me you looked through the trash before you did that.

speaker: Dirge
dialogue: Take it easy, Vekel. How long we known each other? Yeah. I checked it. All the stuff is in the safe.

speaker: Dirge
dialogue: Job's done, boss. Gave the package to her just like you said.

speaker: Vekel
dialogue: Good. Did she say anything we need to know?

speaker: Dirge
dialogue: Yep. She said that the Jarl was planning a surprise raid on us, but she talked her out of it. Said she saved us a lot of trouble.

speaker: Vekel
dialogue: That she did. Very good. I'll tell Brynjolf.

speaker: Dirge
dialogue: Sure, Ton. You know I'm good for it.

speaker: Tonilia
dialogue: There's a new guard nosing around the meadery. Can you do something about it?

speaker: Dirge
dialogue: Gladly. He won't bother you anymore, I promise.

speaker: Dirge
dialogue: Hey Ton, you shouldn't cheat on Vekel. He's a good guy.

speaker: Tonilia
dialogue: What are you talking about?

speaker: Dirge
dialogue: Come on, everyone knows about you and Brynjolf.

speaker: Donnel
dialogue: Just here to work.

speaker: Dorthe
dialogue: Papa says I'm too friendly with strangers, but you seem all right.

speaker: Alvor
dialogue: Sigrid! We have company!

speaker: Sigrid
dialogue: Hadvar! We've been so worried about you! Come, you two must be hungry. Sit down and I'll get you something to eat.

speaker: Alvor
dialogue: Now then, boy, what's the big mystery? What are you doing here looking like you lost an argument with a cave bear?

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: I don't know where to start. You know I was assigned to General Tullius's guard. We were stopped in Helgen when we were attacked by...a dragon.

speaker: Alvor
dialogue: A dragon? That's ridiculous. You aren't drunk, are you boy?

speaker: Sigrid
dialogue: Husband. Let him tell his story.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Not much more to tell. The dragon flew over and just wrecked the whole place. Mass confusion. I don't know if anyone else got out alive. I doubt I'd have made it out if not for my friend here. I need to get back to Solitude and let them know what's happened. I thought you could help us out. Food, supplies, a place to stay.

speaker: Dorthe
dialogue: Hadvar, did you really see a dragon? What did it look like? Did it have big teeth?

speaker: Sigrid
dialogue: Hush, child. Don't pester your cousin.

speaker: Alvor
dialogue: Well, I'd better get back to work. You two make yourselves at home.

speaker: Dorthe
dialogue: You really think I can be a blacksmith someday, papa? As good as Eorlund Gray-Mane? Or maybe... even as good as you?

speaker: Alvor
dialogue: Oh, I know it! You keep working hard, like you been doing, and you could be the greatest blacksmith Skyrim has ever seen.

speaker: Dorthe
dialogue: He he. Thanks, papa.

speaker: Drahff
dialogue: You worry about bashing people's heads in, I'll worry about the Guild. Okay?

speaker: Drascua
dialogue: You won't take my eye, man-thing!

speaker: Dravynea the Stoneweaver
dialogue: Morrowind used to be a lovely place, but you couldn't pay me to live there these days.

speaker: Dravynea
dialogue: Again? But there shouldn't be any earthstreams over there.

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: Well I nearly lost my eyebrows to it.

speaker: Dravynea
dialogue: All right, I'll take a look at it.

speaker: Dravynea
dialogue: What did I tell you about snooping around my wards?

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: Woman, there's a vein of malachite as thick as my leg back there.

speaker: Dravynea
dialogue: And if you don't let me secure the steam channel, your leg could get blown off. So go dig at the other corner for a bit.

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: Well... just get it done.

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: Is the new shaft cleared yet?

speaker: Dravynea
dialogue: No, I've been busy trying to keep the whole mine from collapsing, if that's all right with you.

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: You're busy. I'll come back later.

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: Kjeld bothering you again?

speaker: Dravynea
dialogue: Nothing I can't handle.

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: Well, you send that blowhard to me if he steps over the line.

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: How's the mine today?

speaker: Dravynea
dialogue: Not too bad. Careful around the more obvious scorchers.

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: As usual. I've always got an eye on the rocks.

speaker: Phinis Gestor
dialogue: Summoning an Unbound Dremora is not like other Conjuration spells. It will not simply do your bidding.

speaker: Drevis Neloren, when told he can be seen
dialogue: Confound it all. I was quite sure I was invisible, or at least transparent.

speaker: Drifa, talking about Bersi Honey-Hand
dialogue: All the crime and corruption in Riften is really getting to him... and now that we hear rumors about the dragons, he's been very depressed.

speaker: Drifa
dialogue: Spices? I'm certain I have no idea what you're talking about.

speaker: Bersi
dialogue: You sure? It was in your hand writing. If you can't keep the books straight then let me do them.

speaker: Drifa
dialogue: You keep giving and giving Bersi, and they'll keep taking and taking. When is it going to end?

speaker: Bersi
dialogue: What would you have me do, woman? Cross the Guild? Take them all on one by one?

speaker: Drifa
dialogue: You know I don't mean that. We need to find a way out of this. Perhaps talk to Laila...

speaker: Bersi
dialogue: Laila is as clueless as she is stupid. No. If anything's to be done about this, we have to deal with it ourselves.

speaker: Drifa
dialogue: Grelka, have you had anyone come by and try to sell you an iron war axe?

speaker: Grelka
dialogue: Not lately. Why?

speaker: Drifa
dialogue: Well, we had one go missing from the Pawned Prawn, and I was just wondering...

speaker: Grelka
dialogue: Oh I get it. 'It's missing so Grelka must have it.' I wish this town would stop pointing their fingers at me. There is a Thieves Guild in town you know.

speaker: Drifa
dialogue: We have a few pieces of jewelry at the Prawn, Madesi. Want to come look at them later?

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: I wish I could, milady. Sadly, I haven't sold enough of my own jewelry, let alone buy some from you. I'm sorry.

speaker: Drifa
dialogue: Oh, I'm so sorry. I'm certain Bolli would be happy to lend you a few septims.

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: Much appreciated, Lady Drifa, but I'll manage.

speaker: Drifa
dialogue: Thanks for that bushel of apples, Marise. They're wonderful. How did you keep them so fresh?

speaker: Marise
dialogue: Can't tell you. It's a bit of a trade secret I picked up when I was living in High Rock.

speaker: Drifa
dialogue: Well, whatever you're doing, keep doing it and you'll have me as a customer for life.

speaker: Drifa
dialogue: So how are things with you and Bolli?

speaker: Drifa
dialogue: Nivenor! How can you say that? He gives you everything you ask for.

speaker: Nivenor
dialogue: If I cared for your opinion on our affairs, I'd ask. Now, if you'll excuse me.

speaker: Dryston
dialogue: You've been digging around where you don't belong.

speaker: Dushnamub
dialogue: Don't you ever wonder, father?

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: All the time.

speaker: Dushnamub
dialogue: But your aunts don't even seem to care.

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: They are good women. They love me. You will speak no more ill of them.

speaker: Dushnamub
dialogue: I've just never heard of a midwife losing all her mothers like that.

speaker: Dushnamub
dialogue: Father, I'm worried about Gadba and Mul.

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: What about them?

speaker: Dushnamub
dialogue: You don't worry about two Orc men coming into your stronghold? That they might challenge you?

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: They're miners. Harmless.

speaker: Dushnamub
dialogue: I've just learned not to trust luck around here.

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: Someday, you can have your own stronghold.

speaker: Dushnamub
dialogue: I think it may have to be far away from here.

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: Oh, if you're worried about me trying to meddle with you...

speaker: Dushnamub
dialogue: It's not you I'm worried about.

speaker: Edith
dialogue: Quicksilver ore is rare. Worth digging.

speaker: Edorfin
dialogue: What I lack in strength, I make up for with tenacity.

speaker: Eirid
dialogue: The mages don't let us go in the College. They said it's not safe in there.

speaker: Eisa Blackthorn
dialogue: Damn it, not now!

speaker: Bandit
dialogue: There she is!

speaker: Bandit 2
dialogue: Get her!

speaker: Elda Early-Dawn
dialogue: This here's Candlehearth Hall. Great room's upstairs, an' there's a bed for rent on the ground floor.

speaker: Elda
dialogue: Tell me about the Great War. I hear you were in the battle of...

speaker: Brunwulf
dialogue: Elda, honey, let's not talk about the war. It's in the past.

speaker: Elda
dialogue: I'm sorry. What would you like to talk about?

speaker: Brunwulf
dialogue: Hows about we figure out some way to keep warm tonight?

speaker: Elda
dialogue: Oh! You behave, now!

speaker: Brunwulf
dialogue: How long have you run this place, again?

speaker: Elda
dialogue: Nearly thirty years now.

speaker: Brunwulf
dialogue: Just wondering when you'll be ready to give it up and settle down. Seems like you're always working.

speaker: Elda
dialogue: I just feel like if I'm not here, then something could go wrong. Nils is a hard worker, but I wouldn't trust him to run things.

speaker: Brunwulf
dialogue: One of these days he'll have to learn.

speaker: Elda
dialogue: Perhaps. But not today.

speaker: Brunwulf
dialogue: I've been thinking about building that cabin we talked about.

speaker: Elda
dialogue: Oh? Where?

speaker: Brunwulf
dialogue: There's a clear spot just west of Riften. You know the area?

speaker: Elda
dialogue: I've been there before, but I don't know it well.

speaker: Brunwulf
dialogue: Well that's where I want to build. In the fall forest. Give it an easterly view. The sunrise is almost as pretty as you are.

speaker: Elda
dialogue: That sounds lovely. You're very sweet.

speaker: Elda
dialogue: Calixto, someone left an interesting ring in here a few weeks ago. Would you like a look?

speaker: Calixto
dialogue: Of course, my dear. It may prove to be quite the curiosity! One must always be alert.

speaker: Elda
dialogue: Well, I seem to have misplaced it at the moment. But it was white, like alabaster, with three bright rubies set in it.

speaker: Calixto
dialogue: Be very careful with that. It sounds as if it may be the Death Ring of Dro'farahn. A ring of the most dangerous sort.

speaker: Elda
dialogue: Oh dear. What should I do?

speaker: Calixto
dialogue: Bring it to me straight away when you find it. Don't dally. I can keep it safe.

speaker: Elda
dialogue: Oh, thank the gods you're in Windhelm, Calixto!

speaker: Calixto
dialogue: Think nothing of it.

speaker: Elda
dialogue: Calixto, do you know if there's any truth to these rumors of dragons?

speaker: Calixto
dialogue: Eh. I try not to trouble myself with stories of the outside world. Now, if someone brings me a dragon scale, that's a different story.

speaker: Elda
dialogue: But how would you know it's real?

speaker: Calixto
dialogue: Ah, I can't reveal all my secrets to you. But rest assured, I would know.

speaker: Elda
dialogue: Oh, Jora. Good to see you. I was wondering if you might ask Lortheim something for me.

speaker: Jora
dialogue: Don't bother. I don't have much chance of seeing my husband these days. He's always up in the palace with Ulfric.

speaker: Elda
dialogue: Oh, I'm sorry to hear that. Is everything all right?

speaker: Jora
dialogue: It's been better, I'll be honest with you.

speaker: Elda
dialogue: Here, let me get you some mead. This one's on me.

speaker: Jora
dialogue: I just don't know what to do anymore. He's hardly ever in the temple. I see him at breakfast, and that's it.

speaker: Elda
dialogue: I know, dear. He's a busy man, though, and loyal to the Stormcloaks.

speaker: Jora
dialogue: What about being loyal to his wife?

speaker: Elda
dialogue: I... I'm sorry, dear, I've got some other customers. I'll be back around in a minute.

speaker: Elda
dialogue: Captain, have you heard these stories of dragons?

speaker: Elda
dialogue: But they're saying that one of them freed Ulfric... that he's in league with them.

speaker: Lonely-Gale
dialogue: Think about how ridiculous that sounds. Come now.

speaker: Elda
dialogue: So what's the news on the street, Captain?

speaker: Lonely-Gale
dialogue: The dark elves are uneasy. There's a killer on the streets. And Viola Giordano won't leave me alone.

speaker: Elda
dialogue: How would you like a drink?

speaker: Lonely-Gale
dialogue: Oh, very much so.

speaker: Elda
dialogue: Coming right up.

speaker: Elenwen
dialogue: The Empire, in its wisdom, has come to recognize Talos worship as a barbaric remnant of a bygone age.

speaker: Malborn
dialogue: Madame Ambassador, I'm so sorry to interrupt...

speaker: Elenwen
dialogue: What is it, Malborn?

speaker: Malborn
dialogue: It's just that we've run out of the Alto wine. Do I have your permission to uncork the Arenthia red...

speaker: Elenwen
dialogue: Of course. I've told you before not to bother me with such trifles.

speaker: Malborn
dialogue: Yes, Madame Ambassador.

speaker: Ingun? Or did you wish to buy something?
dialogue: You here for lessons like Ingun Black-Briar

speaker: Ingun Black-Briar
dialogue: I don't understand, Elgrim. The formulas you're giving me are for novices but I've advanced well passed that point.

speaker: Elgrim
dialogue: Until you can do those formulas with your eyes shut, you'll never be ready to master the more difficult ones.

speaker: Ingun Black-Briar
dialogue: This is an utter waste of time.

speaker: Elgrim
dialogue: Ingun! If you want to remain in my shop as an apprentice I expect you to act like one. No exceptions!

speaker: Ingun Black-Briar
dialogue: Very well, I'll keep practicing them.

speaker: Elgrim
dialogue: Ingun, you clumsy fool! You've tainted our entire supply of Painted Troll Fat. You have no idea how hard that was to get.

speaker: Ingun Black-Briar Black-Briar
dialogue: I'm sure my mother can compensate you for it.

speaker: Elgrim
dialogue: I'll draft a letter to Rythe. If you could have it sent to Cheydinhal for me, that would make up for your blunder.

speaker: Ingun Black-Briar
dialogue: I'll make sure it's sent right away.

speaker: Elisif the Fair
dialogue: With the passing of my dear husband Torygg, the weighty position of Jarl has fallen to me. Please direct questions to my Steward.

speaker: Elisif the Fair
dialogue: Go. Away. Please!

speaker: Falk
dialogue: I've brought a friend. Someone who can help. A bodyguard. To protect you.

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: I thought you didn't believe I was in danger!

speaker: Falk
dialogue: It doesn't really matter what I believe, now does it? I've brought you someone who can protect you. That's what you want, isn't it?

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: (Sounds of unlocking and unbarring a door)<!--sic--> Well, what are you waiting for?!

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: Steward, I have an idea that might help to bolster the morale of our people in this difficult time. I think we shall have a grand parade, and let General Tullius march his troops from the Blue Palace to Castle Dour in all their finery.

speaker: Falk
dialogue: What a... fine idea, my Jarl. However, I would suggest we wait until the war has ended. After all, the General needs his soldiers out in the field, fighting battles against the Stormcloaks.

speaker: Bolgeir
dialogue: I must protest, my Jarl. A parade would make you an easy target for a Stormcloak assassin. You're safer here in the palace.

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: Oh, very well. I can see there's no changing your stubborn Nord minds. But when this war is won, I will have my parade!

speaker: Falk
dialogue: Yes, my Jarl.

speaker: Bolgeir
dialogue: We lost another five guardsmen, my Jarl. If General Tullius continues to conscript our men and send them off to battle, we'll have none left to protect the city.

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: Yes, I know. The general acted with my blessing. It is vital that we bring Ulfric to justice, but that cannot happen until his army of Stormcloaks is defeated utterly.

speaker: Bolgeir
dialogue: Told you that, did he? I'm sworn to protect you, my Jarl, but I'm the last line of defense. The first line is the walls around this city and the men who patrol them. Men whom, I might add, we're precious short on.

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: I'm aware of that, Bolgeir, and I appreciate your dedication. However, if we lose the war, the guardsmen of Solitude will make little difference in the end.

speaker: Bolgeir
dialogue: No disrespect toward the general, but sometimes I wonder if he's got your best interests at heart. In any case he won't be turnin' me into no Imperial soldier. I know my place, and it's at your side.

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: It comforts me to know that, Bolgeir.

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: As you know, Solitude's coffers are much depleted by the war efforts. Thane Erikur, you have a strong head for business. What do you suggest?

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: This is an unfortunate but unavoidable ebb in revenue. But as long as we continue to support the Empire, our sacrifices will be well rewarded.

speaker: Bryling
dialogue: Listen to you, speaking of sacrifice. You've never gone hungry a day in your life, Erikur!

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: And what would my impetuous Thane Bryling suggest, instead?

speaker: Bryling
dialogue: Simple. Let the Empire fight its own war, with its own funds, and without hijacking our supplies and soldiers. Let Haafingar rebuild.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: My lady... Surely you're not that naïve. Such foolishness would only leave us defenseless. The rebels would storm the palace in an afternoon.

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: That is quite enough. Perhaps I will raise these issues when I have an audience with General Tullius.

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: Thane Bryling, what do you have to report about the state of Haafingar's defenses?

speaker: Bryling
dialogue: The news is the same as it's been for the rest of the war, your grace. Our borders are secure, but at the cost of the guards for our towns and roads.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: I don't see any reason why we'd need them. As long as those dogs stay outside of our borders, we're fine.

speaker: Bryling
dialogue: The Stormcloaks are far from the only threat to the hold. The roads are beset by bandits and beasts... and now there's even talk of bloody dragons.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: My dear Bryling. Barring any... fancy and folly... the good people of Haafingar are surely capable of dealing with the odd highwayman or stray dog.

speaker: Bryling
dialogue: Trouble on the roads and cities means less commerce. Less commerce means less money and more starving people. And that means more crime.

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: That may well be our only answer. I will empower my Steward to seek out capable individuals to secure Haafingar. Thank you, my Thanes.

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: Steward Falk, I have a task for you. I want to begin stockpiling food and water in the event we come under siege, and I would like you to oversee this work personally.

speaker: Falk
dialogue: A wise course of action, my Jarl. However, we have little food or water to spare.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: General Tullius will never allow that. He's ordered all surplus food to be given over for the war effort.

speaker: Falk
dialogue: General Tullius does not run this city, Thane Erikur. Or have you forgotten your oaths of fealty?

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: My apologies, Jarl Elisif. I was thinking only of the importance of the war effort.

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: There's no need for an apology, and you're right about the war. Perhaps this is a matter best discussed with the general in person.

speaker: Falk
dialogue: I will make the arrangements, my Jarl.

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: Steward, when is my appointment to meet with General Tullius? There are some issues we must speak about.

speaker: Falk
dialogue: I'm afraid he's had to reschedule, my grace. By all accounts, waging war takes his every moment.

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: Again? He can't simply cancel an appointment with the Jarl! He serves in my capital city!

speaker: Falk
dialogue: I'm afraid he can. His authority comes from the emperor, whom you also serve, technically.

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: He uses all of Haafingar's resources, and doesn't answer to me in the slightest? This hardly seems fair.

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: Then we will immediately send out a legion to scour the cave and secure the town. Haafingar's people will always be safe under my rule.

speaker: Varnius
dialogue: Th... thank you, my Jarl. Thank you.

speaker: Sybille
dialogue: Your eminence, my scrying has suggested nothing in the area. Dragon Bridge is under imperial control. This is likely superstitious nonsense.

speaker: Falk
dialogue: Perhaps a more... tempered reaction... might be called for?

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: Oh. Yes, of course you are right. Falk, tell Captain Aldis I said to assign a few extra soldiers to Dragon Bridge.

speaker: Varnius
dialogue: Thank you, Jarl Elisif. But about the cave...

speaker: Falk
dialogue: I will have someone take care of the cave as well, Varnius, you can rest easy. You're dismissed.

speaker: Elrindir
dialogue: He shot an arrow that pierced my... well, rump. After such a memorable adventure, we knew we had the name for our shop.

speaker: Anoriath
dialogue: I've been thinking of hunting out beyond the boundaries of Whiterun Hold.

speaker: Elrindir
dialogue: Again? You just had an 'extended hunt' last month. To the pine forest, wasn't it?

speaker: Anoriath
dialogue: That was three days. I'm thinking more like three weeks.

speaker: Elrindir
dialogue: Three weeks? You're mad! You can't keep the stand closed for that long!

speaker: Anoriath
dialogue: Why not? Business has been terrible. Most folk would rather hunt their own meat than buy ours.

speaker: Elrindir
dialogue: Nonsense. That's just an excuse for you to avoid working, and 'commune with the greenwood like our fathers of old' and blah blah.

speaker: Anoriath
dialogue: Congratulations, brother. You've been living in Skyrim so long, you've become a Nord.

speaker: Elrindir
dialogue: At least the Nords don't shirk their responsibilities.

speaker: Elrindir
dialogue: Our stock of arrows is running a bit low.

speaker: Anoriath
dialogue: All right. I'll fletch some more when I get the time.

speaker: Elrindir
dialogue: Good. I'll do the same. We've still got plenty of shafts from that Riverwood shipment.

speaker: Anoriath
dialogue: It's been two months, and no word from father.

speaker: Elrindir
dialogue: Don't worry, brother. I'm sure he's fine. We've waited longer before receiving a letter.

speaker: Anoriath
dialogue: Might be worth riding out to Solitude, see if a messenger ship's come in.

speaker: Elrindir
dialogue: If it'll put your mind at ease, then I agree. But not now, all right? We need the business from the stand.

speaker: Eltrys
dialogue: Gods. A woman attacked right on the streets.

speaker: Elvali
dialogue: I can't believe we're doing this.

speaker: Savos
dialogue: Can you imagine the looks on their faces when we come back?

speaker: Hafnar
dialogue: You keep talking like you're sure we'll find something useful in here.

speaker: Girduin
dialogue: Given the history of this place, it's more than likely there's still some amount of power here.

speaker: Savos
dialogue: Enchanted weapons, tomes of ancient knowledge, Shalidor's secrets themselves -- who knows what we could find!

speaker: Takes-In-Light
dialogue: And what if... What if there are things guarding this place?

speaker: Atmah
dialogue: Against six College-trained mages? I think we'll be fine.

speaker: Elvali
dialogue: We... we have to go back. We can't leave Girduin...

speaker: Hafnar
dialogue: We barely made it out alive, and you want to go back in?

speaker: Atmah
dialogue: It's too late. There isn't enough of him left to go back in after.

speaker: Takes-In-Light
dialogue: Gods, what have we done?

speaker: Savos
dialogue: We can't go back. Might as well go forward. We can still do this.

speaker: Atmah
dialogue: Savos is right. We can make it if we just stay alert.

speaker: Embry
dialogue: How's about a drink, Hod.

speaker: Hod
dialogue: You'll be wantin' me to pay for them?

speaker: Embry
dialogue: It's only right seein' as {{sic|your|you're}} the important lumber man.

speaker: Hod
dialogue: You come do an honest day's work at my mill, and I'll pay you an honest day's wages. Then we'll drink.

speaker: Embry
dialogue: Gimme a mug of ale.

speaker: Embry
dialogue: Care to have a drink with me, sweet Sigrid?

speaker: Sigrid
dialogue: Drunk again, Embry? Don't let Alvor hear you talking to me that way. He'll stick your head in his forge.

speaker: Embry
dialogue: So that's a no I take it?

speaker: Endarie
dialogue: I can help with purchases, but if you come to talk, see my sister. She's the one who gets on with people. It is her one virtue really.

speaker: Irnskar
dialogue: She does, my lady. But apparently, she hates you just a little less than the others.

speaker: Taarie
dialogue: Good. And while you're at it, perhaps you should sew your mouth shut when our fine customers are within earshot, hmm?

speaker: Endon
dialogue: Markarth has changed, but the inn is as lively as ever.

speaker: Adara
dialogue: Mama, when is Cade coming home?

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: He's off fighting, Adara, with the Stormcloaks. He'll return when the war is over.

speaker: Endon
dialogue: Our son joining the Stormcloaks. If this war had never happened, Cade would have joined the Imperial Legion, like grandfather.

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: Endon, we talked about this... Are you still disappointed in Cade's choice?

speaker: Endon
dialogue: No. I think if I was a young man, I would have done the same.

speaker: Adara
dialogue: Can I join the Legion when I grow up?

speaker: Endon
dialogue: If there's still a Legion left, Adara. I'm sure you'd make a great soldier. Just like your brother.

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: We sold all those lovely little necklaces you brought me today. Did you make them yourself?

speaker: Adara
dialogue: That's right! Papa helped me with the clasps, but I did all the links on my own.

speaker: Endon
dialogue: Adara bends the silver so naturally. Grandmother would have cried if she saw how deft our daughter has become.

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: Well, I'm proud of both of you. I haven't been so busy since those nobles from Solitude come into the city three years ago.

speaker: Endon
dialogue: I miss those days, before the Forsworn took up arms again, when you could walk the roads in peace.

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: Endon, dear, please don't.... Save your frustrations for work.

speaker: Endon
dialogue: You're right, dear. I'm sorry to worry you.

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: What am I supposed to do? Never leave the house? You want that, Endon?

speaker: Endon
dialogue: You're closing the stall, and that's final.

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: You want to give up now? Out of fear? Is that what we're teaching our daughter?

speaker: Adara
dialogue: Mama, why are you and papa fighting?

speaker: Endon
dialogue: We're not fighting, we're just...Why don't I get you something to eat? Mama and papa will talk later.

speaker: Endon
dialogue: How are the necklaces selling, my wife? We could make more.

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: I'm afraid the necklaces aren't selling well. Customers aren't interested in medallions and engraved symbols of other provinces.

speaker: Endon
dialogue: Hmph. Used to be everyone in Markarth wore a necklace showing his home province, from Elsweyr, to High Rock, to Hammerfell and Cyrodiil...

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: We don't take travelers from Hammerfell or High Rock anymore, Endon. Only natives from Markarth and Skyrim.

speaker: Endon
dialogue: As they always have, along with those crazed Forsworn. They've driven off the color that used to make this city great.

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: I need to get back to the customers. We'll talk more of this when I get home tonight.

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: What should we have tonight?

speaker: Endon
dialogue: Something simple, a stew perhaps.

speaker: Adara
dialogue: Stew again, papa? I want steak.

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: Maybe we could spend a little bit more and buy some meat, Endon.

speaker: Endon
dialogue: Maybe. Let me think about it.

speaker: Endon
dialogue: Markarth has changed, but the inn is as lively as ever.

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: The city hasn't changed that much, dear. Some old dwarven stones gathering the same old moss.

speaker: Endon
dialogue: The stones aren't what bother me, love. The Forsworn are tearing the Reach apart.

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: Let's not talk about this over dinner.

speaker: Enmon
dialogue: Fjotra, dear. Did they hurt you?

speaker: Fjotra
dialogue: Of course not. My spirit remains strong.

speaker: Enmon
dialogue: My little girl. Always strong. Do you know where you have to go?

speaker: Fjotra
dialogue: I'm to go to the temple in Markarth. I... I'll have to leave you and mother.

speaker: Fjotra
dialogue: Of course.

speaker: Ennis
dialogue: Name's Ennis. If you've got friends who do business in Whiterun, they might know me.

speaker: Enthir
dialogue: I've been known to handle items of questionable interest from time to time and I'll see what I can do.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: Does the journal say where this wealth came from?

speaker: Enthir
dialogue: Yes. Gallus seems certain that Mercer had been removing funds from the Guild's treasury without anyone's knowledge.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: Anything else, Enthir? Anything about... the Nightingales?

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: Shadows preserve us. So it's true...

speaker: Enthir
dialogue: I'm not familiar with the Twilight Sepulcher. What is it? What's Mercer Frey done?

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: I'm sorry Enthir, I can't say. All that matters is we deliver your translation to the Guild immediately. Farewell, Enthir... words can't express...

speaker: Enthir
dialogue: It's alright Karliah. You don't have to say a word.

speaker: Eola
dialogue: Namira grind your bones for my bread!

speaker: Verulus
dialogue: Who... who are you? What's going on?

speaker: Eola
dialogue: Priest of Arkay. I'm your friend.

speaker: Verulus
dialogue: You're my... friend....

speaker: Eola
dialogue: Yes. I'm your friend, and I've invited you to dinner.

speaker: Verulus
dialogue: I've been invited to dinner.... I'm so hungry....

speaker: Eola
dialogue: Why don't you lay down and rest, while we get the meal ready?

speaker: Verulus
dialogue: I need to lay down. I'll just be a minute....

speaker: Eola
dialogue: Come with me. Our feast is about to begin.

speaker: Eola
dialogue: The meal is on Namira's table. Go ahead. Carve.

speaker: Eola
dialogue: Thank you for coming to dinner, Hogni.

speaker: Hogni
dialogue: I never miss a good meal.

speaker: Eola
dialogue: Not too full on bread and wine, I hope?

speaker: Banning
dialogue: I always leave room for the main course, Eola.

speaker: Eorlund Gray-Mane
dialogue: Skyforge Steel is my art and honor. The Companions need the best, so they come to me.

speaker: Eorlund
dialogue: Who will start?

speaker: Aela
dialogue: I'll do it. Before the ancient flame... We grieve.

speaker: Eorlund
dialogue: We grieve.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: We grieve.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: We grieve.

speaker: Eorlund
dialogue: At this loss... We weep.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: We weep.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: We weep.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: We weep.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: For the fallen... We shout.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: We shout.

speaker: Eorlund
dialogue: We shout.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: We shout.
