speaker: Farkas
dialogue: And for ourselves... We take our leave.

speaker: Eorlund
dialogue: We take our leave.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: We take our leave.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: We take our leave.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: His spirit is departed. Members of the Circle, let us withdraw to the Underforge, to grieve our last together.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: The old man had one wish before he died. And he didn't get it. It's as simple as that.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: Being moon-born is not so much of a curse as you might think, Vilkas.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: That's fine for you. But he wanted to be clean. He wanted to meet Ysgramor and know the glories of Sovngarde. But all that was taken from him.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: And you avenged him.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: Kodlak did not care for vengeance.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: No, Farkas, he didn't. And that's not what this is about. We should be honoring Kodlak, no matter our own thoughts on the blood.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: You're right. It's what he wanted, and he deserved to have it.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: Kodlak used to speak of a way to cleanse his soul, even in death. You know the legends of the Tomb of Ysgramor.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: There the souls of Harbingers will heed the call of northern steel. We can't even enter the tomb without Wuuthrad, and it's in pieces, like it has been for a thousand years.

speaker: Eorlund
dialogue: And dragons were just stories. And the elves once ruled Skyrim. Just because something is, doesn't mean it must be. The blade is a weapon. A tool. Tools are meant to be broken. And repaired.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: Is that? Did you repair the blade?

speaker: Fralia
dialogue: Eorlund, dearest, are you hungry? Would you like me to fix you something?

speaker: Fralia
dialogue: A venison pie, maybe? With a nice cup of mulled mead?

speaker: Fralia
dialogue: When will you be makin' some more jewelry, love? Some silver lockets and amulets would fetch a nice price at the stand.

speaker: Fralia
dialogue: Wonderful, dear. Thank you.

speaker: Erandur
dialogue: Everyone, please. I'm doing what I can to end these nightmares.

speaker: Erandur
dialogue: Wait... Veren... Thorek... you're alive!

speaker: Veren Duleri
dialogue: No thanks to you, Casimir.

speaker: Erandur
dialogue: I no longer use that name. I'm Erandur, Priest of Mara.

speaker: Veren Duleri
dialogue: You're a traitor. You left us to die and then ran before the Miasma took you.

speaker: Erandur
dialogue: No. I... I was scared. I wasn't ready to sleep.

speaker: Veren Duleri
dialogue: Enough of your lies! I can't allow you to destroy the Skull, Priest of Mara.

speaker: Erandur
dialogue: Then you leave me no choice!

speaker: Erandur
dialogue: Listen to your friend, Fruki. They are just dreams, my dear. I assure you that it is quite normal.

speaker: Irgnir
dialogue: It's the same dream over and over again. You think that's normal? It's evil I tell you!

speaker: Fruki
dialogue: Erandur, she has a point. You keep telling us no harm will follow these dreams, but they must be an omen.

speaker: Thoring
dialogue: Give him a chance to speak. He's trying to help us.

speaker: Erandur
dialogue: Everyone, please. I'm doing what I can to end these nightmares. In the meantime all I ask is you remain strong and put your trust in Lady Mara.

speaker: Irgnir
dialogue: I... I will. Thank you...

speaker: Erdi
dialogue: Are you my gallant hero? Have you come to whisk me away, to a life of adventure and romance?

speaker: Una
dialogue: I'm pleased when the palace is clean, I'm pleased when the beds are made on time, I'm pleased when Erdi isn't around. Most of those don't happen very often.

speaker: Any hireling
dialogue: Sure I'm a little green, but what I lack in experience, I make up for in courage.

speaker: Erik
dialogue: Thanks for the offer, Jouane, but I'm saving up for a new sword.

speaker: Erik
dialogue: I'm not saying it's my business, but I have to ask. Why are you so cruel to your little girls?

speaker: Erik
dialogue: You keep on like you are, you'll end up with two daughters who hate you.

speaker: Lemkil
dialogue: Hah! And what would a witless oaf like you know about raising children?

speaker: Erik
dialogue: Father, how old were you when you left home?

speaker: Mralki
dialogue: I know where this is going, son. As I've said many a time. the world is a dangerous place. You're much safer here at the farm, with me.

speaker: Erik
dialogue: But I don't want to be safe! I'm not afraid of the dangers out there. The only thing I'm afraid of is wasting my life on this farm.

speaker: Mralki
dialogue: Yes, that's your mother's side of the family talking. Just stay on for one more season, that's all I ask.

speaker: Mralki
dialogue: I heard you sneaking around downstairs last night. Were you trying to break into my chest again, son? I've told you to leave it alone.

speaker: Erik
dialogue: I just wanted to try on your old armor, from back when you were a soldier. I thought I might be old enough to wear it.

speaker: Mralki
dialogue: I've told you a hundred times, I lock that chest for a reason. I don't want you getting a head full of ideas about adventure and glory.

speaker: Erik
dialogue: I'm old enough to decide how to live my life, and I'd be honored to wear your armor, if you'd just let me. I'm strong enough to handle it.

speaker: Mralki
dialogue: Strong, yes, but how clever are you? I'll tell you what, if you can open the lock on my chest, you can have everything in it.

speaker: Erik
dialogue: I'll take your challenge, but if I win I get to start a new life as an adventurer, and with no objections from you.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: Half of the businesses in town owe me money, and I own most of the rest. I practically run Solitude already.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: There's a likely-looking filly. Even if she is an elf. You there! Serving girl! What's your name, dear?

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: No, no, that's not what I'm interested in right now. I just wanted to get a better look at you. I like what I see, my dear. And believe me, I don't say that to everyone. I'm very discriminating when it comes to the female form.

speaker: Brelas
dialogue: Um, thank you. Sir. Was there anything else I can do for you?

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: Oh... not at the moment. Maybe later. Don't go far.

speaker: Brelas
dialogue: Yes, sir.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: Hello, my dear. I got your message. Where shall we go?

speaker: Brelas
dialogue: What? I'm sorry, sir, but you must have misunderstood. I'm not permitted to leave the party.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: Oh, I don't think so. I think I understand perfectly. Don't worry, my dear, I will make any necessary excuses to your employer.

speaker: Brelas
dialogue: No, I'm sorry, but I can't go anywhere with you. I won't. Please, I must get back to my duties.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: Don't you dare walk away from me, you slut! Do you know who I am?

speaker: Brelas
dialogue: Please, sir, leave me alone!

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: Now you're going to be sorry you crossed me. Elenwen! This servant girl has been throwing herself at me in a most disgusting manner.

speaker: Elenwen
dialogue: Is that so, Erikur? And you with such delicate sensibilities. It must have been most upsetting.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: I demand that you have this wench removed from my presence at once!

speaker: Elenwen
dialogue: Well. Whatever the truth of it, I'm sure a few word with Master Rulindil will have a salutary effect. Take her downstairs.

speaker: Thalmor Soldier
dialogue: Yes, Madame Ambassador.

speaker: Brelas
dialogue: No! Mistress Elenwen, it's not true! I did nothing! Sir, you must tell her! You don't know what they'll do to me! Please!

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: Well, I'm glad that little unpleasantness is over.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: So. You think you can toy with me, is that it? No, my dear. I have my heart set on you, and I always get what I want.

speaker: Brelas
dialogue: I'm sorry, sir. I didn't mean to give you the wrong impression earlier. I meant no disrespect.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: Oh, don't worry. I'll let you make it up to me. Now, where can we go for a little privacy, hmm?

speaker: Brelas
dialogue: No, I'm sorry, but I can't go anywhere with you. I won't. Please, I must get back to my duties.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: Don't you dare walk away from me, you slut! Do you know who I am?

speaker: Brelas
dialogue: Please, sir, leave me alone!

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: Now you're going to be sorry you crossed me. Elenwen! This servant girl has been throwing herself at me in a most disgusting manner.

speaker: Elenwen
dialogue: Is that so, Erikur? And you with such delicate sensibilities. It must have been most upsetting.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: I demand that you have this wench removed from my presence at once!

speaker: Elenwen
dialogue: Well. Whatever the truth of it, I'm sure a few word with Master Rulindil will have a salutary effect. Take her downstairs.

speaker: Thalmor Soldier
dialogue: Yes, Madame Ambassador.

speaker: Brelas
dialogue: No! Mistress Elenwen, it's not true! I did nothing! Sir, you must tell her! You don't know what they'll do to me! Please!

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: Well, I'm glad that little unpleasantness is over.

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: As you know, Solitude's coffers are much depleted by the war efforts. Thane Erikur, you have a strong head for business. What do you suggest?

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: This is an unfortunate but unavoidable ebb in revenue. But as long as we continue to support the Empire, our sacrifices will be well rewarded.

speaker: Bryling
dialogue: Listen to you, speaking of sacrifice. You've never gone hungry a day in your life, Erikur!

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: And what would my impetuous Thane Bryling suggest, instead?

speaker: Bryling
dialogue: Simple. Let the Empire fight its own war, with its own funds, and without hijacking our supplies and soldiers. Let Haafingar rebuild.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: My lady... Surely you're not that naïve. Such foolishness would only leave us defenseless. The rebels would storm the palace in an afternoon.

speaker: Bryling
dialogue: The Stormcloaks only rebel because the Empire uses Skyrim as its personal larder. The more they take, the more support the rebels gain!

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: That is quite enough. Perhaps I will raise these issues when I have an audience with General Tullius.

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: Thane Bryling, what do you have to report about the state of Haafingar's defenses?

speaker: Bryling
dialogue: The news is the same as it's been for the rest of the war, your grace. Our borders are secure, but at the cost of the guards for our towns and roads.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: I don't see any reason why we'd need them. As long as those dogs stay outside of our borders, we're fine.

speaker: Bryling
dialogue: The Stormcloaks are far from the only threat to the hold. The roads are beset by bandits and beasts... and now there's even talk of bloody dragons.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: My dear Bryling. Barring any... fancy and folly... the good people of Haafingar are surely capable of dealing with the odd highwayman or stray dog.

speaker: Bryling
dialogue: Trouble on the roads and cities means less commerce. Less commerce means less money and more starving people. And that means more crime.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: Humph. That's only a problem for people who can't afford to hire their own security.

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: That may well be our only answer. I will empower my Steward to seek out capable individuals to secure Haafingar. Thank you, my Thanes.

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: Steward Falk, I have a task for you. I want to begin stockpiling food and water in the event we come under siege, and I would like you to oversee this work personally.

speaker: Falk
dialogue: A wise course of action, my Jarl. However, we have little food or water to spare.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: General Tullius will never allow that. He's ordered all surplus food to be given over for the war effort.

speaker: Falk
dialogue: General Tullius does not run this city, Thane Erikur. Or have you forgotten your oaths of fealty?

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: My apologies, Jarl Elisif. I was thinking only of the importance of the war effort.

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: There's no need for an apology, and you're right about the war. Perhaps this is a matter best discussed with the general in person.

speaker: Falk
dialogue: I will make the arrangements, my Jarl.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: I've heard the Empire plans to levy a tax on our trading ships. Falk, you've got to do something about this.

speaker: Falk
dialogue: General Tullius needs more money for the war effort. We need the funds to arm and provision more troops.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: Then let's increase the taxes on the farms and merchants. We can't afford to lose the loyalty of the ship captains.

speaker: Falk
dialogue: We know full well about your investment in shipping ventures, Erikur. I've also heard troubling rumors about dealings between you and the crew of that pirate ship, the Red Wave. Thankfully, Jarl Elisif cares far less about your lost profits than she does about winning the war!

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: The Jarl would be wise to remember that it is her Thanes―and my profits―that are paying for this war.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: Sister, how is my fortune coming along?

speaker: Gisli
dialogue: Profits continue to rise. The warehouse continues to bring in good revenues, and rent on your stores in the Well is acceptable.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: I'm afraid 'acceptable' just isn't acceptable anymore. I'm sure they can spare a few more coins in monthly rent.

speaker: Gisli
dialogue: Yes, brother. I'm sure they'll agree it's a fair price to pay in order to avoid interacting with you on a daily basis.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: Fair or not, they'll pay it, and that's all I need to care about. Bear that in mind, sister.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: That clumsy maid at the palace spilled wine on my best suit. Sister, I believe it's time for a replacement.

speaker: Gisli
dialogue: I can commission one from the Radiant Raiment. It won't be cheap, but if you want the best, they're the only choice.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: I swear, those scheming elves charge us twice what anyone else would pay.

speaker: Gisli
dialogue: Of course they do, brother. You keep raising their rent.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: Yes, I agree with you. Have you heard any news about the other parts of Skyrim?

speaker: Idgrod
dialogue: I heard those mages up in Winterhold have been trying to figure out how many dragons there are in Skyrim. They seem to think it's at least a dozen, but I'm sure they're exaggerating. They're probably trying to scare us into giving them more money and influence, so they can save us from the dragons threat.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: I hope they'll serve the roast venison with bittergreen sauce that we had at the last party. That was delicious.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: The Gray Quarter in Windhelm is little better than a slum. It's shameful that the dark elves are made to live that way.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: You speak truly. Have you heard any interesting rumors of late?

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Well, there might be nothing to it, but I've heard that the feud between the Gray-Manes and the Battle-Borns in Whiterun has grown ugly. Fralia Gray-Mane is convinced that the Battle-Borns have abducted one of her sons.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: Melaran, you lazy milk-drinker, have you finished studying the imports from Black Marsh?

speaker: Melaran
dialogue: Indeed I have, sir. Elven weapons for their armies, sir. Elven material, but poor workmanship, like most of what we get from them.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: Scary, thinking of those boots with an army of Elven weapons at their command. Let's be thankful they're half a world away, eh?

speaker: Melaran
dialogue: Even a fine weapon is only as good as its wielder, sir. But they should fetch a high price from the Imperial army.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: Right you are, elf! Or even from the rebels, if they've got enough money to make a competitive offer.

speaker: Melaran
dialogue: As always, lord, your loyalty is a shining example to us all.

speaker: Erith
dialogue: Have you met Torom? He's the best dog in the Reach.

speaker: Esbern
dialogue: You've done it... Just as the prophecy said... I knew you could do it... I believed in you, and yet... I still didn't think I'd live to see this day. Thank you. Thank you, Dragonborn. You've done a great service for us all.

speaker: Delphine
dialogue: There's still the matter of Paarthurnax. I'm not ungrateful for what you've done. Esbern speaks for both of us. But our oath as Blades binds us. Paarthurnax must die. There's no excuse now that Alduin is dead.

speaker: Esbern
dialogue: I'm afraid she's right. I'm deeply sorry this has to come between us. But just as Paarthurnax's later deeds does not expiate his crimes, your deeds do not allow us to ignore our duty. I hope you will return to us soon with the news that justice has finally been done. With both Alduin and Paarthurnax dead, a dark chapter in history will finally be closed.

speaker: Esbern
dialogue: Delphine! I... it's good to see you. It's been... a long time.

speaker: Delphine
dialogue: It's good to see you, too, Esbern. It's been too long, old friend. Too long. Well, then. You made it, safe and sound. Good. Come on, I have a place we can talk.

speaker: Delphine
dialogue: Orgnar, hold down the bar for a minute, will you?

speaker: Orgnar
dialogue: Yeah, sure.

speaker: Delphine
dialogue: Now then. I assume you know about...

speaker: Esbern
dialogue: Oh yes! Dragonborn! Indeed, yes. This changes everything, of course. There's no time to lose. We must locate... let me show you. I know I had it here, somewhere...

speaker: Delphine
dialogue: Esbern, what...

speaker: Esbern
dialogue: Give me... just a moment... Ah! Here it is. Come, let me show you. You see, right here. Sky Haven Temple, constructed around one of the main Akaviri military camps in the Reach, during their conquest of Skyrim.

speaker: Delphine
dialogue: Do {{Hide|you|To the Dragonborn}} know what he's talking about?

speaker: Esbern
dialogue: Shh! This is where they built Alduin's Wall, to set down in stone all their accumulated dragonlore. A hedge against the forgetfulness of centuries. A wise and foresighted policy, in the event. Despite the far-reaching fame of Alduin's Wall at the time - one of the wonders of the ancient world - its location was lost.

speaker: Delphine
dialogue: Esbern. What are you getting at?

speaker: Esbern
dialogue: You mean... you don't mean to say you haven't heard of Alduin's Wall? Either of you?

speaker: Delphine
dialogue: Let's pretend we haven't. What's Alduin's Wall and what does it have to do with stopping the dragons?

speaker: Esbern
dialogue: Alduin's Wall was where the ancient Blades recorded all they knew of Alduin and his return. Part history, part prophecy. Its location has been lost for centuries, but I've found it again. Not lost, you see, just forgotten. The Blades archives held so many secrets... I was only able to save a few scraps...

speaker: Delphine
dialogue: So you think that Alduin's Wall will tell us how to defeat Alduin?

speaker: Esbern
dialogue: Well, yes, but... there's no guarantee, of course.

speaker: Delphine
dialogue: Sky Haven Temple it is, then. I knew you'd have something for us, Esbern.

speaker: Delphine
dialogue: This looks promising.

speaker: Esbern
dialogue: Yes. Definitely early Akaviri stonework here.

speaker: Delphine
dialogue: We've got to get this bridge down. These pillars must have something to do with it.

speaker: Delphine
dialogue: Why are you stopping?

speaker: Esbern
dialogue: We should be careful here. See these symbols on the floor?

speaker: Esbern
dialogue: Be careful.

speaker: Delphine
dialogue: Looks safe now. Let's move.

speaker: Esbern
dialogue: Yes, yes! I think we must be close to the entrance.

speaker: Esbern
dialogue: Fascinating! Original Akaviri bas reliefs... almost entirely intact! Amazing... you can see how the Akaviri craftsmen were beginning to embrace the more flowing Nordic style...

speaker: Delphine
dialogue: We're here for Alduin's Wall, right, Esbern?

speaker: Esbern
dialogue: Yes, of course. We'll have more time to look around later, I suppose. Let's see what's up ahead.

speaker: Esbern
dialogue: Shor's bones! Here it is! Alduin's Wall... so well preserved... I've never seen a finer example of early second era Akaviri sculptural relief...

speaker: Delphine
dialogue: Esbern. We need information, not a lecture on art history.

speaker: Esbern
dialogue: Yes, yes. Let's see what we have... Look, here is Alduin! This panel goes back to the beginning of time, when Alduin and the Dragon Cult ruled over Skyrim. Here the humans rebel against their dragon overlords -- the legendary Dragon War. Alduin's defeat is the centerpiece of the Wall. You see, here he is falling from the Sky. The Nord Tongues -- masters of the Voice -- are arrayed against him.

speaker: Delphine
dialogue: So, does it show how they defeated him? Isn't that why we're here?

speaker: Delphine
dialogue: You mean they used a shout to defeat Alduin? You're sure?

speaker: Esbern
dialogue: Hmm? Oh, yes. Presumably something rather specific to dragons, or even Alduin himself. Remember, this is where they recorded all they knew of Alduin and his return.

speaker: Delphine
dialogue: So we're looking for a Shout, then. Damn it.

speaker: Delphine
dialogue: Well, I'm going to look around some more. See what the Blades left for us.

speaker: Esbern
dialogue: Yes... yes, that's an excellent idea. Who knows what lost treasures we might discover?

speaker: Etienne
dialogue: Stop. Please. I don't know anything else. Don't you think I'd have told you already?

speaker: Thalmor guard
dialogue: Silence. You know the rules. Do not speak unless spoken to. Master Rulindil will ask the questions.

speaker: Rulindil
dialogue: Let's begin again.

speaker: Etienne
dialogue: No...for pity's sake...I've already told you everything...

speaker: Rulindil
dialogue: You know the rules.

speaker: Etienne
dialogue: [Guard hits him] Nooooo!!!

speaker: Rulindil
dialogue: Start at the beginning, as usual. If you persist in this stubbornness I'll have...

speaker: Etienne
dialogue: No, wait! I was...just catching my breath...why wouldn't I tell you again? I don't even know anything...There's an old man...he lives in Riften. He could be this Esbern you're looking for. I don't know. He's old and seemed kind of crazy. That's all I know.

speaker: Rulindil
dialogue: And his name is...?

speaker: Etienne
dialogue: I don't know his name. Like I've already told you a hundred-- [guard hits him] Ahhh!

speaker: Rulindil
dialogue: You know the rules. Just answer the questions. And where is this nameless old man?

speaker: Etienne
dialogue: Like I said, I don't know. I've seen him down in the Ratway. Maybe he lives down there, but I don't know for sure.

speaker: Rulindil
dialogue: That will be all for now. I must say I continue to be disappointed in your lack of cooperation. I hope next time you will do better.

speaker: Etienne
dialogue: What else do you want from me? I've told you everything. Listen, If you let me go I can take you to Riften, show you where-- [guard hits him again] Ghaaa!!!

speaker: Thalmor guard
dialogue: Silence, prisoner!

speaker: Evette San
dialogue: Spiced wine for ya? It's a family recipe.

speaker: Evette
dialogue: I haven't known you to drink before, Ataf.

speaker: Ataf
dialogue: Viarmo is trying to get Elisif to allow the Burning of King Olaf. I don't want to look like I don't know how to drink in front of the other bards.

speaker: Evette
dialogue: A bottle of spiced wine for ya, Ataf?

speaker: Ataf
dialogue: No thank you. I'm still feeling sick from the festival.

speaker: Evette
dialogue: A bit of warming wine, Illdi? You know you can't resist.

speaker: Evette
dialogue: You and everyone else. Word is it may not happen this year though.

speaker: Evette
dialogue: Father, could you clean up the house a little while I'm away?

speaker: Evette
dialogue: I'm on my feet all day. Can you please do this one thing for me?

speaker: Octieve
dialogue: Sure, whatever.

speaker: Octieve
dialogue: Where've you been all day?

speaker: Evette
dialogue: At the market, father.

speaker: Octieve
dialogue: Well, did you bring back any mead?

speaker: Evette
dialogue: I barely make enough for us to eat as it is, father. You can't just drink it all away.

speaker: Octieve
dialogue: Humph. Some daughter you are.

speaker: Evette
dialogue: Of course. And I'm sure it's mostly for ceremonial purposes.

speaker: Silana
dialogue: It should be quite the affair. Nice to have something happy in the midst of the war.

speaker: Evette
dialogue: Vittoria is practically glowing.

speaker: Evette
dialogue: Spiced Wine for The Winking Skeever?

speaker: Evette
dialogue: Sure, Sorex. Just like you did the last one.

speaker: Sorex
dialogue: The last one was warm up.

speaker: Skuli
dialogue: Mama, where did papa go?

speaker: Eydis
dialogue: He's off fighting the war, dear. For the Stormcloaks.

speaker: Skuli
dialogue: Last time you said he was fighting for the Empire.

speaker: Eydis
dialogue: Yep. I'm sure he's doing well there.

speaker: Eydis
dialogue: Did you clean the linens, yet?

speaker: Skuli
dialogue: I did. Those mead stains are always tricky.

speaker: Faendal
dialogue: I don't like to brag, but I once took down a bear at three hundred yards. In a blizzard.

speaker: Faida
dialogue: Faida's the name. I keep the inn.

speaker: Faldrus
dialogue: I'm on a pilgrimage to the Shrine of Azura, the Goddess of Twilight. If you'll excuse me.

speaker: Faleen
dialogue: Very well, you may approach the Mournful Throne, but watch your words.

speaker: Igmund
dialogue: Raerek, how is The Reach faring against this Forsworn menace?

speaker: Raerek
dialogue: Things are bad, Igmund. Our forces are barely able to keep the Forsworn in check. Merchants are reporting the loss of more of their shipments.

speaker: Igmund
dialogue: This is why I say we take the fight to them. Gather the Legion and drive those blasted beasts out of the Reach for good.

speaker: Faleen
dialogue: And what do Legion soldiers know about the hills the Reach? And the caves that make up those hills? The Forsworn can hide and ambush every assault.

speaker: Raerek
dialogue: The safety of the city and our settlements must be our only concern, Igmund. The rest of the Reach is on its own.

speaker: Igmund
dialogue: Cowards, the both of you. My father would not sit idly back and wait while evil men take over his lands. We're done discussing this for now.

speaker: Falion
dialogue: When you have a gem and have filled it return to me and I will perform the ritual. I will bring life to your dead body, vampire.

speaker: Falion
dialogue: Have you been working on your concentration?

speaker: Agni
dialogue: Yes sir, I have.

speaker: Falion
dialogue: Good. Concentration is paramount when dealing with magical forces.

speaker: Falion
dialogue: Because an unfocused mind will almost certainly be obliterated. Destroyed by the forces you attempt to control and yield.

speaker: Falion
dialogue: Have no fear. I believe it is within you to excel in your studies. But you must learn to concentrate!

speaker: Agni
dialogue: Yes, sir.

speaker: Agni
dialogue: When I grow up, will I go to the College in Winterhold?

speaker: Falion
dialogue: No, I don't think that will be necessary.

speaker: Agni
dialogue: But I'm learning about magic, and that's what they do there. Shouldn't I go?

speaker: Falion
dialogue: The College is not the only place to learn about magic.

speaker: Agni
dialogue: But you went there, didn't you? Isn't that where you learned?

speaker: Falion
dialogue: I was there only for a short time. Much of what I have learned has been on my own. And I will teach you. You have no reason to go there.

speaker: Falion
dialogue: That is enough.

speaker: Agni
dialogue: I had a bad dream again last night.

speaker: Agni
dialogue: I dreamt that you went away. You made monsters.

speaker: Falion
dialogue: It's just a dream, child. Nothing more.

speaker: Agni
dialogue: It was scary. It was like it was real!

speaker: Falion
dialogue: Hush now. Think no more of it.

speaker: Agni
dialogue: Is it true that you kill deer and eat their hearts?

speaker: Falion
dialogue: What? Where did you hear such a thing?

speaker: Agni
dialogue: I don't know. Someone in town said it.

speaker: Falion
dialogue: It's not true, I assure you.

speaker: Falion
dialogue: Don't believe everything you hear, child.

speaker: Falk Firebeard
dialogue: The Jarl is not to be disturbed with common affairs of court. You direct those concerns to me.

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: Go. Away. Please!

speaker: Falk
dialogue: I've brought a friend. Someone who can help. A bodyguard. To protect you.

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: I thought you didn't believe I was in danger!

speaker: Falk
dialogue: It doesn't really matter what I believe, now does it? I've brought you someone who can protect you. That's what you want, isn't it?

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: (Sounds of unlocking and unbarring a door)<!--sic--> Well, what are you waiting for?!

speaker: Falk
dialogue: Speak your mind, Bryling. You're among friends here.

speaker: Bryling
dialogue: You know that I support the Empire, as we all do. However, I fear General Tullius is underestimating the Stormcloaks. Too often the general has lost good soldiers because he did not take Ulfric and his men seriously. If this continues, and the worst comes to pass, Solitude will pay the price. The Empire is headquartered here, after all.

speaker: Falk
dialogue: We don't have the luxury of hanging back to see who wins before choosing our friends, Bryling. You know this. And besides, no Nord with a shred of honor would consider it. We're no cowards. Have faith, Bryling. When this war is over and Ulfric is dead, you'll see that you were jumping at shadows, and nothing more.

speaker: Bryling
dialogue: Falk, you shouldn't have come. You know what'd happen if people found out about us.

speaker: Falk
dialogue: I know, my lady. I just needed to see you outside of court, away from all of the politics.

speaker: Bryling
dialogue: I'm serious. If Erikur knew about us, he'd force you to resign from your position. And without you, he'd have the Jarl bent around his little finger.

speaker: Falk
dialogue: You're right, of course. But when this war is over, I'll gladly resign and we can stop sneaking around like this.

speaker: Bryling
dialogue: One more reason to pray for the fighting to end then, my love.

speaker: Falk
dialogue: It's nearly time to collect taxes on your properties here in the city, Bryling. We'll need to visit each home for an assessment.

speaker: Bryling
dialogue: Is it that time again already? Very well, let's meet this evening and make the arrangements.

speaker: Sybille
dialogue: Oh, well done. Very subtle.

speaker: Bryling
dialogue: I beg your pardon?

speaker: Sybille
dialogue: Oh, I'm sorry, did I imply that you'd be meeting for purposes other than court business? You must forgive me.

speaker: Falk
dialogue: Hold your tongue, wizard, or you're likely to lose it.

speaker: Sybille
dialogue: I should very much like to see you try it, my dear steward.

speaker: Bryling
dialogue: Stop it, both of you. You're acting like children.

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: Steward, when is my appointment to meet with General Tullius? There are some issues we must speak about.

speaker: Falk
dialogue: I'm afraid he's had to reschedule, my grace. By all accounts, waging war takes his every moment.

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: Again? He can't simply cancel an appointment with the Jarl! He serves in my capital city!

speaker: Falk
dialogue: I'm afraid he can. His authority comes from the emperor, whom you also serve, technically.

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: He uses all of Haafingar's resources, and doesn't answer to me in the slightest? This hardly seems fair.

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: Steward, I have an idea that might help to bolster the morale of our people in this difficult time. I think we shall have a grand parade, and let General Tullius march his troops from the Blue Palace to Castle Dour in all their finery.

speaker: Falk
dialogue: What a... fine idea, my Jarl. However, I would suggest we wait until the war has ended. After all, the General needs his soldiers out in the field, fighting battles against the Stormcloaks.

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: Oh, very well. I can see there's no changing your stubborn Nord minds. But when this war is won, I will have my parade!

speaker: Falk
dialogue: Yes, my Jarl.

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: Steward Falk, I have a task for you. I want to begin stockpiling food and water in the event we come under siege, and I would like you to oversee this work personally.

speaker: Falk
dialogue: A wise course of action, my Jarl. However, we have little food or water to spare.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: General Tullius will never allow that. He's ordered all surplus food to be given over for the war effort.

speaker: Falk
dialogue: General Tullius does not run this city, Thane Erikur. Or have you forgotten your oaths of fealty?

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: My apologies, Jarl Elisif. I was thinking only of the importance of the war effort.

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: There's no need for an apology, and you're right about the war. Perhaps this is a matter best discussed with the general in person.

speaker: Falk
dialogue: I will make the arrangements, my Jarl.

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: Then we will immediately send out a legion to scour the cave and secure the town. Haafingar's people will always be safe under my rule.

speaker: Varnius
dialogue: Th... thank you, my Jarl. Thank you.

speaker: Falk
dialogue: Perhaps a more... tempered reaction... might be called for?

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: Oh. Yes, of course you are right. Falk, tell Captain Aldis I said to assign a few extra soldiers to Dragon Bridge.

speaker: Varnius
dialogue: Thank you, Jarl Elisif. But about the cave...

speaker: Falk
dialogue: I will have someone take care of the cave as well Varnius, you can rest easy. You're dismissed.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: I've heard the Empire plans to levy a tax on our trading ships. Falk, you've got to do something about this.

speaker: Falk
dialogue: General Tullius needs more money for the war effort. We need the funds to arm and provision more troops.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: Then let's increase the taxes on the farms and merchants. We can't afford to lose the loyalty of the ship captains.

speaker: Falk
dialogue: We know full well about your investment in shipping ventures, Erikur. I've also heard troubling rumors about dealings between you and the crew of that pirate ship, the Red Wave. Thankfully, Jarl Elisif cares far less about your lost profits than she does about winning the war!

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: The Jarl would be wise to remember that it is her Thanes―and my profits―that are paying for this war.

speaker: Sybille
dialogue: Steward, I will need the following reagents for my studies. Please see to them.

speaker: Falk
dialogue: Miss Stentor, these are quite expensive. I trust you know how limited the Hold's funds are at this time?

speaker: Sybille
dialogue: Yes, and I'm also aware of how necessary my divinations and wards have been in the city's defense. My experiments are all I ask for in return.

speaker: Falk
dialogue: Very well. But I suspect her grace will not be pleased.

speaker: Sybille
dialogue: And? I've seen Jarls come and go. This one only became Jarl because her husband died. She'll be replaced in a matter of months.

speaker: Falk
dialogue: Miss Stentor, watch your tongue in the Jarl's court!

speaker: Sybille
dialogue: On threat of what, exactly? This city wouldn't run without me! Now if you'll excuse me, my work awaits.

speaker: Faralda
dialogue: Tolfdir as Master Wizard. Certainly didn't anticipate that.

speaker: Faralda
dialogue: Come on, Arniel. Let's go.

speaker: Arniel
dialogue: Do we have to? They'd never lift a finger to help us.

speaker: Faralda
dialogue: Arniel, stay on your guard. We can't let harm come to these people.

speaker: Farengar Secret-Fire
dialogue: One sure mark of a fool is to dismiss anything that falls outside his experience as being impossible.

speaker: Farengar
dialogue: You see? The terminology is clearly First Era or even earlier. I'm convinced this is a copy of a much older text. Perhaps dating to just after the Dragon War. If so, I could use this to cross-reference the names with other later texts.

speaker: Delphine
dialogue: Good. I'm glad you're making progress. My employers are anxious to have some tangible answers.

speaker: Farengar
dialogue: Oh, have no fear. The Jarl himself has finally taken an interest, so I'm now able to devote most of my time to this research.

speaker: Delphine
dialogue: Time is running, Farengar, don't forget. This isn't some theoretical question. Dragons have come back.

speaker: Farengar
dialogue: Yes, yes. Don't worry. Although the chance to see a living dragon up close would be tremendously valuable... Now, let me show you something else I found... very intriguing... I think your employers may be interested as well...

speaker: Farengar
dialogue: Hmm? Ah, yes, the Jarl's protege! Back from Bleak Falls Barrow? You didn't die, it seems. Ah! The Dragonstone of Bleak Falls Barrow! Seems you are a cut above the usual brutes the Jarl sends my way. My... associate here will be pleased to see your handiwork. She discovered its location, by means she has so far declined to share with me.

speaker: Farengar
dialogue: So your information was correct after all. And we have our friend here to thank for recovering it for us.

speaker: Delphine
dialogue: {{Hide|You|Referring to the Dragonborn}} went into Bleak Falls Barrow and got that? Nice work. Just send me a copy when you've deciphered it.

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: Farengar! Farengar, you need to come at once. A dragon's been sighted nearby. {{Hide|You|Referring to the Dragonborn}} should come, too.

speaker: Farengar
dialogue: A dragon! How exciting! Where was it seen? What was it doing?

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: I'd take this a bit more seriously if I were you. If a dragon decides to attack Whiterun, I don't know if we can stop it. Let's go.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: So, Irileth tells me you came from the western watchtower?

speaker: Whiterun Guard
dialogue: Yes, my lord.

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: Tell him what you told me. About the dragon.

speaker: Whiterun Guard
dialogue: Uh... that's right. We saw it coming from the south. It was fast... faster than anything I've ever seen.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: What did it do? Is it attacking the watchtower?

speaker: Whiterun Guard
dialogue: No, my lord. It was just circling overhead when I left. I never ran so fast in my life... I thought it would come after me for sure.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Good work, son. We'll take it from here. Head down to the barracks for some food and rest. You've earned it. Irileth, you'd better gather some guardsmen and get down there.

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: I've already ordered my men to muster near the main gate.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Good. Don't fail me.

speaker: Farengar
dialogue: I should come along. I would very much like to see this dragon.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: No. I can't afford to risk both of you. I need you here working on ways to defend the city against these dragons.

speaker: Farengar
dialogue: As you command.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: One last thing, Irileth. This isn't a death or glory mission. I need to know what we're dealing with.

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: Don't worry, my lord. I'm the very soul of caution.

speaker: Farengar
dialogue: Incredible! Uh... sir, you have no idea how long I have waited for such an opportunity! I would be most appreciative if you would permit me to perform some, ah, tests on you. Purely in the interests of the advancement of knowledge.

speaker: Odahviing
dialogue: Begone, mage. Do not test my promise to the Dovahkiin.

speaker: Farengar
dialogue: I assure you, you will not even notice me. Most of them are hardly painful at all to a large dragon such as yourself.

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: Farengar, very bad idea. Even for you.

speaker: Farengar
dialogue: Surely you won't miss a few scales... or a small amount of blood...

speaker: Odahviing
dialogue: Joor mey! What are you doing back there? Yol... Toor...Shul!

speaker: Jarl Balgruuf the Greater
dialogue: Farengar! Enough, fool!

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: Skjor says I have the strength of Ysgramor, and my brother has his smarts.

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: I told you, this is the whelp that Vilkas mentioned.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: Ah, yes. I heard you gave him quite a thrashing.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: Did you call me?

speaker: Aela
dialogue: Of course we did, icebrain. Show this newblood where the rest of the whelps sleep.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: New blood? Oh, hello. I'm Farkas. Come, follow me.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: Brothers and sisters of the Circle, today we welcome a new soul into our mortal fold. This {{hide|man|woman}} has endured, has challenged, and has shown {{hide|his|her}} valor. Who will speak for {{hide|him|her}}?

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: I stand witness to the courage of the soul before us.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: Would you raise your shield in {{hide|his|her}} defense?

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: I would stand at {{hide|his|her}} back, that the world might never overtake us.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: And would you raise your sword in {{hide|his|her}} honor?

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: It stands ready to meet the blood of {{hide|his|her}} foes.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: And would you raise a mug in {{hide|his|her}} name?

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: I would lead the song of triumph as our mead hall reveled in {{hide|his|her}} stories.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: Then the judgement of this Circle is complete. {{hide|His|Her}} heart beats with fury and courage that have united the Companions since the days of the distant green summers. Let it beat with ours, that the mountains may echo and our enemies may tremble at the call.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: It shall be so.

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: It shall be so.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: It shall be so.

speaker: Eorlund
dialogue: Who will start?

speaker: Aela
dialogue: I'll do it. Before the ancient flame... We grieve.

speaker: Eorlund
dialogue: We grieve.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: We grieve.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: We grieve.

speaker: Eorlund
dialogue: At this loss... We weep.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: We weep.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: We weep.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: We weep.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: For the fallen... We shout.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: We shout.

speaker: Eorlund
dialogue: We shout.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: We shout.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: And for ourselves... We take our leave.

speaker: Eorlund
dialogue: We take our leave.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: We take our leave.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: We take our leave.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: His spirit is departed. Members of the Circle, let us withdraw to the Underforge, to grieve our last together.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: The old man had one wish before he died. And he didn't get it. It's as simple as that.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: Being moon-born is not so much of a curse as you might think, Vilkas.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: That's fine for you. But he wanted to be clean. He wanted to meet Ysgramor and know the glories of Sovngarde. But all that was taken from him.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: And you avenged him.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: Kodlak did not care for vengeance.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: No, Farkas, he didn't. And that's not what this is about. We should be honoring Kodlak, no matter our own thoughts on the blood.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: You're right. It's what he wanted, and he deserved to have it.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: Kodlak used to speak of a way to cleanse his soul, even in death. You know the legends of the Tomb of Ysgramor.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: There the souls of Harbingers will heed the call of northern steel. We can't even enter the tomb without Wuuthrad, and it's in pieces, like it has been for a thousand years.

speaker: Eorlund
dialogue: And dragons were just stories. And the elves once ruled Skyrim. Just because something is, doesn't mean it must be. The blade is a weapon. A tool. Tools are meant to be broken. And repaired.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: Is that? Did you repair the blade?

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: Tiny blades don't hurt enough. A sword needs weight.

speaker: Athis
dialogue: But ten little cuts...

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: All I need is one to cut you in half.

speaker: Athis
dialogue: [nervous gulp] Well, when you put it that way...

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: You only use the little swords.

speaker: Athis
dialogue: It's called a shortsword, you oaf. It's quicker. Sharper. And it can cut through a whale like a razor.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: But whales eat razorfish.

speaker: Athis
dialogue: And they always come to regret it.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: Relax, new blood.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: Fighting people is different. Smarter.

speaker: Torvar
dialogue: Some of 'em, anyway.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: Time to train.

speaker: Torvar
dialogue: Enough with the training, I want to go fight something.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: No fighting, not just yet. Not 'till Skjor says so. You train now.

speaker: Torvar
dialogue: Easy for you to say. You get to fight.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: But before I fought, I had to train.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: Some are too happy to fight. Blood runs hot.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: I remember when you were the same way. The more they train, the more they'll cool down.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: I hope so.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: Just have them focus on the calm in the battle. Control the rage, don't let it control you.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: What weapon do you like, Harbinger?

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: When I was young, I favored huge swords, much like you. Hard to lift these days, but I still enjoy the heft of a good hammer.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: Big swords should always beat little swords.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: Brave hearts beat lesser ones. That's the decider.

speaker: Faryl Atheron
dialogue: Farm work is hard work. It's good to relax when I can, but I still have to listen to my brothers harping about 'injustices'.

speaker: Bolfrida
dialogue: Now, I've been reading about the best ways to grow corn in permafrost...

speaker: Faryl
dialogue: I keep telling you, without a warming enchantment, it will never grow past your ankles.

speaker: Bolfrida
dialogue: Right, but if you plow the soil with fire salts...

speaker: Faryl
dialogue: Then you've salted it and nothing will grow at all. Genius.

speaker: Bolfrida
dialogue: Oh dear, I hadn't thought of that.

speaker: Faryl
dialogue: I don't think we're going to get those potatoes to come in.

speaker: Bolfrida
dialogue: Well of course, not with an attitude like that!

speaker: Faryl
dialogue: The ground is practically frozen. We can't dig down far enough.

speaker: Bolfrida
dialogue: Come on, we just need a little elbow grease.

speaker: Bolfrida
dialogue: I'll bet this is better than trying to grow something in Morrowind, though, isn't it?

speaker: Faryl
dialogue: Firstly, I've never even seen Morrowind. Secondly, in volcanic soil the plants practically grow themselves.

speaker: Bolfrida
dialogue: Oh, my, I hadn't thought of that.

speaker: Faryl
dialogue: There are places in the world that aren't wrapped in ice, you know.

speaker: Fastred
dialogue: I wish I could go with you...

speaker: Felldir the Old
dialogue: Alduin escaped us long ago. Today we take our well-tempered revenge.

speaker: Hakon
dialogue: Gormlaith! We're running out of time! The battle...

speaker: Dragon
dialogue: Daar sul thur se Alduin vakrii. Today Alduin's lordship will be restored. But I honor your courage. Krif voth ahkrin. Die now, in vain.

speaker: Hakon
dialogue: For Skyrim!

speaker: Gormlaith
dialogue: Hyah! Know that Gormlaith sent you down to death! Hakon! A glorious day, is it not?

speaker: Hakon
dialogue: Have you no thought beyond the blooding of your blade?

speaker: Gormlaith
dialogue: What else is there?

speaker: Hakon
dialogue: The battle below goes ill. If Alduin does not rise to our challenge, I fear all may be lost.

speaker: Gormlaith
dialogue: You worry too much, brother. Victory will be ours.

speaker: Hakon
dialogue: Why does Alduin hang back? We've staked everything on this plan of yours, old man.

speaker: Felldir
dialogue: He will come. He cannot ignore our defiance. And why should he fear us, even now?

speaker: Gormlaith
dialogue: We've bloodied him well. Four of his kin have fallen to my blade alone this day.

speaker: Felldir
dialogue: But none have yet stood against Alduin himself. Galthor, Sorri, Birkir...

speaker: Gormlaith
dialogue: They did not have Dragonrend. Once we bring him down, I promise I will have his head.

speaker: Felldir
dialogue: You do not understand. Alduin cannot be slain like a lesser dragon. He is beyond our strength. Which is why I brought the Elder Scroll.

speaker: Hakon
dialogue: Felldir! We agreed not to use it!

speaker: Felldir
dialogue: I never agreed. And if you are right, I will not need it.

speaker: Hakon
dialogue: No. We will deal with Alduin ourselves, here and now.

speaker: Gormlaith
dialogue: We shall see soon enough. Alduin approaches!

speaker: Hakon
dialogue: So be it.

speaker: Alduin
dialogue: Meyye! Tahrodiis aanne! Him hinde pah liiv! Zu'u hin daan!

speaker: Gormlaith
dialogue: Let those that watch from Sovngarde envy us this day! Joor... Zah...Frul!

speaker: Alduin
dialogue: Nivahriin joorre! What have you done? What twisted Words have you created?! Tahrodiis Paarthurnax! My teeth to his neck! But first... dir ko maar. You will die in terror, knowing your final fate... To feed my power when I come for you in Sovngarde!

speaker: Gormlaith
dialogue: If I die today, it will not be in terror! You feel fear for the first time, worm. I see it in your eyes.

speaker: Felldir
dialogue: Fo... Krah Diin!

speaker: Gormlaith
dialogue: Skyrim will be free!

speaker: Hakon
dialogue: No, damn you! It's no use! Use the Scroll, Felldir! Now!

speaker: Felldir
dialogue: Hold, Alduin on the Wing! Sister Hawk, grant us your sacred breath to make this contract heard! Begone, World-Eater! By words with older bones than your own we break your perch on this age and send you out! You are banished! Alduin, we shout you out from all our endings unto the last!

speaker: Felldir
dialogue: You are banished!

speaker: Hakon
dialogue: It worked... you did it...

speaker: Felldir
dialogue: Yes, the World-Eater is gone... may the spirits have mercy on our souls.

speaker: Gormlaith
dialogue: At long last! Alduin's doom is now ours to seal - just speak the word and with high hearths we'll hasten forth to smite the worm wherever he lurks.

speaker: Felldir
dialogue: Hold, comrades - let us counsel take before battle is blindly joined. Alduin's mist is more than a snare - its shadowy gloom is his shield and cloak. But with four Voices joined, our valor combined, we can blast the mist and bring him to battle.

speaker: Hakon
dialogue: Felldir speaks wisdom - the World-Eater, coward, fears you, Dragonborn. We must drive away his mist, Shouting together, and then unsheathe our blades in desperate battle with our black-winged foe.

speaker: Fenrig
dialogue: It doesn't matter. I'm here. We're together now. And we will be forever.

speaker: Festus Krex
dialogue: Well, you know the old saying. When life gives you lemons...

speaker: Arnbjorn
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Veezara
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha! Again! Again! Do the part where he tries to buy you some candy.

speaker: Gabriella
dialogue: Oh Babette, but you are so wicked.

speaker: Nazir
dialogue: What about you, Festus? How did that last contract turn out?

speaker: Arnbjorn
dialogue: Oh, yes, please, old man. Regale us with your tales of wizardry...

speaker: Gabriella
dialogue: And what of your latest, Arnbjorn. Something about a Khajiit? Merchant was it?

speaker: Babette
dialogue: Oh, a big doggy chasing a little kitty! How adorable!

speaker: Nazir
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Festus
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Veezara
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Arnbjorn
dialogue: I am not adorable, it was not funny, and he wasn't a merchant. He was a Khajiit monk, a master of the Whispering Fang style. But now he's dead... and I have a new loincloth.

speaker: Nazir
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Festus
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Veezara
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Babette
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Veezara
dialogue: Tell me, brother. Are the stories true?

speaker: Festus Krex
dialogue: You must be talking about the caravan job...

speaker: Veezara
dialogue: You infiltrated the position, eliminated the target, and made it look like an accident. Impressive. I'd say you earned your bonus on that one!

speaker: Festus Krex
dialogue: What? You think me too old, too feeble? There is more knowledge in me than in two of you pups together. And knowledge... knowledge is my weapon.

speaker: Cicero
dialogue: But the Night Mother is mother to all! It is her voice we follow! Her will! Would you dare risk disobedience? And surely... punishment?

speaker: Festus Krex
dialogue: Oh, be quiet you great lumbering lapdog. The man has had a long journey. You can at least be civil. Mister Cicero, I for one am delighted you and the Night Mother have arrived. Your presence here signals a welcome return to tradition.

speaker: Cicero
dialogue: Oh, what a kind and wise wizard you are. Sure to earn our Lady's favor.

speaker: Astrid
dialogue: You and the Night Mother are of course welcome here, Cicero. And you will be afforded the respect deserving of your position as Keeper. Understood... husband?

speaker: Cicero
dialogue: Oh, yes yes yes! Thank you, thank you, thank you!

speaker: Astrid
dialogue: But make no mistake. I am the leader of this Sanctuary. My word is law. Are we clear on that point?

speaker: Cicero
dialogue: Oh yes, mistress. Perfectly! You're the boss.

speaker: Babette
dialogue: Just try to relax, Veezara. Let the elixir do its work. You'll feel better, shortly.

speaker: Veezara
dialogue: Achh... Thank you, dear. You are most kind. The jester's cut feels as bad as it looks, I'm afraid.

speaker: Astrid
dialogue: Damn it, this never should have happened! We knew better. We knew better, and still we let our guards down. Agh!

speaker: Festus Krex
dialogue: It's true, I'm afraid, Cicero was a little whirlwind, slashing this way and all that. It would have been funny, if he weren't trying to murder us all.

speaker: Veezara
dialogue: Bested by a fool. Who's the fool now, hmm?

speaker: Babette
dialogue: Hush, Veezara. You were very brave. Astrid may well be dead if not for you.

speaker: Astrid
dialogue: She's right. I'll be forever in your debt, dearest brother. Now be quiet. Just... just rest.

speaker: Fianna
dialogue: Ain't nobody high and mighty in these halls, exceptin' the Jarl. And don't you forget!

speaker: Fihada
dialogue: True, I may look the part of a dashing swordsman, but I prefer the art of wit to that of warfare.

speaker: Fihada
dialogue: How's it coming there, Jawanan?

speaker: Fihada
dialogue: Slow's the only way to do it! Work too hard and you'll warp the wood.

speaker: Jawanan
dialogue: Fihada, where did you learn how to make bows so well?

speaker: Fihada
dialogue: The same place I learned my charm and quick wits; I used to be an Imperial ranger, my boy!

speaker: Jawanan
dialogue: Wish I could learn some of that charm. I'm just good with bows, not people.

speaker: Fihada
dialogue: You'd make a better Imperial ranger than me. I may have charmed the locals, but my fellow soldiers hated my waggling tongue.

speaker: Grogmar
dialogue: I've been cracking rock ever since I've been able to hold a pickaxe and I'm telling you, this mine is drying up.

speaker: Filnjar
dialogue: And I'm telling you, you're wrong.

speaker: Grogmar
dialogue: What makes you so sure? What if I'm right?

speaker: Filnjar
dialogue: I know there's ore still in there, I can smell it. You think you're right, you can pack up and leave any time you like.

speaker: Odfel
dialogue: You think living with Grogmar is easy? Did you see how he lives?

speaker: Filnjar
dialogue: You two will just have to learn how to get along until we can build you another house.

speaker: Odfel
dialogue: At this rate that'll never happen.

speaker: Filnjar
dialogue: Quit your bellyaching. We've all got our problems.

speaker: Fisherman
dialogue: It's not like my poaching is hurting anyone. The Jarl can hardly eat every deer now can he?

speaker: Fjori
dialogue: Take {{Hide|this|Referring to the Ghostblade.}} with our gratitude.

speaker: Fjotra
dialogue: Please, let's hurry to the Temple before the Forsworn find me again.

speaker: Enmon
dialogue: Fjotra, dear. Did they hurt you?

speaker: Fjotra
dialogue: Of course not. My spirit remains strong.

speaker: Enmon
dialogue: My little girl. Always strong. Do you know where you have to go?

speaker: Fjotra
dialogue: I'm to go to the temple in Markarth. I... I'll have to leave you and mother.

speaker: Fjotra
dialogue: Of course.

speaker: Frabbi
dialogue: Unlike my husband Kleppr, I watch after our guests.

speaker: Frabbi
dialogue: Kleppr, you idiot! Can't you do anything right?

speaker: Kleppr
dialogue: What? What did I do this time? I was just standing here.

speaker: Frabbi
dialogue: You were just standing there when you were supposed to be serving drinks to our customers!

speaker: Kleppr
dialogue: Shouldn't you be helping me then, wife of mine? Sharing my problems? Being my better half?

speaker: Frabbi
dialogue: I am your better half. And your better half is telling you to stop being an idiot and serve the customers their drinks!

speaker: Frabbi
dialogue: All the wood furniture in the inn is rotten to the core. Do you know why that is, Kleppr?

speaker: Kleppr
dialogue: I don't know. I suppose you're going to tell me?

speaker: Frabbi
dialogue: Its rotten because the wood is cheap and soaked with ale! Now we'll have to replace all the furniture before bugs set in.

speaker: Kleppr
dialogue: Don't worry, my love. Just show the bugs your adoring face, and they'll scurry away in complete fear in no time.

speaker: Frabbi
dialogue: You're an idiot, Kleppr. Why did I ever marry you?

speaker: Kleppr
dialogue: Not a day goes by I don't ask myself that same question, my dear.

speaker: Kleppr
dialogue: Frabbi, my dear loving wife, would you please clean out the guest rooms?

speaker: Frabbi
dialogue: Clean the rooms yourself, Kleppr. Its not like you do anything important around here.

speaker: Kleppr
dialogue: No, just check in the guests and manage the coin and keep a roof over your head. No, nothing important.

speaker: Fralia Gray-Mane
dialogue: Come see my collection of Gray-Mane's finest trinkets! You'll not find their like in all Tamriel!

speaker: Fralia
dialogue: Lillith―always a pleasure. Just browsing, or were you looking for something particular?

speaker: Lillith
dialogue: Funny you should ask. I'm in the market for a new locket. Something in polished silver, maybe. Big enough to hold, say, a folded-up letter?

speaker: Fralia
dialogue: Ahhh, I see. I think I know just what you need. I don't have anything like that here now, but my Eorlund―he can make you one right quick. When I get home, I'll have him start on it right away. Come back to pick it up in, oh... three days?

speaker: Lillith
dialogue: Perfect, my dear. Absolutely perfect. I'll see you then.

speaker: Fralia
dialogue: Eorlund, dearest, are you hungry? Would you like me to fix you something?

speaker: Fralia
dialogue: A venison pie, maybe? With a nice cup of mulled mead?

speaker: Fralia
dialogue: When will you be makin' some more jewelry, love? Some silver lockets and amulets would fetch a nice price at the stand.

speaker: Fralia
dialogue: Wonderful, dear. Thank you.

speaker: Fralia
dialogue: Nothing? And what of my son, hmm? What of Thorald? Is he nothing? So don't talk to me about suffering!

speaker: Fralia
dialogue: I will never accept his death! My son still lives. I feel it in my heart. So tell me, Battle-Borns, where is he? Where are you holding my Thorald?

speaker: Idolaf
dialogue: Come on, father. There's nothing more to be said here.

speaker: Fralia
dialogue: Welcome to our home.

speaker: Avulstein
dialogue: We can't trust anyone! Who knows what they'll do if they find me here.

speaker: Fralia
dialogue: I can't take anymore of this. No weapons, please. Let's just talk.

speaker: Avulstein
dialogue: All right, mother.

speaker: Fralia
dialogue: Plenty of people here that need Eorlund's craftsmanship, my dear. We've never had any reason to deal with those caravans of theirs.

speaker: Grelod
dialogue: Those who shirk their duties will get an extra beating. Do I make myself clear?

speaker: Samuel
dialogue: Yes, Grelod.

speaker: Runa
dialogue: Yes, Grelod.

speaker: Hroar
dialogue: Yes, Grelod.

speaker: Francois
dialogue: Yes, Grelod.

speaker: Grelod
dialogue: And one more thing! I will hear no more talk of adoptions! None of you riff-raff is getting adopted. Nobody needs you, nobody wants you. That, my darlings, is why you're here. Why you'll always be here, until you come of age and get thrown into that wide, horrible world. Now, what do you all say?

speaker: Samuel
dialogue: We love you, Grelod. Thank you for your kindness.

speaker: Runa
dialogue: We love you, Grelod. Thank you for your kindness.

speaker: Hroar
dialogue: We love you, Grelod. Thank you for your kindness.

speaker: Francois
dialogue: We love you, Grelod. Thank you for your kindness.

speaker: Grelod
dialogue: That's better. Now scurry off, my little guttersnipes.

speaker: Freir
dialogue: Blessings of the Eight Divines upon you. How may I help?

speaker: Rorlund
dialogue: Ah, that must be it. So many of the men are serving in battle. I shall pray to Stendarr that they return victorious.

speaker: Frida
dialogue: Pfft. I'm the oldest woman in Dawnstar. Was here when the Skald the Elder was Skald the younger.

speaker: Fridrika
dialogue: My family's weathered its share of problems, but we don't dwell on the past.

speaker: Frodnar
dialogue: You're new around here, so I'll go easy on ya. But don't get on my bad side.

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: Mara's Mercy, its good to see you! But is it safe for you to be here?

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: We had heard that Ulfric had been captured...

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Gerdur... I'm fine. At least now I am.

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: Are you hurt? What's happened? [looks at player] And who's this? One of your comrades?

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Not a comrade yet...but a friend. I owe him/her my life, in fact. Is there somewhere we can talk? There's no telling when the news from Helgen will reach the Imperials...

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: Helgen? Has something happened...? You're right. Follow me. Hod! Come here a minute. I need your help with something.

speaker: Hod
dialogue: What is it, woman? Sven drunk on the job again?

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: Hod. Just come here.

speaker: Hod
dialogue: Ralof! What are you doing here? Ah...I'll be right down!

speaker: Frodnar
dialogue: Uncle Ralof! Can I see your axe? How many Imperials have you killed? Do you really know Ulfric Stormcloak?

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: Hush, Frodnar. This is no time for your games. Go and watch the south road. Find us if you see any Imperial soldiers coming.

speaker: Frodnar
dialogue: Aw, mama, I want to stay and talk with uncle Ralof!

speaker: Hod
dialogue: Mind your mother, boy.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Look at you, almost a grown man! Won't be long before you'll be joining the fight yourself!

speaker: Frodnar
dialogue: That's right! Don't worry uncle Ralof, I won't let those soldiers sneak up on you!

speaker: Dorthe
dialogue: Wait, so...a costume? You're not serious...

speaker: Frodnar
dialogue: Sure I am! We get some furs and tree branches and paint them white and tie them to Stump. Instant Frostbite Spider!

speaker: Dorthe
dialogue: Frodnar, nobody's going believe your dog is a Frostbite Spider...And if they do...they'll kill him. Its not much of a prank.

speaker: Frodnar
dialogue: Oh yeah? And what would you rather do?

speaker: Dorthe
dialogue: How about...a game of tag? You're it! [Dorthe runs off]

speaker: Frodnar
dialogue: Hey, no fair! [to dog] Get her, Stump!

speaker: Froki Whetted-Blade
dialogue: Well, look at this. Another city rat crawled outside the walls. I don't suppose you've come up here to tell old Froki about your supposed Divines?

speaker: From-Deepest-Fathoms
dialogue: You. You must take the Lexicon. Free me of my burden.

speaker: Drennen
dialogue: I don't like this place. It feels like we're being...watched.

speaker: Breya
dialogue: It's a simple job, Drennen. We get in, we steal the Lexicon, we leave. Don't get jumpy.

speaker: Fathoms
dialogue: If you two cannot handle this, we can find others to hire.

speaker: Roots
dialogue: Enough. Their services will be more than adequate. Let us continue.

speaker: Breya
dialogue: I told you we should have hired a thief.

speaker: Fathoms
dialogue: We are thieves, you fool. We're stealing the cube.

speaker: Breya
dialogue: [heh] And yet none of us can pick a damned lock.

speaker: Drennen
dialogue: This place is huge.

speaker: Roots
dialogue: It is large, indeed. I did not anticipate Avanchnzel's size or the time needed to uncover the entrance. A few hours sleep and we should be ready to continue through.

speaker: Drennen
dialogue: Maybe we should turn back. I don't want to sleep here.

speaker: Roots
dialogue: Drennen, do you understand that the Lexicon at the bottom of this place holds the accumulated memories of centuries of Dwemer.

speaker: Breya
dialogue: Not to mention our pay.

speaker: Fathoms
dialogue: So we're not turning back, you fool.

speaker: Breya
dialogue: Besides, you're not afraid of a few sleeping metal men. Are you, Drennen?

speaker: Drennen
dialogue: I can't do this. We shouldn't be here. I'm sorry.

speaker: Fathoms
dialogue: Let the field mouse run. Your pay will be double.

speaker: Breya
dialogue: My pay will be nothing if we die in here!

speaker: Roots
dialogue: Calm yourself, Breya. We are close to the Lexicon. I can feel it calling. We can do it without Drennen.

speaker: Roots
dialogue: We are close now. Can you feel the Lexicon calling out?

speaker: Fathoms
dialogue: [sarcastic] Sure.

speaker: Breya
dialogue: So we get it and get out, right?

speaker: Roots
dialogue: Once we have the Lexicon, we need to take it to its podium. I know what to do from there. Soon the Lexicon's knowledge will be mine.

speaker: Fathoms
dialogue: Ours. Soon the Lexicon's knowledge will be ours.

speaker: Roots
dialogue: Of course.

speaker: Frothar
dialogue: Father says I'm too young to train with a sword, so I practice with my fists!

speaker: Dagny
dialogue: I'm so angry, I can hardly stand it! Father promised me a new dress days ago, now where is it?

speaker: Frothar
dialogue: It takes a while to make a dress, Dagny. You have to be patient.

speaker: Dagny
dialogue: But I don't want to be patient! I want my dress right now! Father promised!

speaker: Frothar
dialogue: All you ever do is complain about what you want. You're a spoiled baby.

speaker: Dagny
dialogue: I'm going to tell father you said that. He'll tan your hide for sure!

speaker: Fruki
dialogue: Lady Mara will save us from these nightmares. You'll see.

speaker: Fruki
dialogue: Irgnir, get a hold of yourself. They're just dreams. Please tell her, Erandur.

speaker: Erandur
dialogue: Listen to your friend, Fruki. They are just dreams, my dear. I assure you that it is quite normal.

speaker: Irgnir
dialogue: It's the same dream over and over again. You think that's normal? It's evil I tell you!

speaker: Fruki
dialogue: Erandur, she has a point. You keep telling us no harm will follow these dreams, but they must be an omen.

speaker: Erandur
dialogue: Everyone, please. I'm doing what I can to end these nightmares. In the meantime all I ask is you remain strong and put your trust in Lady Mara.

speaker: Irgnir
dialogue: I... I will. Thank you...

speaker: Irgnir
dialogue: You should quit working in the Eastern Mine. Leigelf's no good to work for.

speaker: Fruki
dialogue: Leigelf is a good man, and I'm not running out on him now.

speaker: Irgnir
dialogue: Oh, got a bit of an interest in your boss do you?

speaker: Fruki
dialogue: No, not that it's any of your business.

speaker: Irgnir
dialogue: Tough day at the mines. I swear the ore is getting harder to dig.

speaker: Fruki
dialogue: You're just getting older.

speaker: Irgnir
dialogue: That's why I come here to talk to you. You're all heart.

speaker: Fultheim the Fearless
dialogue: My name is Fultheim. I'm a soldier. Well, mercenary, really. You know, a... a sellsword. I've lived in Skyrim all my life.

speaker: Gabriella, when asked about herself
dialogue: What a curious question. Well, I enjoy moonlit nights, taking long walks on the beach, knitting and unicorns.

speaker: Arnbjorn
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Veezara
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha! Again! Again! Do the part where he tries to buy you some candy.

speaker: Gabriella
dialogue: Oh Babette, but you are so wicked.

speaker: Nazir
dialogue: What about you, Festus? How did that last contract turn out?

speaker: Arnbjorn
dialogue: Oh, yes, please, old man. Regale us with your tales of wizardry...

speaker: Gabriella
dialogue: And what of your latest, Arnbjorn. Something about a Khajiit? Merchant was it?

speaker: Babette
dialogue: Oh, a big doggy chasing a little kitty! How adorable!

speaker: Nazir
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Festus
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Veezara
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Arnbjorn
dialogue: I am not adorable, it was not funny, and he wasn't a merchant. He was a Khajiit monk, a master of the Whispering Fang style. But now he's dead... and I have a new loincloth.

speaker: Nazir
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Festus
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Veezara
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Babette
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Gaius
dialogue: Father, you worry too much. I'll be fine.

speaker: Commander Maro
dialogue: I know you will. But all the same, remember everything I said. Stay alert, and when you get to the cities, make your observations and move on.

speaker: Gaius
dialogue: I understand, but you're being paranoid. I'm inspecting security, not charging off into battle. There's not a lot that can go wrong.

speaker: Commander Maro
dialogue: Son, when the Emperor's safety is concerned, anything could go wrong. Off with you, now. And good travels.

speaker: Gaius
dialogue: Farewell, father. I'll return as soon as I'm able.

speaker: Faida
dialogue: Well, this is it, then. Look after yourself, Gaius. You're doing your duty, and I'm proud of you. But you'd better come back to me. You hear?

speaker: Gaius Maro
dialogue: Oh, Faida. I may travel alone, but you know I carry you always in my heart. I'll see you soon.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: He was a scholar, a master thief and a natural leader. Everyone respected him and followed him without question.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: Gallus! I feared I would never see you again. I was afraid you'd become like the others.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: What will you do now, my love?

speaker: Gallus
dialogue: Nocturnal calls me to the Evergloam. My contract has been fulfilled.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: Will I ever see you again?

speaker: Gallus
dialogue: When your debt to Nocturnal has been paid, we'll embrace once again.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: Farewell, Gallus. Eyes open... walk with the shadows.

speaker: Gallus
dialogue: Goodbye, Karliah.

speaker: Galmar Stone-Fist
dialogue: We are the sons and daughters of Skyrim!

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Balgruuf won't give us a straight answer.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: He's a true Nord. He'll come around.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Don't be so sure of that. We've intercepted couriers from Solitude. The Empire's putting a great deal of pressure on Whiterun.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: And what would you have me do?

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: If he's not with us, he's against us.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: He knows that. They all know that.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: How long are you going to wait?

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: You think I need to send Balgruuf a stronger message.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: If by message you mean shoving a sword through his gullet.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Taking his city and leaving him in disgrace would make a more powerful statement, don't you think?

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: So we're ready to start this war in earnest then?

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: I still say you should take them all out like you did Deadking Torygg.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Torygg was merely a message to the other Jarls. Whoever we replace them with will need the support of our armies.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: We're ready when you are.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Things hinge on Whiterun. If we can take the city without bloodshed all the better. But if not...

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: The people are behind you.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Many I fear still need convincing.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Then let them die with their false kings.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: We've been soldiers a long time. We know the price of freedom. The people are still weighing things in their hearts.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: What's left of Skyrim to wager?

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: They have families to think of.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: How many of their sons and daughters follow your banner? We are their families.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Well put, friend. Tell me, Galmar, why do you fight for me?

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: I'd follow you into the depths of Oblivion, you know that.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Yes, but why do you fight? If not for me, what then?

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: I'll die before elves dictate the fates of men. Are we not one in this?

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Your words give voice to what we all feel, Ulfric. And that's why you will be High King. But the day words are enough, will be the day when soldiers like us are no longer needed.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: I would gladly retire from the world were such a day to dawn.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Aye. But in the meantime, we have a war to plan.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Tell me again why we're wasting time and dwindling resources chasing a legend. We don't even know it exists!

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: The Jarls are upset. They don't all support you.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Damn the Jarls.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: They demand the Moot.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: All the more reason then. The crown would legitimize your claim.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: A crown doesn't make a king.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: No, but this one...

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: If it even exists.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: It exists. And it'll be the symbol of the righteousness of our cause. Think about it. The Jagged Crown! It heralds back to a time before Jarls and Moots. Back to the time when a king was a king because his enemies fell before him, and his people rose because they loved him. Skyrim needs that king. You will be that king, Ulfric. You must be.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: You're certain you've found it?

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: When have I ever been false with you?

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Fine. I'll send the {{hide|Unblooded|The Dragonborn's military rank during the quest.}} here with you. Fancy a crawl through a moldering dungeon to see if you can't stir up Galmar's Jagged Crown?

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: It'll be there. You'll see.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: What's the situation?

speaker: Stormcloak Soldier
dialogue: Cold as the inside of an ice wraith. That and some Imperials are camped out around the entrance, staying nice and warm around their fires.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Imperials? Well, if they're keeping themselves comfortable, let's slip in and send them to their graves that way.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Follow me, quickly and quietly now. I want their guts on the ground before they even know we're here.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: That's the way I like it. Short and bloody; they never knew what hit them. But do not make the mistake of underestimating the Legion. Plenty of them are Nords, same as us. We had the advantage of surprise this time, but things won't be so easy from here on out. Enough talk, let's go kill some Imperials.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Pick a man, and put him down. We attack on my signal. Time to show what you're really made of. For Skyrim!

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Gretta, Engar, stay and guard the entrance. We don't want any Imperial reinforcements taking us by surprise. The rest of you lot are with me.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: I don't like the look of this. Perfect spot for an ambush. Ten to one they're just waiting for us on the other side.

speaker: Stormcloak Soldier
dialogue: But there isn't any other way through.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: You sure about that? Then please, be my guest and go strolling on in there. We'll stay here and watch your back. Not so sure? Oh, then perhaps we should take a moment to look around a little, eh? You there, Unblooded, see if you can find another way through. We'll charge in to help as soon as we hear fighting.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Careful, boys. There's bound to be more up ahead.

speaker: Stormcloak Soldier
dialogue: What in the nine holds is that?

speaker: Stormcloak Soldier 2
dialogue: Draugr. Ain't you ever seen one before?

speaker: Stormcloak Soldier
dialogue: No, and I'm not sure I'm better off for it now neither.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Steady. A few dusty bonewalkers aren't going to stop us anymore than the Imperials could. We are not leaving until we get what we came for. Now let's keep moving.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Ah! The Hall of Stories... we must be getting close now.

speaker: Stormcloak Soldier
dialogue: Oh... I've heard of this. They say these walls show the history of the ancients who built this place.

speaker: Stormcloak Soldier 2
dialogue: Too bad we can't read these carvings. Who knows what secrets we'd uncover?

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: One thing at a time. We're here for the Crown. Any of these carvings show a crown?

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Alright everyone! Keep your guard up. No telling what we'll find down here.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Come on, boys. Let's spread out, and see what we've got. Unblooded, do what you do best. See if you can find some way to get that gate open.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: That's done it! Alright, boys, let's get moving. We've got more... Steady now! They may be uglier than Imperials but they'll go down just the same.

speaker: Galmar
