dialogue: Let's hope that's the last of them. Come on, let's see what's down this way.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: That crown should be around here somewhere. Just keep an eye out for the bonewalkers...

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: The crown must be around here somewhere. Spread out, and keep your eyes open.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Hey, I found the crown over here on this corpse. Is this the one we're looking for?

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Ralof! get away from there, fool!

speaker: Galmar Stone-Fist
dialogue: Alright, get the crown off that draugr!

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: You were right, Galmar.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: I'm in no mood to joke.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Give the word, my lord, and Whiterun is yours.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Whiterun is only a means to an end.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: I've toured our camps. We're ready, Ulfric... Whenever you are.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Is any man ever ready to give the order that will mean the deaths of many?

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: No. But neither is every man able to give that order when he must. But you are that man, Ulfric. You've been that man before, and you'll be him again. And these men and women―they call themselves Stormcloaks because they believe in you. They are the meanest, toughest sons of bitches Skyrim has to offer. And they want this. They want this as much as you do. Perhaps they want it more.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: We are ready. And I might be old myself, but I'll kick those damn walls down with my bare feet―if you would only ask me to do it.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Ha. And I'm sure you could do it, too. Alright. This is it.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Aye, and the sons of Skyrim will greet that dawn teeth and swords flashing.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: So it begins.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Vignar Gray-Mane! Your family was noticeably absent from the walls. Now I know why. Wouldn't a dagger in the back have sufficed?

speaker: Vignar
dialogue: You think this is personal? The Empire has no place in Skyrim... not any more. And you? You have no place in Whiterun anymore.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: A convenient position to hold now. But mark my words, old man, in the days to come, Ulfric will spread his rebellion thin. And what then? We need the Empire, as much as it needs us. We Nords are the Empire! Our blood built it. Our blood sustains it! You of all people should know that.

speaker: Vignar
dialogue: If this was my Empire, I'd be able to worship whoever I damned well pleased. You wish to see an Empire without Talos? Without its soul? We should be fighting those witch-elves, not bending knee to them. The Emperor is nothing more than a puppet of the Thalmor. Skyrim needs a High King who will fight for her, and Whiterun needs a Jarl who will do the same.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Tell me, Vignar. Was all this worth it? How many of those corpses lining our streets wear the faces of men who once called you friend? What about their families?

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Enough! Both of you! There is a burning city out there that needs a government.

speaker: Vignar
dialogue: He's right. Galmar, come, let us restore order.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: This isn't over. You hear me you old fool! This isn't over! {{hide|And you. A Stormcloak? I'd thought better of you.|Referring to the Dragonborn.}} You'll all come to regret this day.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Secure the door.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Already done.

speaker: Rikke
dialogue: Ulfric. Stop.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Stop what? Taking Skyrim back from those who'd leave her to rot?

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: You were there with us. You saw it. The day the Empire signed that damn treaty was the day the Empire died.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: The Empire is weak, obsolete. Look at how far we've come and with so little. When we're done rooting out Imperial influence here at home, then we will take our war to the Aldmeri Dominion.

speaker: Rikke
dialogue: You're a damn fool.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Stand aside woman. We've come for the General.

speaker: Rikke
dialogue: He has given up. But I have not.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Rikke. Go. You're free to leave.

speaker: Rikke
dialogue: I'm also free to stay and fight for what I believe in.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: You're also free to die for it.

speaker: Rikke
dialogue: This is what you wanted? Shield brothers and sisters killing each other? Families torn apart? This is the Skyrim you want?!

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Damnit woman, stand aside.

speaker: Rikke
dialogue: That's not the Skyrim I want to live in.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Rikke. You don't have to do this.

speaker: Rikke
dialogue: You've left me no choice... Talos preserve us.

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Enough... enough...

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: This is it for you. Any last words before I send you to Oblivion?

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: You realize this is exactly what they wanted.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: What who wanted?

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: The Thalmor. They stirred up trouble here. Forced us to divert needed resources and throw away good soldiers quelling this rebellion.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: It's a little more than a rebellion, don't you think?

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: We aren't the bad guys you know.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Maybe not, but you certainly aren't the good guys.

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Perhaps you're right. But then what does that make you?

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: You just said it yourself.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: It makes us right.

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: And if I surrender?

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: The Empire I remember never surrendered.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: That Empire is dead. And so are you.

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: So be it.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Just kill him and let's be done with it already.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Come, Galmar. Where's your sense of the dramatic moment?

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: By the gods! If it's a good ending to some damn story you're after - perhaps the Dragonborn should be the one to do it.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Good point.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Good. It's done.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Well, I suppose some kind of speech is in order.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: I'll go gather the men in the courtyard.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: And Elisif?

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Don't you worry about her. I've sent my best men to round her up.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: And now, I present to you, Ulfric Stormcloak, hero of the people, liberator and High King of Skyrim!

speaker: Soldier
dialogue: And what about Jarl Elisif?

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: I do!

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: How'd I do?

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Eh, not so bad. Nice touch about the High King.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Thank you, I thought so, too.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: It's a foregone conclusion, you know.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Oh, I know.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: The Imperials aren't going to leave us alone. They still have camps in the hills. They'll continue to strike out at us, whenever and wherever they can.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: I'm not afraid of the remnants of the Legion, in time they'll all give up and go home. What I fear, is that the Thalmor will see our victory here and turn greater attention to our shores. We must be prepared to face them.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: May the gods preserve us all.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Come, Galmar. We've still much work to do.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Is there any news from High Rock?

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Not a peep. Those prissy Bretons can't be made to lift a finger to help their neighbors.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: I suppose we shouldn't be surprised. They've never had many problems with the Empire.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Those milk-drinkers? Might as well be elves. Think they're better than us.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Regardless, it appears Skyrim must stand alone, again.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Calm yourself, Galmar. Save it for the battlefield.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Our men are getting massacred out there. Damn Imperials.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: We can't march on Solitude. Not yet. One thing at a time.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: We need to move faster. Keep them off balance.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: It's working, Galmar. Our patience has won us friends and allies. And our armies are systematically taking care of the rest.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Do you think we could persuade one of the dragons to join our side?

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: I'm fairly sure that the dragons don't care about our matters one way or the other.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: But just think of the advantage.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: I'm not saying it wouldn't be useful. But there are better uses of our resources right now.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: I don't suppose we would ever really trust the thing anyway.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: Ahhh... It's good to be home.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Welcome back. I've left a few surprises for you to discover.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: How kind of you. And I've brought an army to give you a going away parade.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: If you two are finished with the touching homecoming, there's a city in chaos out there.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: Indeed. Come, there is much to be done.

speaker: Gemma
dialogue: I'll never understand why you're so bitter about everything.

speaker: Ganna
dialogue: I'm bitter because we had lives in Cyrodiil. And we came out here to be paupers.

speaker: Gemma
dialogue: But we choose our own path now.

speaker: Ganna
dialogue: And a whole lot of good that's gotten us.

speaker: Gemma
dialogue: There is some good news though. I think the borders of the shrine may be smaller than we think.

speaker: Ganna
dialogue: Wait, so you think we'll be able to harvest some of the sacred trees up there?

speaker: Gemma
dialogue: Well that's just it. Some of them might not be sacred.

speaker: Ganna
dialogue: I'll let you explain that one to the Nords.

speaker: Gemma
dialogue: They have to be reasonable about it at some point.

speaker: Ganna
dialogue: Gemma. This town is called 'Kynesgrove.' That stand of trees is Kyne's Grove. You don't honestly think you can just cut some down.

speaker: Gemma
dialogue: Well, we have to cut down something!

speaker: Ganna
dialogue: Maybe we should just admit that this is a horrible place for a mill.

speaker: Ganna
dialogue: What about Ulfric? Did you ever hear back from him?

speaker: Gemma
dialogue: No, but his housecarl sent us a letter.

speaker: Ganna
dialogue: Why didn't you tell me? What did he say?

speaker: Gemma
dialogue: He... thanked us for contacting him, but said they didn't need any more lumber at the moment.

speaker: Gemma
dialogue: You see? That's why I didn't tell you!

speaker: Gemma
dialogue: We've got a new order in.

speaker: Ganna
dialogue: Is that a joke?

speaker: Gemma
dialogue: No! Roggi and Kjeld need some more support timbers for the mine.

speaker: Ganna
dialogue: I suppose Kjeld asked for the usual discount?

speaker: Gemma
dialogue: Well, he is the mayor.

speaker: Ganna
dialogue: No, it's fine. I don't mind being poor.

speaker: Ganna
dialogue: That last brigade of soldiers said there's a tall forest on the eastern edge of the White River.

speaker: Gemma
dialogue: Yes, but that's too close to Mixwater Mill. We don't want to get Gilfre angry at us by stealing her trees.

speaker: Ganna
dialogue: Well we have to harvest somewhere! This is getting absurd.

speaker: Gemma
dialogue: I want to make money just as much as you do, but we don't want to make the Nords angry.

speaker: Ganna
dialogue: Who could tell the difference?

speaker: Gemma
dialogue: Did I tell you I got a letter from General Tullius? They've conscripted some more archers and will need...

speaker: Ganna
dialogue: Sssssh! That's not something we want everyone to be hearing.

speaker: Gemma
dialogue: Oh, like the sleepy rebel supporters in this town are going to tell anyone.

speaker: Ganna
dialogue: Let's just not take the chance. We can talk about this later.

speaker: Garakh
dialogue: Every blade I make honors Malacath. Every rivet, every plate of armor is for him.

speaker: Garvey
dialogue: The Warrens isn't a place for your type. What do you want?

speaker: Gat
dialogue: Well I'm glad you were there. I don't know how I would have gotten past the Forsworn without you.

speaker: Gat
dialogue: Still shaken from all the fighting, my friend. It's been too long since I had to kill someone.

speaker: Pavo
dialogue: Thank the Divines we survived that.

speaker: Gat
dialogue: Those Forsworn were fierce fighters. Fiercer than I could have imagined.

speaker: Gat
dialogue: I feel like we're mining even more ore than before.

speaker: Pavo
dialogue: It's the rush of good fortune, my friend. It makes you work harder.

speaker: Pavo
dialogue: Are you worried the Forsworn might return?

speaker: Gat
dialogue: I doubt the Forsworn would risk holding this mine a second time. They lost many of their warriors.

speaker: Pavo
dialogue: Do you remember the Legion? Fighting the Thalmor in the Great War?

speaker: Gat
dialogue: There were many good battles, friend. I miss those days.

speaker: Pavo
dialogue: You miss them? I don't know how many times I feared for my life.

speaker: Gat
dialogue: You didn't die. A battle you live through is a great honor.

speaker: Pavo
dialogue: Did you ever want to return to your stronghold? Go back to your family?

speaker: Gat
dialogue: I would need to challenge the chief, and take his head, to return home. I'd rather stay here.

speaker: Pavo
dialogue: Don't tell me you, of all people, are afraid of a battle.

speaker: Gat
dialogue: If you had to kill your own brother to be allowed back home, you'd think twice as well.

speaker: Gavros Plinius
dialogue: Find... Paratus... in Oculory.

speaker: Geimund
dialogue: Work hard for the future and leave the past be. That's my motto.

speaker: Geirlund
dialogue: I owe Thorald my life. Helping to save him is the least I can do.

speaker: Gemma
dialogue: I'll never understand why you're so bitter about everything.

speaker: Ganna
dialogue: I'm bitter because we had lives in Cyrodiil. And we came out here to be paupers.

speaker: Gemma
dialogue: But we choose our own path now.

speaker: Ganna
dialogue: And a whole lot of good that's gotten us.

speaker: Gemma

dialogue: Let's just not take the chance. We can talk about this later.

speaker: General Tullius, at Helgen to Ulfric Stormcloak (Skyrim)
dialogue: Ulfric Stormcloak. Some here in Helgen call you a hero, but a hero doesn't use a power like the Voice to murder his King and usurp his throne. You started this war, plunged Skyrim into chaos, and now the Empire is going to put you down, and restore the peace.

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: Sir, we can't just keep trading blows with the rebels like this - it's only strengthening their resolve.

speaker: General Tullius
dialogue: Your concerns are duly noted, Legate, but unfounded. I assure you, this war will be over in another six months.

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: Sir, this is costing lives of both imperial loyalists and Skyrim citizens alike. And it's winning the rebels support where they had none before.

speaker: General Tullius
dialogue: We must maintain order and put the rebellious Jarls in their place, before we have a full scale war on our hands.

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: You don't think this is a war already? Sir, I...

speaker: General Tullius
dialogue: Thank you, Legate. In the future, I'll let you know when your opinion is needed.

speaker: Imperial
dialogue: General Tullius, sir! The headsman is waiting!

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Good. Let's get this over with.

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: Shor, Mara, Dibella, Kynareth, Akatosh. Divines, please help me.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Look at him, General Tullius, the Military Governor. And it looks like the Thalmor are with him. Damn elves. I bet they had something to do with this. This is Helgen. I used to be sweet on a girl from here. Wonder if Vilod is still making that mead with juniper berries mixed in. Funny, when I was a boy, Imperial walls and towers used to make me feel so safe.

speaker: Haming
dialogue: Who are they, daddy? Where are they going?

speaker: Torolf
dialogue: You need to go inside, little cub.

speaker: Haming
dialogue: Why? I want to watch the soldiers.

speaker: Torolf
dialogue: Inside the house. Now.

speaker: Haming
dialogue: Yes, papa.

speaker: Captain
dialogue: Get these prisoners out of the carts. Move it!

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: Why are we stopping?

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Why do you think? End of the line. Let's go. Shouldn't keep the gods waiting for us.

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: No! Wait! We're not rebels!

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Face your death with some courage, thief.

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: You've got to tell them! We weren't with you! This is a mistake!

speaker: Captain
dialogue: Step towards the block when we call your name. One at a time.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Empire loves their damn lists.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Ulfric Stormcloak. Jarl of Windhelm.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: It has been an honor, Jarl Ulfric!

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Ralof of Riverwood. Lokir of Rorikstead.

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: You're not going to kill me!

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Captain. What should we do? He/She's not on the list.

speaker: Captain
dialogue: Forget the list. He/She goes to the block.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: By your orders, Captain. Follow the Captain, prisoner.

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Ulfric Stormcloak. Some here in Helgen call you a hero. But a hero doesn't use a power like The Voice to murder his king and usurp his throne.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: [muffled grunts]

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: You started this war, plunged Skyrim into chaos, and now the Empire is going to put you down, and restore the peace.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: What was that?

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: It's nothing. Carry on.

speaker: Captain
dialogue: Yes, General Tullius. Give them their last rites.

speaker: Priestess of Arkay
dialogue: As we commend your souls to Aetherius, blessings of the Eight Divines upon you, for you are the salt and earth of Nirn, our beloved...

speaker: Stormcloak Soldier
dialogue: For the love of Talos, shut up and let's get this over with.

speaker: Priestess of Arkay
dialogue: As you wish.

speaker: Stormcloak
dialogue: You Imperial bastards!

speaker: Ingrid
dialogue: Death to the Stormcloaks!

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: As fearless in death as he was in life.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: There it is again. Did you hear that?

speaker: Captain
dialogue: I said, next prisoner!

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: To the block, prisoner. Nice and easy.

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: What in Oblivion is that?

speaker: Captain
dialogue: Sentries! What do you see?

speaker: Imperial
dialogue: It's in the clouds!

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Don't just stand there! Kill that thing! Guards, get the townspeople to safety!

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Hey, [race-dependent comment]. Get up! Come on, the gods won't give us another chance!

speaker: Alduin
dialogue: Yol... Toor... Shul

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Quickly, follow me!

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Hadvar! Into the keep, soldier, we're leaving!

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Ralof! You damned traitor. Out of my way!

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: We're escaping, Hadvar. You're not stopping us this time.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Fine. I hope that dragon takes you all to Sovngarde.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: You! Come on, into the keep!

speaker: General Tullius
dialogue: Tell me again, why I'm wasting men chasing after a fairy tale.

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: If Ulfric gets his hand on that crown, it won't be a fairy tale. It'll be a problem.

speaker: General Tullius
dialogue: Don't you Nords put any stock in your own traditions? I thought the Moot chose the king. We're backing Elisif. When the Moot meets, they'll do the sensible thing.

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: Not everyone's agreed to the Moot. You've been here long enough to know that Nords aren't always sensible. We follow our hearts.

speaker: General Tullius
dialogue: So what - Ulfric gets this crown and then suddenly he's High King?

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: No, it's not as simple as that, but the Jagged Crown would be a potent symbol for his cause to rally around. But, if we found it first...

speaker: General Tullius
dialogue: And we gave it to Elisif?

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: In the absence of the Moot, it would further legitimize her claim.

speaker: General Tullius
dialogue: Perhaps... I'm entrusting you with what resources I can spare. But I'm warning you, if this turns out to be a waste of time and men...

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: It won't be a waste.

speaker: General Tullius
dialogue: Make sure you take the Auxiliary here. You can send him/her back when you get there and find nothing but old bones and cobwebs.

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: The Stonefist's no fool. He's found the Crown. But we'll get to it first.

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: I'm telling you, Ulfric's planning an attack on Whiterun.

speaker: General Tullius
dialogue: He'd be insane to try. He doesn't have the men.

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: That's not what my scouts report, sir. Every day more join his cause. Riften, Dawnstar, and Winterhold support him.

speaker: General Tullius
dialogue: It's not a cause. It's a rebellion.

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: Call it whatever you like, General. The man's going to try to take Whiterun.

speaker: General Tullius
dialogue: Jarl Balgruuf...

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: Balgruuf refuses the Legion's right to garrison troops in his city. On the other hand, he also refuses to acknowledge Ulfric's claim.

speaker: General Tullius
dialogue: Well, if he wants to stand outside the protection of the Empire, fine. Let Ulfric pillage his city.

speaker: General Tullius
dialogue: You people and your damn Jarls.

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: Sir? You can't force a Nord to accept help he hasn't asked for.

speaker: General Tullius
dialogue: If Ulfric's making a move for Whiterun, then we need to be there to stop him. Draft another letter with the usual platitudes, but this time share some of your intelligence regarding Ulfric's plans. Embellish if you have to. We'll let it seem like it's his idea.

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: Yes, sir.

speaker: General Tullius
dialogue: You Nords and your bloody sense of honor.

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Enough... enough...

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: This is it for you. Any last words before I send you to Oblivion?

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: You realize this is exactly what they wanted.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: What who wanted?

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: The Thalmor. They stirred up trouble here. Forced us to divert needed resources and throw away good soldiers quelling this rebellion.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: It's a little more than a rebellion, don't you think?

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: We aren't the bad guys you know.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Maybe not, but you certainly aren't the good guys.

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Perhaps you're right. But then what does that make you?

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: You just said it yourself.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: It makes us right.

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: And if I surrender?

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: The Empire I remember never surrendered.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: That Empire is dead. And so are you.

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: So be it.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Just kill him and let's be done with it already.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Come, Galmar. Where's your sense of the dramatic moment?

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: By the gods! If it's a good ending to some damn story you're after - perhaps the Dragonborn should be the one to do it.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Good point.

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: Mara's Mercy, its good to see you! But is it safe for you to be here?

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: We had heard that Ulfric had been captured...

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Gerdur... I'm fine. At least now I am.

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: Are you hurt? What's happened? [looks at player] And who's this? One of your comrades?

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Not a comrade yet...but a friend. I owe him/her my life, in fact. Is there somewhere we can talk? There's no telling when the news from Helgen will reach the Imperials...

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: Helgen? Has something happened...? You're right. Follow me. Hod! Come here a minute. I need your help with something.

speaker: Hod
dialogue: What is it, woman? Sven drunk on the job again?

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: Hod. Just come here.

speaker: Hod
dialogue: Ralof! What are you doing here? Ah...I'll be right down!

speaker: Frodnar
dialogue: Uncle Ralof! Can I see your axe? How many Imperials have you killed? Do you really know Ulfric Stormcloak?

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: Hush, Frodnar. This is no time for your games. Go and watch the south road. Find us if you see any Imperial soldiers coming.

speaker: Frodnar
dialogue: Aw, mama, I want to stay and talk with uncle Ralof!

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Look at you, almost a grown man! Won't be long before you'll be joining the fight yourself!

speaker: Frodnar
dialogue: That's right! Don't worry uncle Ralof, I won't let those soldiers sneak up on you!

speaker: Hod
dialogue: Now, Ralof, what's going on? You two look pretty well done in.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: I can't remember the last time I slept. Where to start? Well, the news you heard about Ulfric was true. The Imperials ambushed us outside Darkwater Crossing. Like they knew exactly where we'd be. That was...two days ago, now. We stopped at Helgen this morning, and I thought it was all over. Had us lined up for the headsman's block and ready to start chopping!

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: The cowards!

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: They wouldn't dare give Ulfric a fair trial. Treason, for fighting for your own people! All of Skyrim would have seen the truth then! But then...out of nowhere...a dragon attacked.

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: You don't mean a real, live...

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: I can hardly believe it myself, and I was there! As strange as it sounds, we'd be dead if not for that dragon. In the confusion, we managed to slip away. Are we really the first to make it to Riverwood?

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: Nobody has come up the south road today, as far as I know.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Good. Maybe we can lay up for a while. I'd hate to put your family in danger, Gerdur, but...

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Thanks, sister. I knew I could count on you.

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: I ought to get back to work before I'm missed, but did anyone else escape? Did Ulfric...

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Don't worry. I'm sure he made it out. It'll take more than a dragon to stop Ulfric Stormcloak!

speaker: Hod
dialogue: I'll let them into the house and, you know, show them where everything is.

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: Hhmm. Help them drink up our mead, you mean. [to Ralof] Good luck, brother. I'll see you later.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Don't worry about me. I know how to lay low.

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: Are those parts ready yet?

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: They don't have to be perfect. Just send them over when they're ready.

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: Can the sawmill handle those logs? They look a might big.

speaker: Hod
dialogue: Ay, it can. Wouldn't want them any bigger though.

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: And the blade?

speaker: Hod
dialogue: Gettin' dull. We'll need a new one soon.

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: I'll talk to Alvor about getting us a new one.

speaker: Gestur Rockbreaker
dialogue: I spend every waking moment making sure the mine is put to good use.

speaker: Gestur
dialogue: Let's make sure we're just as productive this month as we were last. If Bryling's happy, we're happy.

speaker: Gestur
dialogue: All right. Keep up the good work.

speaker: Gestur
dialogue: Is everything well with you, my scaly friend?

speaker: Gestur
dialogue: Yes, well... That's all we ask of you. Carry on.

speaker: Teeba-Ei
dialogue: Yes sir.

speaker: Ghak
dialogue: Malacath has given me the task to mine. Good ore brings strength to our people.

speaker: Burguk
dialogue: I saw you working the forge today, wife. Your muscles have grown strong from the metal shaping!

speaker: Gharol
dialogue: Do they, my chief? Am I now favored enough to replace Shel by your side at the feast? Back your words with action!

speaker: Burguk
dialogue: No more talk of Shel. As chief, I will do what I please, so point your fiery gaze to our enemies.

speaker: Gharol
dialogue: Imagine the heads of your enemies as you forge. Let your hatred work the steel.

speaker: Umurn
dialogue: Yes, mother.

speaker: Umurn
dialogue: The metal has been stubborn today. It refuses to bend.

speaker: Gharol
dialogue: Save your anger for the forge. The steel cannot hear your whining.

speaker: Umurn
dialogue: Sorry, mother. I'll focus on my work.

speaker: Gharol
dialogue: Ah, is there any weapon finer than an Orc blade?

speaker: Umurn
dialogue: No, mother. It's no wonder our enemies fear the sight of an Orc warrior.

speaker: Ghorbash
dialogue: Serving in the Legion taught me to respect leadership. The stronghold needs Burguk.

speaker: Ghorbash
dialogue: It is a fine day to work the mines.

speaker: Oglub
dialogue: This metal will serve the forge well, my brother.

speaker: Ghorza gra-Bagol
dialogue: That's right. An Orc stronghold. Kept to ourselves. Lived as our ancestors would have wanted.

speaker: Ghorza
dialogue: You strike the metal like a mother giving her babe a slap. Hit it harder!

speaker: Ghorza
dialogue: If you can't pound the dust out of your iron, it'll break when it's finished. Hit. It. Harder!

speaker: Tacitus
dialogue: When will I learn to forge weapons and armor? Isn't that my job?

speaker: Ghorza
dialogue: Your job is to do what I say. And I say you have many nails and fittings to make before you even touch a blade. Now get to work.

speaker: Ghorza
dialogue: Tacitus, what is this?

speaker: Tacitus
dialogue: Uh, a nail?

speaker: Tacitus
dialogue: I...I'm sorry. I just, well, the forge gets so hot and I thought...

speaker: Ghorza
dialogue: You thought what? You would skip a step? Not heat the metal all the way through? Useless! Now do it again.

speaker: Eydis
dialogue: Hjalti? I've never heard of anyone named Hjalti. Tiber Septim had many names. Maybe that's one of them?

speaker: Noblewoman
dialogue: But aren't you the least bit nervous? After everything that's happened?

speaker: Emperor Titus Mede II
dialogue: You mean the wedding? My cousin's apparent murder? An unfortunate misunderstanding, no more. Cold mead, hot tempers... these things happen.

speaker: Nobleman
dialogue: Quite. Yet that recent business with the young officer. Maro, was it? How dreadful. The son of your commander, plotting your assassination.

speaker: Emperor Titus Mede II
dialogue: Aha! Here we are. Honored guests, I present to you - the Gourmet! Ah, the Potage le Magnifique. So delicious. My friends, as emperor, I of course reserve the right of first taste.

speaker: Emperor Titus Mede II
dialogue: Oh... Oh how marvelous. Just delicious. It is everything I had hoped it would be. Please, everyone. Enjoy.

speaker: Noblewoman
dialogue: But aren't you the least bit nervous? After everything that's happened?

speaker: Emperor Titus Mede II
dialogue: You mean the wedding? My cousin's apparent murder? An unfortunate misunderstanding, no more. Cold mead, hot tempers... these things happen.

speaker: Nobleman
dialogue: Quite. Yet that recent business with the young officer. Maro, was it? How dreadful. The son of your commander, plotting your assassination.

speaker: Emperor Titus Mede II
dialogue: Aha! Here we are. Honored guests, I present to you - the Gourmet! Ah, the Potage le Magnifique. So delicious. My friends, as emperor, I of course reserve the right of first taste.

speaker: Emperor Titus Mede II
dialogue: Oh... Oh how marvelous. Just delicious. It is everything I had hoped it would be. It.... I.... I think something's... wrong... I... Hunh...

speaker: Penitus Oculatus Agent
dialogue: By the gods! The Gourmet and the chef have poisoned the Emperor! Get them!

speaker: Gianna
dialogue: What? No! No, you don't understand! There's been some kind of mistake! I... Aggghhh!

speaker: Gilfre
dialogue: There's plenty of good wood around here, but I just can't harvest it all by myself. Everyone able-bodied is fighting.

speaker: Giraud Gemane
dialogue: If you love history, you're in the right place. Skyrim is steeped in it.

speaker: Girduin
dialogue: Given the history of this place, it's more than likely there's still some amount of power here.

speaker: Savos
dialogue: Come on, we're finally here! Let's not waste any more time!

speaker: Takes-In-Light
dialogue: Are we truly sure this is a good idea?

speaker: Atmah
dialogue: We'll be back at the College before anyone even knows we're gone.

speaker: Girduin
dialogue: You would care about that, since you're the Arch-Mage's favorite!

speaker: Savos
dialogue: Don't forget, this whole idea was Atmah's to begin with.

speaker: Hafnar
dialogue: Let's just get inside, see what's in there.

speaker: Elvali
dialogue: I can't believe we're doing this.

speaker: Savos
dialogue: Can you imagine the looks on their faces when we come back?

speaker: Hafnar
dialogue: You keep talking like you're sure we'll find something useful in here.

speaker: Girduin
dialogue: Given the history of this place, it's more than likely there's still some amount of power here.

speaker: Savos
dialogue: Enchanted weapons, tomes of ancient knowledge, Shalidor's secrets themselves -- who knows what we could find!

speaker: Takes-In-Light
dialogue: And what if... What if there are things guarding this place?

speaker: Atmah
dialogue: Against six College-trained mages? I think we'll be fine.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: Sister, how is my fortune coming along?

speaker: Gisli
dialogue: Profits continue to rise. The warehouse continues to bring in good revenues, and rent on your stores in the Well is acceptable.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: I'm afraid 'acceptable' just isn't acceptable anymore. I'm sure they can spare a few more coins in monthly rent.

speaker: Gisli
dialogue: Yes, brother. I'm sure they'll agree it's a fair price to pay in order to avoid interacting with you on a daily basis.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: Fair or not, they'll pay it, and that's all I need to care about. Bear that in mind, sister.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: That clumsy maid at the palace spilled wine on my best suit. Sister, I believe it's time for a replacement.

speaker: Gisli
dialogue: I can commission one from the Radiant Raiment. It won't be cheap, but if you want the best, they're the only choice.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: I swear, those scheming elves charge us twice what anyone else would pay.

speaker: Gisli
dialogue: Of course they do, brother. You keep raising their rent.

speaker: Gissur
dialogue: But I need that money, I earned it! I have my own expenses, you know.

speaker: Rulindil
dialogue: Silence! Do not presume, Gissur. You are most useful, but do not presume. We have more informants who are less...offensive.

speaker: Gissur
dialogue: But no one else has brought you such valuable information, have they? [pause] Etienne, he's talked, hasn't he? He knows where that old man you're looking for is, he told me himself.

speaker: Rulindil
dialogue: You'll get your money when he's told the rest of his story, as agreed.

speaker: Gissur
dialogue: So he has talked! I knew it!

speaker: Rulindil
dialogue: Everyone talks, in the end. Now, I have work to do. Leave me to it, if you ever want to see the rest of your payment.

speaker: Gissur
dialogue: Can I...I could help you. He'd talk to me. He trusts me.

speaker: Rulindil
dialogue: You'd like to come downstairs with me, is that it, Gissur? Shall we loose his bonds and put you in a cell together? You can ask him anything you like and see how he answers.

speaker: Gissur
dialogue: No, no. I...I'll wait outside.

speaker: Rulindil
dialogue: That would probably be best. [pause] Now get out!

speaker: Gjak
dialogue: Been working in Iron-Breaker since I was a boy.

speaker: Golldir to Vals Veran
dialogue: I'll return my ancestors to Sovngarde, and you with them!

speaker: Gorm
dialogue: Morthal doesn't need any trouble. You keep your nose clean, understand?

speaker: Gorm
dialogue: What would Hroggar say if he heard I was drinking with you?

speaker: Alva
dialogue: Forget about Hroggar. He's always so tired lately. I need someone with a little fire in their blood.

speaker: Gorm
dialogue: After all you've put that man through. You should be more loyal to him.

speaker: Gorm
dialogue: Buy you a drink?

speaker: Benor
dialogue: Not right now. Anything new?

speaker: Gorm
dialogue: Still the same. I tell you, something's got to be done.

speaker: Benor
dialogue: When the time is right, friend. When we're sure.

speaker: Gorm
dialogue: The longer we wait, the worse it gets.

speaker: Benor
dialogue: Let's talk about it some other time.

speaker: Hakon
dialogue: Gormlaith! We're running out of time! The battle...

speaker: Dragon
dialogue: Daar sul thur se Alduin vakrii. Today Alduin's lordship will be restored. But I honor your courage. Krif voth ahkrin. Die now, in vain.

speaker: Hakon
dialogue: For Skyrim!

speaker: Gormlaith
dialogue: Hyah! Know that Gormlaith sent you down to death! Hakon! A glorious day, is it not?

speaker: Hakon
dialogue: Have you no thought beyond the blooding of your blade?

speaker: Gormlaith
dialogue: What else is there?

speaker: Hakon
dialogue: The battle below goes ill. If Alduin does not rise to our challenge, I fear all may be lost.

speaker: Gormlaith
dialogue: You worry too much, brother. Victory will be ours.

speaker: Hakon
dialogue: Why does Alduin hang back? We've staked everything on this plan of yours, old man.

speaker: Felldir
dialogue: He will come. He cannot ignore our defiance. And why should he fear us, even now?

speaker: Gormlaith
dialogue: We've bloodied him well. Four of his kin have fallen to my blade alone this day.

speaker: Felldir
dialogue: But none have yet stood against Alduin himself. Galthor, Sorri, Birkir...

speaker: Gormlaith
dialogue: They did not have Dragonrend. Once we bring him down, I promise I will have his head.

speaker: Felldir
dialogue: You do not understand. Alduin cannot be slain like a lesser dragon. He is beyond our strength. Which is why I brought the Elder Scroll.

speaker: Hakon
dialogue: Felldir! We agreed not to use it!

speaker: Felldir
dialogue: I never agreed. And if you are right, I will not need it.

speaker: Hakon
dialogue: No. We will deal with Alduin ourselves, here and now.

speaker: Gormlaith
dialogue: We shall see soon enough. Alduin approaches!

speaker: Hakon
dialogue: So be it.

speaker: Alduin
dialogue: Meyye! Tahrodiis aanne! Him hinde pah liiv! Zu'u hin daan!

speaker: Gormlaith
dialogue: Let those that watch from Sovngarde envy us this day! Joor... Zah...Frul!

speaker: Alduin
dialogue: Nivahriin joorre! What have you done? What twisted Words have you created?! Tahrodiis Paarthurnax! My teeth to his neck! But first... dir ko maar. You will die in terror, knowing your final fate... To feed my power when I come for you in Sovngarde!

speaker: Gormlaith
dialogue: If I die today, it will not be in terror! You feel fear for the first time, worm. I see it in your eyes.

speaker: Felldir
dialogue: Fo... Krah Diin!

speaker: Gormlaith
dialogue: Skyrim will be free!

speaker: Hakon
dialogue: No, damn you! It's no use! Use the Scroll, Felldir! Now!

speaker: Felldir
dialogue: Hold, Alduin on the Wing! Sister Hawk, grant us your sacred breath to make this contract heard! Begone, World-Eater! By words with older bones than your own we break your perch on this age and send you out! You are banished! Alduin, we shout you out from all our endings unto the last!

speaker: Felldir
dialogue: You are banished!

speaker: Hakon
dialogue: It worked... you did it...

speaker: Felldir
dialogue: Yes, the World-Eater is gone... may the spirits have mercy on our souls.

speaker: Gormlaith
dialogue: At long last! Alduin's doom is now ours to seal - just speak the word and with high hearths we'll hasten forth to smite the worm wherever he lurks.

speaker: Felldir
dialogue: Hold, comrades - let us counsel take before battle is blindly joined. Alduin's mist is more than a snare - its shadowy gloom is his shield and cloak. But with four Voices joined, our valor combined, we can blast the mist and bring him to battle.

speaker: Hakon
dialogue: Felldir speaks wisdom - the World-Eater, coward, fears you, Dragonborn. We must drive away his mist, Shouting together, and then unsheathe our blades in desperate battle with our black-winged foe.

speaker: Grelka
dialogue: Fine. It'll be five septims to repair it.

speaker: Bolli
dialogue: Why should I pay for a repair on something I just bought?

speaker: Grelka
dialogue: All right, all right. Just bring it to me tomorrow and I'll fix it for you.

speaker: Grelka
dialogue: So, Brand-Shei... business as awful for you as it is for all of us?

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: Worse. The Khajiit Caravans are the only way to get supplies into the city, and even those are becoming more infrequent.

speaker: Grelka
dialogue: Well, let's all raise a flagon to Ulfric; future King of Skyrim and bringer of poverty to the working class!

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: Grelka! Lower your voice before you get us both in trouble.

speaker: Grelka
dialogue: What's so good about it? I've got deadbeats who don't pay me, the city guard looking over my shoulder and Maven Black-Briar breathing down my neck.

speaker: Dinya
dialogue: You poor thing. You should come by the temple, speak to Maramal.

speaker: Grelka
dialogue: Religion isn't going to save me. So unless Mara is going to start raining coin from the heavens, why don't you mind your own business.

speaker: Grelka
dialogue: Not lately. Why?

speaker: Drifa
dialogue: Well, we had one go missing from the the Pawned Prawn, and I was just wondering...

speaker: Grelka
dialogue: Oh I get it. 'It's missing so Grelka must have it.' I wish this town would stop pointing their fingers at me. There is a Thieves Guild in town you know.

speaker: Grelka
dialogue: Oh, Haelga!...There you are. Your special shipment just came in from Hammerfell on the Khajiit caravan.

speaker: Grelka
dialogue: 'Try it on'? What do you need a leather harness for anyway?

speaker: Haelga
dialogue: It's [pause] a religious thing.

speaker: Grelka
dialogue: Hey, greenskin... close your mouth. Some of us are trying to eat over here.

speaker: Grelka
dialogue: Or perhaps you should crawl back into whatever swamp you came from, lizard man.

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: You're not going to goad me into a fight so I'll get kicked out, Grelka. Eat your food and leave me in peace.

speaker: Grelka
dialogue: I don't usually deal in weapons, but I know someone who can get them for me. You mind paying a little extra to get them fast?

speaker: Maven
dialogue: I don't care what it costs. I need four longbows and four score of arrows. Just make it happen.

speaker: Grelka
dialogue: I'll contact my man tonight and let you know what he says.

speaker: Grelka
dialogue: If he paid what he owes, I wouldn't have to say anything. Besides, what in Oblivion do you care?

speaker: Nivenor
dialogue: What's that supposed to mean?

speaker: Grelka
dialogue: Oh come off it, Niv. We both know you married that fisherman for his gold. You don't need to put on an act for my benefit.

speaker: Grelka
dialogue: Did you do everything I said, Shadr?

speaker: Shadr
dialogue: Yes. The man came by at noon just like you said. I gave him the package and he gave me this pouch for you. The package was heavy... I needed his help getting it on his horse. What was inside?

speaker: Grelka
dialogue: Hey, I told you not to ask any questions. Now, here. For your trouble.

speaker: Shadr
dialogue: Thanks, Grelka!

speaker: Grelka
dialogue: Leather? If they're armored, you should talk to Balimund over at The Scorched Hammer.

speaker: Tythis
dialogue: Horker skin, actually.

speaker: Grelka
dialogue: Why in goodness name would you have... oh never mind, just bring them by my house later and I'll see what I can do.

speaker: Aventus Aretino
dialogue: The headmistress is an evil, cruel woman. They call her Grelod the Kind. But she's not kind. She's terrible! To all of us!

speaker: Grelod
dialogue: Those who shirk their duties will get an extra beating. Do I make myself clear?

speaker: Samuel
dialogue: Yes, Grelod.

speaker: Runa
dialogue: Yes, Grelod.

speaker: Hroar
dialogue: Yes, Grelod.

speaker: Francois
dialogue: Yes, Grelod.

speaker: Grelod
dialogue: And one more thing! I will hear no more talk of adoptions! None of you riff-raff is getting adopted. Nobody needs you, nobody wants you. That, my darlings, is why you're here. Why you'll always be here, until you come of age and get thrown into that wide, horrible world. Now, what do you all say?

speaker: Samuel
dialogue: We love you, Grelod. Thank you for your kindness.

speaker: Runa
dialogue: We love you, Grelod. Thank you for your kindness.

speaker: Hroar
dialogue: We love you, Grelod. Thank you for your kindness.

speaker: Francois
dialogue: We love you, Grelod. Thank you for your kindness.

speaker: Grelod
dialogue: That's better. Now scurry off, my little guttersnipes.

speaker: Grelod
dialogue: Samuel is getting to be a problem. Fancies himself something of a 'leader'  to the other children. Put an end to the nonsense, or I will.

speaker: Grelod
dialogue: We haven't had an adoption in months. At this rate, we'll be stuck with these brats forever. We need to get the word out. A sale, if need be.

speaker: Grelod
dialogue: I can't abide Samuel's constant talk of his parents. 'They're coming for me.' 'This is only temporary.' The boy must accept his fate.

speaker: Grelod
dialogue: Seven septims are missing from my purse. I know it was Runa. You get those coins back, or by Stendarr, I'll see her rot in the dungeon.

speaker: Grelod
dialogue: This place is filthy. I've a mind to cancel all town privileges unless those brats start pulling their weight.

speaker: Grelod
dialogue: The stores are running low. We'll need to water down the milk again. Besides, don't want the little darlings getting fat.

speaker: Greta
dialogue: If you want to talk about my brother, I'm not interested.

speaker: Addvar
dialogue: Svari, Jala said you stole an apple from her cart yesterday. Is this true?

speaker: Svari
dialogue: Just a little one! I was hungry!

speaker: Greta
dialogue: I'll talk with Jala, dear. I'm sure she'll accept a potato as repayment.

speaker: Addvar
dialogue: I suppose. But Svari, we don't steal. We're better than that. Understand?

speaker: Svari
dialogue: Yes, papa.

speaker: Greta
dialogue: Eat up, Svari.

speaker: Addvar
dialogue: It's all we've got for today. Don't be greedy.

speaker: Greta
dialogue: Maybe we'll have better luck tomorrow.

speaker: Addvar
dialogue: We'll make it, Greta. We always have so far...

speaker: Grim Shieldmaiden
dialogue: Did you want something? I'm quite busy.

speaker: Grimvar Cruel-Sea
dialogue: But I don't want to be a sailor or a farmer. I want to be a warrior! The strongest one ever!

speaker: Grimvar
dialogue: Then it's true, what everyone is saying? That Aventus Aretino is doing the Black Sacrament? Trying to summon the Dark Brotherhood?

speaker: Idesa
dialogue: Oh, Grimvar... always with the nonsense. No, no, of course not. Those are just tales...

speaker: Grimvar
dialogue: Fine. Then I'll invite him out to play. He lives right there. I'm going to knock on his door...

speaker: Idesa
dialogue: No, child! Wait! That boy, that house - they're cursed.

speaker: Grimvar
dialogue: Ha! Then I'm right. I knew it. He's trying to have somebody killed!

speaker: Idesa
dialogue: All right. I won't deny it, child. What you heard is true. But Aventus Aretino walks a dark path. His actions can lead only to ruin. Now, enough. We will speak no more of this. I am the only friend you need.

speaker: Grisvar the Unlucky
dialogue: I swear, if I ever get out of here, I'm giving up thieving. Really.

speaker: Grogmar
dialogue: May the road favor the foolish...

speaker: Grogmar
dialogue: I've been cracking rock ever since I've been able to hold a pickaxe and I'm telling you, this mine is drying up.

speaker: Filnjar
dialogue: And I'm telling you, you're wrong.

speaker: Grogmar
dialogue: What makes you so sure? What if I'm right?

speaker: Filnjar
dialogue: I know there's ore still in there, I can smell it. You think you're right, you can pack up and leave any time you like.

speaker: Odfel
dialogue: All I'm asking is that you clean up once and a while. How you can find anything in your half of the house is beyond me.

speaker: Grogmar
dialogue: I'd rather spend more time in the mine hauling up iron than doing woman's work keeping the house clean.

speaker: Odfel
dialogue: I'll have you know that I can haul up just as much iron as you in a day and still manage to clean up my messes.

speaker: Grogmar
dialogue: You think so, huh? Maybe you'd like to put some Septims behind that boast.

speaker: Odfel
dialogue: You have yourself a bet.

speaker: Grosta, on Leifnarr's fate.
dialogue: No, it can't be... oh my... and all this time, I was thinking he'd been unfaithful to me. I feel so stupid.

speaker: Gul
dialogue: The mines are hard, but Malacath rewards those who rise to the challenge.

speaker: Brynjolf (Skyrim)
dialogue: There are thieves and then there is Gulum-Ei. No honor, no code at all. He'd shake your hand and stab you in the back at the same time.

speaker: Gunding
dialogue: Any time I get tired of working, I just think maybe that next swing wil make me rich. It keeps me going.

speaker: Ralof, to Gunjar's corpse
dialogue: We'll meet again in Sovngarde, brother.

speaker: Gunnar
dialogue: Gods guide you, Hadvar

speaker: Guthrum
dialogue: Once sailing gets in your blood, it don't get out.

speaker: Gwilin
dialogue: So I took his advice, and here I am. This life might not look like much to you, but I'm content, and isn't that all that matters?

speaker: Gwilin
dialogue: On your way up the 7,000 Steps again, Klimmek?

speaker: Klimmek
dialogue: Not today. I'm just not ready to make the climb to High Hrothgar. The path isn't safe.

speaker: Gwilin
dialogue: Aren't the Greybeards expecting some supplies?

speaker: Klimmek
dialogue: Honestly, I'm not certain. I've yet to be allowed into the monastery. Perhaps one day.

speaker: Hadring
dialogue: Ah, hello there, traveler. Come to the Nightgate for food or lodging?

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Hey, you. You're finally awake. You were trying to cross the border, right? Walked right into that Imperial ambush, same as us, and that thief over there.

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: Damn you Stormcloaks. Skyrim was fine until you came along. Empire was nice and lazy. If they hadn't been looking for you, I could've stolen that horse and been halfway to Hammerfell. You there... You and me, we shouldn't be here. It's these Stormcloaks the Empire wants.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: We're all brothers and sisters in binds now, thief.

speaker: Imperial Soldier
dialogue: Shut up back there!

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: And what's wrong with him, huh?

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Watch your tongue. You're speaking to Ulfric Stormcloak, the true High King.

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: Ulfric? The Jarl of Windhelm? You're the leader of the rebellion. But if they've captured you... Oh gods, where are they taking us?

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: I don't know where we're going, but Sovngarde awaits.

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: No, this can't be happening. This isn't happening.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Hey, what village are you from, horse thief?

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: Why do you care?

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: A Nord's last thoughts should be of home.

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: Rorikstead. I'm... I'm from Rorikstead.

speaker: Imperial
dialogue: General Tullius, sir! The headsman is waiting!

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Good. Let's get this over with.

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: Shor, Mara, Dibella, Kynareth, Akatosh. Divines, please help me.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Look at him, General Tullius, the Military Governor. And it looks like the Thalmor are with him. Damn elves. I bet they had something to do with this. This is Helgen. I used to be sweet on a girl from here. Wonder if Vilod is still making that mead with juniper berries mixed in. Funny, when I was a boy, Imperial walls and towers used to make me feel so safe.

speaker: Haming
dialogue: Who are they, daddy? Where are they going?

speaker: Torolf
dialogue: You need to go inside, little cub.

speaker: Haming
dialogue: Why? I want to watch the soldiers.

speaker: Torolf
dialogue: Inside the house. Now.

speaker: Haming
dialogue: Yes, papa.

speaker: Captain
dialogue: Get these prisoners out of the carts. Move it!

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: Why are we stopping?

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Why do you think? End of the line. Let's go. Shouldn't keep the gods waiting for us.

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: No! Wait! We're not rebels!

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Face your death with some courage, thief.

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: You've got to tell them! We weren't with you! This is a mistake!

speaker: Imperial Captain
dialogue: Step towards the block when we call your name. One at a time.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Empire loves their damn lists.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Ulfric Stormcloak. Jarl of Windhelm.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: It has been an honor, Jarl Ulfric!

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Ralof of Riverwood. Lokir of Rorikstead.

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: No, I'm not a rebel. You can't do this!

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: You're not going to kill me!

speaker: Captain
dialogue: Anyone else feel like running?

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Wait. You there. Step forward. Who are you?

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Ulfric Stormcloak. Some here in Helgen call you a hero. But a hero doesn't use a power like The Voice to murder his king and usurp his throne.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: [muffled grunts]

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: You started this war, plunged Skyrim into chaos, and now the Empire is going to put you down, and restore the peace.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: What was that?

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: It's nothing. Carry on.

speaker: Captain
dialogue: Yes, General Tullius. Give them their last rites.

speaker: Priestess of Arkay
dialogue: As we commend your souls to Aetherius, blessings of the Eight Divines upon you, for you are the salt and earth of Nirn, our beloved...

speaker: Stormcloak Soldier
dialogue: For the love of Talos, shut up and let's get this over with.

speaker: Priestess of Arkay
dialogue: As you wish.

speaker: Stormcloak
dialogue: You Imperial bastards!

speaker: Ingrid
dialogue: Death to the Stormcloaks!

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: As fearless in death as he was in life.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: There it is again. Did you hear that?

speaker: Captain
dialogue: I said, next prisoner!

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: To the block, prisoner. Nice and easy.

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: What in Oblivion is that?

speaker: Captain
dialogue: Sentries! What do you see?

speaker: Imperial
dialogue: It's in the clouds!

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Don't just stand there! Kill that thing! Guards, get the townspeople to safety!

speaker: Alduin
dialogue: Yol... Toor... Shul!

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Still alive, prisoner? Keep close to me if you want to stay that way. Gunnar, take care of the boy. I have to find General Tullius and join their defense.

speaker: Gunnar
dialogue: Gods guide you, Hadvar.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Stay close to the wall!

speaker: Alduin
dialogue: Yol... Toor... Shul

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Quickly, follow me!

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Hadvar! Into the keep, soldier, we're leaving!

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: It's you and me, prisoner. Stay close! Ralof! You damned traitor. Out of my way!

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: We're escaping, Hadvar. You're not stopping us this time.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Fine. I hope that dragon takes you all to Sovngarde.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: You! Come on, into the keep!

speaker: Stormcloak 1
dialogue: We need to get moving! That dragon is tearing up the whole keep!

speaker: Stormcloak 2
dialogue: Just give me a minute... I'm out of breath...

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Hear that? Stormcloaks. Maybe we can reason with them.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Hold on, now, we only want to...

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: If you want to die, so be it.

speaker: Stormcloak 1
dialogue: Freedom or Sovngarde!

speaker: Stormcloak 2
dialogue: For Ulfric and Skyrim!

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: I guess that'll teach me to try to reason with a Stormcloak. Let me see if I can get that door open.

speaker: Torturer
dialogue: You fellows happened along just in time. These boys seemed a bit upset at how I've been entertaining their comrades.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Don't you even know what's going on? A dragon is attacking Helgen!

speaker: Torturer
dialogue: A dragon? Please. Don't make up nonsense. Although, come to think of it, I did hear some odd noises coming from over there.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Come with us. We need to get out of here.

speaker: Torturer
dialogue: You have no authority over me, boy.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Didn't you hear me? I said the keep is under attack!

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Wait a second. Looks like there's something in this cage.

speaker: Torturer
dialogue: Don't bother with that. Lost the key ages ago. Poor fellow screamed for weeks.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: See if {{Hide|you|Referring to the Last Dragonborn.}} can get it open with some picks. We'll need everything we can get.

speaker: Tortuer
dialogue: Sure, take all my things. Please.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Grab what you can and let's go.

speaker: Torturer
dialogue: There's no way out that way, you know...

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Uncle Alvor! Hello!

speaker: Alvor
dialogue: Hadvar? What are you doing here? Are you on leave from...Shor's bones, what happened to you, boy? Are you in some kind of trouble?

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Shh. Uncle, please. Keep your voice down. I'm fine. But we should go inside to talk.

speaker: Alvor
dialogue: What's going on? [looks at player] And who's this?

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: He's/She's a friend. Saved my life, in fact. Come on, I'll explain everything but we need to go inside.

speaker: Alvor
dialogue: Okay, okay. Come inside, then. Sigrid will get you something to eat, and you can tell me all about it.

speaker: Alvor
dialogue: Sigrid! We have company!

speaker: Sigrid
dialogue: Hadvar! We've been so worried about you! Come, you two must be hungry. Sit down and I'll get you something to eat.

speaker: Alvor
dialogue: Now then, boy, what's the big mystery? What are you doing here looking like you lost an argument with a cave bear?

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: I don't know where to start. You know I was assigned to General Tullius's guard. We were stopped in Helgen when we were attacked by...a dragon.

speaker: Alvor
dialogue: A dragon? That's ridiculous. You aren't drunk, are you boy?

speaker: Sigrid
dialogue: Husband. Let him tell his story.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Not much more to tell. The dragon flew over and just wrecked the whole place. Mass confusion. I don't know if anyone else got out alive. I doubt I'd have made it out if not for my friend here. I need to get back to Solitude and let them know what's happened. I thought you could help us out. Food, supplies, a place to stay.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: How'd you end up here?

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: My cousin disappeared one night. Some say the Thalmor grabbed him. It wasn't long before I found myself under Ulfric's banner.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: So why did you join the Stormcloaks?

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: I'm a true Nord. Simple as that.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: So why'd you join the Legion?

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: My father was a Legionnaire, and his before him. I guess I never considered doing anything else.

speaker: Haelga
dialogue: If word got out that I'm practicing my Dibellan Arts in Riften, they'll run me out of town.

speaker: Bolli
dialogue: Haelga, we need to stop seeing each other.

speaker: Haelga
dialogue: Oh, Bolli you silly man. You weren't saying that when you were licking that honey off my...

speaker: Bolli
dialogue: Haelga! That's just it. I can't keep up with you. Your Dibellan techniques... they're exhausting.

speaker: Haelga
dialogue: Is it really me, or is it your wife? You need to make a choice Bolli. The honey or her.

speaker: Haelga
dialogue: When are you going to take me away from here Bolli?

speaker: Bolli
dialogue: I told you, I can't just pick up and leave. I have my wife, my business... not to mention you have the Bunkhouse.

speaker: Haelga
dialogue: That old place? I could care less about it. It's you I want, Bolli.

speaker: Bolli
dialogue: I... I'm sorry Haelga, I can't. Not yet.

speaker: Haelga
dialogue: Oh, good. I want to try it on as soon as possible.

speaker: Grelka
dialogue: 'Try it on'? What do you need a leather harness for anyway?

speaker: Haelga
dialogue: It's [pause] a religious thing.

speaker: Haelga
dialogue: Oh, splendid! I can't wait to use them.

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: Begging your pardon milady... I know these have something to do with Dibella, but whatever are they for?

speaker: Haelga
dialogue: Maybe I'll show you one day, Madesi. Have them delivered to the Bunkhouse, won't you?

speaker: Haelga
dialogue: He wasn't protesting, Maven.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Of course he wasn't you stupid whore; he's a man. Now I'm not going to warn you again. Is that clear?

speaker: Haelga
dialogue: Very well.

speaker: Haelga
dialogue: Its only a bit of fun. You're a lovely young thing, you should try it sometime.

speaker: Svana
dialogue: No! I'm saving myself for someone special. Someone who loves me dearly.

speaker: Haelga
dialogue: You mean Sibbi? You must be joking! All he wants to do is bed you and be done with it. You may as well get it over with and let him.

speaker: Svana
dialogue: You're wrong! Sibbi and I are in love and you're just jealous.

speaker: Haelga
dialogue: Svana, has that Skooma-riddled addict paid her rent yet? Or does she have more excuses?

speaker: Svana
dialogue: She said she'll have it soon. She still has her job at the Meadery for now, so she'll be able to pay us.

speaker: Haelga
dialogue: Why do you insist on defending that woman? All she does with her money is spend it on that Dark Elf garbage.

speaker: Svana
dialogue: Just be patient, aunt. She'll have it, I promise.

speaker: Haelga
dialogue: So, Tythis... you coming by the Bunkhouse later?

speaker: Tythis
dialogue: Of course. I rented a bed there. Where else would I sleep?

speaker: Haelga
dialogue: I have plenty of room in my bed.

speaker: Tythis
dialogue: Good, that must be very comfortable for you. I think mine's a bit too small. Perhaps we could trade?

speaker: Hafjorg
dialogue: This place has seen better days, but it's not my fault.

speaker: Hafnar
dialogue: We barely made it out alive, and you want to go back in?

speaker: Savos
dialogue: Come on, we're finally here! Let's not waste any more time!

speaker: Takes-In-Light
dialogue: Are we truly sure this is a good idea?

speaker: Atmah
dialogue: We'll be back at the College before anyone even knows we're gone.

speaker: Girduin
dialogue: You would care about that, since you're the Arch-Mage's favorite!

speaker: Savos
dialogue: Don't forget, this whole idea was Atmah's to begin with.

speaker: Hafnar
dialogue: Let's just get inside, see what's in there.

speaker: Elvali
dialogue: I can't believe we're doing this.

speaker: Savos
dialogue: Can you imagine the looks on their faces when we come back?

speaker: Hafnar
dialogue: You keep talking like you're sure we'll find something useful in here.

speaker: Girduin
dialogue: Given the history of this place, it's more than likely there's still some amount of power here.

speaker: Savos
dialogue: Enchanted weapons, tomes of ancient knowledge, Shalidor's secrets themselves -- who knows what we could find!

speaker: Takes-In-Light
dialogue: And what if... What if there are things guarding this place?

speaker: Atmah
dialogue: Against six College-trained mages? I think we'll be fine.

speaker: Elvali
dialogue: We... we have to go back. We can't leave Girduin...

speaker: Hafnar
dialogue: We barely made it out alive, and you want to go back in?

speaker: Atmah
dialogue: It's too late. There isn't enough of him left to go back in after.

speaker: Takes-In-Light
dialogue: Gods, what have we done?

speaker: Savos
dialogue: We can't go back. Might as well go forward. We can still do this.

speaker: Atmah
dialogue: Savos is right. We can make it if we just stay alert.

speaker: Savos
dialogue: Come on, we can't stop now. We have to keep moving!

speaker: Atmah
dialogue: Where's Elvali? She was right behind me.

speaker: Hafnar
dialogue: Dead. Something grabbed her from behind. Gone before I could do anything.

speaker: Takes-In-Light
dialogue: This is insanity. We never should've come here.

speaker: Atmah
dialogue: You're right. This is all my fault. Should we turn around, head back?

speaker: Hafnar
dialogue: I don't think going back is a good idea.

speaker: Savos
dialogue: Going back would be the end of all of us. We keep pushing forward, and we'll make it. We will!

speaker: Atmah
dialogue: Come on, you can make it. Let's go.

speaker: Atmah
dialogue: We shouldn't have left her there to die!

speaker: Savos
dialogue: What else could we do? Stay there and die with her? She refused to go on, we didn't have a choice!

speaker: Hafnar
dialogue: This is it, you know. Through this door. Can you feel it?

speaker: Atmah
dialogue: We're not going to make it, are we?

speaker: Hafnar
dialogue: We stay together, no matter what. Agreed?

speaker: Atmah
dialogue: I'll be right with you.

speaker: Savos
dialogue: Agreed. We all stay together.

speaker: Hakon One-Eye
dialogue: For a hundred lifetimes my heart has burned for revenge on Alduin; too long delayed!

speaker: Hakon
dialogue: Gormlaith! We're running out of time! The battle...

speaker: Dragon
dialogue: Daar sul thur se Alduin vakrii. Today Alduin's lordship will be restored. But I honor your courage. Krif voth ahkrin. Die now, in vain.

speaker: Hakon
dialogue: For Skyrim!

speaker: Gormlaith
dialogue: Hyah! Know that Gormlaith sent you down to death! Hakon! A glorious day, is it not?

speaker: Hakon
dialogue: Have you no thought beyond the blooding of your blade?

speaker: Gormlaith
dialogue: What else is there?

speaker: Hakon
dialogue: The battle below goes ill. If Alduin does not rise to our challenge, I fear all may be lost.

speaker: Gormlaith
dialogue: You worry too much, brother. Victory will be ours.

speaker: Hakon
dialogue: Why does Alduin hang back? We've staked everything on this plan of yours, old man.

speaker: Felldir
dialogue: He will come. He cannot ignore our defiance. And why should he fear us, even now?

speaker: Gormlaith
dialogue: We've bloodied him well. Four of his kin have fallen to my blade alone this day.

speaker: Felldir
dialogue: But none have yet stood against Alduin himself. Galthor, Sorri, Birkir...

speaker: Gormlaith
dialogue: They did not have Dragonrend. Once we bring him down, I promise I will have his head.

speaker: Felldir
dialogue: You do not understand. Alduin cannot be slain like a lesser dragon. He is beyond our strength. Which is why I brought the Elder Scroll.

speaker: Hakon
dialogue: Felldir! We agreed not to use it!

speaker: Felldir
dialogue: I never agreed. And if you are right, I will not need it.

speaker: Hakon
dialogue: No. We will deal with Alduin ourselves, here and now.

speaker: Gormlaith
dialogue: We shall see soon enough. Alduin approaches!

speaker: Hakon
dialogue: So be it.

speaker: Alduin
dialogue: Meyye! Tahrodiis aanne! Him hinde pah liiv! Zu'u hin daan!

speaker: Gormlaith
dialogue: Let those that watch from Sovngarde envy us this day! Joor... Zah...Frul!

speaker: Alduin
dialogue: Nivahriin joorre! What have you done? What twisted Words have you created?! Tahrodiis Paarthurnax! My teeth to his neck! But first... dir ko maar. You will die in terror, knowing your final fate... To feed my power when I come for you in Sovngarde!

speaker: Gormlaith
dialogue: If I die today, it will not be in terror! You feel fear for the first time, worm. I see it in your eyes.

speaker: Felldir
dialogue: Fo... Krah Diin!

speaker: Gormlaith
dialogue: Skyrim will be free!

speaker: Hakon
dialogue: No, damn you! It's no use! Use the Scroll, Felldir! Now!

speaker: Felldir
dialogue: Hold, Alduin on the Wing! Sister Hawk, grant us your sacred breath to make this contract heard! Begone, World-Eater! By words with older bones than your own we break your perch on this age and send you out! You are banished! Alduin, we shout you out from all our endings unto the last!

speaker: Felldir
dialogue: You are banished!

speaker: Hakon
dialogue: It worked... you did it...

speaker: Felldir
dialogue: Yes, the World-Eater is gone... may the spirits have mercy on our souls.

speaker: Gormlaith
dialogue: At long last! Alduin's doom is now ours to seal - just speak the word and with high hearths we'll hasten forth to smite the worm wherever he lurks.

speaker: Felldir
dialogue: Hold, comrades - let us counsel take before battle is blindly joined. Alduin's mist is more than a snare - its shadowy gloom is his shield and cloak. But with four Voices joined, our valor combined, we can blast the mist and bring him to battle.

speaker: Hakon
dialogue: Felldir speaks wisdom - the World-Eater, coward, fears you, Dragonborn. We must drive away his mist, Shouting together, and then unsheathe our blades in desperate battle with our black-winged foe.

speaker: Haldyn
dialogue: You'll be so much easier to rob when you're dead!

speaker: Hamal
dialogue: Dibella, guide us.

speaker: Haming
dialogue: Why? I want to watch the soldiers.

speaker: Haming
dialogue: Who are they, daddy? Where are they going?

speaker: Torolf
dialogue: You need to go inside, little cub.

speaker: Haming
dialogue: Why? I want to watch the soldiers.

speaker: Torolf
dialogue: Inside the house. Now.

speaker: Haming
dialogue: Yes, papa.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: See the inn on the other side? Jump through the roof and keep going! Go! We'll follow when we can!

speaker: Alduin
dialogue: Yol... Toor... Shul!

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Still alive, prisoner? Keep close to me if you want to stay that way. Gunnar, take care of the {{hide|boy| (referring to Haming)}}. I have to find General Tullius and join their defense.

speaker: Gunnar
dialogue: Gods guide you, Hadvar.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Stay close to the wall!

speaker: Haran
dialogue: Ranmir beg a drink from you, yet? That's gold wasted, friend.

speaker: Harrald
dialogue: Out of my way. The son of the Jarl has no time for idle conversation with travelers.

context: Another foul day at the smelter
speaker: Omluag
dialogue: Another foul day at the smelter.

context: Another foul day at the smelter
speaker: Omluag
dialogue: Sometimes I think we deserve these miserable lives of ours.

speaker: Hathrasil
dialogue: Surprised to see you working. Mulush almost broke your arm yesterday.

speaker: Omluag
dialogue: Does it look like I can afford losing a day's wage? That damn Orc isn't getting the best of me.

speaker: Omluag
dialogue: Divines, I'm tired. This is too much work.

speaker: Hathrasil
dialogue: Just keep at it, or Mulush will beat you.

speaker: Hathrasil
dialogue: Careful of the molten metal. That gets on you, kiss your fingers goodbye.

speaker: Omluag
dialogue: I know what I'm doing. Stop telling me.

speaker: Omluag
dialogue: First war, and now dragons. Everywhere they go, the Nords bring nothing but ruin.

speaker: Hathrasil
dialogue: Ain't nothing for it. They're still in charge.

speaker: Mulush
dialogue: I could smelt metal in half the time as you weak-willed pink-skins. Do I have to do everything?

speaker: Hathrasil
dialogue: No Mulush. I'll work harder.

speaker: Mulush
dialogue: I don't want any of you thieving workers even thinking about stealing any silver. If I see you sneaking off with even one speck of silver, I'll break your leg and throw you into the river.

speaker: Hathrasil
dialogue: Yes, Mulush.

speaker: Hefid the Deaf
dialogue: Inkpot. Stone. Bucket. Book. Knife.

speaker: Heimskr
dialogue: Trust in me, Whiterun! Trust in Heimskr! For I am the chosen of Talos! I alone have been anointed by the Ninth to spread his holy word!

speaker: Heimvar
dialogue: Think I'll forge me a new sword, just in case things go awry here in Solitude. I'm the blacksmith's apprentice, you see.

speaker: Helgird
dialogue: My job's simple enough. The dead don't really complain much.

speaker: Hemming Black-Briar
dialogue: My Mother spares no expense where I'm concerned. I'm heir to the family fortune after all.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Hemming, I want you to personally supervise the next shipment.

speaker: Hemming
dialogue: We already have people that do that and they make quite a bit of coin for it.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: I don't trust them. Come to think of it, I don't trust you either, but at least you're family.

speaker: Hemming
dialogue: Anything you say, Mother.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Hemming, I need you to bring a note to Sibbi. I need him to do something for me.

speaker: Hemming
dialogue: Sibbi? He's in prison... you put him there.

speaker: Hemming
dialogue: Why do you tolerate him, mother? All he contributes to this family is embarrassment and disgrace.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: I tolerate your son because he'll do anything I ask, without question. I'd expect the same from my own son.

speaker: Hemming
dialogue: I understand, mother. Forgive me.

speaker: Hemming
dialogue: So, Talen. Have you reconsidered my offer?

speaker: Talen-Jei
dialogue: Sorry Hemming, I've no interest in becoming your valet.

speaker: Hemming
dialogue: What's the matter, I thought you people were used to indentured servitude.

speaker: Talen-Jei
dialogue: Xhuth! Black-Briar or not, say that again and so help me you're going to need more than your mother to protect you from me.

speaker: Hemming
dialogue: Yes, she's been grooming herself for this for quite a long time.

speaker: Maul
dialogue: It's surprising the Council is allowing a Nord rule Riften under the Imperial flag. That can't be their first choice.

speaker: Hemming
dialogue: Let's just say my mother knows which pockets to line and keep it at that.

speaker: Hemming
dialogue: There's still the matter of the prisoner to discuss. Now, his family is willing to contribute handsomely if we release him.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: The execution will proceed as planned.

speaker: Hemming
dialogue: But, mother... this is quite a sizable contribution and the crime doesn't befit such a harsh punishment.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Are you going soft on me, Hemming? Perhaps I made the wrong choice installing you as steward.

speaker: Hemming
dialogue: No, mother. The execution will proceed as planned.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Hemming, have you dispatched that letter I gave you yesterday?

speaker: Hemming
dialogue: Yes, and I sent it with our fastest courier and under the cover of night, exactly as you specified.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Good. If I need to light a few fires in order to get what we need to defend this place from the Stormcloaks, so be it.

speaker: Hemming
dialogue: I'm almost certain he'll reach the Imperial City tomorrow, so we should have an answer by the end of the week.

speaker: Hemming
dialogue: So, have you thought about what I said?

speaker: Hemming
dialogue: You listen to me. I'd be careful wagging that pretty little tongue at me like that otherwise I may just have it cut off.

speaker: Wylandriah
dialogue: Just stay away from me and maybe I won't weave a spell to shrink something that matters to you.

speaker: Herluin Lothaire
dialogue: Need some sort of toxin for a special occasion? That's where I come in.

speaker: Hermir Strong-Heart
dialogue: A word of advice―don't buy discounted armor.

speaker: Hermir
dialogue: Is Ulfric's armor done yet?

speaker: Oengul
dialogue: No, I want to take my time with it.

speaker: Hermir
dialogue: Can I help with it? Maybe just the cuirass?

speaker: Oengul
dialogue: This is more delicate work than you're used to.

speaker: Hermir
dialogue: I did that engraved piece just last month!

speaker: Oengul
dialogue: This is the royal armor, lass. Maybe in a few years.

speaker: Oengul
dialogue: Did you use my good hammer?

speaker: Oengul
dialogue: Blast, girl, I told you to leave my tools alone. You have yours, and I have mine.

speaker: Hermir
dialogue: I didn't touch it!

speaker: Oengul
dialogue: Hammers don't have legs.

speaker: Hermir
dialogue: Did you look behind the forge? I think I saw it there.

speaker: Oengul
dialogue: Oh... yes. Now that you mention it, I think... sorry about that.

speaker: Oengul
dialogue: Have you been learning your ores?

speaker: Hermir
dialogue: I think I've got a handle on it, but Orichalcum is confusing.

speaker: Oengul
dialogue: Don't even bother with that one. Leave it to the Orcs.

speaker: Hermir
dialogue: Oh, right. That makes sense. Kind of a messy metal, anyway.

speaker: Hern
dialogue: Well now. What have we here? A lost little lamb?

speaker: Hero 1
dialogue: I crave a tale of tall ships and fearless heroes, for heart's ease.

speaker: Hero 2
dialogue: Listen well, friend, and lighten your mood while words I'll spin of warriors bold, whose deeds of valor brought undying fame.

speaker: Hero 1
dialogue: Come, let us share a cup of mead, and trade tales of our time on Mundus, reliving the glory of our remembered deeds.

speaker: Hero 2
dialogue: A cup I'll gladly raise in company with you. None have yet bested me in boasting or drinking.

speaker: Hert
dialogue: Why don't you stay a while?

speaker: Drahff
dialogue: This far? We're livin' in a sewer. You said we'd have a house as big as the Black-Briars' by now.

speaker: Hilde
dialogue: By Shor, what do you want?

speaker: Hilde
dialogue: Has my son Sven asked to join the war?

speaker: Hilde
dialogue: If he does, tell him how bad the food is. And how dangerous it is.

speaker: Legion Soldier/Stormcloak Soldier
dialogue: Look old woman. If your boy wants to learn how to fight, we'll teach him. Now off with you.

speaker: Hilde
dialogue: It seems like Dorthe grows a head taller every season.

speaker: Hilde
dialogue: She'll make a fine wife someday.

speaker: Sigrid
dialogue: Thank Shor I have a lot of years before I have to worry about that!

speaker: Hilde
dialogue: A dragon! I saw a dragon!

speaker: Sven
dialogue: What? What is it now, mother?

speaker: Hilde
dialogue: It was as big as the mountain and black as night. It flew right over the barrow!

speaker: Sven
dialogue: Dragons, now, is it? Please, mother. If you keep on like this everyone in town will think you're crazy. And I've got better things to do than listen to more of your fantasies.

speaker: Hilde
dialogue: You'll see! It was a dragon! It'll kill us all and then you'll believe me!

speaker: Hillevi
dialogue: There's an old saying that only a Nord can work the soil in Skyrim. I don't think anyone else would have the patience for it.

speaker: Torbjorn
