dialogue: I wanted to thank you again for the mince pie you sent over. It was delicious.

speaker: Hillevi
dialogue: It was my pleasure, Torbjorn. I enjoy cooking, and after what you and Tova have been through, it was the least I could do.

speaker: Torbjorn
dialogue: My little Friga loved to cook, but she was terrible at it. Then one day, out of nowhere, she made the most amazing leek soup. She watched while we ate it, and when she saw how much we loved it, she was... so proud...

speaker: Hillevi
dialogue: I... I'm so sorry, Torbjorn. You must be suffering terribly. I wish there was some way I could help.

speaker: Torbjorn
dialogue: You've done more than enough already. You've been a good friend in a time of need, and we won't forget that. I'm sorry I lost myself for a moment there. I just need some time to get over the loss.

speaker: Nilsine
dialogue: Is that new batch of tomatoes ready for sale yet, Hillevi?

speaker: Hillevi
dialogue: You know, I'm not sure. My husband's been tending to the vines, so I'll have to ask him.

speaker: Nilsine
dialogue: Just promise me when you get some more in, I'll have the first crack at them.

speaker: Nilsine
dialogue: So serious! Ha ha ha!

speaker: Torsten
dialogue: How's business today?

speaker: Hillevi
dialogue: Well enough, I suppose. Nilsine bought up most of the tomatoes, and was asking if we could get more.

speaker: Torsten
dialogue: We've got another dozen ripening on the vine. They should be ready in a few days.

speaker: Hillevi
dialogue: I'll be sure to tell her.

speaker: Hillevi
dialogue: How have things been with you?

speaker: Tulvur
dialogue: I got another harangue from Torsten yesterday.

speaker: Hillevi
dialogue: Don't worry about him. I know you work hard, and I'm the one who gets you your money.

speaker: Tulvur
dialogue: Thank you, miss, I appreciate that.

speaker: Hillevi
dialogue: And what about the dogs? How are those precious little angels?

speaker: Tullvur
dialogue: Healthy and strong. Ysgramor's coat's gotten so thick, he looks fat!

speaker: Hillevi
dialogue: Oh, that's just adorable.

speaker: Hired Thug
dialogue: We're here to teach you a lesson.

speaker: Hjorunn
dialogue: Honest gold for honest work.

speaker: Hod
dialogue: At least the damned war hasn't gotten here. Yet.

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: Mara's Mercy, its good to see you! But is it safe for you to be here?

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: We had heard that Ulfric had been captured...

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Gerdur... I'm fine. At least now I am.

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: Are you hurt? What's happened? [looks at player] And who's this? One of your comrades?

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Not a comrade yet...but a friend. I owe him/her my life, in fact. Is there somewhere we can talk? There's no telling when the news from Helgen will reach the Imperials...

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: Helgen? Has something happened...? You're right. Follow me. Hod! Come here a minute. I need your help with something.

speaker: Hod
dialogue: What is it, woman? Sven drunk on the job again?

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: Hod. Just come here.

speaker: Hod
dialogue: Ralof! What are you doing here? Ah...I'll be right down!

speaker: Frodnar
dialogue: Uncle Ralof! Can I see your axe? How many Imperials have you killed? Do you really know Ulfric Stormcloak?

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: Hush, Frodnar. This is no time for your games. Go and watch the south road. Find us if you see any Imperial soldiers coming.

speaker: Frodnar
dialogue: Aw, mama, I want to stay and talk with uncle Ralof!

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Look at you, almost a grown man! Won't be long before you'll be joining the fight yourself!

speaker: Frodnar
dialogue: That's right! Don't worry uncle Ralof, I won't let those soldiers sneak up on you!

speaker: Hod
dialogue: Now, Ralof, what's going on? You two look pretty well done in.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: I can't remember the last time I slept. Where to start? Well, the news you heard about Ulfric was true. The Imperials ambushed us outside Darkwater Crossing. Like they knew exactly where we'd be. That was...two days ago, now. We stopped at Helgen this morning, and I thought it was all over. Had us lined up for the headsman's block and ready to start chopping!

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: The cowards!

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: They wouldn't dare give Ulfric a fair trial. Treason, for fighting for your own people! All of Skyrim would have seen the truth then! But then...out of nowhere...a dragon attacked.

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: You don't mean a real, live...

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: I can hardly believe it myself, and I was there! As strange as it sounds, we'd be dead if not for that dragon. In the confusion, we managed to slip away. Are we really the first to make it to Riverwood?

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: Nobody has come up the south road today, as far as I know.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Good. Maybe we can lay up for a while. I'd hate to put your family in danger, Gerdur, but...

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Thanks, sister. I knew I could count on you.

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: I ought to get back to work before I'm missed, but did anyone else escape? Did Ulfric...

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Don't worry. I'm sure he made it out. It'll take more than a dragon to stop Ulfric Stormcloak!

speaker: Hod
dialogue: I'll let them into the house and, you know, show them where everything is.

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: Hhmm. Help them drink up our mead, you mean. [to Ralof] Good luck, brother. I'll see you later.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Don't worry about me. I know how to lay low.

speaker: Hod
dialogue: Ay, we can get that for ya. We just finished the timber for those catapults.

speaker: Alvor
dialogue: War may be good for business, but it's hard on families.

speaker: Hod
dialogue: A hard truth, that is. Let's drink to the fallen ones.

speaker: Hod
dialogue: You need to choose between those two boys. It ain't fair to Sven or Faendal to keep tuggin' on their heart strings like that.

speaker: Hod
dialogue: I'm just sayin' you should pick one to settle down with.

speaker: Hod
dialogue: You'll be wantin' me to pay for them?

speaker: Embry
dialogue: It's only right seein' as {{Sicquote|your|you're}} the important lumber man.

speaker: Hod
dialogue: You come do an honest day's work at my mill, and I'll pay you an honest day's wages. Then we'll drink.

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: Can the sawmill handle those logs? They look a might big.

speaker: Hod
dialogue: Ay, it can. Wouldn't want them any bigger though.

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: And the blade?

speaker: Hod
dialogue: Gettin' dull. We'll need a new one soon.

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: I'll talk to Alvor about getting us a new one.

speaker: Hofgrir Horse-Crusher
dialogue: Not me, I'm no weakling. In fact, I bet I've got the strongest arms in all of Skyrim.

speaker: Hogni Red-Arm
dialogue: The secret to chopping meat is never washing your hands.

speaker: Hogni Red-Arm
dialogue: What did you say to me, Reachman?

speaker: Degaine
dialogue: I said give me some meat. I'm hungry, and the Divines know you don't need more food in that huge gut of yours.

speaker: Hogni
dialogue: You little twig. I'll snap you in two!

speaker: Degaine
dialogue: Just try it. Maybe a little time inside Cidhna Mine will get rid of all that fat on you.

speaker: Hogni
dialogue: Look at you, begging on the streets. Learn a trade.

speaker: Degaine
dialogue: Picking on me again, you backbiting Nord? Tired of those prissy nobles turning down your rotten slabs of venison?

speaker: Hogni
dialogue: How dare you. No one turns down cut meat from Hogni Red-Arm!

speaker: Degaine
dialogue: Hogni Red-Arm, more like Hogni Fat-Arm.

speaker: Hogni
dialogue: You there, pretty lady. You need some fresh meat for your family? Just look at the blood coming from this cut....

speaker: Hogni
dialogue: What's wrong? You have to look at the blood closely to see the quality of the meat. How else will you know it's fresh?

speaker: Hroki
dialogue: I don't need to know if it's fresh from this distance.

speaker: Hroki
dialogue: Ugh. You're the most disgusting merchant I have ever seen. The guards should take you away.

speaker: Hogni
dialogue: The only people I offend are cheats who don't pay me enough gold coin, or idiots who don't know good meat when I throw it at their faces.

speaker: Hroki
dialogue: If you ever think of throwing meat at me, I will have you dragged off to Cidhna Mine so fast the guards will yank those filthy arms of yours off.

speaker: Hogni
dialogue: What do I do to deserve such hatred? You give people good food and good prices, and all they do is insult you.

speaker: Eola
dialogue: Thank you for coming to dinner, Hogni.

speaker: Hogni
dialogue: I never miss a good meal.

speaker: Hogni
dialogue: The toes are my favorite part. I hope I get to take a few home with me.

speaker: Lisbet
dialogue: I always preferred the liver myself. My brother had such a juicy liver.

speaker: Hogni
dialogue: When was your first meal, Banning?

speaker: Banning
dialogue: Do dogs count?

speaker: Hogni
dialogue: Of course they don't count!

speaker: Banning
dialogue: My friend Marex. We were hunting, and I thought he was an elk.

speaker: Hogni
dialogue: That must have been quite a surprise.

speaker: Banning
dialogue: Either way, I came back with meat for the table.

speaker: Hold Guard
dialogue: You have committed crimes against Skyrim and her people, what say you in your defense?

speaker: Wuunferth
dialogue: What is the meaning of this?

speaker: Jorleif
dialogue: You're under {{Sicblock|the arrest|arrest}}, for the Murder of Susanna of Candlehearth Hall. And Friga Shatter-Shield. And all the rest. We're wise to your scheming, you coward.

speaker: Wuunferth
dialogue: Has the whole city lost their brains? I've been scrying and auguring to find the murderer myself.

speaker: Jorleif
dialogue: Make your excuses from the Bloodworks, wizard. Get him out of my sight.

speaker: Windhelm Guard
dialogue: Yes, sir! I'm sorry, sir. But you'll have to come with me.

speaker: Wuunferth
dialogue: This isn't over, Jorleif!

speaker: Guard
dialogue: You there! Fool! Hold fast. You've been accused of a crime against the laws of this land. What say you in your defense?

speaker: Cicero
dialogue: Wh... What? A crime? Me? Preposterous! Poor Cicero is just standing here! Cicero loves order. Oh yes! He would never disrespect the law!

speaker: Guard
dialogue: You look like a crazy man to me. And what's in that coffin, hmm? Maybe some time in a cell will help loosen that lying tongue.

speaker: Cicero
dialogue: Damn that Loreius. Oh, how he will pay for this treachery...

speaker: Guard
dialogue: You just keep quiet and stay where you are. Soon as my relief arrives, we'll all take a nice little trip.

speaker: Markarth City Guard
dialogue: What a waste! There must be a dozen men up there!

speaker: Markarth City Guard 2
dialogue: Yeah. Calcelmo called in his entire expedition team - said he needed every man he could get to protect his research.

speaker: Markarth City Guard
dialogue: Better them than us. We lost three good men to the traps up there, and for what- just to see another damn spider clanking around?

speaker: Markarth City Guard 2
dialogue: Well, at least this post is safe enough. Come on, let's get back to work.

speaker: Fjori
dialogue: Thank {{Hide|you|Referring to the Dragonborn.}} for releasing us from her spell.

speaker: Holgeir
dialogue: Now we can rest in peace once again. Come Fjori, my love...

speaker: Fjori
dialogue: Take {{Hide|this|Referring to the Ghostblade.}} with our gratitude.

speaker: Horgeir
dialogue: Working hard gives a man reason for drinking hard. Well, that and putting up with a wife like mine.

speaker: Horik Halfhand
dialogue: I've been in the Legion all my life. I'm content to serve.

speaker: Horm
dialogue: I grew up tending some of these horses. They're almost family.

speaker: Housecarl
dialogue: Honor to you, my Thane.

speaker: Hrefna
dialogue: The Stormcloaks are named after Ulfric. He's a bad man, but don't tell the soldiers I said that.

speaker: Hrefna
dialogue: Sondas, I've heard about Morrowind.

speaker: Sondas
dialogue: Oh? What about it?

speaker: Hrefna
dialogue: That it was black and gross and nobody wanted to live there anymore.

speaker: Sondas
dialogue: I'll have to take your word on that one, my dear.

speaker: Hrefna
dialogue: Do you ever want to go to Morrowind, Sondas?

speaker: Sondas
dialogue: I've been in Skyrim my whole life. Why would I want to leave?

speaker: Hrefna
dialogue: To see the fires!

speaker: Sondas
dialogue: I think I like the lake here just a little more.

speaker: Hrefna
dialogue: And Meieran thinks we should go there!

speaker: Tormir
dialogue: I don't want to hear another word about what you're learning from the elf! It's high time you learned to be a Nord, too!

speaker: Hrefna
dialogue: But mama...

speaker: Tormir
dialogue: He's a half-decent farmer. Ask him to teach you to farm!

speaker: Hreinn
dialogue: My father Kleppr is the one you want to talk to. I just clean up.

speaker: Hroar
dialogue: I was named after the sound a lion makes. You know: rrroooaaaarr! Really.

speaker: Benor
dialogue: You tempt me mightily, Alva. But I won't cuckhold another man, even a murderer like Hroggar.

speaker: Hroggar
dialogue: How are you feeling?

speaker: Alva
dialogue: I feel wonderful, just like every night.

speaker: Hroggar
dialogue: Do you need anything? Are you hungry?

speaker: Alva
dialogue: Oh Hroggar, you know I'm always hungry. Don't worry, I'll eat when I need to. Oh, look! We have company!

speaker: Hroki
dialogue: Don't mind the yelling. My parents are always going at each other.

speaker: Hogni
dialogue: The only people I offend are cheats who don't pay me enough gold coin, or idiots who don't know good meat when I throw it at their faces.

speaker: Hrongar
dialogue: I'm not a man, I'm a weapon in human form. Just unsheathe me, and point me at the enemy.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: Good. You're finally here. The Jarl's been waiting for you.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: You heard the summons. What else could it mean? The Greybeards...

speaker: Hrongar
dialogue: We were just talking about you. My brother needs a word with you.

speaker: Hrongar
dialogue: That was the voice of the Greybeards, summoning you to High Hrothgar! This hasn't happened in ... centuries, at least. Not since Tiber Septim himself was summoned when he was still Talos of Atmora!

speaker: Hrongar
dialogue: Nord nonsense?! Why you puffed-up ignorant... these are our sacred traditions that go back to the founding of the First Empire!

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Hrongar. Don't be so hard on Avenicci.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Back to business, Proventus. We still have a city to defend.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: Yes, my lord.

speaker: Hrongar
dialogue: Proventus, you must help me. We need to convince my brother to do more for the war effort.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: What would you have me do, Hrongar? Your brother is the Jarl. You know I can't question his judgement.

speaker: Hrongar
dialogue: I'm not asking you to defy the Jarl, just to open his eyes. Use subtlety and suggestion to turn his thoughts to the war. You're his steward, he'll listen to you.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: Leave me out of your intrigues, Hrongar. If you have something to say to the Jarl, say it with your own tongue.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: My lord Jarl, if we do not take steps soon, our coffers will be empty.

speaker: Hrongar
dialogue: Raise the taxes, then! Put anyone that refuses to pay in the stocks and make an example of them.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: As you command, my lord. But, the issue could be solved another way. If we spend less on new arms and armor for the guards, for example...

speaker: Hrongar
dialogue: We're at war, old fool, or have you forgotten? Whiterun is the crown jewel of Skyrim, and you would leave us defenseless?

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: Forgive me, my lord. It was foolish of me to make such a suggestion.

speaker: Huki Seven-Swords
dialogue: All right, meat, it's time for you to earn your freedom.

speaker: Hulda
dialogue: Come on in. Let me know if you need anything, or take a seat by the fire and I'll send someone over.

speaker: Iddra
dialogue: I'm going to need your help in the kitchen tomorrow.

speaker: Kjeld the Younger
dialogue: But papa was going to take me hunting tomorrow!

speaker: Iddra
dialogue: Oh, I don't think you're old enough for that yet. You can help me salt the cheese curd.

speaker: Kjeld the Younger
dialogue: Why can't Froa do it?

speaker: Iddra
dialogue: Because I'm telling you to.

speaker: Iddra
dialogue: You need to take better care of your sister.

speaker: Kjeld the Younger
dialogue: But she's so stupid!

speaker: Iddra
dialogue: She said you threw her into a goat pen yesterday.

speaker: Kjeld the Younger
dialogue: Because she was being stupid!

speaker: Iddra
dialogue: Don't make me bring your father into this.

speaker: Kjeld the Younger
dialogue: Mama, when can we go play in the river again?

speaker: Iddra
dialogue: Not with all those soldiers all over the hold. Their horses can't see you, you know.

speaker: Kjeld the Younger
dialogue: I know, but...

speaker: Iddra
dialogue: And you'll be trampled to death!

speaker: Kjeld the Younger
dialogue: No way. I'm quick!

speaker: Iddra
dialogue: Well why don't you be quick about finding my book that you lost?

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: How are the little ones?

speaker: Iddra
dialogue: Oh, you know. Little Kjeld is a handful, and Froa is just so quiet.

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: He takes after his father, and she takes after you.

speaker: Iddra
dialogue: Well, that's the good and the bad of it.

speaker: Iddra
dialogue: If you like mead so much, why not go live in Riften?

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: Oh, I wouldn't be able to help them. Their skills were given by the Divines.

speaker: Iddra
dialogue: Maybe you could be a taster or something.

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: Ah, but I can do that right here. Right now!

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: Have you heard about Goldenglow Meadery?

speaker: Iddra
dialogue: Did something happen to it?

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: All the apiaries... it will take years to get those bees happy again.

speaker: Iddra
dialogue: Do the bees need to be happy?

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: Of course! You can't make good mead without happy honey!

speaker: Idesa Sadri
dialogue: I try to keep Grimvar safe, but these are dangerous times.

speaker: Grimvar
dialogue: Then it's true, what everyone is saying? That Aventus Aretino is doing the Black Sacrament? Trying to summon the Dark Brotherhood?

speaker: Idesa
dialogue: Oh, Grimvar... always with the nonsense. No, no, of course not. Those are just tales...

speaker: Grimvar
dialogue: Fine. Then I'll invite him out to play. He lives right there. I'm going to knock on his door...

speaker: Idesa
dialogue: No, child! Wait! That boy, that house - they're cursed.

speaker: Grimvar
dialogue: Ha! Then I'm right. I knew it. He's trying to have somebody killed!

speaker: Idesa
dialogue: All right. I won't deny it, child. What you heard is true. But Aventus Aretino walks a dark path. His actions can lead only to ruin. Now, enough. We will speak no more of this. I am the only friend you need.

speaker: Idgrod Ravencrone
dialogue: I stand where I have always stood. Here in Morthal.

speaker: Idgrod
dialogue: The people still doubt me, don't they.

speaker: Idgrod
dialogue: It does not surprise me. They do not share in what I see, and I cannot explain it to them.

speaker: Aslfur
dialogue: Just guide them well, and all will work out.

speaker: Idgrod
dialogue: I have never doubted that, husband.

speaker: Aslfur
dialogue: Have you made a decision about Falion?

speaker: Idgrod
dialogue: What decision is there to be made? I allowed him to live here. I stand by that.

speaker: Aslfur
dialogue: Yes, but there are concerns. Rumors that he's up to something.

speaker: Idgrod
dialogue: We are all up to something, my dear. All is as it should be.

speaker: Idgrod
dialogue: What troubles you, husband?

speaker: Aslfur
dialogue: What? Oh, nothing. All is well.

speaker: Idgrod
dialogue: What troubles you, husband?

speaker: Aslfur
dialogue: It's Joric. I fear his condition is worse. He calls out in his sleep sometimes. I've heard Falion's name. What does it mean?

speaker: Idgrod
dialogue: Joric will be what Joric will be. Give it time.

speaker: Idgrod
dialogue: Well, I did hear that Ulfric Stormcloak was slain while defending Windhelm against a dragon, but it sounds too good to be true. I'll wager it was Ulfric himself who started the rumor. Maybe he thought it would bolster recruitment.

speaker: Idgrod
dialogue: You are troubled, Gorm.

speaker: Idgrod
dialogue: No, Gorm. I am simply telling you what I see.

speaker: Gorm
dialogue: Yes, okay. Well thank you.

speaker: Gorm
dialogue: How are you feeling, Jarl Idgrod?

speaker: Idgrod
dialogue: The visions continue to hold me in balance, Gorm.

speaker: Gorm
dialogue: So, the same then.

speaker: Idgrod
dialogue: Do not worry, my friend. All is well.

speaker: Idgrod Ravencrone
dialogue: You are looking after your brother, yes?

speaker: Idgrod Ravencrone
dialogue: Good. He must be kept safe from harm.

speaker: Idgrod the Younger
dialogue: What sort of harm? Have you had a vision?

speaker: Idgrod Ravencrone
dialogue: No, no. Just watch over him.

speaker: Idgrod the Younger
dialogue: I will be Jarl someday, mother?

speaker: Idgrod Ravencrone
dialogue: That is what the Divines have planned for you, yes.

speaker: Idgrod the Younger
dialogue: Have you... Do you see that future? Will I be a good leader?

speaker: Idgrod Ravencrone
dialogue: All things are possible, my child. But I believe it is within you to succeed.

speaker: Idgrod the Younger
dialogue: Someday I'll be Jarl. Mother reminds me often. I hope I can help the people of Morthal the way she has.

speaker: Idgrod Ravencrone
dialogue: You are looking after your brother, yes?

speaker: Idgrod the Younger
dialogue: Yes, mother.

speaker: Idgrod Ravencrone
dialogue: Good. He must be kept safe from harm.

speaker: Idgrod the Younger
dialogue: What sort of harm? Have you had a vision?

speaker: Idgrod Ravencrone
dialogue: No, no. Just watch over him.

speaker: Idgrod the Younger
dialogue: I will be Jarl someday, mother?

speaker: Idgrod Ravencrone
dialogue: That is what the Divines have planned for you, yes.

speaker: Idgrod the Younger
dialogue: Have you... Do you see that future? Will I be a good leader?

speaker: Idgrod Ravencrone
dialogue: All things are possible, my child. But I believe it is within you to succeed.

speaker: Idolaf Battle-Born
dialogue: Sooner or later, we all have to choose a side.

speaker: Idolaf
dialogue: We'll pay whatever it takes. But we must have more swords for the Imperial soldiers.

speaker: Adrianne
dialogue: I just can't fill an order that size on my own. Why don't you swallow that stubborn pride of yours and ask Eorlund Gray-Mane for help?

speaker: Idolaf
dialogue: Ha! I'd sooner bend my knee to Ulfric Stormcloak. Besides, Gray-Mane would never make steel for the Legion.

speaker: Adrianne
dialogue: Have it your way. I'll take the job, but don't expect a miracle.

speaker: Olfrid
dialogue: Foolish old woman! You know nothing! Nothing of our struggles, our suffering!

speaker: Fralia
dialogue: Nothing? And what of my son, hmm? What of Thorald? Is he nothing? So don't talk to me about suffering!

speaker: Idolaf
dialogue: Your son chose his side, and he chose poorly. And now he's gone. Such is the way of war. The sooner you accept his loss, the better.

speaker: Fralia
dialogue: I will never accept his death! My son still lives. I feel it in my heart. So tell me, Battle-Borns, where is he? Where are you holding my Thorald?

speaker: Idolaf
dialogue: Come on, father. There's nothing more to be said here.

speaker: Jarl Igmund
dialogue: Forsworn have troubled the Reach for too long. I intend to deal with them.

speaker: Igmund
dialogue: More settlements have sent riders to say dragons are being spotted throughout Skyrim. The Forsworn ambush our roads and dragons cloud the skies. Is there any good news?

speaker: Raerek
dialogue: Umm.... No, my Jarl. I'm afraid there isn't.

speaker: Raerek
dialogue: Igmund, we need to talk about the Silver-Blood family.

speaker: Igmund
dialogue: What about them? They seem loyal enough.

speaker: Raerek
dialogue: Loyal? Thongvor supports Ulfric and his Stormcloaks! We should imprison the entire family as a precaution.

speaker: Faleen
dialogue: I second that, Igmund. Who knows what that family will do for power? They could be working with the Forsworn for all we know.

speaker: Igmund
dialogue: Enough! We can't imprison the very people who own the jail we would be throwing them into. The Silver-Bloods are to be left alone, am I clear?

speaker: Raerek
dialogue: Yes, my Jarl.

speaker: Faleen
dialogue: Yes, my Jarl.

speaker: Raerek
dialogue: My Jarl, we need to discuss Markarth's collapsing trade with the other Holds.

speaker: Igmund
dialogue: Of course there's a collapse in trade. The Stormcloaks stalk every road and the Forsworn attack every caravan.

speaker: Faleen
dialogue: Not to mention the rebels completely control Windhelm and all of Eastmarch hold.

speaker: Igmund
dialogue: Why do you pester me with battles we can't win? I need my steward to plan for victory, not nag me with every ill account.

speaker: Raerek
dialogue: Forgive me for worrying about the furture of Markarth. The lifeblood of the city is gold, Igmund, and it doesn't stop beating because there's a war on.

speaker: Raerek
dialogue: It's not that simple, Igmund. There are reports of Forsworn here in the city.

speaker: Igmund
dialogue: It doesn't matter if they're in the city. We fight them where they live, we won't have to fight them here.

speaker: Raerek
dialogue: They live here too, my Jarl. That's what I'm telling you.

speaker: Igmund
dialogue: Raerek, how is The Reach faring against this Forsworn menace?

speaker: Raerek
dialogue: Things are bad, Igmund. Our forces are barely able to keep the Forsworn in check. Merchants are reporting the loss of more of their shipments.

speaker: Igmund
dialogue: This is why I say we take the fight to them. Gather the Legion and drive those blasted beasts out of the Reach for good.

speaker: Faleen
dialogue: And what do Legion soldiers know about the hills the Reach? And the caves that make up those hills? The Forsworn can hide and ambush every assault.

speaker: Raerek
dialogue: The safety of the city and our settlements must be our only concern, Igmund. The rest of the Reach is on its own.

speaker: Igmund
dialogue: Cowards, the both of you. My father would not sit idly back and wait while evil men take over his lands. We're done discussing this for now.

speaker: Illdi
dialogue: You know, I don't get the impression that I'm very well-liked at the College.

speaker: Viarmo
dialogue: How are your students coming along?

speaker: Pantea
dialogue: Passably. Aia is my star pupil; none of the others can hold a candle to her, especially not that wretched Illdi.

speaker: Viarmo
dialogue: Try not to play favorites, Lady Ateia. It does a disservice to the whole class.

speaker: Pantea
dialogue: Yes, Headmaster.

speaker: Ataf
dialogue: I think Illdi's better than Dean Pantea actually knows. She just gets intimidated when she's in class and can't sing.

speaker: Jorn
dialogue: I think someone has a crush on Illdi.

speaker: Inge
dialogue: Your solo performance is about a week away. I expect to hear your early rendition tomorrow, understand?

speaker: Illdi
dialogue: Oh, thank you! I've been working on an original piece. I hope it can stand up to the classics!

speaker: Inge
dialogue: I'll be the judge of that. Now, back to your practice.

speaker: Evette
dialogue: A bit of warming wine, Illdi? You know you can't resist.

speaker: Illdi
dialogue: Not fair. You're well aware I can't seem to get warm here.

speaker: Ilia
dialogue: Greetings, mother.

speaker: Silvia
dialogue: Daughter. Who is this you have brought me?

speaker: Ilia
dialogue: I found a willing subject for you. Payment has already been discussed, of course.

speaker: Silvia
dialogue: I'll just prepare the subject now...

speaker: Ilia
dialogue: I can't let you do this, mother. You have to die now!

speaker: Imedhnain
dialogue: Lisbet handles the customers. I just check the shipments.

speaker: Imperial Captain
dialogue: Forget the list. He goes to the block.

speaker: Captain
dialogue: Get these prisoners out of the carts. Move it!

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: Why are we stopping?

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Why do you think? End of the line. Let's go. Shouldn't keep the gods waiting for us.

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: No! Wait! We're not rebels!

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Face your death with some courage, thief.

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: You've got to tell them! We weren't with you! This is a mistake!

speaker: Captain
dialogue: Step towards the block when we call your name. One at a time.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Empire loves their damn lists.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Ulfric Stormcloak. Jarl of Windhelm.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: It has been an honor, Jarl Ulfric!

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Ralof of Riverwood. Lokir of Rorikstead.

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: No, I'm not a rebel. You can't do this!

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: You're not going to kill me!

speaker: Captain
dialogue: Anyone else feel like running?

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Wait. You there. Step forward. Who are you?

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: By your orders, Captain. I'm sorry. {{Hide|At least you'll die here, in your homeland|If the Dragonborn is a Nord}}. Follow the Captain, prisoner.

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Ulfric Stormcloak. Some here in Helgen call you a hero. But a hero doesn't use a power like The Voice to murder his king and usurp his throne.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: [muffled grunts]

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: You started this war, plunged Skyrim into chaos, and now the Empire is going to put you down, and restore the peace.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: What was that?

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: It's nothing. Carry on.

speaker: Captain
dialogue: Yes, General Tullius. Give them their last rites.

speaker: Priestess of Arkay
dialogue: As we commend your souls to Aetherius, blessings of the Eight Divines upon you, for you are the salt and earth of Nirn, our beloved...

speaker: Stormcloak Soldier
dialogue: For the love of Talos, shut up and let's get this over with.

speaker: Priestess of Arkay
dialogue: As you wish.

speaker: Stormcloak Soldier
dialogue: Come on, I haven't got all morning. My ancestors are smiling at me, Imperials. Can you say the same?

speaker: Stormcloak
dialogue: You Imperial bastards!

speaker: Ingrid
dialogue: Death to the Stormcloaks!

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: As fearless in death as he was in life.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: There it is again. Did you hear that?

speaker: Captain
dialogue: I said, next prisoner!

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: To the block, prisoner. Nice and easy.

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: What in Oblivion is that?

speaker: Captain
dialogue: Sentries! What do you see?

speaker: Imperial
dialogue: It's in the clouds!

speaker: Alduin
dialogue: [Meteor-shower shout]

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Don't just stand there! Kill that thing! Guards, get the townspeople to safety!

speaker: Captain
dialogue: Come on soldier! Keep moving!

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: It's the Imperials! Take cover!

speaker: Captain
dialogue: Get this gate open. {{Hide|It's the escaped prisoners!

speaker: Imperial
dialogue: General Tullius, sir! The headsman is waiting!

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Good. Let's get this over with.

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: Shor, Mara, Dibella, Kynareth, Akatosh. Divines, please help me.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Look at him, General Tullius, the Military Governor. And it looks like the Thalmor are with him. Damn elves. I bet they had something to do with this. This is Helgen. I used to be sweet on a girl from here. Wonder if Vilod is still making that mead with juniper berries mixed in. Funny, when I was a boy, Imperial walls and towers used to make me feel so safe.

speaker: Haming
dialogue: Who are they, daddy? Where are they going?

speaker: Torolf
dialogue: You need to go inside, little cub.

speaker: Haming
dialogue: Why? I want to watch the soldiers.

speaker: Torolf
dialogue: Inside the house. Now.

speaker: Haming
dialogue: Yes, papa.

dialogue: Captain. What should we do? He/She's not on the list.

dialogue: Forget the list. He/She goes to the block.

speaker: Imperial
dialogue: It's in the clouds!

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Don't just stand there! Kill that thing! Guards, get the townspeople to safety!

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Hey, [race-dependent comment]. Get up! Come on, the gods won't give us another chance!

speaker: Imperial Soldier
dialogue: The wounds are deep, Vilod! I can't stop the blood.

speaker: Vilod
dialogue: Tell my family I fought bravely.

speaker: Imperial Soldier
dialogue: Come on. Give me your hand, I'm getting you out of here.

speaker: Vilod
dialogue: It's too late for that. Leave me. Save yourself.

speaker: Captain Valmir
dialogue: The research I've done seems to indicate that Skorm Snow-Strider left part of his journal here after laying siege. I believe it should indicate how to enter the blocked off sections of the stronghold. I should warn you, Forelhost is quite haunted, but I'm sure you can handle it. Return to me here once you've obtained the staff.

speaker: Imperial Soldier
dialogue: Wait it's haunted? I don't like ghosts... let me think about this for a minute... Wait... who in the blazes is this?

speaker: Captain Valmir
dialogue: Oh! Um, he he... Hold on... I... I can explain...

speaker: Imperial Soldier
dialogue: Valmir, you rat. You're not a soldier at all! Must be one of the Thalmor!

speaker: Imperial Soldier 1
dialogue: I'm still sore where I took that arrow, I hate archers.

speaker: Imperial Soldier 1
dialogue: This Imperial armor is damn heavy.

speaker: Imperial Soldier 1
dialogue: I'm sick of waiting, when are we going to see some action?

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: What's the situation?

speaker: Imperial Soldier
dialogue: Stormcloaks were already camped out around the entrance when we got here. They don't know we're here yet, though.

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: Well, that's something at least.

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: I don't like the look of this. Perfect spot for an ambush. Ten to one they're just waiting for us on the other side.

speaker: Imperial Soldier
dialogue: But there isn't any other way through, Legate.

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: Let's not jump to conclusions, soldier. The Legion always finds a way. I'd rather take a moment and look around than walk blindly into an ambush. Auxiliary, see if you can find another way through. We'll charge in to help as soon as we hear fighting.

speaker: Imperial Soldier 1
dialogue: What in the nine holds is that?

speaker: Imperial Soldier 2
dialogue: Is this what killed that Stormcloak over there? Can't be. It looks like it's been dead for a hundred years.

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: Steady now. The Legion has faced down worse than a few dusty old bonewalkers. We're not leaving here until we get what we came for. Now let's keep moving

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: And this must be the Hall of Stories.

speaker: Imperial Soldier 1
dialogue: Oh... I've heard of this. These walls are supposed to show the history of the ancients who built this place.

speaker: Imperial Soldier 2
dialogue: Too bad we can't read these carvings. Who knows what secrets we'd uncover?

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: One thing at a time soldier. Focus on our primary mission. We're searching for the crown. Looks like we weren't the first ones here, either. Even if these carvings tell us where the crown is, I'm sure we're going to have to find a way through this door. See what you can figure out auxillary, I'm going to check out these carvings over here. Let me know if you find something.

speaker: Imperial Soldier
dialogue: You hear anything?

speaker: Imperial Soldier 2
dialogue: No, but I know they're out there. No other way they can come. Now shut up or you'll blow our ambush.

speaker: Imperial Soldier
dialogue: I don't like it. What are they waiting for?

speaker: Imperial Soldier 2
dialogue: Maybe they're so scared of you they ran away.

speaker: Imperial Soldier
dialogue: Hardly likely.

speaker: Imperial Soldier 2
dialogue: Just shut up and keep out of sight.

speaker: Imperial Soldier
dialogue: It must be the Stormcloaks, find them!

speaker: Imperial Soldier
dialogue: Sir! I... I have...

speaker: Cipius
dialogue: Take a moment to breathe, soldier.

speaker: Imperial Soldier
dialogue: But... Sir...

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: The outer walls are strong. If we can hold them there...

speaker: Cipius
dialogue: They have catapults.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Damnit. Where'd they get catapults? The city walls are already falling apart as it is.

speaker: Cipius
dialogue: My scouts tell me they're loading them with fire.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: So, he wants to take my city, walls intact.

speaker: Cipius
dialogue: The men will be fighting in the flames.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: My men are fearless. It's the Imperial milk drinkers I'm worried about.

speaker: Cipius
dialogue: If you prefer I took my men and left...

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: No. Of course not. Just - don't let me down Cipius. We'll need to set up water brigades to combat the flames.

speaker: Cipius
dialogue: Already taken care of.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: You Imperials are efficient, I'll give you that. How long until they arrive?

speaker: Cipius
dialogue: Not long. They're hiding in the country side.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Damnit. What's he waiting for?

speaker: Imperial Soldier
dialogue: Sir, they're on the move. They'll be at the gates at any moment!

speaker: Cipius
dialogue: Why didn't you say so immediatly?!

speaker: Imperial Soldier
dialogue: Sir, I tried.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: This is it! Time to see what these Stormcloaks are made of.

speaker: Cipius
dialogue: The men are already gathering at the gates. Move it soldier. Spread the word. Go. Go. Go.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Oblivion take them. Every miserable last one of them.

speaker: Indara Caerellia
dialogue: How could people see all the graves of Falkreath and still want to make war?

speaker: Indaryn
dialogue: I'm the brewmaster around here. What did you want?

speaker: Inge Six Fingers
dialogue: You here to apply at the Bards College? Well don't bother―you're too damned old. Start past four, and it's all wasted effort.

speaker: Inge
dialogue: Your solo performance is about a week away. I expect to hear your early rendition tomorrow, understand?

speaker: Aia
dialogue: At this point, I hardly see how your advice would improve it; it's flawless.

speaker: Inge
dialogue: I'll be the judge of that. Now, back to your practice.

speaker: Inge
dialogue: Your solo performance is about a week away. I expect to hear your early rendition tomorrow, understand?

speaker: Jorn
dialogue: I've converted the classic tale of Eyldi the Bear to be performed with drums. I think you'll be impressed!

speaker: Inge
dialogue: I'll be the judge of that. Now, back to your practice.

speaker: Inge
dialogue: Your solo performance is about a week away. I expect to hear your early rendition tomorrow, understand?

speaker: Illdi
dialogue: Oh, thank you! I've been working on an original piece. I hope it can stand up to the classics!

speaker: Inge
dialogue: I'll be the judge of that. Now, back to your practice.

speaker: Viarmo
dialogue: How are your students coming along?

speaker: Inge
dialogue: Some of them have a long way to go, but they're mostly passable. Don't let them hear I said that, though!

speaker: Viarmo
dialogue: Of course not! Complacency is the bane of art. They're in good hands with you, Inge.

speaker: Inge
dialogue: Yes, Headmaster.

speaker: Ingrid
dialogue: Death to the Stormcloaks!

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: What was that?

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: It's nothing. Carry on.

speaker: Captain
dialogue: Yes, General Tullius. Give them their last rites.

speaker: Priestess of Arkay
dialogue: As we commend your souls to Aetherius, blessings of the Eight Divines upon you, for you are the salt and earth of Nirn, our beloved...

speaker: Stormcloak Soldier
dialogue: For the love of Talos, shut up and let's get this over with.

speaker: Priestess of Arkay
dialogue: As you wish.

speaker: Stormcloak
dialogue: You Imperial bastards!

speaker: Ingrid
dialogue: Death to the Stormcloaks!

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: As fearless in death as he was in life.

speaker: Captain
dialogue: Next, the [player race] in the rags!

speaker: Ingun Black-Briar
dialogue: It's exhilarating to observe the effects of my potions on the body. Watching the heart stop... the eyes go blind.

speaker: Ingun Black-Briar
dialogue: I don't understand, Elgrim. The formulas you're giving me are for novices but I've advanced well passed that point.

speaker: Elgrim
dialogue: Until you can do those formulas with your eyes shut, you'll never be ready to master the more difficult ones.

speaker: Ingun Black-Briar
dialogue: This is an utter waste of time.

speaker: Elgrim
dialogue: Ingun! If you want to remain in my shop as an apprentice I expect you to act like one. No exceptions!

speaker: Ingun Black-Briar
dialogue: Very well, I'll keep practicing them.

speaker: Elgrim
dialogue: Ingun, you clumsy fool! You've tainted our entire supply of Painted Troll Fat. You have no idea how hard that was to get.

speaker: Ingun Black-Briar
dialogue: I'm sure my mother can compensate you for it.

speaker: Elgrim
dialogue: I'll draft a letter to Rythe. If you could have it sent to Cheydinhal for me, that would make up for your blunder.

speaker: Ingun Black-Briar
dialogue: I'll make sure it's sent right away.

speaker: Maven Black-Briar
dialogue: Ingun, how much longer do you intend to waste your life concocting your foolish little potions?

speaker: Ingun Black-Briar
dialogue: I've told you, my interest in the family business is quite low. I wish to be much more than just a merchant.

speaker: Maven Black-Briar
dialogue: Your interests lay where I wish them to lay otherwise my favorite daughter may end up homeless and without a septim to her name. Is that clear?

speaker: Ingun Black-Briar
dialogue: Yes, mother.

speaker: Irgnir
dialogue: You should speak to the Jarl if you need something, stranger.

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: Oh yes, there have been attempts on the Jarl's life. More than one would-be assassin has met his end at the tip of my blade.

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: The Jarl has finally agreed to send you back to Riverwood.

speaker: Whiterun Guard
dialogue: Yes, Housecarl. We'll leave immediately.

speaker: Whiterun Guard 2
dialogue: It's just us against a dragon, is that it?

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: I can't afford to send anyone else. And we don't know where the dragon is. Your main job will be to keep an eye out and get the people to safety if the town is attacked. I don't expect the three of you to fight off a dragon by yourselves. But I do expect you to do your duty.

speaker: Whiterun Guard
dialogue: Of course. We'll keep Riverwood safe. You can count on it. Let's move out. Time's a wasting.

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: Farengar! Farengar, you need to come at once. A dragon's been sighted nearby. {{Hide|You|Referring to the Dragonborn}} should come, too.

speaker: Farengar
dialogue: A dragon! How exciting! Where was it seen? What was it doing?

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: I'd take this a bit more seriously if I were you. If a dragon decides to attack Whiterun, I don't know if we can stop it. Let's go.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: So, Irileth tells me you came from the western watchtower?

speaker: Whiterun Guard
dialogue: Yes, my lord.

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: Tell him what you told me. About the dragon.

speaker: Whiterun Guard
dialogue: Uh... that's right. We saw it coming from the south. It was fast... faster than anything I've ever seen.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Wat did it do? Is it attacking the watchtower?

speaker: Whiterun Guard
dialogue: No, my lord. It was just circling overhead when I left. I never ran so fast in my life... I thought it would come after me for sure.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Good work, son. We'll take it from here. Head down to the barracks for some food and rest. You've earned it. Irileth, you'd better gather some guardsmen and get down there.

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: I've already ordered my men to muster near the main gate.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Good. Don't fail me.

speaker: Farengar
dialogue: I should come along. I would very much like to see this dragon.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: No. I can't afford to risk both of you. I need you here working on ways to defend the city against these dragons.

speaker: Farengar
dialogue: As you command.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: One last thing, Irileth. This isn't a death or glory mission. I need to know what we're dealing with.

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: Don't worry, my lord. I'm the very soul of caution.

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: Here's the situation. A dragon is attacking the Western Watchtower.

speaker: Whiterun Guard
dialogue: A dragon?

speaker: Whiterun Guard 2
dialogue: Now we're in for it.

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: You heard right! I said a dragon! I don't much care where it came from or who sent it. What I do know is that it's made the mistake of attacking Whiterun!

speaker: Whiterun Guard
dialogue: But Housecarl... how can we fight a dragon?

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: That's a fair question. None of us have ever seen a dragon before, or expected to see one in battle. But we are honorbound to fight it, even if we fail. This dragon is threatening our homes... our families. Could you call yourselves Nords if you ran from this monster? Are you going to let me face this thing alone?

speaker: Whiterun Guard
dialogue: No, Housecarl!

speaker: Whiterun Guard 2
dialogue: We're so dead...

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: But it's more than our honor at stake here. Think of it - the first dragon seen in Skyrim since the last age. The glory of killing it is ours, if you're with me! Now what do you say? Shall we go kill us a dragon?

speaker: Whiterun Guard 2
dialogue: Damn right!

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: Let's move out.

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: No signs of any dragon right now, but it sure looks like he's been here. I know it looks bad, but we've got to figure out what happened. And if that dragon is still skulking around somewhere. Spread out and look for survivors. We need to know what we're dealing with.

speaker: Whiterun Guard
dialogue: No! Get back! It's still here somewhere! Hroki and Tor just got grabbed when they tried to make a run for it!

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: Guardsman! What happened here? Where's this dragon? Quickly now!

speaker: Whiterun Guard
dialogue: I don't know! Kynareth save us, here he comes again...

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: Here he comes! Find cover and make every arrow count!

speaker: Whiterun Guard
dialogue: Dragonborn? What are you talking about?

speaker: Whiterun Guard 2
dialogue: That's right! My grandfather used to tell stories about the Dragonborn. Those born with the Dragon Blood in 'em. Like old Tiber Septim himself.

speaker: Whiterun Guard
dialogue: I never heard of Tiber Septim killing any dragons.

speaker: Whiterun Guard 3
dialogue: There weren't any dragons then, idiot. They're just coming back now for the first time in... forever. But the old tales tell of the Dragonborn who could kill dragons and steal their power. {{Hide|You|Referring to the Last Dragonborn}} must be one!

speaker: Whiterun Guard 4
dialogue: What do you say Irileth? You're being awfully quiet.

speaker: Whiterun Guard 5
dialogue: Come on, Irileth, tell us, do you believe in this Dragonborn business?

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: Hmph. Some of you would be better off keeping quiet than flapping your gums on matters you don't know anything about. Here's a dead dragon, and that's something I definitely understand. Now we know we can kill them. But I don't need some mythical Dragonborn. Someone who can put down a dragon is more than enough for me.

speaker: Whiterun Guard 3
dialogue: You wouldn't understand, Housecarl. You ain't a Nord.

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: I've been all across Tamriel. I've seen plenty of things just as outlandish as this. I'd advise you all to trust in the strength of your sword arm over tales and legends.

speaker: Whiterun Guard 3
dialogue: If {{Hide|you|Referring to the Last Dragonborn}} really are Dragonborn, like the old tales, you aught to be able to Shout. Can you? Have you tried?

speaker: Whiterun Guard 3
dialogue: That was Shouting, what you just did! Must be. You really are dragonborn, then...

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Proventus, what do you make of all this? If Ulfric were to attack Whiterun...

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: As in all things, lord, caution... I urge us to wait and see.

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: Prey waits.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: I'm of a mind with Irileth. It's time to act.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: You plan to march on Windhelm?

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: I'm not a fool, Proventus. I mean it's time to challenge Ulfric to face me as a man, or march his Stormcloaks up to the gates.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: He'll do no such thing! A dagger in the back is all you could expect!

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: He was rather straightforward with Torygg.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: Torygg? He simply walked up to the boy and murdered him!

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: True. He's already proven his personal strength. Now he seeks to prove his army's.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: Then might I urge you to consider General Tullius' request? I mean, if you are bent on offending Jarl Ulfric...

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: Ulfric is the one who has offended. But, Proventus has a point. Ulfric has made it clear; in his mind, to refuse his claim is to side with the Empire.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: And what harm is there in letting a few Legionnaires die in place of your own men?

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: It seems cowardly.

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: Was it cowardly then to accept the White-Gold Concordat?

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: This again? That was different. Was I given a chance to object to the terms of the treaty? No. The Jarls weren't asked. We were told. And we had to like it.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: The chests of gold didn't hurt.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Damnit! This isn't about gold!

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: It's time to decide.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: Lord, wait. Let us see if Ulfric is serious.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Oh, he's serious. But so am I.

speaker: Farengar
dialogue: Incredible! Uh... sir, you have no idea how long I have waited for such an opportunity! I would be most appreciative if you would permit me to perform some, ah, tests on you. Purely in the interests of the advancement of knowledge.

speaker: Odahviing
dialogue: Begone, mage. Do not test my promise to the Dovahkiin.

speaker: Farengar
dialogue: I assure you, you will not even notice me. Most of them are hardly painful at all to a large dragon such as yourself.

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: Farengar, very bad idea. Even for you.

speaker: Farengar
dialogue: Surely you won't miss a few scales... or a small amount of blood...

speaker: Odahviing
dialogue: Joor mey! What are you doing back there? Yol... Toor...Shul!

speaker: Jarl Balgruuf the Greater
dialogue: Farengar! Enough, fool!

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: Balgruuf, did you slip out again last night for a drink at the Bannered Mare?

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Heard about that, did you? Yes, I went out for a pint or two. What of it?

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: These secret visits to the tavern will make you an easy target for an enemy assassin. You should have told me first.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Damn it, woman, I'm the Jarl of Whiterun! I won't apologize for talking to my people. You can't protect me every moment of the day.

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: That might be so, but it will never stop me from trying.

speaker: Irnskar Ironhand
dialogue: When I was a young rascal, I broke a man's arm with a single punch. Course, I had a horseshoe hidden in my glove...

speaker: Bryling
dialogue: What news have you heard from the war, Irnskar?

speaker: Irnskar
dialogue: You won't like it, my lady.

speaker: Bryling
dialogue: I'm well aware that I won't like it. But it's my duty to keep my people safe. Tell me.

speaker: Irnskar
dialogue: Possession of the holds change on an almost daily basis, but I can report that Haafingar is still secure. Your people are safe.

speaker: Bryling
dialogue: I'm not just talking about my subjects. I'm talking about my people: the proud Nords of Skyrim.

speaker: Irnskar
dialogue: I told you you wouldn't like the news.

speaker: Irnskar
dialogue: My lady, I'm pleased to inform you that you have a new gown for court, specially tailored by madame Endarie.

speaker: Bryling
dialogue: Really? How did we afford that? Besides, I like the gown I already have.

speaker: Irnskar
dialogue: Madame Endarie insisted. She made it free of charge, in honor of your lenience about last month's rent discrepancies.

speaker: Bryling
dialogue: That was suspiciously nice of her. I thought she hated everyone.

speaker: Irnskar
dialogue: She does, my lady. But apparently, she hates you just a little less than the others.

speaker: J'darr
dialogue: What? Who is this, Brother? Another of the smooth skins looking for food? But this one wasn't trapped with us...

speaker: J'Kier
dialogue: Has the Bloodmoon called you, fellow Hunter?

speaker: J'zargo
dialogue: Oh, yes. J'zargo hopes to find things that will make him a more powerful mage here.

speaker: Tolfdir
dialogue: Welcome, welcome! We were just beginning. Please, stay and listen. So, as I was saying, the first thing to understand is that magic is, by its very nature, volatile and dangerous. Unless you can control it, it can and will destroy you.

speaker: Brelyna
dialogue: Sir, I think we all understand that fairly well. We wouldn't be here if we couldn't control magic!

speaker: Tolfdir
dialogue: Of course, my dear. Of course. You all certainly possess some inherent natural ability. That much is not being questioned. What I'm talking about is true control, mastery of magic. It takes years, if not decades, of practice and study.

speaker: Tolfdir
dialogue: Please, please! This is exactly what I'm talking about. Eagerness must be tempered with caution, or else disaster is inevitable.

speaker: Onmund
dialogue: But we've only just arrived here -- you've no idea what any of us are capable of. Why not give us a chance to show you what we can do?

speaker: Onmund
dialogue: We're all pretty new to this, right? Let's just give it a chance. What's the worst that could happen?

speaker: Tolfdir
dialogue: All right, let's settle down. I suppose we can try something practical... In continuing with our theme of safety, we'll start with Wards. Wards are protective spells that block magic. I'll teach you all a ward, and we'll see if you can successfully use it to block spells, all right?

speaker: Tolfdir
dialogue: All right, let's settle down. I suppose we can try something practical... In continuing with our theme of safety, we'll start with Wards. Wards are protective spells that block magic. I'll teach you all a ward, and we'll see if you can successfully use it to block spells, all right?

speaker: Tolfdir
dialogue: All right, let's settle down. I suppose we can try something practical... In continuing with our theme of safety, we'll start with Wards. Wards are protective spells that block magic. I'll teach you all a ward, and we'll see if you can successfully use it to block spells, all right?

speaker: Jala
dialogue: You look like you could do with a ripe apple. Or a tomato, cabbage, or leek?

speaker: Svari
dialogue: They can't hurt uncle Roggvir. Tell them he didn't do it.

speaker: Addvar
dialogue: Svari, you need to go home. Go home and stay there until your mother comes.

speaker: Aldis
dialogue: Lock the city gate.

speaker: Vivienne
dialogue: You should tell her that her uncle is scum that betrayed his High King. Best she know now, Addvar.

speaker: Addvar
dialogue: You're all heart, Vivienne.

speaker: Aldis
dialogue: Roggvir. You helped Ulfric Stormcloak escape this city after he murdered High King Torygg. By opening that gate for Ulfric you betrayed the people of Solitude.

speaker: Sorex
dialogue: He doesn't deserve to speak!

speaker: Roggvir
dialogue: There was no murder! Ulfric challenged Torygg. He beat the High King in fair combat.

speaker: Roggvir
dialogue: Such as our way! Such as the ancient custom of Skyrim, and all Nords!

speaker: Vivienne
dialogue: Cut 'em down!

speaker: Aldis
dialogue: Guard. Prepare the prisoner.

speaker: Roggvir
dialogue: I don't need your help.

speaker: Aldis
dialogue: Very well, Roggvir. Bow your head.

speaker: Roggvir
dialogue: On this day... I go to Sovngarde.

speaker: Jala
dialogue: Brave man, with the Blackbloods out there. Did you catch anything?

speaker: Ataf
dialogue: Naw, mostly just froze.

speaker: Jala
dialogue: Well, keep at it. The fish have to get to know you before they're willing to bite.

speaker: Ataf
dialogue: Um, excuse me. Could I buy two leeks?

speaker: Jala
dialogue: Fine, Ataf. You should eat some more tomatoes, though.

speaker: Ataf
dialogue: My mother always used to say that too.

speaker: Jaree-Ra
dialogue: If you're looking for opportunities to make some coin, well... I'm your man.

speaker: Jaree
dialogue: You might want to rethink that. You're missing out on some opportunities, working in that bar.

speaker: Jawanan
dialogue: Ah, yet another new face. I'm from Hammerfell, you see. I can hardly keep track of all the people I've been meeting.

speaker: Jawanan
dialogue: I think I may wait until the Burning of King Olaf to have a Spiced Wine.

speaker: Fihada
dialogue: How's it coming there, Jawanan?

speaker: Jawanan
dialogue: Slow, but looking good, sir.

speaker: Fihada
dialogue: Slow's the only way to do it! Work too hard and you'll warp the wood.

speaker: Jawanan
dialogue: Fihada, where did you learn how to make bows so well?

speaker: Fihada
dialogue: The same place I learned my charm and quick wits; I used to be an Imperial ranger, my boy!

speaker: Jawanan
dialogue: Wish I could learn some of that charm. I'm just good with bows, not people.

speaker: Fihada
dialogue: You'd make a better Imperial ranger than me. I may have charmed the locals, but my fellow soldiers hated my waggling tongue.

speaker: Jenassa
dialogue: Blade and shadow, silence and death - these are my arts. For a modest fee, I'll make great art for you.

speaker: Jervar
dialogue: Father says I ain't smart enough to be stablemaster. Some day.

speaker: Jesper
dialogue: I'm just trying to make a living. I've no interest in trouble.

speaker: Jod
dialogue: My only aim is to keep the peace.

speaker: Jod
dialogue: My Jarl, I have concerns about the safety of Dawnstar.

speaker: Skald
dialogue: Safety? Don't I have you to handle the town's safety? What is this about, Jod?

speaker: Jod
dialogue: You keep pledging more and more of our guard to the frontlines. The way this is going, we won't be able to defend our own borders.

speaker: Skald
dialogue: Nonsense. The best place for our men is driving the Imperials back. I will ensure that men from Dawnstar get every opportunity for glory.

speaker: Jod
dialogue: Glory is meaningless if they have no home to return to. I urge you to lower our commitments to the front until I'm sure we're safe.

speaker: Skald
dialogue: I won't have you rob our soldiers of their chance to drive out the Empire. I'm done discussing this, Jod.

speaker: Skald
dialogue: We are poised for glory, Jod. The Empire will never take Dawnstar while every last man, woman, and child here draws breathe!

speaker: Jod
dialogue: With respect, Jarl. You can't ask everyone to throw themselves against trained Legionnaires. Let's leave the fighting to the Stormcloaks.

speaker: Skald
dialogue: You're right. Why dilute the glory with too many souls fighting over it? We'll drive out the Empire and be celebrated as heroes when we win.

speaker: Jod
dialogue: If we win. This war is going to drag on for years. I can feel it. We need to prepare for a long struggle ahead.

speaker: Skald
dialogue: Enough of your dire predictions! We will talk about this another time.

speaker: Jofthor
dialogue: If you ever settle down to have children, think twice before you do it.

speaker: Jon Battle-Born
dialogue: People have forgotten humor, poetry and romance. I love a good sword fight as much as the next man, but there's more to life.

speaker: Jon
dialogue: So I'm, uh... writing a song for you...

speaker: Olfina
dialogue: Why, Jon Battle-Born, you're writing me a song? Does it somehow involve blood, or beheadings, or the honor of my forebears?

speaker: Jon
dialogue: Well, that's where I started. But it turned into something of a ballad.

speaker: Olfina
dialogue: A ballad? Oh, now I know you're joking with me.

speaker: Jon
dialogue: It's all true, I swear it. You can hear it when it's done. I'll just need a year or two to smooth the rough edges.

speaker: Olfina
dialogue: Ha! I thought as much.

speaker: Olfina
dialogue: So have you spoken to that man from the Bards College?

speaker: Jon
dialogue: No, not yet. But I will. I just haven't... gotten around to it yet.

speaker: Olfina
dialogue: Oh Jon, stop dallying. You know you have to go. It's why Mara put you on this earth. You think a few miles can truly keep us apart?

speaker: Jon
dialogue: You mean you won't forget about me the moment I'm out of sight? Get yourself a nice old rich husband, have sixteen babies?

speaker: Olfina
dialogue: Tsk. You've uncovered my master plan. Now I suppose you'll never leave.

speaker: Jon
dialogue: I want to see you when you're done working.

speaker: Olfina
dialogue: I can't. Not tonight. I need to go home. I swear, my father is starting to suspect something.

speaker: Jon
dialogue: That's your imagination running wild. Nobody knows how we feel about each other.

speaker: Olfina
dialogue: Don't talk about my father like that, Jon. And the answer's still no. But tomorrow, definitely.

speaker: Jon
dialogue: Sing you a special song tonight, beautiful lass?

speaker: Olfina
dialogue: Not now, I'm working.

speaker: Jon
dialogue: Bah. You're always working. Why else would I spend so much time here?

speaker: Olfina
dialogue: Mikael is quite the songbird. Maybe he's the reason you're here all the time.

speaker: Jon
dialogue: Aye, the bard's got talent, I'll give him that. You just make sure his music is the only thing you're admiring.

speaker: Olfina
dialogue: Oh Jon, darling. You know you're the only stone-biting, knuckle-dragging Nord for me.

speaker: Jon
dialogue: Ha! That's my girl.

speaker: Jonna
dialogue: Runnin' an inn weren't my plan. But, Falion decided to move here, so I joined him.

speaker: Alva
dialogue: Why, good evening Jonna!

speaker: Jonna
dialogue: What can I getcha, Alva?

speaker: Alva
dialogue: What can't you get me, sweetie?

speaker: Jonna
dialogue: Umm... Did you want somethin' to eat?

speaker: Alva
dialogue: Eat? No, I don't think I'm... hungry. Not now, at least.

speaker: Jonna
dialogue: Right. Okay, tell me if you change yer mind.

speaker: Jonna
dialogue: When are you gonna do somethin' to help Falion? Stop people sayin' things about him?

speaker: Jonna
dialogue: They got used to Idgrod just fine, didn't they? So what's the difference?

speaker: Aslfur
dialogue: Yes, well. Perhaps you're right.

speaker: Aslfur
dialogue: How's business?

speaker: Jonna
dialogue: Very funny.

speaker: Aslfur
dialogue: No, I... I was just asking.

speaker: Jonna
dialogue: It's as bad as ever.

speaker: Lurbuk
dialogue: Jonna, do you think that the townspeople are warming to my serenades?

speaker: Jonna
dialogue: No. They ain't. And they aren't gonna. If you weren't paying for your room, I'd have thrown you out a long time ago.

speaker: Lurbuk
dialogue: Yes. But they'll come around. You'll see.

speaker: Jonna
dialogue: Oh. I wouldn't be surprised if they came 'round. And you're never seen or heard from again.

speaker: Lurbuk
dialogue: I'm thinking about composing a song about you, Jonna. Would you prefer I proclaim your beauty, your strength, your...

speaker: Jonna
dialogue: Nah. Just...don't. Leave me outta it.

speaker: Lurbuk
dialogue: No interest in being immortalized in song? Remembered and praised for all eternity?

speaker: Jonna
dialogue: No. I mean it.

speaker: Lurbuk
dialogue: When I'm known throughout Tamriel, you'll regret this decision.

speaker: Jora
dialogue: Oblivion take the Thalmor! I'll never give up Talos, not even if it means my life. Let them come and make me a martyr!

speaker: Niranye
dialogue: Hello, Jora. I'm glad to see you. In fact, I was just thinking about you and your husband.

speaker: Jora
dialogue: Is that so? And what were you thinking, exactly?

speaker: Niranye
dialogue: Well, I've heard awful stories about these Thalmor, and how they're rounding up everyone who still worships Talos. The interrogations are quite merciless, from what I've heard. I fear for you and your husband, should the Thalmor come here. But perhaps there's a way I can help.

speaker: Jora
dialogue: I doubt Ulfric would let Thalmor into Windhelm without a fight. But please, do continue. How would you help us?

speaker: Niranye
dialogue: Well, let's just say that I know some people who are experts at helping others disappear when they need to. They are discreet and thorough, though not inexpensive. I hope you'll keep that in mind, should the worst come to pass.

speaker: Jora
dialogue: We accept the risks that come with our faith, but I'll keep your offer in mind. Thank you, Niranye.

speaker: Elda
dialogue: Oh, Jora. Good to see you. I was wondering if you might ask Lortheim something for me.

speaker: Jora
dialogue: Don't bother. I don't have much chance of seeing my husband these days. He's always up in the palace with Ulfric.

speaker: Elda
dialogue: Oh, I'm sorry to hear that. Is everything all right?

speaker: Jora
dialogue: It's been better, I'll be honest with you.

speaker: Elda
dialogue: Here, let me get you some mead. This one's on me.

speaker: Jora
dialogue: I just don't know what to do anymore. He's hardly ever in the temple. I see him at breakfast, and that's it.

speaker: Elda
dialogue: I know, dear. He's a busy man, though, and loyal to the Stormcloaks.

speaker: Jora
dialogue: What about being loyal to his wife?

speaker: Elda
dialogue: I... I'm sorry, dear, I've got some other customers. I'll be back around in a minute.

speaker: Jorgen, on Sorli the Builder
dialogue: The world's going mad, and our Jarl doesn't care. She's only in it for herself.

speaker: Jorgen
dialogue: What's the Jarl going to do about it?

speaker: Jorgen
dialogue: We have no need for wizards in our midst!

speaker: Thonnir
dialogue: Morthal has enough problems as it is!

speaker: Jorgen
dialogue: Bah, its no use. Let's get back to it then.

speaker: Jorgen
dialogue: And it looks creepy, too.

speaker: Thonnir
dialogue: Cowards! We must kill the vampires! We have to make them pay!

speaker: Joric
dialogue: I get lost sometimes. I'm not sure where I go, but I'm not... I'm not here.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Galmar thinks we should double our men in the Reach.

speaker: Jorleif
dialogue: A reasonable strategy.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: And you, Jorleif?

speaker: Jorleif
dialogue: Well, sir, the hold of Falkreath is fairly vulnerable, and blocks the only road from Cyrodiil.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: A good point, old friend.

speaker: Jorleif
dialogue: To be sure, my lord, I am not skilled in the arts of war or military tactics.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: But you're able to see the whole in the parts, and for that I'm grateful.

speaker: Jorleif
dialogue: As you wish, sir.

speaker: Jorleif
dialogue: Sir, there continues to be unrest in the Gray Quarter.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Blasted dark elves. I don't suppose you could tell them that I presently have larger concerns? Such as all of Skyrim?

speaker: Jorleif
dialogue: They don't seem to be very sympathetic to our cause, sir.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Let me know if you hear anything more substantial.

speaker: Jorleif
dialogue: Of course, my lord.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Jorleif, I want you to send a messenger to our western camps.

speaker: Jorleif
dialogue: And the message, sir?

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: I'm diverting Gar and Haddring's men to join him.

speaker: Jorleif
dialogue: Is that wise, sir?

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: It will work if we can pull Hran's men from the south. And find a bit of luck.

speaker: Jorleif
dialogue: Of course. Something that seems to be in short supply these days.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: I'm not seeking advice right now, friend. Just send the message.

speaker: Jorleif
dialogue: You. You're coming with me. We're finally going to arrest the Butcher.

speaker: Windhelm Guard
dialogue: Yes, sir.

speaker: Wuunferth
dialogue: What is the meaning of this?

speaker: Jorleif
dialogue: You're under {{Sicblock|the arrest|arrest}}, for the Murder of Susanna of Candlehearth Hall. And Friga Shatter-Shield. And all the rest. We're wise to your scheming, you coward.

speaker: Wuunferth
dialogue: Has the whole city lost their brains? I've been scrying and auguring to find the murderer myself.

speaker: Jorleif
dialogue: Make your excuses from the Bloodworks, wizard. Get him out of my sight.

speaker: Windhelm Guard
dialogue: Yes, sir! I'm sorry, sir. But you'll have to come with me.

speaker: Wuunferth
dialogue: This isn't over, Jorleif!

speaker: Jorn
dialogue: I wish only to graduate and enroll with the Legion. My drums will lead our troops to victory.

speaker: Inge
dialogue: Your solo performance is about a week away. I expect to hear your early rendition tomorrow, understand?

speaker: Jorn
dialogue: I've converted the classic tale of Eyldi the Bear to be performed with drums. I think you'll be impressed!

speaker: Inge
dialogue: I'll be the judge of that. Now, back to your practice.

speaker: Giraud
dialogue: Pardon me, but I trust you've been working on your poem, on the classical heroes of Skyrim, yes?

speaker: Jorn
dialogue: Yes sir, Professor Gemane! It's a war epic about Hoag Merkiller's last stand!

speaker: Giraud
dialogue: I'm sure it will be fine, just don't be late.

speaker: Ataf
dialogue: I think Illdi's better than Dean Pantea actually knows. She just gets intimidated when she's in class and can't sing.

speaker: Jorn
dialogue: I think someone has a crush on Illdi.

speaker: Jouane
dialogue: Yes, child?

speaker: Sissel
dialogue: I was just wondering. The next time we meet, do you think maybe you could teach me some fire magic? Nothing dangerous! Maybe a candle lighting spell?

speaker: Jouane
dialogue: By the Eight, keep your voice down! Do you want the entire village to learn our secrets?

speaker: Sissel
dialogue: Oh! I'm... I'm sorry. I didn't mean to upset you.

speaker: Jouane
dialogue: Shh shh. It's fine, child. It's fine. But we must be cautious, hmm? What we do, the things I teach you. The others wouldn't understand.

speaker: Sissel
dialogue: I understand. I'm sorry. I just get so excited thinking about it. So... can we. Do some fire magic?

speaker: Jouane
dialogue: Hmph. Most certainly not. But perhaps I can teach you how to put some candles out. We'll start there.

speaker: Sissel
dialogue: Oooh, wonderful! I can't wait!

speaker: Jouane
dialogue: Today I'll teach you a useful spell that might just save your life. If you should ever fall into a river, you'll be very glad you learned it.

speaker: Sissel
dialogue: Oh! Are you going to teach me how to turn into a mud crab?

speaker: Jouane
dialogue: Oh, it's much better than that. I will teach you how to breathe underwater, with no need to turn into one of those ugly creatures.

speaker: Sissel
dialogue: Wow! Then I could dive into a river and swim so far away that Britte and father could never find me.

speaker: Jouane
dialogue: Now, clear your mind and breathe deeply. Good concentration is very important for spellcasting.

speaker: Jouane
dialogue: I picked up a set of fine silver brushes in the city, Reldith. I thought you might be interested.

speaker: Reldith
dialogue: How thoughtful! I'll come take a look after supper.

speaker: Jouane
dialogue: The last time I was in Whiterun, the tradesmen were talking about you. It seems your reputation as a businessman is growing.

speaker: Ennis
dialogue: Glad to hear all my hard work has paid off. Maybe we'll fetch a better price for our crops next time we're in the city.

speaker: Jouane
dialogue: Anything I can pick up for you on my next trip into the city, Erik?

speaker: Erik
dialogue: Thanks for the offer, Jouane, but I'm saving up for a new sword.

speaker: Jouane
dialogue: Good day, Lemkil. I saw some nice dresses for your little girls while I was in Whiterun. I'd be happy to purchase them, if you like.

speaker: Lemkil
dialogue: We don't need your charity, Breton. If my girls deserve something nice, it'll be their father who buys it.

speaker: Rorik
dialogue: Looks like we're in for quite a harvest. We've had better luck with our planting than any village in the hold.

speaker: Jouane
dialogue: Luck? I think it has more to do with the hard work and good soil.

speaker: Rorik
dialogue: Maybe you're right. Even so, I can't help wondering if some other force it at work here.

speaker: Jouane
dialogue: The last wheat shipment fetched a fine price at market.

speaker: Rorik
dialogue: Well done! I don't know where I'd be without you, my old friend.

speaker: Jouane
dialogue: It pleases me to know that I can still be of use even in the twilight of my life.

speaker: Julienne Lylvieve
dialogue: Faida's teaching me the innkeeper's trade. She runs the Four Shields.

speaker: Jurgen Windcaller
dialogue: My disciples still follow the difficult path - the Way of the Voice is neither wide, nor easy.

speaker: Karita
dialogue: The Windpeak Inn features the finest bard in all of Dawnstar. Me.

speaker: Karita
dialogue: You beasts are the worst.

speaker: Stig
dialogue: Come now, dearie, surely we aren't all that bad.

speaker: Karita
dialogue: Just... leave me alone! I've brought your mead, now drink it and shut your filthy mouths.

speaker: Alding
dialogue: Oh, we've got other things in mind for our mouths, sweetie.

speaker: Karita
dialogue: Walking the Steps. Meditating on the emblems. I make this trip every few years.

speaker: Karl
dialogue: I'm no one special, just a miner who swings a pickaxe for his drinking money.

speaker: Beitild
dialogue: Keep at it. We need to work twice as hard now that fat-headed Leigelf has declared war!

speaker: Beitild
dialogue: No he isn't! He's the enemy, and we are going to crush him.

speaker: Karl
dialogue: Drafted into a war, how could my life get worse?

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: We may be Nightingales, but in our hearts we're still thieves and we're damn good at what we do.

speaker: Mercer Frey
dialogue: Do you honestly think your arrow will reach me before my blade finds your heart?

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: Give me a reason to try.

speaker: Mercer Frey
dialogue: You're a clever girl, Karliah. Buying Goldenglow Estate and funding Honningbrew Meadery was inspired.

speaker: Mercer Frey
dialogue: You always were a quick study.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: Not quick enough, otherwise Gallus would still be alive.

speaker: Mercer Frey
dialogue: Gallus had his wealth and he had you. All he had to do was look the other way.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: Did you forget your oath we took as Nightingales? Did you expect him to simply ignore your methods?

speaker: Mercer Frey
dialogue: Enough of all this mindless banter! Come on, Karliah. It's time for you and Gallus to become reunited!

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: I'm no fool, Mercer. Crossing blades with you would be a death sentence. But I can promise the next time we meet, it will be your undoing.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: Does the journal say where this wealth came from?

speaker: Enthir
dialogue: Yes. Gallus seems certain that Mercer had been removing funds from the Guild's treasury without anyone's knowledge.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: Anything else, Enthir? Anything about... the Nightingales?

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: Shadows preserve us. So it's true...

speaker: Enthir
dialogue: I'm not familiar with the Twilight Sepulcher. What is it? What's Mercer Frey done?

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: I'm sorry Enthir, I can't say. All that matters is we deliver your translation to the Guild immediately. Farewell, Enthir... words can't express...

speaker: Enthir
dialogue: It's alright Karliah. You don't have to say a word.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: You better have a damn good reason to be here with that murderer.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: Please, lower your weapons so we can speak. I have proof that you've all been misled!

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: No tricks, Karliah or I'll cut you down where you stand. Now what's this so-called proof you speak of?

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: I have Gallus' journal. I think you'll find its contents disturbing.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Let me see. No, it... it can't be. This can't be true. I've known Mercer too long...

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: It's true, Brynjolf. Every word. Mercer's been stealing from the Guild for years, right under your noses.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: There's only one way to find out if what the lass says is true. Delvin, I'll need you to open the Vault.

speaker: Delvin
dialogue: Wait just a blessed moment, Bryn. What's in that book? What did it say?

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: It says Mercer's been stealing from our vault for years. Gallus was looking into it before he was murdered.

speaker: Delvin
dialogue: How can Mercer open up a vault that needs two keys? It's impossible. Could he pick his way in?

speaker: Vex
dialogue: That door has the best puzzle locks money can buy. There's no way it can be picked open.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: He didn't need to pick the lock.

speaker: Delvin
dialogue: What's she on about?

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Use your key on the vault, Delvin. We'll open it up and find out the truth.

speaker: Delvin
dialogue: I've used my key, but the vault's still locked up tighter than a drum. Now use yours.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: By the Eight! It's gone, everything's gone! Get in here, all of you!

speaker: Delvin
dialogue: The gold, the jewels... it's all gone.

speaker: Vex
dialogue: That son-of-a-bitch! I'll kill him!

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Vex! Put it away... right now. We can't afford to lose our heads... we need to calm down and focus.

speaker: Delvin
dialogue: Do what he says, Vex. This isn't helpin' right now.

speaker: Vex
dialogue: Fine. We do it your way. For now.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Delvin, Vex... watch the Flagon. If you see Mercer, come tell me right away.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: Brynjolf, the time has come to decide Mercer's fate. Until a new Guild Master is chosen, the decision falls to you.

speaker: Brynjolf
