dialogue: Aye, lass... and I've come to a decision. Mercer Frey tried to kill both of you, he betrayed the Guild, murdered Gallus and made us question our future. He needs to die.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: We have to be very careful, Brynjolf. Mercer is a Nightingale, an Agent of Nocturnal.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Then it's all true... everything I heard in the stories. The Nightingales, their allegiance to Nocturnal and the Twilight Sepulcher.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: Yes. That's why we need to prepare ourselves and meet Mercer on equal footing. Just outside of Riften, beyond the Southeast Gate is a small path cut up the mountainside. At the end of that path is a clearing and an old standing stone. I'd ask you both meet me there.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: So, this is Nightingale Hall. I heard about this place when I joined the Guild, but I never believed it existed.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: The assumption that the Nightingales were just a myth was seeded within the Guild on purpose. It helped avert attention from our true nature. What's wrong, Brynjolf? I can almost hear your brow furrowing.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: I'm trying to understand why I'm here, lass. I'm no priest, and I'm certainly not religious. Why pick me?

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: This isn't about religion, Brynjolf... it's business. This is Nightingale Hall. You're the first of the uninitiated to set foot inside in over a century. Now, if you'll both proceed to the armory to don your Nightingale Armor, we can begin the Oath.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Okay, lass. We've got these getups on... now what?

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: Beyond this gate is the first step in becoming a Nightingale.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Woah there, lass. I appreciate the armor, but becoming a Nightingale? That was never discussed.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: To hold any hope of defeating Mercer, we must have Nocturnal at our backs. If she's to accept you as one of her own, an arrangement must be struck.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: What sort of arrangement? I need to know the terms.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: The terms are quite simple, Brynjolf. Nocturnal will allow you to become a Nightingale and use your abilities for whatever you wish. And in return, both in life and in death, you must serve as a guardian of the Twilight Sepulcher.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Aye, there's always a catch. But at this point, I suppose there isn't much to lose. If it means the end of Mercer Frey, you can count me in.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: I call upon you Lady Nocturnal, Queen of Murk and Empress of Shadow... hear my voice!

speaker: Nocturnal
dialogue: Ah, Karliah. I was wondering when I'd hear from you again. Lose something did we?

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: My Lady, I've come before you to throw myself upon your mercy and to accept responsibility for my failure.

speaker: Nocturnal
dialogue: You're already mine, Karliah. Your terms were struck long ago. What could you possibly offer me now?

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: I have two others that wish to transact the Oath; to serve you both in life and in death.

speaker: Nocturnal
dialogue: You surprise me, Karliah. This offer is definitely weighted in my favor.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: My appetite for Mercer's demise exceeds my craving for wealth, Your Grace.

speaker: Nocturnal
dialogue: Revenge? How interesting... Very well, the conditions are acceptable. You may proceed.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: Lady Nocturnal, we accept your terms. We dedicate ourselves to you as both your avengers and your sentinels. We will honor our agreement in this life and the next until your conditions have been met.

speaker: Nocturnal
dialogue: Very well. I name your initiates Nightingale and I restore your status to the same, Karliah. And in the future, I'd suggest you refrain from disappointing me again.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: Wait a moment... what's that? It's Mercer! Look... down there!

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: I'm on it, lass. Damn it! There's no way through.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: He's toying with us. He wants us to follow.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Aye, lass... and we'll be ready for him. Let's keep moving.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Look at the size of this place. Have you ever seen anything like it in your life, lass?

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: Can't say that I have. Imagine the riches hidden within these walls.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: So this is what we heard. The entire tower collapsed.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: The only reason to do that would be to block pursuit. It must be Mercer. We'll have to find another way around.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Mercer was able to knock this thing down? Gods...

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: It's the Key, Brynjolf. In his hands, there's no telling what he's capable of.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: Mercer must have triggered these pistons. We're going to have to search for a way to open them.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: I'll bet my last septim that there's a mechanism around here somewhere.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Shor's Bones! Look at that monstrosity.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: It's a Dwarven Centurion. Very tough and very deadly.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: We can take the beast on or sneak around. It's your call, {{Hide|lad|or lass, referring to the Dragonborn}}. We're right behind you.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: The stench... this place reeks of Falmer.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: This must be their hive. We'll have to keep silent if we want to avoid drawing their attention.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: There's a mass of the Falmer in this chamber. We can sneak through or take them down... I don't care. As long as we get to Mercer.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Aye. Whatever {{Hide|you|referring to the Dragonbrorn}} want to do, we're with you.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: He's close. I'm certain of it. We must prepare ourselves.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Then this is it. We do this for Gallus and for the Guild.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: He's here and he hasn't seen us yet. Brynjolf, watch the door.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Aye, lass. Nothing's getting by me.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: Climb down that ledge and see if you can...

speaker: Mercer
dialogue: Karliah, when will you learn you can't get the drop on me?

speaker: Mercer
dialogue: Karliah, I'll deal with you after I rid myself of your irksome companions. In the meantime, perhaps you and Brynjolf should get better acquainted.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: What's... what's happening... I can't stop myself.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: Damn you, Mercer! Fight it, Brynjolf... he's taken control of you!

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: I'm sorry lass, I... I can't...

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: Damn! This place is coming down! Quick, get the Skeleton Key and the Eye and lets get out of here!

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: No luck there, lass. Something must have fallen on the other side of the door because it isn't moving!

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: We have to find another way out of here before the place fills with water!

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Look, I've never been good at these things, so I'm just going to keep it short. Being Guild Master means more than just getting a cut of all the loot, it's about being a leader and keeping this rabble in order. With that in mind, I propose that the position of Guild Master should be {{Hide|yours|referring to the Dragonborn}}. Delvin?

speaker: Vex
dialogue: Sure, why not.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Everyone is in agreement, so all I can do now is name {{Hide|you|referring to the Dragonborn}} Guild Master and wish you good fortune and long life. Now everyone get back to work.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: Gallus! I feared I would never see you again. I was afraid you'd become like the others.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: What will you do now, my love?

speaker: Gallus
dialogue: Nocturnal calls me to the Evergloam. My contract has been fulfilled.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: Will I ever see you again?

speaker: Gallus
dialogue: When your debt to Nocturnal has been paid, we'll embrace once again.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: Farewell, Gallus. Eyes open... walk with the shadows.

speaker: Gallus
dialogue: Goodbye, Karliah.

speaker: Katla
dialogue: It's hard work keeping Solitude fed, but I wouldn't trust any other family to do it.

speaker: Katla
dialogue: Another gorgeous gray day, right dear?

speaker: Snilling
dialogue: It's too cold for my bones, but that never seems to stop you, dear.

speaker: Knud
dialogue: I'm gonna go play soldier with a tree!

speaker: Katla
dialogue: That's nice, son. Just don't stomp on the crop like last time!

speaker: Snilling
dialogue: I'll see if I can't get some work done inside, where it's warm.

speaker: Kayd
dialogue: Hey! Wanna play tag?

speaker: Keeper Carcette
dialogue: I am Keeper of the Vigil here in Skyrim. We bring Stendarr's Mercy to the innocent and His Justice to the Daedra.

speaker: Keerava
dialogue: I can't stand this city. It's impossible to make a decent living here.

speaker: Keerava
dialogue: Maybe they're afraid of you. Maybe it's your breath. How should I know?

speaker: Indaryn
dialogue: They always try to take advantage of me. Give them an inch and they'll take a mile.

speaker: Keerava
dialogue: I'll tell you one thing, if you don't make peace with them soon you may get a walkout on your hands. Then we're both in trouble.

speaker: Keerava
dialogue: No, no, Maramal...We talked about this...Talen...

speaker: Maramal
dialogue: Keerava, certainly we can come to some sort of understanding? These people must be made aware of the chaos they've sown.

speaker: Talen
dialogue: Enough, Maramal. We've all heard of the dragons and their return. There's no need to use them as an excuse to harass our customers.

speaker: Maramal
dialogue: Very well, Talen. I'll remove myself from this den of iniquity.

speaker: Talen
dialogue: We're not kicking you out, just keep the sermons at the temple and let us all sin in peace.

speaker: Keerava
dialogue: I love when you spin that yarn. Gets better every time you add something new.

speaker: Romlyn
dialogue: He killed six Imperial Guards before they dragged him into the prisons.

speaker: Keerava
dialogue: Was this before or after the Mythic Dawn attacked the Emperor and Valen single-handedly fought them off? Just shut up and drink, Romlyn.

speaker: Talen
dialogue: Keerava, we're running low on Black-Briar Mead.

speaker: Keerava
dialogue: If only Maven would stop raising the price on it maybe I could afford to stock more cases.

speaker: Talen
dialogue: We could always look for another brand.

speaker: Keerava
dialogue: That isn't an option. Maven sees me serve a competitor's brand here and we may as well dig our own graves.

speaker: Keerava
dialogue: Don't worry, the time will come when we can walk away from here.

speaker: Talen
dialogue: I hope so. I can't stand this city anymore.

speaker: Keerava
dialogue: Damn it, Talen. We still don't have enough this year to get out of Riften.

speaker: Keerava
dialogue: Talen, do you believe what they're saying? Do you really think the dragons have returned?

speaker: Talen
dialogue: I don't know what to believe. If it's true, then dark times may be upon us.

speaker: Keerava
dialogue: What should we do?

speaker: Talen
dialogue: We hold each other close and hope that all of this ends well.

speaker: Kematu
dialogue: We meet at last, my dear lady.

speaker: Saadia
dialogue: What is this? What have {{Hide|you|referring to the Dragonborn}} done?

speaker: Kematu
dialogue: Oh, come now. You didn't really expect to manipulate people forever, did you? Your luck had to run out sometime.

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: A bit of jewelry for your journey home?

speaker: Weylin
dialogue: I die for my people.

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: By the Divines, the Forsworn are here in the city!

speaker: Markarth City Guard
dialogue: Everyone stay back. The Markarth city guard have this all under control. There are no Forsworn here.

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: What am I supposed to do? Never leave the house? You want that, Endon?

speaker: Endon
dialogue: You're closing the stall, and that's final.

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: You want to give up now? Out of fear? Is that what we're teaching our daughter?

speaker: Adara
dialogue: Mama, why are you and papa fighting?

speaker: Endon
dialogue: We're not fighting, we're just...Why don't I get you something to eat? Mam and papa will talk later.

speaker: Endon
dialogue: How are the necklaces selling, my wife? We could make more.

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: I'm afraid the necklaces aren't selling well. Customers aren't interested in medallions and engraved symbols of other provinces.

speaker: Endon
dialogue: Hmph. Used to be everyone in Markarth wore a necklace showing his home province, from Elsweyr, to High Rock, to Hammerfell and Cyrodiil...

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: We don't take travelers from Hammerfell or High Rock anymore, Endon. Only natives from Markarth and Skyrim.

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: I need to get back to the customers. We'll talk more of this when I get home tonight.

speaker: Endon
dialogue: Markarth has changed, but the inn is as lively as ever.

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: The city hasn't changed that much, dear. Some old dwarven stones gathering the same old moss.

speaker: Endon
dialogue: The stones aren't what bother me, love. The Forsworn are tearing the Reach apart.

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: Let's not talk about this over dinner.

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: What should we have tonight?

speaker: Endon
dialogue: Something simple, a stew perhaps.

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: Maybe we could spend a litle bit more and buy some meat, Endon.

speaker: Endon
dialogue: May be. Let me think about it.

speaker: Adara
dialogue: Mama, when is Cade coming home?

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: He's off fighting, Adara, with the Stormcloaks. He'll return when the war is over.

speaker: Endon
dialogue: Our son joining the Stormcloaks. If this war had never happened, Cade would have joined the Imperial Legion, like grandfather.

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: Endon, we talked about this... Are you still disappointed in Cade's choice?

speaker: Endon
dialogue: No. I think if I was a young man, I would have done the same.

speaker: Adara
dialogue: Can I join the Legion when I grow up?

speaker: Endon
dialogue: If there's still a Legion left, Adara. I'm sure you'd make a great soldier. Just like your brother.

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: We sold all those lovely little necklaces you brought me today. Did you make them yourself?

speaker: Adara
dialogue: That's right! Papa helped me with the clasps, but I did all the links on my own.

speaker: Endon
dialogue: Adara bends the silver so naturally. Grandmother would have cried if she saw how deft our daughter has become.

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: Well, I'm proud of both of you. I haven't been so busy since those nobles from Solitude come into the city three years ago.

speaker: Endon
dialogue: I miss those days, before the Forsworn took up arms again, when you could walk the roads in peace.

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: Endon, dear, please don't.... Save your frustrations for work.

speaker: Endon
dialogue: You're right, dear. I'm sorry to worry you.

speaker: Kharjo
dialogue: If anyone sneaks up on us, I'll smell them coming. Or, I might not. We will see.

speaker: Kharjo
dialogue: Soon it will be time to replenish our supply of water.

speaker: Zaynabi
dialogue: The road takes us past many cold rivers. We can fill our skins there.

speaker: Kharjo
dialogue: If the river is not frozen to ice, perhaps.

speaker: Khayla
dialogue: The road makes this one weary.

speaker: Kibell
dialogue: Traveling in the Reach is dangerous. You need a good carriage.

speaker: Kjar
dialogue: The North Wind is my mistress, and I'm her master. I don't tolerate any disloyalty.

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: You going to be at the inn tonight?

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: Not sure. Feeling like taking another trip.

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: What's your wife think of your trips?

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: They're none of her business, and none of yours either.

context: Heat makes the mead go down
speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: Sweltering in here.

context: Heat makes the mead go down
speaker: Roggi
dialogue: I'd like the fresh air better, but this isn't so bad.

context: Heat makes the mead go down
speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: How do you stay cheery down in these blazes?

context: Heat makes the mead go down
speaker: Roggi
dialogue: I don't know. Maybe because it makes the mead taste that much better at night.

context: Heat makes the mead go down
speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: Again with the mead!

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: Found another one of those vents in back near the scaffold.

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: Does Dravynea know?

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: She hasn't had a chance to look at it yet. Just be careful over there.

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: Roggi tell you about the scorcher we found under the scaffolding?

speaker: Dravynea
dialogue: Again? But there shouldn't be any earthstreams over there.

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: Well I nearly lost my eyebrows to it.

speaker: Dravynea
dialogue: All right, I'll take a look at it.

speaker: Dravynea
dialogue: What did I tell you about snooping around my wards?

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: Woman, there's a vein of malachite as thick as my leg back there.

speaker: Dravynea
dialogue: And if you don't let me secure the steam channel, your leg could get blown off. So go dig at the other corner for a bit.

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: Well... just get it done.

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: Is the new shaft cleared yet?

speaker: Dravynea
dialogue: No, I've been busy trying to keep the whole mine from collapsing, if that's all right with you.

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: You're busy. I'll come back later.

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: So, Roggi, when are you going to get yourself a woman?

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: Oh, I'm not sure I could ever settle down like you have, friend.

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: Who says I've settled down?

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: I think this is yet another conversation that wouldn't make your wife happy.

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: That's just it... if she's not happy, there are plenty of other women who will be.

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: Oh, you old charmer.

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: I'm not sure that's a good joke to tell with women present...

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: But don't you get it? She thought he was a troll!

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: I get it. It's funny. It just might upset your wife.

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: Eh, let her get upset. She'll be angry no matter what I say, might as well enjoy myself.

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: How much do you know about the brewing of mead?

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: I know all there is to know about the drinking of it, and that suits me just fine.

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: I've been trying to figure out what makes Riften mead better than the stuff from Whiterun.

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: Better honey?

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: There has to be more to it than that, though. I wish I knew where the bees got it from.

speaker: Kjeld the Younger
dialogue: When do I get to go hunting?

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: When you're able to draw a bow all the way to your shoulder.

speaker: Kjeld the Younger
dialogue: I can do that! I did it yesterday!

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: Oh, really?

speaker: Kjeld the Younger
dialogue: So can I come?

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: We'll see.

speaker: Kjeld the Younger
dialogue: And then I told her about the vampires and how much they would pay me for her.

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: That is rich. What did she do?

speaker: Kjeld the Younger
dialogue: She's a girl. She cried.

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: It's good to toughen her up. Not an easy world out here. Keep at it.

speaker: Kjeld the Younger
dialogue: Papa, mama's making me do kitchen work again.

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: And what did you say to that?

speaker: Kjeld the Younger
dialogue: She can't tell me what to do!

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: There you go, son. Be your own man!

speaker: Kjeld the Younger
dialogue: My pa runs this town, and you're going to be in big trouble if you mess with me.

speaker: Kjeld the Younger
dialogue: When do I get to go hunting?

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: When you're able to draw a bow all the way to your shoulder.

speaker: Kjeld the Younger
dialogue: I can do that! I did it yesterday!

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: Oh, really?

speaker: Kjeld the Younger
dialogue: So can I come?

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: We'll see.

speaker: Kjeld the Younger
dialogue: And then I told her about the vampires and how much they would pay me for her.

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: That is rich. What did she do?

speaker: Kjeld the Younger
dialogue: She's a girl. She cried.

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: It's good to toughen her up. Not an easy world out here. Keep at it.

speaker: Kjeld the Younger
dialogue: Papa, mama's making me do kitchen work again.

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: And what did you say to that?

speaker: Kjeld the Younger
dialogue: She can't tell me what to do!

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: There you go, son. Be your own man!

speaker: Iddra
dialogue: I'm going to need your help in the kitchen tomorrow.

speaker: Kjeld the Younger
dialogue: But papa was going to take me hunting tomorrow!

speaker: Iddra
dialogue: Oh, I don't think you're old enough for that yet. You can help me salt the cheese curd.

speaker: Kjeld the Younger
dialogue: Why can't Froa do it?

speaker: Iddra
dialogue: Because I'm telling you to.

speaker: Iddra
dialogue: You need to take better care of your sister.

speaker: Kjeld the Younger
dialogue: But she's so stupid!

speaker: Iddra
dialogue: She said you threw her into a goat pen yesterday.

speaker: Kjeld the Younger
dialogue: Because she was being stupid!

speaker: Iddra
dialogue: Don't make me bring your father into this.

speaker: Kjeld the Younger
dialogue: Mama, when can we go play in the river again?

speaker: Iddra
dialogue: Not with all those soldiers all over the hold. Their horses can't see you, you know.

speaker: Kjeld the Younger
dialogue: I know, but...

speaker: Iddra
dialogue: And you'll be trampled to death!

speaker: Kjeld the Younger
dialogue: No way. I'm quick!

speaker: Iddra
dialogue: Well why don't you be quick about finding my book that you lost?

speaker: Kleppr
dialogue: Come on in. The Silver-Blood Inn has plenty of strong drink and clean rooms.

speaker: Kleppr
dialogue: Another drink, Cosnach? A porter from Arnleif and Sons deserves nothing but the finest here.

speaker: Cosnach
dialogue: All your drinks are watered down, Kleppr. You aren't fooling me, and you know Lisbet can't afford to pay me enough for the finest drinks anyhow.

speaker: Kleppr
dialogue: I wasn't aware Lisbet was having trouble, Cosnach. Is Arnleif and Sons not having a good turn of business these days?

speaker: Cosnach
dialogue: What are you, blind? That store is empty. The Forsworn get almost every shipment that comes in.

speaker: Kleppr
dialogue: That's just terrible. I'm so sorry to hear that.

speaker: Cosnach
dialogue: No you aren't.

speaker: Frabbi
dialogue: Kleppr, you idiot! Can't you do anything right?

speaker: Kleppr
dialogue: What? What did I do this time? I was just standing here.

speaker: Frabbi
dialogue: You were just standing there when you were supposed to be serving drinks to our customers!

speaker: Kleppr
dialogue: Shouldn't you be helping me then, wife of mine? Sharing my problems? Being my better half?

speaker: Frabbi
dialogue: I am your better half. And your better half is telling you to stop being an idiot and serve the customers their drinks!

speaker: Frabbi
dialogue: All the wood furniture in the inn is rotten to the core. Do you know why that is, Kleppr?

speaker: Kleppr
dialogue: I don't know. I suppose you're going to tell me?

speaker: Frabbi
dialogue: Its rotten because the wood is cheap and soaked with ale! Now we'll have to replace all the furniture before bugs set in.

speaker: Kleppr
dialogue: Don't worry, my love. Just show the bugs your adoring face, and they'll scurry away in complete fear in no time.

speaker: Frabbi
dialogue: You're an idiot, Kleppr. Why did I ever marry you?

speaker: Kleppr
dialogue: Not a day goes by I don't ask myself that same question, my dear.

speaker: Kleppr
dialogue: Frabi, my dear loving wife, would you please clean out the guest rooms?

speaker: Frabbi
dialogue: Clean the rooms yourself, Kleppr. Its not like you do anything important around here.

speaker: Kleppr
dialogue: No, just check in the guests and manage the coin and keep a roof over your head. No, nothing important.

speaker: Hreinn
dialogue: Father, why do you and mother fight so much?

speaker: Kleppr
dialogue: We don't fight. We, um, talk. Loudly.

speaker: Kleppr
dialogue: How are your chores coming, my son?

speaker: Hreinn
dialogue: Today, I've cleaned the linens, washed the floors and checked in on all the guests.

speaker: Kleppr
dialogue: Ah, my son, you'll be a fine innkeeper someday, like your father.

speaker: Hreinn
dialogue: But mother says you're a terrible innkeeper!

speaker: Kleppr
dialogue: Never mind your mother, Hreinn. You listen to me and you'll be a great man one day.

speaker: Kleppr
dialogue: Playing tonight, Ogmund? Everyone here is anxious to hear ballads performed by the true Skald of the Reach.

speaker: Ogmund
dialogue: Son, I know thousands of the old ballads. If I played all of them, everyone in this inn would be as grey as I am before I finished.

speaker: Kleppr
dialogue: Uh, right. Maybe just one of the popular songs, like 'The Slaying of the Falmer Princes'?

speaker: Ogmund
dialogue: That's a sensible lad. Now fetch me a drink.

speaker: Kleppr
dialogue: Please. Those savages are no match for us. The Jarl is just biding his time.

speaker: Vorstag
dialogue: Biding his time for what? Until another person is lying dead in the streets? Don't be naive.

speaker: Knjakr
dialogue: I'm going to eat well tonight, my darling!

speaker: Knud
dialogue: Father says I don't have the knack for reading, but mama says I won't need it to work the farm.

speaker: Katla
dialogue: Another gorgeous gray day, right dear?

speaker: Snilling
dialogue: It's too cold for my bones, but that never seems to stop you, dear.

speaker: Katla
dialogue: That's nice, son. Just don't stomp on the crop like last time!

speaker: Snilling
dialogue: I'll see if I can't get some work done inside, where it's warm.

speaker: Kodlak Whitemane
dialogue: Some nights, I dream about the mists of Sovngarde.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: We all do. It is our burden to bear. But we can overcome.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: You have my brother and I, obviously. But I don't know if the rest will go along quite so easily.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: Leave that to me.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: Master, you're not truly considering accepting him?

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: I am nobody's master, Vilkas. And last I checked, we had some empty beds in Jorrvaskr for those with a fire burning in their hearts.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: Apologies. But perhaps this isn't the time. I've never even heard of this outsider.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: Sometimes the famous come to us. Sometimes men and women come to us to seek their fame. It makes no difference. What matters is their heart.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: Vilkas, take him out to the yard and see what he can do.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: Brothers and sisters of the Circle, today we welcome a new soul into our mortal fold. This man has endured, has challenged, and has shown his valor. Who will speak for him?

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: I stand witness to the courage of the soul before us.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: Would you raise your shield in his defense?

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: I would stand at his back, that the world might never overtake us.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: And would you raise your sword in his honor?

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: It stands ready to meet the blood of his foes.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: And would you raise a mug in his name?

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: I would lead the song of triumph as our mead hall reveled in his stories.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: Then the judgement of this Circle is complete. His heart beats with fury and courage that have united the Companions since the days of the distant green summers. Let it beat with ours, that the mountains may echo and our enemies may tremble at the call.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: It shall be so.

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: It shall be so.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: It shall be so.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: Tradition is very important to me, son.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: If you want to lead this pack when I'm gone, you have to see farther. Look closer.

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: Well which is it? Look farther or closer?

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: Come on now, boy, you know what I meant...

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: You speak in riddles sometimes.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: I don't mean to confuse you.

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: It's not confusing... just frustrating.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: You're a strong warrior, Skjor. Your heart is fiery and that serves you well in battle.

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: Thank you, Harbinger.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: But even the bravest of men consider their actions. I want you to survive long enough to take the mantle.

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: Don't worry about me.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: I worry that you've been spending too many nights out.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: Where I go is my business. If you have a concern about my honor, bring it before the Circle.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: You forget yourself, young one.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: I'm sorry. I didn't mean to snap. Just... these hunters. We're all on edge.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: That's why it's best to not mistake foolhardiness for bravery.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: How goes the hunt?

speaker: Aela
dialogue: Skjor's heard rumors of a bear the size of a mammoth in Hammerfell. We're going to seek it out.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: What glorious prey. Come back alive, and with stories to tell!

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: How are the young ones coming along?

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: I remember when you were the same way. The more they train, the more they'll cool down.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: I hope so.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: Just have them focus on the calm in the battle. Control the rage, don't let it control you.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: What weapon do you like, Harbinger?

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: When I was young, I favored huge swords, much like you. Hard to lift these days, but I still enjoy the heft of a good hammer.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: Big swords should always beat little swords.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: Brave hearts beat lesser ones. That's the decider.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: My title is Harbinger, child. I am no man's master.

speaker: Torvar
dialogue: Forgive me. You're just the one in charge, and it's what I'm used to.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: No one is in charge here. Each Shield-Brother is his own man, each Shield-Sister her own woman.

speaker: Torvar
dialogue: Well why do I have to listen to Skjor, then?

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: Skjor has been a warrior for a long time. You would be wise to listen to him. Any warrior that gets to be old is either fearsome or a coward. I'll let you find out which Skjor is.

speaker: Torvar
dialogue: Do you think I could be a member of the Circle? Some day? If I work hard?

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: Don't worry about such things. Just focus on your own honor. Bring glory to the Companions, and that glory will return upon you.

speaker: Torvar
dialogue: I just want to make sure I'm moving up.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: This isn't the military, son. There are no ranks.

speaker: Torvar
dialogue: But aren't the Circle in charge? And don't you lead them?

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: I guide the Companions. The Circle advises me. But we are all free warriors. Only our honor binds us together.

speaker: Kodrir
dialogue: Strangers are always trouble.

speaker: Jarl Korir
dialogue: I don't care how many Colleges they build, or how much the sea swallows up. I'll outlast them all.

speaker: Assur
dialogue: Eirid says the mages at the College are nice people, but you said they're bad.

speaker: Korir
dialogue: Eirid's a little girl who doesn't understand that they're responsible for destroying our home.

speaker: Assur
dialogue: Why did they do that? Why would they be so evil?

speaker: Korir
dialogue: Because they don't care about you or I, cub. They think they're better than all of us, and that we can just be thrown away.

speaker: Assur
dialogue: I hate them.

speaker: Korir
dialogue: That's my boy.

speaker: Thaena
dialogue: That...wizard is still at the inn. I can't believe Dagur allows him to stay there.

speaker: Korir
dialogue: That is what its come to. No one seems to care what they've done to our home.

speaker: Thaena
dialogue: Its clear that memories are far too short.

speaker: Korir
dialogue: And its clear that money matters more to Dagur than honor.

speaker: Korir
dialogue: Looks to be another cold day.

speaker: Thaena
dialogue: Aren't they all?

speaker: Korir
dialogue: Not like this. Feels colder than usual. Bet it's those damned Mages.

speaker: Thaena
dialogue: I'm sure you're right.

speaker: Kornalus
dialogue: What? No! Get back in your cage!

speaker: Kraldar
dialogue: I'd like nothing more than to see Winterhold regain its former glory.

speaker: Kraldar
dialogue: So, what's the latest exciting news about goings-on in Winterhold?

speaker: Thonjolf
dialogue: There is no news, I'm afraid.

speaker: Kraldar
dialogue: None? Nothing at all? Nothing from the College, even?

speaker: Thonjolf
dialogue: I shall inform you the moment something noteworthy happens.

speaker: Kraldar
dialogue: Yes, that will be fine. Thank you.

speaker: Thonjolf
dialogue: Will you be needing anything special today?

speaker: Kraldar
dialogue: Why don't you see if Arch-Mage Aren is interested in joining me for a meal?

speaker: Thonjolf
dialogue: Again? Are you sure? He still hasn't answered your last several requests.

speaker: Kraldar
dialogue: Well, he's been very busy. Perhaps today he'll have some free time.

speaker: Thonjolf
dialogue: As you wish.

speaker: Aela the Huntress (Skyrim)
dialogue: They call him "the Skinner."

speaker: Kust
dialogue: Strangers like you bring war. I've seen enough war.

speaker: Laila Law-Giver
dialogue: Welcome to Riften, traveler. I hope the road fared well for you.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: Have our scouts come up with any information on these reports of dragons?

speaker: Anuriel
dialogue: Yes, milady. That unpleasantness at Helgen supposedly involved a dragon. It killed several soldiers before it departed.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: I want you to speak to the city guard. Make sure there's a contingency plan in effect in case Riften falls under attack.

speaker: Anuriel
dialogue: Yes, milday. I've also taken the liberty in preparing a private carriage... just in case.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: Good. If Riften should fall, it's only right that its leader be spared.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: Anuriel, a word please.

speaker: Anuriel
dialogue: Yes, my lady?

speaker: Laila
dialogue: It's been brought to my attention that the poison known as skooma may be present in our city. What do you know of this?

speaker: Anuriel
dialogue: I believe it to be a falsehood perpetrated by the Empire in order to weaken the citizen's confidence in your ability to rule.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: Excellent, then they'll be no need to devote any resources to stopping it. Thank you, Anuriel. That will be all.

speaker: Anuriel
dialogue: My lady, Maven Black-Briar has sent word that she requires your seal in order to expand her shipments into Morrowind.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: But of course! Tell her she'll have it. Maven is one of the few people I can trust and I'd be delighted to give her my blessing.

speaker: Anuriel
dialogue: Yes, my lady. I will pass the good news on to her.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: Harrald, I have need of you.

speaker: Harrald
dialogue: Yes mother? What is it?

speaker: Laila
dialogue: This situation with the sewers beneath the city. I hear people have entered this place and have gone missing. Do you know of this?

speaker: Harrald
dialogue: Yes, I've heard such things. Anuriel assures me they're just fabrications and there's nothing down there save a few stray skeever.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: Well, make sure we keep the patrols out night and day, just to be certain.

speaker: Harrald
dialogue: Mother, how long must we put up with Saerlund spouting his nonsense about the Empire?

speaker: Laila
dialogue: What would you have me do, send him to the gallows for treason? He's your brother, Harrald.

speaker: Harrald
dialogue: My only concern is your safety, mother. One can only imagine the sordid types he may be conspiring with to bring about your downfall.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: I will hear no more of this, Harrald. Do you understand me? No more!

speaker: Laila
dialogue: Maven! Always a pleasure to receive you. What can I help you with today?

speaker: Laila
dialogue: Yes, indeed. An entire caravan shipment of your mead taken by Imperial soldiers. What of it?

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Well, I'm also certain you're aware that our own city guard failed to provide the protection required to ensure safe passage of the shipment.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: Indeed. We lost three soldiers in that attack. A sad day for Riften.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: We... don't have enough to...

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Laila, Riften is my home, but if my meadery can't be safe here, I'll just move it elsewhere.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: No, that won't be necessary. You'll have compensation for your loss.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Thank you, Laila.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: Unmid, I wish to travel about the city. Prepare an escort please.

speaker: Unmid
dialogue: Begging your pardon my lady, but I strongly recommend against it.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: Anuriel seems to think that seeing me on the streets might bolster the city's morale.

speaker: Unmid
dialogue: My lady, there could be agents of the Empire looking for an opportunity like that to have you killed. Are you willing to take that risk?

speaker: Laila
dialogue: No. Of course you're right, Unmid. I'll stay here for now.

speaker: Wylandriah
dialogue: Do you realize how delicate the experiment is you've interrupted by sending for me? I may need to throw out the components and start again.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: How dare you take that kind of tone. You're in service to me, remember?

speaker: Wylandriah
dialogue: I'm sorry my lady. The stresses of all this research... it's becoming more than I can bear.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: You're forgiven. Now, I want to know if you've made any progress with my son. Is he cursed? Has he been possessed?

speaker: Wylandriah
dialogue: Sorry, my lady. I've been looking but I'm convinced Saerlund says truly believes what he is saying.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: Very well. Keep at it. You may go.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: Ahhh... It's good to be home.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Welcome back. I've left a few surprises for you to discover.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: How kind of you. And I've brought an army to give you a going away parade.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: If you two are finished with the touching homecoming, there's a city in chaos out there.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: Indeed. Come, there is much to be done.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: I think I'll like living here.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: So enters Maven Black-Briar, the glint of Imperial coin in her eyes. So tell me, what's the price for a woman's integrity these days?

speaker: Maven
dialogue: You never were able to see the forest for the trees, were you?

speaker: Laila
dialogue: We Nords were proud warriors once. And we still could be. Evidenced by the men and women who fought and died bravely today. You could see that if you had any faith left in that black heart of yours. But no, you're content to snatch scraps falling off the Emperor's table. Fine. Take my home. Take my city. May it burn down around you.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: A bit melodramatic, even for you Laila. Pack your things and go.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: One day when you can see past your own interests, you will come to see that we were right. And this... This is all wrong.

speaker: Rikke
dialogue: If you ladies are finished bickering, there's much to be done. Jarl Black-Briar put your government together. Do it now, or there will be rioting in the streets. We must move quickly to prevent further violence.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Jarl Black-Briar. I must admit, I do like the sound of that. And don't worry about any rioting, Legate. I have it under control. We will soon begin publicly executing captured men. That should send a clear message to the people.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: Yes, but not likely the one you intend.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Oh? I don't expect anyone to miss my meaning. Come, Legate. There's much to do.

speaker: Lami
dialogue: If you need any alchemy supplies, I'll do my best to provide them. Assuming I haven't used them all up.

speaker: Lars Battle-Born
dialogue: It's no fun getting pushed around all the time...

speaker: Lars
dialogue: That's all right, grandmother. I like staying home with you.

speaker: Bergritte
dialogue: It's that Braith girl again, isn't it? Has she been bothering you again? I've a mind to speak with her mother.

speaker: Lars
dialogue: No! Please, grandmother, don't do that. I'm fine. Really. Can we just... not talk about this anymore?

speaker: Bergritte
dialogue: All right, dear.

speaker: Braith
dialogue: Battle-Born! Give me your money!

speaker: Lars
dialogue: I... I don't have any money.

speaker: Braith
dialogue: You'd better give me five Septims, right now, or I'm going to bloody your nose...

speaker: Lars
dialogue: No! Please! I really don't have any money, Braith! I'll give you ten septims tomorrow. Just don't hit me.

speaker: Braith
dialogue: Ten Septims tomorrow, baby Battle-Born. Or I'm gonna bloody your nose and your lip.

speaker: Braith
dialogue: Oh look, it's little baby Battle-Born.

speaker: Lars
dialogue: Leave me alone, Braith...

speaker: Braith
dialogue: What are you gonna do if I don't? Huh? Gonna cry to your papa?

speaker: Lars
dialogue: Just go away!

speaker: Lash gra-Dushnikh
dialogue: I work in the mines. I hunt. Everything else I do is my business.

speaker: Galmar Stone-Fist
dialogue: Hero of the Nords I name you, Dragonborn, let none deny it.

speaker: Adventus Caesennius
dialogue: What the rebels like to forget is that the Empire's what's keeping the Dominion out of Skyrim.

speaker: Legate Emmanuel Admand
dialogue: Keep an eye out for trouble. It's only a matter of time.

speaker: Fasendil
dialogue: Ulfric and his thugs are stirring up trouble for their own agenda, the Empire is the only thing keeping the Dominion from walking all over Skyrim.

speaker: Imperial Soldier
dialogue: Sir! I... I have...

speaker: Cipius
dialogue: Take a moment to breathe, soldier.

speaker: Imperial Soldier
dialogue: But... Sir...

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: The outer walls are strong. If we can hold them there...

speaker: Cipius
dialogue: They have catapults.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Damnit. Where'd they get catapults? The city walls are already falling apart as it is.

speaker: Cipius
dialogue: My scouts tell me they're loading them with fire.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: So, he wants to take my city, walls intact.

speaker: Cipius
dialogue: The men will be fighting in the flames.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: My men are fearless. It's the Imperial milk drinkers I'm worried about.

speaker: Cipius
dialogue: If you prefer I took my men and left...

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: No. Of course not. Just - don't let me down Cipius. We'll need to set up water brigades to combat the flames.

speaker: Cipius
dialogue: Already taken care of.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: You Imperials are efficient, I'll give you that. How long until they arrive?

speaker: Cipius
dialogue: Not long. They're hiding in the country side.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Damnit. What's he waiting for?

speaker: Imperial Soldier
dialogue: Sir, they're on the move. They'll be at the gates at any moment!

speaker: Cipius
dialogue: Why didn't you say so immediatly?!

speaker: Imperial Soldier
dialogue: Sir, I tried.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: This is it! Time to see what these Stormcloaks are made of.

speaker: Cipius
dialogue: The men are already gathering at the gates. Move it soldier. Spread the word. Go. Go. Go.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Oblivion take them. Every miserable last one of them.

speaker: Rikke
dialogue: You're wrong. Ulfric. We need the Empire. Without it Skyrim will assuredly fall to the Dominion.

speaker: General Tullius
dialogue: Tell me again, why I'm wasting men chasing after a fairy tale.

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: If Ulfric gets his hand on that crown, it won't be a fairy tale. It'll be a problem.

speaker: General Tullius
dialogue: Don't you Nords put any stock in your own traditions? I thought the Moot chose the king. We're backing Elisif. When the Moot meets, they'll do the sensible thing.

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: Not everyone's agreed to the Moot. You've been here long enough to know that Nords aren't always sensible. We follow our hearts.

speaker: General Tullius
dialogue: So what - Ulfric gets this crown and then suddenly he's High King?

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: No, it's not as simple as that, but the Jagged Crown would be a potent symbol for his cause to rally around. But, if we found it first...

speaker: General Tullius
dialogue: And we gave it to Elisif?

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: In the absence of the Moot, it would further legitimize her claim.

speaker: General Tullius
dialogue: Perhaps... I'm entrusting you with what resources I can spare. But I'm warning you, if this turns out to be a waste of time and men...

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: It won't be a waste.

speaker: General Tullius
dialogue: Make sure you take the Auxiliary here. You can send him/her back when you get there and find nothing but old bones and cobwebs.

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: The Stonefist's no fool. He's found the Crown. But we'll get to it first.

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: What's the situation?

speaker: Imperial Soldier
dialogue: Stormcloaks were already camped out around the entrance when we got here. They don't know we're here yet, though.

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: Well, that's something at least.

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: Well done. They never knew what hit them. But don't underestimate the Stormcloaks. Many are Legion veterans. They may be traitors, but they know how to fight. We had the advantage of surprise this time, but don't expect it to last. Let's move out.

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: Everybody ready? We charge on my signal. Time to show what you're really made of. For the Empire!

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: You two, stay and guard the entrance. We don't want any Stormcloak reinforcements taking us by surprise. Everyone else, with me.

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: I don't like the look of this. Perfect spot for an ambush. Ten to one they're just waiting for us on the other side.

speaker: Imperial Soldier
dialogue: But there isn't any other way through, Legate.

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: Let's not jump to conclusions, soldier. The Legion always finds a way. I'd rather take a moment and look around than walk blindly into an ambush. Auxiliary, see if you can find another way through. We'll charge in to help as soon as we hear fighting.

speaker: Imperial Soldier 1
dialogue: What in the nine holds is that?

speaker: Imperial Soldier 2
dialogue: Is this what killed that Stormcloak over there? Can't be. It looks like it's been dead for a hundred years.

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: And this must be the Hall of Stories.

speaker: Imperial Soldier 1
dialogue: Oh... I've heard of this. These walls are supposed to show the history of the ancients who built this place.

speaker: Imperial Soldier 2
dialogue: Too bad we can't read these carvings. Who knows what secrets we'd uncover?

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: One thing at a time soldier. Focus on our primary mission. We're searching for the crown. Looks like we weren't the first ones here, either. Even if these carvings tell us where the crown is, I'm sure we're going to have to find a way through this door. See what you can figure out auxillary, I'm going to check out these carvings over here. Let me know if you find something.

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: Alright legionnaires! Spread out and see what we've got. Auxiliary, do what you do best. See if you can find some way to get that gate open.

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: Steady, legionnaires! We've been through worse. Just keep your guard up!

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: Follow me. Let's see where this leads.

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: The crown should be around here somewhere. Spread out, and keep your eyes open.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Hey, I found a crown over here on this corpse. Is this the one we're looking for?

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: Hadvar... get away from there!

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: By the nine!

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: Well, King... If you don't mind, we'll just take that crown of yours and be on our way.

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: Have it your way. Let's get that crown men!

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: Alright, get the crown off that draugr! Take that crown back to Solitude, soldier. We'll stay here and see if we can find anything else that could be of use.

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: I'm telling you, Ulfric's planning an attack on Whiterun.

speaker: General Tullius
dialogue: He'd be insane to try. He doesn't have the men.

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: That's not what my scouts report, sir. Every day more join his cause. Riften, Dawnstar, and Winterhold support him.

speaker: General Tullius
dialogue: It's not a cause. It's a rebellion.

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: Call it whatever you like, General. The man's going to try to take Whiterun.

speaker: General Tullius
dialogue: Jarl Balgruuf...

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: Balgruuf refuses the Legion's right to garrison troops in his city. On the other hand, he also refuses to acknowledge Ulfric's claim.

speaker: General Tullius
dialogue: Well, if he wants to stand outside the protection of the Empire, fine. Let Ulfric pillage his city.

speaker: General Tullius
dialogue: You people and your damn Jarls.

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: Sir? You can't force a Nord to accept help he hasn't asked for.

speaker: General Tullius
dialogue: If Ulfric's making a move for Whiterun, then we need to be there to stop him. Draft another letter with the usual platitudes, but this time share some of your intelligence regarding Ulfric's plans. Embellish if you have to. We'll let it seem like it's his idea.

speaker: Legate Rikke
dialogue: Yes, sir.

speaker: General Tullius
dialogue: You Nords and your bloody sense of honor.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Secure the door.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Already done.

speaker: Rikke
dialogue: Ulfric. Stop.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Stop what? Taking Skyrim back from those who'd leave her to rot?

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: You were there with us. You saw it. The day the Empire signed that damn treaty was the day the Empire died.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: The Empire is weak, obsolete. Look at how far we've come and with so little. When we're done rooting out Imperial influence here at home, then we will take our war to the Aldmeri Dominion.

speaker: Rikke
dialogue: You're a damn fool.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Stand aside woman. We've come for the General.

speaker: Rikke
dialogue: He has given up. But I have not.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Rikke. Go. You're free to leave.

speaker: Rikke
dialogue: I'm also free to stay and fight for what I believe in.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: You're also free to die for it.

speaker: Rikke
dialogue: This is what you wanted? Shield brothers and sisters killing each other? Families torn apart? This is the Skyrim you want?!

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Damnit woman, stand aside.

speaker: Rikke
dialogue: That's not the Skyrim I want to live in.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Rikke. You don't have to do this.

speaker: Rikke
dialogue: You've left me no choice... Talos preserve us.

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Secure the door.

speaker: Rikke
dialogue: Already done, sir.

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Ulfric Stormcloak! You are guilty of insurrection, murder of Imperial citizens, the assassination of King Torygg, and high treason against the Empire. It's over.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Not while I'm still breathing, it's not.

speaker: Rikke
dialogue: Step aside Galmar. We're here to accept Ulfric's surrender.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: I'll never surrender Skyrim into the hands of a corrupt and dying Empire.

speaker: Rikke
dialogue: Skyrim doesn't belong to you, Ulfric.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: No... But I belong to her.

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Enough! You are traitors and will die traitors' deaths. Stand down and face public execution, or advance and face summary execution by my hands. It matters little to me. Either way I'll be sending your heads back to Cyrodiil.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Well? What are we waiting for?

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Well Ulfric, you can't escape from me this time. Any last requests before I send you to... to wherever you people go when you die.

speaker: Rikke
dialogue: Sovngarde... sir.

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Right. Well?

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Let the Dragonborn be the one to do it. It'll make for a better song.

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Song or not, I just want it done.

speaker: Rikke
dialogue: Talos be with you...

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: What was that, Legate?

speaker: Rikke
dialogue: Nothing. Just saying goodbye.

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Well, the men will be expecting some kind of speech. And we'll need to hand the city over to that Free-Winter fellow.

speaker: Rikke
dialogue: Brunwulf. Yes, I've sent men to protect him and bring him here. Windhelm will need a government quickly if we are to prevent more violence.

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: The Legion will be staying here for quite some time. I don't expect there to be any further violence.

speaker: Rikke
dialogue: Attention! General Tullius has an announcement!

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: The rebellion is over! Ulfric Stormcloak is dead!

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: I am proud of all of you! All hail the Emperor! All hail his legionnaires!

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: I hate giving speeches.

speaker: Rikke
dialogue: It wasn't so bad.

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: I hope we haven't just created a martyr.

speaker: Rikke
dialogue: There's bound to be resistance. There are still Stormcloak camps, tucked away in the hills. They'll no doubt strike wherever and whenever they can. But, without Ulfric to inflame their passions, they'll settle down and return to their homes eventually.

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: I pray you're right, Legate. In the meantime, we'll continue to root them out and put them to the sword. {{hide|We couldn't have done this without you. The Empire glories in your accomplishments.|Speaking to the Dragonborn.}} Come Rikke, there's still much to be done.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: I think I'll like living here.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: So enters Maven Black-Briar, the glint of Imperial coin in her eyes. So tell me, what's the price for a woman's integrity these days?

speaker: Maven
dialogue: You never were able to see the forest for the trees, were you?

speaker: Laila
dialogue: We Nords were proud warriors once. And we still could be. Evidenced by the men and women who fought and died bravely today. You could see that if you had any faith left in that black heart of yours. But no, you're content to snatch scraps falling off the Emperor's table. Fine. Take my home. Take my city. May it burn down around you.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: A bit melodramatic, even for you Laila. Pack your things and go.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: One day when you can see past your own interests, you will come to see that we were right. And this... This is all wrong.

speaker: Rikke
dialogue: If you ladies are finished bickering, there's much to be done. Jarl Black-Briar put your government together. Do it now, or there will be rioting in the streets. We must move quickly to prevent further violence.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Jarl Black-Briar. I must admit, I do like the sound of that. And don't worry about any rioting, Legate. I have it under control. We will soon begin publicly executing captured men. That should send a clear message to the people.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: Yes, but not likely the one you intend.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Oh? I don't expect anyone to miss my meaning. Come, Legate. There's much to do.

speaker: Leigelf
dialogue: Quicksilver Mine is the best mine in Dawnstar, and you can tell those Iron-Breaker miners I said so.

speaker: Lemkil
dialogue: You're right, it's none of your business. How about you keep your nose out of it?

speaker: Erik
dialogue: You keep on like you are, you'll end up with two daughters who hate you.

speaker: Lemkil
dialogue: Hah! And what would a witless oaf like you know about raising children?

speaker: Lemkil
dialogue: We don't need your charity, Breton. If my girls deserve something nice, it'll be their father who buys it.

speaker: Lemkil
dialogue: They've grown, all right - lazier and more stupid.

speaker: Mralki
dialogue: There's times I think you're the coldest man in Skyrim. This is your own flesh and blood you're talking about.

speaker: Lemkil
dialogue: Yes, and just like weeds, they're nothin' but trouble.

speaker: Leontius Salvius
dialogue: You should head on inside. Eydis or Skuli can take care of you.

speaker: Lillith Maiden-Loom
dialogue: Come to chat with an old woman, hmm? Do your good deed for the day?

speaker: Lillith
dialogue: Hello, Fralia dear.

speaker: Fralia
dialogue: Lillith―always a pleasure. Just browsing, or were you looking for something particular?

speaker: Lillith
dialogue: Funny you should ask. I'm in the market for a new locket. Something in polished silver, maybe. Big enough to hold, say, a folded-up letter?

speaker: Fralia
dialogue: Ahhh, I see. I think I know just what you need. I don't have anything like that here now, but my Eorlund―he can make you one right quick. When I get home, I'll have him start on it right away. Come back to pick it up in, oh... three days?

speaker: Lillith
dialogue: Perfect, my dear. Absolutely perfect. I'll see you then.

speaker: Lillith
dialogue: Everyone in this city is so on edge. I could use some good news, Skulvar.

speaker: Skulvar
dialogue: Ha! Four more geldings sold. Sound like good news to you?

speaker: Lillith
dialogue: Indeed. I do hate to admit it, but if nothing else, all the fighting lately has been a complete blessing to this business.

speaker: Skulvar
dialogue: Aye, that it has. Trust me, mum―once you've killed a man from a horse, you'll never want to fight on the ground again. Ain't no goin' back.

speaker: Lillith
dialogue: Why, thank you for that most colorful assessment, Skulvar. So we'll be needing fresh horses, then?

speaker: Skulvar
dialogue: Aye, mum. That we will. Mares, stallions, donkeys―I don't think it matters. Pretty sure I can sell any steeds we get.

speaker: Lillith
dialogue: Excellent. I'll send the proper letters, then, and have some fresh horses delivered straightaway.

speaker: Skulvar
dialogue: Lookin' forward to it.

speaker: Imedhnain
dialogue: Old Arnleif would be proud of Lisbet. She's kept this place running, thick and thin.

speaker: Lisbet
dialogue: What do I pay you for, to stand around all day? You're supposed to be bringing goods to the store.

speaker: Cosnach
dialogue: There are no goods to bring to the store. That's what I'm saying.

speaker: Lisbet
dialogue: Lazy oaf.

speaker: Lisbet
dialogue: Where are my goods? Did the shipment come in?

speaker: Cosnach
dialogue: Only a few things came today. Cedran said he'd drop it off later.

speaker: Lisbet
dialogue: Cedran said he'd... what am I paying you for? Next time, you bring the shipment in yourself.

speaker: Lisbet
dialogue: Imedhnain, I was just comparing the ledgers from last season.

speaker: Imedhnain
dialogue: Not too bad, I hope?

speaker: Lisbet
dialogue: Worse. The loss of shipments from Forsworn attacks are really hitting us hard.

speaker: Lisbet
dialogue: Where's Cosnach, is that lazy idiot out drinking at the Silver-Blood Inn again? On my coin?

speaker: Imedhnain
dialogue: He's just waiting for the shipments, Lisbet. He'll be back as soon as they come in.

speaker: Lisbet
dialogue: There are no shipments scheduled today. Stop covering for him!

speaker: Imedhnain
dialogue: He's my cousin. Just give him another chance. Please.

speaker: Lisbet
dialogue: Fine, I won't fire him, but I'm doing this for your sake. Not his.

speaker: Imedhnain
dialogue: Did you hear all that noise outside?

speaker: Lisbet
dialogue: It's just the market rabble. We should get back to work. {{Hide|You|Referring to the Dragonborn}} there. If you're here to trade, step up to the counter.

speaker: Hogni
dialogue: The toes are my favorite part. I hope I get to take a few home with me.

speaker: Lisbet
dialogue: I always preferred the liver myself. My brother had such a juicy liver.

speaker: Lisette
dialogue: Stick around! Still plenty of songs to sing and mead to drink.

speaker: Lisette
dialogue: Absolutely not. I prefer to be near enough to come visit but free to come and go as I please.

speaker: Lisette
dialogue: Not in our nature.

speaker: Una
dialogue: I'm pleased when the palace is clean, I'm pleased when the beds are made on time, I'm pleased when Erdi isn't around. Most of those don't happen very often.

speaker: Lod
dialogue: Men and women join the war, they travel far on these roads to spill each other's blood.

speaker: Lodvar
dialogue: Keep walking, stranger.

speaker: Logrolf the Willful
dialogue: You there. Are you here to kill me? Slay the mighty Logrolf while he sits tied and helpless?

speaker: Logrolf
dialogue: Molag Bal. You think you can best Boethiah's faithful? I have won this contest before!

speaker: Molag Bal
dialogue: Ah. But I have my own champion this time, Logrolf.

speaker: Logrolf
dialogue: What? {{Hide|You|Refering to the Dragonborn}}!

speaker: Molag Bal
dialogue: Mortal. I give you my mace, in all its rusted spitefulness. Crush the spirit from Logrolf's bones. Make him bend to me.

speaker: Logrolf
dialogue: No more.... No more.... I submit, Molag Bal. I submit!

speaker: Molag Bal
dialogue: You bend to me?

speaker: Molag Bal
dialogue: You pledge your soul to me?

speaker: Molag Bal
dialogue: You forsake the weak and pitiful Boethiah?

speaker: Molag Bal
dialogue: You're mine now, Logrolf. Kill him.

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: No, I'm not a rebel. You can't do this!

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Hey, you. You're finally awake. You were trying to cross the border, right? Walked right into that Imperial ambush, same as us, and that thief over there.

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: Damn you Stormcloaks. Skyrim was fine until you came along. Empire was nice and lazy. If they hadn't been looking for you, I could've stolen that horse and been halfway to Hammerfell. You there... You and me, we shouldn't be here. It's these Stormcloaks the Empire wants.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: We're all brothers and sisters in binds now, thief.

speaker: Imperial Soldier
dialogue: Shut up back there!

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: And what's wrong with him, huh?

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Watch your tongue. You're speaking to Ulfric Stormcloak, the true High King.

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: Ulfric? The Jarl of Windhelm? You're the leader of the rebellion. But if they've captured you... Oh gods, where are they taking us?

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: I don't know where we're going, but Sovngarde awaits.

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: No, this can't be happening. This isn't happening!

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Hey, what village are you from, horse thief?

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: Why do you care?

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: A Nord's last thoughts should be of home.

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: Rorikstead. I'm... I'm from Rorikstead.

speaker: Imperial
dialogue: General Tullius, sir! The headsman is waiting!

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Good. Let's get this over with.

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: Shor, Mara, Dibella, Kynareth, Akatosh. Divines, please help me.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Look at him, General Tullius, the Military Governor. And it looks like the Thalmor are with him. Damn elves. I bet they had something to do with this. This is Helgen. I used to be sweet on a girl from here. Wonder if Vilod is still making that mead with juniper berries mixed in. Funny, when I was a boy, Imperial walls and towers used to make me feel so safe.

speaker: Haming
dialogue: Who are they, daddy? Where are they going?

speaker: Torolf
dialogue: You need to go inside, little cub.

speaker: Haming
dialogue: Why? I want to watch the soldiers.

speaker: Torolf
dialogue: Inside the house. Now.

speaker: Haming
dialogue: Yes, papa.

speaker: Captain
dialogue: Get these prisoners out of the carts. Move it!

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: Why are we stopping?

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Why do you think? End of the line. Let's go. Shouldn't keep the gods waiting for us.

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: No! Wait! We're not rebels!

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Face your death with some courage, thief.

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: You've got to tell them! We weren't with you! This is a mistake!

speaker: Imperial Captain
dialogue: Step towards the block when we call your name. One at a time.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Empire loves their damn lists.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Ulfric Stormcloak. Jarl of Windhelm.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: It has been an honor, Jarl Ulfric!

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Ralof of Riverwood. Lokir of Rorikstead.

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: No, I'm not a rebel. You can't do this! [runs]

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: You're not going to kill me!

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Wait. You there. Step forward. Who are you?

speaker: Lond
dialogue: I mine. Work the smelter. Ain't much else to tell.

speaker: Lond
dialogue: If you don't mind me saying, Leigelf. You're working too hard. Go home.

speaker: Leigelf
dialogue: Never. Not until we turn this mine around, drive Beitild out of business, and force her to apologize to me for everything she's done!

speaker: Lond
dialogue: What is this feud you have with your wife? What started this?

speaker: Leigelf
dialogue: I don't want to talk about it.

speaker: Lond
dialogue: You don't want to talk about it, or you don't know?

speaker: Leigelf
dialogue: I don't want to talk about it.

speaker: Leigelf
dialogue: Thank you for sticking by me.

speaker: Lond
dialogue: Where else would I go? Dawnstar is my home and working here is my job.

speaker: Leigelf
dialogue: It's good to hear you say that. I wish my wife was as simple as you.

speaker: Lond
dialogue: I'll, uh, just take that as a compliment.

speaker: Lortheim
dialogue: Someday all of Skyrim will worship Talos openly, as we do here.

speaker: Elda
dialogue: Oh, Jora. Good to see you. I was wondering if you might ask Lortheim something for me.

speaker: Jora
dialogue: Don't bother. I don't have much chance of seeing my husband these days. He's always up in the palace with Ulfric.

speaker: Elda
dialogue: Oh, I'm sorry to hear that. Is everything all right?

speaker: Jora
dialogue: It's been better, I'll be honest with you.

speaker: Elda
dialogue: Here, let me get you some mead. This one's on me.

speaker: Jora
dialogue: I just don't know what to do anymore. He's hardly ever in the temple. I see him at breakfast, and that's it.

speaker: Elda
dialogue: I know, dear. He's a busy man, though, and loyal to the Stormcloaks.

speaker: Jora
dialogue: What about being loyal to his wife?

speaker: Elda
dialogue: I... I'm sorry, dear, I've got some other customers. I'll be back around in a minute.

speaker: Lu'ah Al-Skaven warning the Dragonborn
dialogue: I am Lu'ah Al-Skaven. Who are you to disrupt my work? Begone, or I will add you to my army of the dead!

speaker: Nazir
dialogue: He is, by all accounts, the worst bard in all of Skyrim.

speaker: Nazir
dialogue: Apparently so many people sought his death, Astrid had to hold a lottery to determine the client.

speaker: Lurbuk
dialogue: Jonna, do you think that the townspeople are warming to my serenades?

speaker: Jonna
dialogue: No. They ain't. And they aren't gonna. If you weren't paying for your room, I'd have thrown you out a long time ago.

speaker: Lurbuk
dialogue: Yes. But they'll come around. You'll see.

speaker: Jonna
dialogue: Oh. I wouldn't be surprised if they came 'round. And you're never seen or heard from again.

speaker: Lurbuk
dialogue: I'm thinking about composing a song about you, Jonna. Would you prefer I proclaim your beauty, your strength, your...

speaker: Jonna
dialogue: Nah. Just...don't. Leave me outta it.

speaker: Lurbuk
dialogue: No interest in being immortalized in song? Remembered and praised for all eternity?

speaker: Jonna
dialogue: No. I mean it.

speaker: Lurbuk
dialogue: When I'm known throughout Tamriel, you'll regret this decision.

speaker: Lydia
dialogue: I am your sword, and your shield.

speaker: Ma'dran
dialogue: It was Ri'saad's idea to come here now, while the land is in turmoil. Where others saw only danger, he saw opportunity.

speaker: Ma'randru-jo
dialogue: May you walk on warm sands.

speaker: Atahbah
dialogue: We have been in this land for so long, I have forgotten what it feels like to walk on warm sand.

speaker: Atahbah
dialogue: Do you ever find that you regret making this journey?

speaker: Atahbah
dialogue: That is true. Perhaps I should be more grateful for this opportunity. Not many Khajiit can say that they have visited Skyrim.

speaker: Ma'zaka
dialogue: Oh, for the salt spray, the creek of the mast and the clash of sabers. Those were the days...

speaker: Madanach
dialogue: That is who we are. The Forsworn. Criminals in our own lands. And we will cut a bloody hole into the Reach until we are free.

speaker: Uraccen
dialogue: What's going on, Madanach? You wouldn't have old Grisvar killed unless you weren't planning on needing him.

speaker: Madanach
dialogue: My brothers, we have been here long enough. It's time to leave Cidhna Mine and continue our fight against the Nords. Through this gate, just beside my quarters, is a tunnel. A tunnel that leads right through the old Dwarven ruins of Markarth, into the city. Well, what do you say, my brothers?

speaker: Duach
dialogue: The Reach belongs to the Forsworn!

speaker: Borkul the Beast
dialogue: The Reach belongs to the Forsworn!

speaker: Braig
dialogue: The Reach belongs to the Forsworn!

speaker: Uraccen
dialogue: The Reach belongs to the Forsworn!

speaker: Odvan
dialogue: The Reach belongs to the Forsworn!

speaker: Kaie
dialogue: Madanach. I've brought what you asked for.

speaker: Madanach
dialogue: Good work. Get ready while I have a word with our favorite outsider.

speaker: Madena
dialogue: I beg you, don't go into Silus's museum.

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: Jewelry with legendary Argonian craftsmanship!

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: Begging your pardon, milord. Your wife has run up quite an account in the last few months.

speaker: Bolli
dialogue: Outrageous! Who does she think she is?!

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: I believe she's trying to look as ravishing as possible for you, milord.

speaker: Bolli
dialogue: Oh, well... I suppose that's a noble cause. I'll settle this bill at the end of the day. Thank you.

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: Sorry Lady Dinya, but I've been busy of late.

speaker: Dinya
dialogue: It only takes but a moment to say a silent prayer to Mara. Please come by soon; not for me, but for yourself.

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: Very well, I'll try milady.

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: I wish I could, milady. Sadly, I haven't sold enough of my own jewelry, let alone buy some from you. I'm sorry.

speaker: Drifa
dialogue: Oh, I'm so sorry. I'm certain Bolli would be happy to lend you a few septims.

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: Much appreciated, Lady Drifa, but I'll manage.

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: There's no need to be rude, Grelka. If you don't care for Argonians, then perhaps you should take residence somewhere else.

speaker: Grelka
dialogue: Or perhaps you should crawl back into whatever swamp you came from, lizard man.

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: You're not going to goad me into a fight so I'll get kicked out, Grelka. Eat your food and leave me in peace.

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: Lady Haelga, so pleased to see you. Your Marks of Dibella are ready.

speaker: Haelga
dialogue: Oh, splendid! I can't wait to use them.

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: Begging your pardon milady... I know these have something to do with Dibella, but whatever are they for?

speaker: Haelga
dialogue: Maybe I'll show you one day, Madesi. Have them delivered to the Bunkhouse, won't you?

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: Lady Maven, how may I help you?

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Is it true that you refused to sell one of your... trinkets to Hemming?

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: Please, milady, it was only because he threatened me. He said he'd have me thrown in the prisons if I didn't give him what he wanted! I can't afford to just give my jewelry away!

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Next time a Black-Briar asks for something, I suggest you respond quickly and affirmatively.

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: Ah, Nivenor. What can I sell you on this fine day?

speaker: Nivenor
dialogue: I'm looking for a necklace. Do you have anything with garnets?

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: I have a single one left, quite expensive, but also quite elegant.

speaker: Nivenor
dialogue: Posh. I'm not paying for it. Put it on Bolli's account if you please.

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: Only thirty more and it'll be all yours. If I might ask, who is the lucky woman?

speaker: Shadr
dialogue: It's for Marise, but don't say a word to her!

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: Don't worry, Shadr, your secret is safe with me.

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: The cold stone...the dampness...it suits me, Svana.

speaker: Svana
dialogue: Are you sure that's the real reason? It wouldn't have anything to do with others making an Argonian unwelcome, because if it is...

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: You have a kind heart, much too kind for Riften. Don't worry about me, I'll be just fine.

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: They aren't invading, milord... it's simply a response to Ulfric and his Stormcloaks. I assure you everything will be fine.

speaker: Tythis
dialogue: But I've heard from the Snow-Shods that they intend to burn this place to the ground!

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: Tythis, please. The Snow-Shods are good people, but tend to exaggerate. Try and stay calm for your own sake.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Everyone! Everyone! Gather 'round! I have something amazing to show you that demands your attention! Gather 'round all! No pushing, no shoving. Plenty of room!

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: Come on, Brynjolf... what is it this time?

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Patience, Brand-Shei. This is a rare opportunity, and I wouldn't want you to get left out.

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: That's what you said about the Wisp Essence and it turned out to be crushed nirnroot mixed with water!

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: That was a simple misunderstanding, but this item is the real thing. Lads and lasses I give you, Falmerblood Elixir!

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: Oh come on, are you talking about the Snow Elves?

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: The one and only. Mystical beings who live in legends and were masters of great magic. Imagine the power that coursed through their veins!

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: How did you get that, then? No one's seen them in years!

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: My sources must remain a secret for their own protection but I can promise that the contents are genuine. One sip of the elixir and your wishes will be granted. Great wealth, everlasting life or perhaps limitless power could be yours!

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: How much does it cost?

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Only twenty gold septims! Hurry before my supply is gone.

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: Don't listen to him, he's making this up.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Please hurry, I have only a few bottles left!

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: That Wisp Essence didn't help, but maybe this will.

speaker: Madwoman
dialogue: You have it! The blessed Wabbajack! You must use it on me. You must.

speaker: Atub
dialogue: Now, we begin the ritual... Great Malacath, we beseech you, aid us in our time of need...

speaker: Yamarz
dialogue: Why are we bothering with this?

speaker: Malacath
dialogue: You pathetic weakling!

speaker: Yamarz
dialogue: What's that?

speaker: Atub
dialogue: Malacath has heard my pleas! He speaks to us!

speaker: Malacath
dialogue: You dare summon me, Yamarz?

speaker: Yamarz
dialogue: What? What is this?

speaker: Malacath
dialogue: You don't deserve to call yourself an Orc! You're weak, you're small, and you're an embarrassment! You let giants... Giants!... overrun my shrine. Bring me their leader's club as an offering, and I might release you from this curse!

speaker: Atub
dialogue: So it will be. Malacath has spoken, Yamarz. Your path is clear.

speaker: Yamarz
dialogue: Very well. {{Hide|You|Referring to the Dragonborn}}, outsider, come here! I want a word.

speaker: Malacath
dialogue: Yamarz was a coward and a weakling. His deceitful ways have cost you all greatly.

speaker: Atub
dialogue: So he has been punished? And what of us? What fate shall we suffer?

speaker: Malacath
dialogue: You'll have to prove yourselves, but I'm willing to give you a chance. Gularzob's in charge now. Let's hope he's a better chief. {{Hide|You|Referring to the Dragonborn}}, place that hammer on the shrine. You're the only one who's proven worthy in all of this...

speaker: Malborn
dialogue: Now the Thalmor will be hunting me for the rest of my life. I hope it was worth it.

speaker: Malborn
dialogue: Madame Ambassador, I'm so sorry to interrupt...

speaker: Elenwen
dialogue: What is it, Malborn?

speaker: Malborn
dialogue: It's just that we've run out of the Alto wine. Do I have your permission to uncork the Arenthia red...

speaker: Elenwen
dialogue: Of course. I've told you before not to bother me with such trifles.

speaker: Malborn
dialogue: Yes, Madame Ambassador.

speaker: Tsavani
dialogue: Who comes, Malborn? You know I don't like strange smells in my kitchen.

speaker: Malborn
dialogue: A guest, feeling ill. Leave the poor wretch be.

speaker: Tsavani
dialogue: A guest? In the kitchens? You know this is against the rules...

speaker: Malborn
dialogue: Rules, is it, Tsavani? I didn't realize that eating Moon Sugar was permitted. Perhaps I should ask the Ambassador...

speaker: Tsavani
dialogue: Tss! Get out of here, I saw nothing.

speaker: Mallus Maccius
dialogue: You need something to do, or do you just enjoy slowing down the hard-working folk?

speaker: Commander Caius
dialogue: Well, Sabjorn. Now that you've taken care of your little pest problem, how about I get a taste of some of your mead?

speaker: Sabjorn
dialogue: Help yourself, milord. It's my finest brew yet... I call it Honningbrew Reserve. I think you'll find it quite pleasing to your palate.
