speaker: Commander Caius
dialogue: Oh come now, this is mead... not some wine to be sipped and savored.

speaker: Commander Caius
dialogue: By the Eight?! What... what's in this?

speaker: Sabjorn
dialogue: I... I don't know. What's wrong?

speaker: Commander Caius
dialogue: You assured me this place was clean! I'll see... see to it that you remain in irons for the rest of your days!

speaker: Sabjorn
dialogue: No, please! I don't understand...

speaker: Commander Caius
dialogue: Silence, idiot! I should have known better... to trust this place after it's been riddled with filth.

speaker: Sabjorn
dialogue: I beg you... please. This is not what it seems!

speaker: Commander Caius
dialogue: You... you're in charge here until I can sort this all out.

speaker: Mallus Maccius
dialogue: It will be my pleasure.

speaker: Commander Caius
dialogue: And you... you're coming with me to Dragonsreach. We'll see how quickly your memory clears in the city's prisons. Now move.

speaker: Sabjorn
dialogue: Look, I assure you, this is all just a huge misunderstanding!

speaker: Commander Caius
dialogue: I said move!

speaker: Mallus Maccius
dialogue: Farewell, Sabjorn.

speaker: Malthyr Elenil
dialogue: I thought the Gray Quarter would be a haven for my kind. I was wrong.

speaker: Malthyr
dialogue: You're a war hero, Brunwulf. Ulfric will listen to you.

speaker: Brunwulf
dialogue: It's not that simple. Ulfric wants a Skyrim for the Nords. He doesn't trust what he calls 'outsiders'.

speaker: Malthyr
dialogue: You've seen how we live―cramped alleys, run-down buildings, few guard patrols. Even the name 'Gray Quarter' is an insult.

speaker: Brunwulf
dialogue: I'll speak to Ulfric soon, but I make no promises that I can change his mind.

speaker: Malthyr
dialogue: That's all I ask. With your help, we have a chance to make a better life for ourselves here. For that, I thank you.

speaker: Thonjolf
dialogue: I haven't even said what it is.

speaker: Malur
dialogue: Doesn't really matter. Thanks, but no.

speaker: Maramal
dialogue: Blessings of Mara upon you!

speaker: Maramal
dialogue: People of Riften, heed my words. The return of the dragons is not mere coincidence. This is one of the signs. The signs that Lady Mara is displeased with your constant inebriation. Put down your flagons filled with your vile liquids, and embrace the teachings of the handmaiden of Kyne.

speaker: Maramal
dialogue: Keerava, certainly we can come to some sort of understanding? These people must be made aware of the chaos they've sown.

speaker: Talen-Jei
dialogue: Enough, Maramal. We've all heard of the dragons and their return. There's no need to use them as an excuse to harass our customers.

speaker: Maramal
dialogue: Very well, Talen. I'll remove myself from this den of iniquity.

speaker: Talen-Jei
dialogue: We're not kicking you out, just keep the sermons at the temple and let us all sin in peace.

speaker: Maramal
dialogue: They laughed at me again, Dinya. They simply don't understand.

speaker: Dinya
dialogue: I'm so sorry my husband. You must remember, they're at the Bee and Barb to drink, not to listen to a sermon.

speaker: Maramal
dialogue: Yes, yes, I know. I just wish to show them there's more to life than drowning your sorrows in a goblet of mead.

speaker: Dinya
dialogue: You're a good man, Maramal. We're lucky to have you watching over us.

speaker: Maramal
dialogue: It fills me with joy to hear you're with child, Dinya. They said it wouldn't... that it couldn't happen, but Mara has shown them {{sicquote|they're|their}} mistake.

speaker: Dinya
dialogue: And to think I was wandering the ash wastes only two years ago. I never knew my path would lead to you.

speaker: Maramal
dialogue: You were guided here; you were always meant to be here. That's the way of things.

speaker: Dinya
dialogue: Then I thank Lady Mara with all my heart; for you, for our child and for our love.

speaker: Marcurio
dialogue: Why settle for just stabbing your foes when you can roast them alive in a gout of arcane fire?

speaker: Margret
dialogue: By the gods, that man nearly killed me. You saved my life.

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: A bit of jewelry for your journey home?

speaker: Weylin
dialogue: I die for my people.

speaker: Kerah
dialogue: By the Divines, the Forsworn are here in the city!

speaker: Markarth City Guard
dialogue: Everyone stay back. The Markarth city guard have this all under control. There are no Forsworn here.

speaker: Marise
dialogue: Sounds good. May I owe you for them?

speaker: Bolli
dialogue: Of course. Say, how are you going to sell all those fish before they spoil?

speaker: Marise
dialogue: You know I can't tell you that. As soon as I do, and you have a few meads in you, everyone will know.

speaker: Marise
dialogue: Dinya? I was reading that missive you gave me and I was wondering something about marriage.

speaker: Dinya
dialogue: Feel free to ask me anything you like.

speaker: Marise
dialogue: There's someone I like very much in Riften. I think I'd like to marry him someday, but... well, he's not of my kind. Would Mara be angry?

speaker: Dinya
dialogue: No, no... not at all. Mara believes that the spark of a union comes from inside us, not from our appearance. Tell you what... if you still feel unsure, come by the temple sometime and we'll talk about it.

speaker: Marise
dialogue: Can't tell you. It's a bit of a trade secret I picked up when I was living in High Rock.

speaker: Drifa
dialogue: Well, whatever you're doing, keep doing it and you'll have me as a customer for life.

speaker: Marise
dialogue: Oh! Miss Maven. What can I do for you?

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Relax, Marise... I have no quarrel with you. I just wish to speak a moment.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: You watch the market, you hear the rumors around Riften. What have you heard about these dragons?

speaker: Marise
dialogue: I heard a traveler say that Helgen was destroyed by one of those creatures. Didn't leave a soul alive they said.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Interesting. Keep your ears open for me and tell me if you hear anything more. I'll make it worth your while.

speaker: Marise
dialogue: What rumors?

speaker: Nivenor
dialogue: You know very well what I'm talking about. You're saying that I only married Bolli for his gold and that I don't really love him.

speaker: Marise
dialogue: Well, if the shoe fits...

speaker: Shadr
dialogue: Hi, Marise. How are you today?

speaker: Marise
dialogue: I'm well. How are things over at the stables? Old Hofgrir giving you a hard time?

speaker: Shadr
dialogue: Naw... he's fine. Look, I wanted to ask if you'll... um, if you'd like to... well, like to have a drink with me at the Bee and Barb sometime?

speaker: Marise
dialogue: Shadr, that's so sweet... I'd love to.

speaker: Marise
dialogue: I've heard. Bolli and Keerava were speaking of it just a little while ago.

speaker: Tythis
dialogue: I hope that doesn't mean things are going to get worse around here.

speaker: Indara Caerellia
dialogue: Mathies is a kind and wise man. The Nords could use more like him. So could the Imperials.

speaker: Maul
dialogue: Your mother seems to have taken to her seat quite well.

speaker: Hemming
dialogue: Yes, she's been grooming herself for this for quite a long time.

speaker: Maul
dialogue: It's surprising the Council is allowing a Nord rule Riften under the Imperial flag. That can't be their first choice.

speaker: Hemming
dialogue: Let's just say my mother knows which pockets to line and keep it at that.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Any word about our little problem in the Ratway?

speaker: Maul
dialogue: I've spoken to Brynjolf and he assures me it'll be taken care of.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Next time you speak to him, tell him to clean up his own messes. I'm not about to jeopardize this position for a bunch of low-life thugs.

speaker: Maul
dialogue: I'll let him know.

speaker: Maul
dialogue: My agents are telling me that we've appropriated the caravan from Hammerfell... with minimal losses.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: For what it's costing me, I should be handed the merchandise on a silver platter.

speaker: Maul
dialogue: The coin isn't just for the men, there's a lot of people that need to be compensated in order to make this happen.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: And a hefty cut for yourself too I'm sure. Just see to it the items are secured and the rest disposed of properly this time.

speaker: Maurice Jondrelle
dialogue: I am a traveler. A pilgrim. I follow the voice of Kynareth wherever it can be heard.

speaker: Maven Black-Briar
dialogue: My title is just a formality. I've always been in charge around here.

speaker: Maul
dialogue: Your mother seems to have taken to her seat quite well.

speaker: Hemming
dialogue: Yes, she's been grooming herself for this for quite a long time.

speaker: Maul
dialogue: It's surprising the Council is allowing a Nord rule Riften under the Imperial flag. That can't be their first choice.

speaker: Hemming
dialogue: Let's just say my mother knows which pockets to line and keep it at that.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: I don't like being made a fool of, Brand-Shei. Not one bit.

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: Maven, please. I didn't know it was your man. Had I known, I would have looked the other way, I swear.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Turning him in to the guards? Have you joined Mjoll as official peacekeepers of Riften? You cost me a lot of coin.

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: Maven, I... please, don't hurt me.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: Heard any news about the other parts of Skyrim?

speaker: Maven
dialogue: I'm not sure that it's news, but lately it seems like every blacksmith in Skyrim is out to prove that he's the equal of Eorlund Gray-Mane. It's not really a fair comparison, if you ask me. After all, Eorlund works the Skyforge. How is any smith going to compete with that?

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: Heard any news about the other parts of Skyrim?

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Well, I did hear that the Argonians have been banned from living inside the walls of Windhelm. They're only allowed on the city docks now. Most of them sleep together in one building, and they're as poor as wretches.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Grelka, how fast can you get your hands on some longbows?

speaker: Grelka
dialogue: I don't usually deal in weapons, but I know someone who can get them for me. You mind paying a little extra to get them fast?

speaker: Maven
dialogue: I don't care what it costs. I need four longbows and four score of arrows. Just make it happen.

speaker: Grelka
dialogue: I'll contact my man tonight and let you know what he says.

speaker: Haelga
dialogue: He wasn't protesting, Maven.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Of course he wasn't you stupid whore; he's a man. Now I'm not going to warn you again. Is that clear?

speaker: Haelga
dialogue: Very well.

speaker: Hemming
dialogue: Bersi still refuses to cooperate. What did you want to do?

speaker: Maven
dialogue: I've known Bersi a long time. Even before he opened that rubbish heap he calls a shop.

speaker: Hemming
dialogue: And if he still refuses?

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Then put the thumbscrews on him and hit him... hard.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Hemming, I want you to personally supervise the next shipment.

speaker: Hemming
dialogue: We already have people that do that and they make quite a bit of coin for it.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: I don't trust them. Come to think of it, I don't trust you either, but at least you're family.

speaker: Hemming
dialogue: Anything you say, Mother.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Hemming, I need you to bring a note to Sibbi. I need him to do something for me.

speaker: Hemming
dialogue: Sibbi? He's in prison... you put him there.

speaker: Hemming
dialogue: Why do you tolerate him, mother? All he contributes to this family is embarrassment and disgrace.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: I tolerate your son because he'll do anything I ask, without question. I'd expect the same from my own son.

speaker: Hemming
dialogue: I understand, mother. Forgive me.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Ingun, how much longer do you intend to waste your life concocting your foolish little potions?

speaker: Ingun
dialogue: I've told you, my interest in the family business is quite low. I wish to be much more than just a merchant.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Your interests lay where I wish them to lay otherwise my favorite daughter may end up homeless and without a septim to her name. Is that clear?

speaker: Ingun
dialogue: Yes, mother.

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: Lady Maven, how may I help you?

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Is it true that you refused to sell one of your... trinkets to Hemming?

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: Please, milady, it was only because he threatened me. He said he'd have me thrown in the prisons if I didn't give him what he wanted! I can't afford to just give my jewelry away!

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Next time a Black-Briar asks for something, I suggest you respond quickly and affirmatively.

speaker: Marise
dialogue: Oh! Miss Maven. What can I do for you?

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Relax, Marise... I have no quarrel with you. I just wish to speak a moment.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: You watch the market, you hear the rumors around Riften. What have you heard about these dragons?

speaker: Marise
dialogue: I heard a traveler say that Helgen was destroyed by one of those creatures. Didn't leave a soul alive they said.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Interesting. Keep your ears open for me and tell me if you hear anything more. I'll make it worth your while.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: Maven. How's the criminal underworld treating you this fine day?

speaker: Maven
dialogue: You may have everyone else impressed around here, but you don't impress me. You couldn't touch me if you wanted to.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: You're a cold, unfeeling bitch.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: My dear, you have no idea who you're trifling with. Now I suggest you turn around and rattle someone else's cage before you get hurt.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: I'm watching you, Maven Black-Briar. One day, you'll slip up and your Imperial friends won't be there to catch your fall.

speaker: Vulwulf
dialogue: Maven! So good to see you again. Hoist a flagon and celebrate with me!

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Vulwulf, it's always a pleasure. When you're standing downwind of me.

speaker: Vulwulf
dialogue: Sorry, what was that?

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Nothing Vulwulf... cheers.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: I'm telling you, Vulwulf, it's the investment you've been waiting for.

speaker: Vulwulf
dialogue: So I pay for the weapon shipments and you oversee their distribution to the Stormcloaks?

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Exactly. What better way to help the cause than to put weapons into the hands of young Nord warriors dying for their homeland?

speaker: Vulwulf
dialogue: Shor's Beard! You're right! I'll do it... provided you supervise the shipments personally.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Don't worry, I'll treat those shipments as if I owned them myself.

speaker: Hemming
dialogue: There's still the matter of the prisoner to discuss. Now, his family is willing to contribute handsomely if we release him.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: The execution will proceed as planned.

speaker: Hemming
dialogue: But, mother... this is quite a sizable contribution and the crime doesn't befit such a harsh punishment.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Are you going soft on me, Hemming? Perhaps I made the wrong choice installing you as steward.

speaker: Hemming
dialogue: No, mother. The execution will proceed as planned.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Hemming, have you dispatched that letter I gave you yesterday?

speaker: Hemming
dialogue: Yes, and I sent it with our fastest courier and under the cover of night, exactly as you specified.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Good. If I need to light a few fires in order to get what we need to defend this place from the Stormcloaks, so be it.

speaker: Hemming
dialogue: I'm almost certain he'll reach the Imperial City tomorrow, so we should have an answer by the end of the week.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: Maven! Always a pleasure to receive you. What can I help you with today?

speaker: Laila
dialogue: Yes, indeed. An entire caravan shipment of your mead taken by Imperial soldiers. What of it?

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Well, I'm also certain you're aware that our own city guard failed to provide the protection required to ensure safe passage of the shipment.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: Indeed. We lost three soldiers in that attack. A sad day for Riften.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: We... don't have enough to...

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Laila, Riften is my home, but if my meadery can't be safe here, I'll just move it elsewhere.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: No, that won't be necessary. You'll have compensation for your loss.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Thank you, Laila.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Any word about our little problem in the Ratway?

speaker: Maul
dialogue: I've spoken to Brynjolf and he assures me it'll be taken care of.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Next time you speak to him, tell him to clean up his own messes. I'm not about to jeopardize this position for a bunch of low-life thugs.

speaker: Maul
dialogue: I'll let him know.

speaker: Maul
dialogue: My agents are telling me that we've appropriated the caravan from Hammerfell... with minimal losses.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: For what it's costing me, I should be handed the merchandise on a silver platter.

speaker: Maul
dialogue: The coin isn't just for the men, there's a lot of people that need to be compensated in order to make this happen.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: And a hefty cut for yourself too I'm sure. Just see to it the items are secured and the rest disposed of properly this time.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Why are the potions I requested not completed?

speaker: Wylandriah
dialogue: I'm sorry, milady. The components for those elixirs are quite volatile and in some cases, very dangerous to handle. I must take care.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Excuses are not acceptable in my court. When I ask for something I expect results, and I expect them immediately.

speaker: Wylandriah
dialogue: Yes, milady. Sorry, milady. They will be completed.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: You've got a lot of nerve, suggesting something like that, to me of all people! If this was Riften, I'd have you thrown in the dungeon!

speaker: Razelan
dialogue: What? I didn't... hmm? No, listen, you must have misunderstood... I would never openly insult your... that is to say...

speaker: Maven
dialogue: You're a disgrace to the Empire. To think that you're actually the representative of the East Empire Company. When people talk about the decadent, tottering Empire, it's people like you they have in mind!

speaker: Elenwen
dialogue: Razelan. And you promised to behave yourself this time. Remove him. He's disturbing the other guests.

speaker: Razelan
dialogue: This is preposterous. Disrespect... insulting! I am tired of being hounded from all sides!

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Well, now. There's no need to ruin the party on my account. I don't think he'll be bothering me again.

speaker: Razelan
dialogue: That is absolutely untrue! Uh, that is, yes, of course. What... I don't understand why everyone... never mind.

speaker: Maul
dialogue: Halt in the name of the Jarl!

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Somehow I doubt that will persuade them.

speaker: Maul
dialogue: Stay back, lord!

speaker: Maven
dialogue: If they want my city, they're going to have to take it from me personally.

speaker: Maul
dialogue: Protect the Jarl with your lives!

speaker: Laila
dialogue: Ahhh... It's good to be home.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Welcome back. I've left a few surprises for you to discover.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: How kind of you. And I've brought an army to give you a going away parade.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: If you two are finished with the touching homecoming, there's a city in chaos out there.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: Indeed. Come, there is much to be done.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: I think I'll like living here.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: So enters Maven Black-Briar, the glint of Imperial coin in her eyes. So tell me, what's the price for a woman's integrity these days?

speaker: Maven
dialogue: You never were able to see the forest for the trees, were you?

speaker: Laila
dialogue: We Nords were proud warriors once. And we still could be. Evidenced by the men and women who fought and died bravely today. You could see that if you had any faith left in that black heart of yours. But no, you're content to snatch scraps falling off the Emperor's table. Fine. Take my home. Take my city. May it burn down around you.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: A bit melodramatic, even for you Laila. Pack your things and go.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: One day when you can see past your own interests, you will come to see that we were right. And this... This is all wrong.

speaker: Rikke
dialogue: If you ladies are finished bickering, there's much to be done. Jarl Black-Briar put your government together. Do it now, or there will be rioting in the streets. We must move quickly to prevent further violence.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Jarl Black-Briar. I must admit, I do like the sound of that. And don't worry about any rioting, Legate. I have it under control. We will soon begin publicly executing captured men. That should send a clear message to the people.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: Yes, but not likely the one you intend.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Oh? I don't expect anyone to miss my meaning. Come, Legate. There's much to do.

speaker: Mehrunes Dagon
dialogue: You found my razor. Good. Can you feel its hunger? Can you feel its..Frustration? Now I will make it again what it once was, what it shall always be. Draw a line of blood across the land in the name of Mehrunes Dagon!

speaker: Melaran
dialogue: No doubt most folk in Skyrim consider the dragons terrifying. I find them... wondrous.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: Melaran, you lazy milk-drinker, have you finished studying the imports from Black Marsh?

speaker: Melaran
dialogue: Indeed I have, sir. Elven weapons for their armies, sir. Elven material, but poor workmanship, like most of what we get from them.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: Scary, thinking of those boots with an army of Elven weapons at their command. Let's be thankful they're half a world away, eh?

speaker: Melaran
dialogue: Even a fine weapon is only as good as its wielder, sir. But they should fetch a high price from the Imperial army.

speaker: Erikur
dialogue: Right you are, elf! Or even from the rebels, if they've got enough money to make a competitive offer.

speaker: Melaran
dialogue: As always, lord, your loyalty is a shining example to us all.

speaker: Mercer Frey
dialogue: Then the die is cast, and once again my blade will taste Nightingale blood!

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Mercer? This is the one I was talking about... our new recruit.

speaker: Mercer Frey
dialogue: This better not be another waste of the Guild's resources, Brynjolf. Before we continue, I want to make one thing perfectly clear. If you play by the rules, you walk away rich. You break the rules and you lose your share. No debates, no discussion... you do what we say, when we say.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Wait a moment, you're not talking about Goldenglow, are you? Even our little Vex couldn't get in.

speaker: Mercer Frey
dialogue: You claim this recruit possesses an aptitude for our line of work. If so, let him prove it. Goldenglow Estate is critically important to one of our largest clients. However, the owner has suddenly decided to take matters into his own hands and shut us out. He needs to be taught a lesson. Brynjolf will provide you with the details.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Mercer, aren't you forgetting something?

speaker: Mercer Frey
dialogue: Hmm? Oh, yes. Since Brynjolf assures me you'll be nothing but a benefit to us, then you're in. Welcome to the Thieves Guild.

speaker: Mercer Frey
dialogue: Brynjolf, have you had a chance to speak to our contact in Whiterun?

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Sorry Mercer, they no longer wish to be involved in our operation.

speaker: Mercer Frey
dialogue: I trust you've applied the appropriate pressure in order to change their mind?

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: I have. I think we may have to turn this one over to the Dark Brotherhood.

speaker: Mercer Frey
dialogue: Yes, I'm afraid you're right. Such a shame...

speaker: Mercer Frey
dialogue: Do you honestly think your arrow will reach me before my blade finds your heart?

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: Give me a reason to try.

speaker: Mercer Frey
dialogue: You're a clever girl, Karliah. Buying Goldenglow Estate and funding Honningbrew Meadery was inspired.

speaker: Mercer Frey
dialogue: You always were a quick study.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: Not quick enough, otherwise Gallus would still be alive.

speaker: Mercer Frey
dialogue: Gallus had his wealth and he had you. All he had to do was look the other way.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: Did you forget your oath we took as Nightingales? Did you expect him to simply ignore your methods?

speaker: Mercer Frey
dialogue: Enough of all this mindless banter! Come on, Karliah. It's time for you and Gallus to become reunited!

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: I'm no fool, Mercer. Crossing blades with you would be a death sentence. But I can promise the next time we meet, it will be your undoing.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: He's here and he hasn't seen us yet. Brynjolf, watch the door.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Aye, lass. Nothing's getting by me.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: Climb down that ledge and see if you can...

speaker: Mercer
dialogue: Karliah, when will you learn you can't get the drop on me?

speaker: Mercer
dialogue: Karliah, I'll deal with you after I rid myself of your irksome companions. In the meantime, perhaps you and Brynjolf should get better acquainted.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: What's... what's happening... I can't stop myself.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: Damn you, Mercer! Fight it, Brynjolf... he's taken control of you!

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: I'm sorry lass, I... I can't...

speaker: Michel Lylvieve
dialogue: It's no easy thing to make a living in the wilds of Skyrim.

speaker: Mikael
dialogue: I don't have much of a reputation in Skyrim yet, but I'm working on that, one sweet lady at a time. Haha!

speaker: Mila Valentia
dialogue: I work with my mother, to sell fruits and vegetables. It's fun most days, but hard work.

speaker: Mila
dialogue: Can you close up the stand early today, mama?

speaker: Carlotta
dialogue: I'm afraid not, little fairy. The fruit has about another day left before it spoils. We've got to sell as much as we can, as soon as we can.

speaker: Mila
dialogue: That's what you always say.

speaker: Carlotta
dialogue: Because it's always true.

speaker: Mila
dialogue: Can we at least go to the tavern for supper?

speaker: Carlotta
dialogue: Tsk. And to think, I was going to feed you cabbages and apples again. Yes, little fairy, we can go to the tavern for supper.

speaker: Minette Vinius
dialogue: Hey, wanna play tag?

speaker: Corpulus
dialogue: Yes, yes, fine. Just hurry! Mustn't keep the customers thirsty!

speaker: Mirabelle
dialogue: I've had yet another complaint. Please stop barging in on experiments in progress.

speaker: Ancano
dialogue: My dear, I am merely observing the proceedings.

speaker: Mirabelle
dialogue: Well then 'observe' from a greater distance. You're making people uncomfortable.

speaker: Mirabelle
dialogue: I continue to hear things about dragon sightings in Skyrim.

speaker: Savos
dialogue: Dragons? Well, that's fascinating. We should have someone look into that.

speaker: Mirabelle
dialogue: Would you like me to send someone? Faralda or Phinis, perhaps?

speaker: Mirabelle
dialogue: Arch-Mage, the Synod have contacted us again, asking if we've any word on their researchers.

speaker: Savos
dialogue: What did you tell them last time?

speaker: Mirabelle
dialogue: That they had arrived, asked for information which was provided to them, and went on their way with no suggestion of further interaction.

speaker: Savos
dialogue: That hasn't changed, has it? Then just tell them again.

speaker: Mirabelle
dialogue: Should we consider investigating the matter?

speaker: Savos
dialogue: No, I don't think so. Respond to their request, and we'll leave it at that.

speaker: Savos
dialogue: Is there anything new I should be aware of, Mirabelle?

speaker: Mirabelle
dialogue: I'm dealing with a few new research proposals, evaluating the results of three long-term projects, and keeping an eye on our new Apprentices. There were also two items requiring disciplinary action recently.

speaker: Savos
dialogue: Everything's under control, then? Right. Keep up the good work.

speaker: Savos
dialogue: The same thing we've told them before, and the same thing we've told these Stormcloaks. It's not our concern.

speaker: Mirabelle
dialogue: Forgive me, but at what point does it become our concern?

speaker: Savos
dialogue: Mirabelle, would you please make sure my schedule is clear for the next few days? I'm working on something important.

speaker: Mirabelle
dialogue: Your schedule is always clear, Arch-Mage. I see to that.

speaker: Mirabelle
dialogue: Its like a ward, but who's casting it? Ancano? How?

speaker: Mithorpa Nasyal
dialogue: I mean no offense. I am but a humble farmer. Not a... a great wanderer, like you.

speaker: Mjoll the Lioness
dialogue: I've been adventuring across Tamriel since I was a fresh-faced young woman barely able to swing a blade.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: I had another run-in with the Thieves Guild.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: They represent the reason I'm here. I can't just ignore them, Aerin.

speaker: Aerin
dialogue: I know. I just don't want you to leave; you're the only good thing that's happened to this city in a long time.

speaker: Aerin
dialogue: Well, you were right. These so called 'Gutter Saints' live in the sewers beneath.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: I suspected as much. The real question now is do we do something about it ourselves or do we speak to the Jarl?

speaker: Aerin
dialogue: I say we go down there and clear the place out, just like old times.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: No, my friend. That would be reckless. We have to help, but help in a way that doesn't directly place anyone in harm's way. For now, give this 'Ratway' a wide berth.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: Sometimes I'm not certain that the people of Riften want to be helped.

speaker: Aerin
dialogue: I think some of them do, Lady Mjoll. They're just too frightened to step up and do something about it like you are.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: Aerin, you never cease to amaze me. You always see the good in everything.

speaker: Aerin
dialogue: It's only because I've had an excellent teacher.

speaker: Aerin
dialogue: You've been in Riften for quite some time now, Lady Mjoll. I fear that you soon may leave us.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: Riften has problems of its own. Now is not the time for exploration and discovery.

speaker: Aerin
dialogue: I'm relieved to hear you say that. If you were to leave, I'd miss you terribly.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: Aerin, I owe you my life. It would take a threat to all of Skyrim for me to depart.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: Aerin, have you seen my ring? The one with the inscription?

speaker: Aerin
dialogue: No, I haven't. Don't tell me you've lost it.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: I hope not. That ring is irreplaceable.

speaker: Aerin
dialogue: I'll look around the house and if I find it, I'll bring it to you right away.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: Well met, Brand-Shei. I've come by to browse your wares today.

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: Is it true you chased a thief from your home? I overheard Aerin mentioning it.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: It's true. Wasn't much of a thief though. Made enough noise to wake the Red Mountain.

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: Good. Maybe that will teach them to leave honest citizens alone.

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: I'm afraid not. I don't deal in stolen goods.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: Stolen? How can you be certain? I may have just misplaced it somewhere in the city.

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: Lady Mjoll, if you lost a gold ring anywhere in this city I'm afraid it's likely never to be seen again. I'm sorry.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: What is it, Drifa? What's the matter?

speaker: Drifa
dialogue: It's Bersi. He's getting so angry about the corruption in Riften, he said he's going to walk right up to Maven and give her a piece of his mind.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: If I see him, I'll make sure he doesn't do anything brash. Don't worry.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: Aerin tells me you might be dealing arms to the Thieves Guild. Is this true?

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: I'm watching you, Grelka. One slip up and I report you to the guards. You got that?

speaker: Grelka
dialogue: Whatever you say.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: Madesi, my friend. How have things been since last week's incident?

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: Ever since you scared off that thug from the Thieves Guild, not one of them's bothered me. We're lucky to have you here.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: It's my pleasure. If you see the Thieves Guild harassing anyone else, you be sure and let me know.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: Maven. How's the criminal underworld treating you this fine day?

speaker: Maven
dialogue: You may have everyone else impressed around here, but you don't impress me. You couldn't touch me if you wanted to.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: You're a cold, unfeeling bitch.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: My dear, you have no idea who you're trifling with. Now I suggest you turn around and rattle someone else's cage before you get hurt.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: I'm watching you, Maven Black-Briar. One day, you'll slip up and your Imperial friends won't be there to catch your fall.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: Have you prepared the stables like I suggested, Shadr?

speaker: Shadr
dialogue: Yes, Lady Mjoll. If Riften gets attacked, we'll retreat inside the city gates and bar the door just like you said.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: Good. You could be our first line of defense since you live outside the city walls, so we're depending on you.

speaker: Moira
dialogue: Darling! I've been waiting for you to return, to consummate our love!

speaker: Serana
dialogue: The first vampire came from Molag Bal. She...was not a willing subject, but she was still the first.

speaker: Molag Bal upon completing his quest.
dialogue: Ah, you have freed the soul of Menta Na. Torment will be his, endless agony is all he will know until the end of time! You have performed well, mortal. Perhaps you will be my servant again one day. Take this, and use it well. Bring strife and discord with you wherever you may travel. Now go!

speaker: Logrolf
dialogue: Molag Bal. You think you can best Boethiah's faithful? I have won this contest before!

speaker: Molag Bal
dialogue: Ah. But I have my own champion this time, Logrolf.

speaker: Logrolf
dialogue: What? {{Hide|You|Refering to the Dragonborn}}!

speaker: Molag Bal
dialogue: Mortal. I give you my mace, in all its rusted spitefulness. Crush the spirit from Logrolf's bones. Make him bend to me.

speaker: Logrolf
dialogue: No more.... No more.... I submit, Molag Bal. I submit!

speaker: Molag Bal
dialogue: You bend to me?

speaker: Molag Bal
dialogue: You pledge your soul to me?

speaker: Molag Bal
dialogue: You forsake the weak and pitiful Boethiah?

speaker: Molag Bal
dialogue: You're mine now, Logrolf. Kill him.

speaker: Molgrom Twice-Killed
dialogue: Brynjolf sent you to rub it in?

speaker: Morven
dialogue: Ugh! That it? That your best?

speaker: Moth gro-Bagol
dialogue: The Empire has always been good to the Orcs, but this war of theirs is none of my concern.

speaker: Moth
dialogue: It's fine. Much better than the rickety tools I had in the Legion.

speaker: Thongvor
dialogue: Remember that old rusty sword I had? Damn thing must have had over a hundred chips in it.

speaker: Moth
dialogue: Well, if you had learned to swing it correctly. A sword is an extension of the arm, not a meat cleaver.

speaker: Thongvor
dialogue: I was about to say how impressed I was that you always managed to put it back together.

speaker: Moth
dialogue: Flattery doesn't suit you, Thongvor.

speaker: Moth
dialogue: Hello, my friend. Come to visit the forge?

speaker: Thongvor
dialogue: I grow tired of counting coin all day. Put steel in my hand, not gold.

speaker: Moth
dialogue: Your family's success burdens you, does it?

speaker: Thongvor
dialogue: Sometimes I miss the Legion, back when the Empire stood up for Skyrim.

speaker: Moth
dialogue: No politics, Thongvor. I told you before.

speaker: Erik
dialogue: Father, how old were you when you left home?

speaker: Mralki
dialogue: I know where this is going, son. As I've said many a time. the world is a dangerous place. You're much safer here at the farm, with me.

speaker: Erik
dialogue: But I don't want to be safe! I'm not afraid of the dangers out there. The only thing I'm afraid of is wasting my life on this farm.

speaker: Mralki
dialogue: Yes, that's your mother's side of the family talking. Just stay on for one more season, that's all I ask.

speaker: Mralki
dialogue: I heard you sneaking around downstairs last night. Were you trying to break into my chest again, son? I've told you to leave it alone.

speaker: Erik
dialogue: I just wanted to try on your old armor, from back when you were a soldier. I thought I might be old enough to wear it.

speaker: Mralki
dialogue: I've told you a hundred times, I lock that chest for a reason. I don't want you getting a head full of ideas about adventure and glory.

speaker: Erik
dialogue: I'm old enough to decide how to live my life, and I'd be honored to wear your armor, if you'd just let me. I'm strong enough to handle it.

speaker: Mralki
dialogue: Strong, yes, but how clever are you? I'll tell you what, if you can open the lock on my chest, you can have everything in it.

speaker: Erik
dialogue: I'll take your challenge, but if I win I get to start a new life as an adventurer, and with no objections from you.

speaker: Muiri
dialogue: Alain used me to get close to my friends. And now they all think I'm some kind of... monster. Alain Dufont took my life. And now I'm taking his.

speaker: Mulush gro-Shugurz
dialogue: I oversee Markarth Smelter. Worker gets out of line, I get him back in line.

speaker: Mulush
dialogue: I could smelt metal in half the time as you weak-willed pink-skins. Do I have to do everything?

speaker: Mulush
dialogue: I don't want any of you thieving workers even thinking about stealing any silver. If I see you sneaking off with even one speck of silver, I'll break your leg and throw you into the river.

speaker: Hathrasil
dialogue: Yes, Mulush.

speaker: Omluag
dialogue: Mulush, we need a break. The heat from the smelter is too much.

speaker: Mulush
dialogue: Are you complaining? Work. If you have strength to whine, you have strength to smelt.

speaker: Mulush
dialogue: Careful. You spill one drop of silver, I'm taking it out of your hide.

speaker: Omluag
dialogue: I'm being as careful as I can.

speaker: Mulush
dialogue: Did you just talk back to me? I'm not paid to listen. I'm paid to keep you working. Now work.

speaker: Burguk
dialogue: Tell me, mother, does Malacath favor our stronghold?

speaker: Murbul
dialogue: He is pleased. Ours is the strongest tribe in all the Reach.

speaker: Nagrub
dialogue: Brother Umurn is a strong warrior. I look forward to fighting him for chiefdom one day.

speaker: Nagrub
dialogue: Ah, the air is good today. I welcome the smell of blood from all the kills I will make.

speaker: Arob
dialogue: Patience, my son. The hunter {{sic|days|does}} not welcome the blood of his prey, he waits for it.

speaker: Arob
dialogue: The air has the smell of beasts. The hunt is good today.

speaker: Nagrub
dialogue: Yes, mother. I'm eager to prove my skills today.

speaker: Rhiada
dialogue: Ildene has been working in the Treasury House since before I was born.

speaker: Ildene
dialogue: Yes, child. Nana Ildene has taken care of the Silver-Bloods for many years....

speaker: Rhiada
dialogue: It's just... aren't you worried about the Forsworn? Maybe it's not safe here.

speaker: Ildene
dialogue: Don't you worry Rhiada. If any Forsworn coming knocking on our door, Nana will let you know....

speaker: Rhiada
dialogue: Thanks Nana. I feel better now.

speaker: Ildene
dialogue: Ah, Thonar, don't you worry. Nana Ildene isn't going anywhere.

speaker: Thonar
dialogue: Um, good. We reward loyalty, you know.

speaker: Ildene
dialogue: Oh, I know, Thonar. Only a mad woman would ever betray the Silver-Blood family.

speaker: Thonar
dialogue: Uh, yes. Quite.

speaker: Naris the Wicked
dialogue: Ah, the sweet smell of burnt flesh. Nothing better really.

speaker: Narri
dialogue: I've half a mind to ask if you'll take me on one of your adventures, but I can't just leave Valga on her own.

speaker: Nazeem
dialogue: Do you get to the Cloud District very often? Oh, what am I saying, of course you don't.

speaker: Nazeem
dialogue: Do you have anything even remotely fresh?

speaker: Anoriath
dialogue: I can assure you, it's all fresh. I hunt the game myself, every day.

speaker: Nazeem
dialogue: Hmm. As you say.

speaker: Anoriath
dialogue: Maybe you'd like to try the horker? Or some beef?

speaker: Nazeem
dialogue: You don't prepare the meat with any of those strange Elven spices, do you?

speaker: Anoriath
dialogue: Ahhhh... No, no Elven spices; just some salt, to preserve it. You're not afraid of salt, are you?

speaker: Nazeem
dialogue: I'm not 'afraid' of anything. I simply prefer quality merchandise. No, no this meat won't do at all. Too much fat, and it all smells... wrong.

speaker: Anoriath
dialogue: Suit yourself, then. The woods are that way. Outside the walls, walk straight ahead. Can't miss them. Good luck on your hunt.

speaker: Nazeem
dialogue: Good day.

speaker: Nazeem
dialogue: These fruits and vegetables are disappointing, Carlotta.

speaker: Carlotta
dialogue: I get them fresh from the farms daily, Nazeem.

speaker: Nazeem
dialogue: If you were getting them from my farm, they'd be twice as fresh.

speaker: Nazeem
dialogue: Ah, Ysolda was it? What brings you to the market?

speaker: Ysolda
dialogue: I'm here to buy food, Nazeem. I suppose you don't need to worry about that.

speaker: Nazeem
dialogue: Owning a farm does have its advantages.

speaker: Nazir
dialogue: I don't like mimes, minstrels, thespians, acrobats, jugglers, troubadours or tumblers. Flutists give me a headache. I particularly hate jesters.

speaker: Arnbjorn
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Veezara
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha! Again! Again! Do the part where he tries to buy you some candy.

speaker: Gabriella
dialogue: Oh Babette, but you are so wicked.

speaker: Nazir
dialogue: What about you, Festus? How did that last contract turn out?

speaker: Arnbjorn
dialogue: Oh, yes, please, old man. Regale us with your tales of wizardry...

speaker: Gabriella
dialogue: And what of your latest, Arnbjorn. Something about a Khajiit? Merchant was it?

speaker: Babette
dialogue: Oh, a big doggy chasing a little kitty! How adorable!

speaker: Nazir
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Festus
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Veezara
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Arnbjorn
dialogue: I am not adorable, it was not funny, and he wasn't a merchant. He was a Khajiit monk, a master of the Whispering Fang style. But now he's dead... and I have a new loincloth.

speaker: Nazir
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Festus
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Veezara
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Babette
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Babette
dialogue: Just try to relax, Veezara. Let the elixir do its work. You'll feel better, shortly.

speaker: Veezara
dialogue: Achh... Thank you, dear. You are most kind. The jester's cut feels as bad as it looks, I'm afraid.

speaker: Astrid
dialogue: Damn it, this never should have happened! We knew better. We knew better, and still we let our guards down. Agh!

speaker: Festus Krex
dialogue: It's true, I'm afraid, Cicero was a little whirlwind, slashing this way and all that. It would have been funny, if he weren't trying to murder us all.

speaker: Veezara
dialogue: Bested by a fool. Who's the fool now, hmm?

speaker: Babette
dialogue: Hush, Veezara. You were very brave. Astrid may well be dead if not for you.

speaker: Astrid
dialogue: She's right. I'll be forever in your debt, dearest brother. Now be quiet. Just... just rest.

speaker: Nazir
dialogue: I'm going... as fast... as I can, you stupid she-devil. I don't see you... helping...

speaker: Babette
dialogue: I'm not exactly built for manual labor. Now come on, you've almost got it.

speaker: Nazir
dialogue: One more... pull... Yeeaahh! There.

speaker: Babette
dialogue: Can you get it open?

speaker: Nazir
dialogue: I think so. Just hold on a moment.

speaker: Nazir
dialogue: Babette, my girl - pack your things. We're moving.

speaker: Babette
dialogue: I was hoping you'd say that.

speaker: Ritual Master
dialogue: Wolf Queen. Hear our call and awaken. We summon Potema!

speaker: Ritual Master
dialogue: We summon Potema!

speaker: Necromancer
dialogue: We summon Potema!

speaker: Necromancer 2
dialogue: We summon Potema!

speaker: Ritual Master
dialogue: Long have you slept the dreamless sleep of death, Potema. No longer. Hear us Wolf Queen! We Summon You!

speaker: Ritual Master
dialogue: Summoned with words. Bounds by blood.

speaker: Necromancer
dialogue: We summon Potema!

speaker: Necromancer 2
dialogue: We summon Potema!

speaker: Potema
dialogue: Yes! Yes! Return me to this realm!

speaker: Ritual Master
dialogue: As our voices summon you the blood of the innocent binds you Wolf Queen!

speaker: Ritual Master
dialogue: Summoned with words. Bounds by blood.

speaker: Necromancer
dialogue: Summoned with words. Bounds by blood.

speaker: Necromancer 2
dialogue: Summoned with words. Bounds by blood.

speaker: Potema
dialogue: What! What are you doing?! You fools! You cannot bind me to your wills!

speaker: Ritual Master
dialogue: Summoned with words. Bounds by blood.

speaker: Necromancer
dialogue: Summoned with words. Bounds by blood.

speaker: Necromancer 2
dialogue: Summoned with words. Bounds by blood.

speaker: Potema
dialogue: You ants don't have the power to bind me!

speaker: Necromancer
dialogue: We offer this soul to The Revenant; he who watches over the opponents of Arkay and his power over life and death. Fie upon Arkay and his followers!

speaker: Necromancer 3
dialogue: Yeah, fie!

speaker: Necromancer
dialogue: Fie! We beseech you. Darken this gem so that we may use its powers to restore The Order of the Black Worm. The Order shall rise. Grant us this power so that in your name we may vanquish our enemies.

speaker: Necromancer
dialogue: More souls are needed for the Star. The last one died before he could be harvested.

speaker: Necromancer 2
dialogue: We can't take another villager from the surface so soon. I told you to prepare everything properly!

speaker: Necromancer
dialogue: We can just sacrifice another disciple. Apprentice Haerlon will be no great waste.

speaker: Necromancer 2
dialogue: Yes. He'll do.

speaker: Neetrenaza
dialogue: The Nords don't appreciate us, but so what? I don't appreciate them right back.

speaker: Nelacar
dialogue: I left Winterhold for some time, and returned to stay here at the inn.

speaker: Nelacar
dialogue: I'm sorry, could you describe the smell?

speaker: Dagur
dialogue: Like some horrible monster was turned inside out, and then exploded. What did you do?

speaker: Nelacar
dialogue: It was a minor miscalculation. I've already corrected it for future experiments.

speaker: Dagur
dialogue: This, this is why people have a problem with your college, Nelacar.

speaker: Dagur
dialogue: Is everything well, Nelacar?

speaker: Nelacar
dialogue: Oh yes, quite fine. My accommodations here continue to be just what I need.

speaker: Dagur
dialogue: And there haven't been any... problems?

speaker: Nelacar
dialogue: Are you referring to your other customers? No, everything is quite all right. I expect a bit of animosity now and then.

speaker: Dagur
dialogue: I see. Well, let me know if things get out of hand.

speaker: Nelacar
dialogue: I say, you didn't hear any loud noises last night, did you? No, ahh... explosion sounds?

speaker: Dagur
dialogue: No, I certainly didn't! Is there a reason you're asking me?

speaker: Nelacar
dialogue: No, certainly not. A small experiment may have gone awry, but clearly with no discernable consequences.

speaker: Dagur
dialogue: I... see. And is this something I'll need to worry about in the future?

speaker: Nelacar
dialogue: Oh, certainly I hope not! That would be quite unfortunate for my research.

speaker: Nelkir
dialogue: Another wanderer, here to lick my father's boots. Good job.

speaker: Nenya
dialogue: For Falkreath and I this is just one more war in a long line.

speaker: Siddgeir
dialogue: Why have taxes not come in from Granite Hill, Nenya? We should send some guards down there.

speaker: Nenya
dialogue: They are only a little late, Jarl. The trade routes are affected by the war, we should give them another day.

speaker: Siddgeir
dialogue: Very well, but when their emissary arrives I want words with him.

speaker: Helvard
dialogue: Preparing the defenses is almost impossible lately, every time we get a new war report our needs change.

speaker: Nenya
dialogue: The trade routes are affected as well. Procuring supplies is a guessing game. Weapons sell well though.

speaker: Helvard
dialogue: Mmmm, careful with that, Nenya, our merchants could be selling weapons to an invading force.

speaker: Nepos the Nose
dialogue: I've been playing this game for almost 20 years. Sending the young to their deaths. All in the name of the Forsworn. And I'm tired. So tired.

speaker: Nerien
dialogue: Take great care, and know that the Order is watching.

speaker: Valdr
dialogue: Spriggans. Niels went down before we even knew to run. Ari died just inside. I never even thought the things were real.

speaker: Nils
dialogue: When I'm cutting wood, I pretend there's an Imperial soldier's head on the stump.

speaker: Brunwulf
dialogue: How long have you run this place, again?

speaker: Elda
dialogue: Nearly thirty years now.

speaker: Brunwulf
dialogue: Just wondering when you'll be ready to give it up and settle down. Seems like you're always working.

speaker: Elda
dialogue: I just feel like if I'm not here, then something could go wrong. Nils is a hard worker, but I wouldn't trust him to run things.

speaker: Brunwulf
dialogue: One of these days he'll have to learn.

speaker: Elda
dialogue: Perhaps. But not today.

speaker: Nilsine Shatter-Shield
dialogue: My father says we need to just get on with our lives. Like it's that easy.

speaker: Nilsine
dialogue: Is that new batch of tomatoes ready for sale yet, Hillevi?

speaker: Hillevi
dialogue: You know, I'm not sure. My husband's been tending to the vines, so I'll have to ask him.

speaker: Nilsine
dialogue: Just promise me when you get some more in, I'll have the first crack at them.

speaker: Nilsine
dialogue: So serious! Ha ha ha!

speaker: Torsten
dialogue: How's business today?

speaker: Hillevi
dialogue: Well enough, I suppose. Nilsine bought up most of the tomatoes, and was asking if we could get more.

speaker: Torsten
dialogue: We've got another dozen ripening on the vine. They should be ready in a few days.

speaker: Hillevi
dialogue: I'll be sure to tell her.

speaker: Niluva Hlaalu
dialogue: Hey, don't look at me that way! Who are you to judge me?

speaker: Niluva
dialogue: Just give me a few more days and I promise I'll come up with it.

speaker: Tythis
dialogue: If you'd stop wasting your coin on that Skooma, you'd have enough gold to live on!

speaker: Niluva
dialogue: Sorry, Tythis. I'll get it to you somehow.

speaker: Niluva
dialogue: Do you know what Indaryn told me? He said that if I'm late one more time, he's going to kick me out the door!

speaker: Niluva
dialogue: What do you mean?

speaker: Romlyn
dialogue: All I'm saying is Indaryn's going to push too far one day and they're going to push back...hard.

speaker: Niranye
dialogue: Just got here from the Summerset Isles. Lots of opportunity in Skyrim.

speaker: Revyn
dialogue: Niranye, I just have to know―what is your secret?

speaker: Niranye
dialogue: My... my what, now?

speaker: Revyn
dialogue: You know. Where do you get your goods? I am always amazed at how you manage to sell things so cheaply.

speaker: Revyn
dialogue: Well, I'll want to meet them next time they're around. Maybe you can give me an introduction.

speaker: Niranye
dialogue: I'll consider it. Many of the people I deal with are... secretive. You know how it is.

speaker: Revyn
dialogue: Of course! I understand completely. You just put us in a room, and I'll do all the talking. No worries at all.

speaker: Niranye
dialogue: Captain Lonely-Gale, it's always a pleasure to see you. In fact, I'm glad you're here. There's something I'd like to ask you.

speaker: Niranye
dialogue: I was wondering if you still had many associates in the shipping profession. I have a business proposition for any sailors who might be looking to make a few extra septims.

speaker: Lonely-Gale
dialogue: If that business proposition includes smuggling, forget it. The sailors I know are plenty good at finding trouble without any help from you.

speaker: Niranye
dialogue: You're such a wet blanket, captain. Can't a girl have a little fun from time to time?

speaker: Jora
dialogue: We accept the risks that come with our faith, but I'll keep your offer in mind. Thank you, Niranye.

speaker: Torbjorn
dialogue: I've been meaning to speak to you, Niranye. Rumor is, you've got ties with the Thieves' Guild.

speaker: Niranye
dialogue: One should never pay too much attention to rumors, Torbjorn. You have piqued my curiosity, however. Please, do continue.

speaker: Torbjorn
dialogue: It's a bad time to be a criminal, what with these murders going on. In fact, thieves have been known to kill, if there's a profit in it. This war's been hard on all of us.

speaker: Niranye
dialogue: Not that I'd know anything about it, of course, but it seems to me that the last thing a thieves' guild would want is to draw attention to itself.

speaker: Torbjorn
dialogue: The eyes of the law are everywhere these days. The guards are looking for a killer, but who knows what else they might turn up? Good day.

speaker: Niruin
dialogue: What in the name of Oblivion is going on in this place?

speaker: Niruin
dialogue: Hey, I still have a contact in Valenwood that may have some work for us. You're welcome to join me.

speaker: Vipir
dialogue: I'll keep that in mind.

speaker: Vipir
dialogue: I tried to fence some goods to Tonilia, and you know what she told me?

speaker: Niruin
dialogue: I think I know, but go ahead.

speaker: Vipir
dialogue: She said that she barely had enough coin to cover it and I should come back later. Can you imagine that?

speaker: Niruin
dialogue: This place is getting worse and worse.

speaker: Vipir
dialogue: How's the training going?

speaker: Niruin
dialogue: Better than ever. With the Guild back on its feet, there's more coin to throw around. How about you?

speaker: Vipir
dialogue: Couldn't be busier.

speaker: Niruin
dialogue: Let's just hope it stays this way for a long time.

speaker: Nirya
dialogue: I'm sure you've made note of who's been the most helpful during your time here, Arch-Mage.

speaker: Nivenor
dialogue: If you're looking for a handout, you'll want to speak with my husband. If you're looking for company, I suppose I could do worse.

speaker: Nivenor
dialogue: And just what's that supposed to mean?

speaker: Bolli
dialogue: It means I have a business to run, I need to have the books straight and you're barely ever here!

speaker: Nivenor
dialogue: For goodness sake, Bolli! You barely lift a finger yourself when you're here except to point at things for your workers to do. Let them do the work, that's what you pay them for!

speaker: Nivenor
dialogue: Bolli, I was looking at the finances and I noticed you've been donating gold to the Temple of Mara. Are you out of your mind?

speaker: Bolli
dialogue: Maramal's been helping me through a rough patch. I just wanted to pay him back. It's not like he's keeping it!

speaker: Nivenor
dialogue: Uh huh. I'm sure he runs outside with the coin and throws it up in the air so Mara herself can catch it. Come off of it, Bolli.

speaker: Bolli
dialogue: You may be my wife, but this is my business, so just do your job. Don't worry, you'll still have plenty of gold left over to waste on trinkets.

speaker: Nivenor
dialogue: Brand-Shei, do you think you can find me some theilul?

speaker: Nivenor
dialogue: That's fine. I have a special occasion coming up, and I'd like to have it.

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: I'll see what I can do.

speaker: Nivenor
dialogue: How do you think? He's a pig. All I am to him is a warm body to lay with.

speaker: Drifa
dialogue: Nivenor! How can you say that? He gives you everything you ask for.

speaker: Nivenor
dialogue: If I cared for your opinion on our affairs, I'd ask. Now, if you'll excuse me.

speaker: Nivenor
dialogue: What's this nonsense I've been hearing? How dare you call Bolli a deadbeat!

speaker: Nivenor
dialogue: What's that supposed to mean?

speaker: Grelka
dialogue: Oh come off it, Niv. We both know you married that fisherman for his gold. You don't need to put on an act for my benefit.

speaker: Nivenor
dialogue: I'm looking for a necklace. Do you have anything with garnets?

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: I have a single one left, quite expensive, but also quite elegant.

speaker: Nivenor
dialogue: Posh. I'm not paying for it. Put it on Bolli's account if you please.

speaker: Nivenor
dialogue: Hey. What's the matter with you? You have no right to spread rumors around town about me.

speaker: Nivenor
dialogue: You know very well what I'm talking about. You're saying that I only married Bolli for his gold and that I don't really love him.

speaker: Marise
dialogue: Well, if the shoe fits...

speaker: Njada Stonearm
dialogue: I'm still trying to figure out why Skjor let you in in the first place.

speaker: Njada
dialogue: I've heard some rumors... about you and Skjor.

speaker: Njada
dialogue: Is it not allowed?

speaker: Aela
dialogue: It's not exactly forbidden, but even so... it's not true. So that's that.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: How do you manage to hold your ground like that?

speaker: Njada
dialogue: You have to remember, it's not about strength. It's about leverage.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: But strength doesn't hurt.

speaker: Njada
dialogue: Well, no. I'm just saying there's more to defense than muscle.

speaker: Njada
dialogue: Just those same ruffians I was bringing in for the Shatter-Shields. So much wasted breath in that crew.

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: I'm imagining you just standing your ground and letting them tire themselves out.

speaker: Njada
dialogue: I'm telling you, it works. Let them ring their own ears on my shield, then scoop them up off the ground.

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: We all have different means to glory, Stonearm. Well done.

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: I've got a bad grip on my shield, could you take a look at it?

speaker: Njada
dialogue: I'm a warrior, not a blacksmith.

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: Can't you just tell me if the grip is bad?

speaker: Njada
dialogue: If Eorlund made it, it's more likely you're gripping it wrong. Find me tomorrow and we can go over it.

speaker: Noblewoman
dialogue: But aren't you the least bit nervous? After everything that's happened?

speaker: Emperor Titus Mede II
dialogue: You mean the wedding? My cousin's apparent murder? An unfortunate misunderstanding, no more. Cold mead, hot tempers... these things happen.

speaker: Nobleman
dialogue: Quite. Yet that recent business with the young officer. Maro, was it? How dreadful. The son of your commander, plotting your assassination.

speaker: Emperor Titus Mede II
dialogue: Aha! Here we are. Honored guests, I present to you - the Gourmet! Ah, the Potage le Magnifique. So delicious. My friends, as emperor, I of course reserve the right of first taste.

speaker: Emperor Titus Mede II
dialogue: Oh... Oh how marvelous. Just delicious. It is everything I had hoped it would be. Please, everyone. Enjoy.

speaker: Noblewoman
dialogue: But aren't you the least bit nervous? After everything that's happened?

speaker: Emperor Titus Mede II

speaker: Emperor Titus Mede II
dialogue: Oh... Oh how marvelous. Just delicious. It is everything I had hoped it would be. It.... I.... I think something's... wrong... I... Hunh...

speaker: Penitus Oculatus Agent
dialogue: By the gods! The Gourmet and the chef have poisoned the Emperor! Get them!

speaker: Gianna
dialogue: What? No! No, you don't understand! There's been some kind of mistake! I... Aggghhh!

dialogue: Quite. Yet that recent business with the young officer. Maro, was it? How dreadful. The son of your commander, plotting your assassination.

speaker: Emperor Titus Mede II
dialogue: Aha! Here we are. Honored guests, I present to you - the Gourmet! Ah, the Potage le Magnifique. So delicious. My friends, as emperor, I of course reserve the right of first taste.

speaker: Emperor Titus Mede II
dialogue: Oh... Oh how marvelous. Just delicious. It is everything I had hoped it would be. Please, everyone. Enjoy.

speaker: Noblewoman
dialogue: But aren't you the least bit nervous? After everything that's happened?

speaker: Emperor Titus Mede II
dialogue: You mean the wedding? My cousin's apparent murder? An unfortunate misunderstanding, no more. Cold mead, hot tempers... these things happen.

speaker: Nobleman
dialogue: Quite. Yet that recent business with the young officer. Maro, was it? How dreadful. The son of your commander, plotting your assassination.

speaker: Emperor Titus Mede II
dialogue: Aha! Here we are. Honored guests, I present to you - the Gourmet! Ah, the Potage le Magnifique. So delicious. My friends, as emperor, I of course reserve the right of first taste.

speaker: Emperor Titus Mede II
dialogue: Oh... Oh how marvelous. Just delicious. It is everything I had hoped it would be. It.... I.... I think something's... wrong... I... Hunh...

speaker: Penitus Oculatus Agent
dialogue: By the gods! The Gourmet and the chef have poisoned the Emperor! Get them!

speaker: Gianna
dialogue: What? No! No, you don't understand! There's been some kind of mistake! I... Aggghhh!

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: I call upon you Lady Nocturnal, Queen of Murk and Empress of Shadow... hear my voice!

speaker: Nocturnal
dialogue: Ah, Karliah. I was wondering when I'd hear from you again. Lose something did we?

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: My Lady, I've come before you to throw myself upon your mercy and to accept responsibility for my failure.

speaker: Nocturnal
dialogue: You're already mine, Karliah. Your terms were struck long ago. What could you possibly offer me now?

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: I have two others that wish to transact the Oath; to serve you both in life and in death.

speaker: Nocturnal
dialogue: You surprise me, Karliah. This offer is definitely weighted in my favor.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: My appetite for Mercer's demise exceeds my craving for wealth, Your Grace.

speaker: Nocturnal
dialogue: Revenge? How interesting... Very well, the conditions are acceptable. You may proceed.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: Lady Nocturnal, we accept your terms. We dedicate ourselves to you as both your avengers and your sentinels. We will honor our agreement in this life and the next until your conditions have been met.

speaker: Nocturnal
dialogue: Very well. I name your initiates Nightingale and I restore your status to the same, Karliah. And in the future, I'd suggest you refrain from disappointing me again.

speaker: Noster Eagle-Eye
dialogue: I was there. I fought in the Great War. I was on the field at Anvil. And when I was struck down, they left me.

speaker: Conjurer
dialogue: These thralls of yours are slower than Argonians in a blizzard.

speaker: Novice Necromancer
dialogue: Feel free to grab a pick and help them out. I prefer not to sully myself with manual labor.

speaker: Conjurer
dialogue: There goes another one.

speaker: Novice Necromancer
dialogue: Bah. Weak-willed rabble. Even dead they're almost useless.

speaker: Conjurer
dialogue: They seem less intelligent each time you raise them, if that's even possible.

speaker: Novice Necromancer
dialogue: As long as they can swing a pickaxe where I tell them, they're as smart as we need them to be.

speaker: Conjurer
dialogue: You hear that? The others must have found something!

speaker: Novice Necromancer
dialogue: We'd better go see. These can tend to themselves for a few minutes.

speaker: Nura Snow-Shod
dialogue: Talos bless you, my child.

speaker: Nurelion
dialogue: Alchemy is simple. Unless, of course, you are simple. Then I can't help you.

speaker: Nurelion
dialogue: Bah, if there was a tonic that could help me, I would have found it by now...

speaker: Nurelion
dialogue: Don't waste time apologizing, just find the book!

speaker: Quintus
dialogue: Yes, master. I'm sorry, I'll get back to those notes straight away.

speaker: Nurelion
dialogue: Out of my sight!

speaker: Octieve San
dialogue: I'm too old to work, but that don't make me too old to drink.

speaker: Evette
dialogue: Father, could you clean up the house a little while I'm away?

speaker: Octieve
dialogue: Maybe. I'll see if I feel like it.

speaker: Evette
dialogue: I'm on my feet all day. Can you please do this one thing for me?

speaker: Octieve
dialogue: Sure, whatever.

speaker: Octieve
dialogue: Where've you been all day?

speaker: Evette
dialogue: At the market, father.

speaker: Octieve
dialogue: Well, did you bring back any mead?

speaker: Evette
dialogue: I barely make enough for us to eat as it is, father. You can't just drink it all away.

speaker: Octieve
dialogue: Humph. Some daughter you are.

speaker: Whiterun Guard
dialogue: Hear that?

speaker: Whiterun Guard 2
dialogue: Shor's bones, here he comes!

speaker: Odahviing
dialogue: Dovahkiin! Here I am!

speaker: Jarl Balgruuf the Greater
dialogue: Steady! Steady, now! Keep under cover until it's down!

speaker: Jarl Balgruuf the Greater
dialogue: Get back! Get back! We need to trap it, not kill it!

speaker: Jarl Balgruuf the Greater
dialogue: That's it! Now, wait until he's inside!

speaker: Jarl Balgruuf the Greater
dialogue: Got him!

speaker: Whiterun Guard 3
dialogue: I think it's holding!

speaker: Farengar
dialogue: Incredible! Uh... sir, you have no idea how long I have waited for such an opportunity! I would be most appreciative if you would permit me to perform some, ah, tests on you. Purely in the interests of the advancement of knowledge.

speaker: Odahviing
dialogue: Begone, mage. Do not test my promise to the Dovahkiin.

speaker: Farengar
dialogue: I assure you, you will not even notice me. Most of them are hardly painful at all to a large dragon such as yourself.

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: Farengar, very bad idea. Even for you.

speaker: Farengar
dialogue: Surely you won't miss a few scales... or a small amount of blood...

speaker: Odahviing
dialogue: Joor mey! What are you doing back there? Yol... Toor...Shul!

speaker: Jarl Balgruuf the Greater
dialogue: Farengar! Enough, fool!

speaker: Whiterun Guard
dialogue: Get ready to open the trap! This seems like a really bad idea to me.

speaker: Jarl Balgruuf the Greater
dialogue: Carry on, soldier. This is all part of the Dragonborn's plan.

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: By all the gods...

speaker: Odahviing
dialogue: {{Hide|Faas nu, zini dein ruthi ahst vaal.|Fear not, my honor holds my rage at bay.}}

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: You're either the bravest person I've ever met or the biggest fool.

speaker: Jarl Balgruuf the Greater
dialogue: May Kynareth guard you while you pass through her realm!

speaker: Odar
dialogue: Jarls come and Jarls go, but a good cook stays for a lifetime. And I'm a very, very good cook.

speaker: Odfel
dialogue: You think living with Grogmar is easy? Did you see how he lives?

speaker: Filnjar
dialogue: You two will just have to learn how to get along until we can build you another house.

speaker: Odfel
dialogue: At this rate, that'll never happen.

speaker: Filnjar
dialogue: Quit your bellyaching. We've all got our problems.

speaker: Odfel
dialogue: All I'm asking is that you clean up once and a while. How you can find anything in your half of the house is beyond me.

speaker: Grogmar
dialogue: I'd rather spend more time in the mine hauling up iron than doing woman's work keeping the house clean.

speaker: Odfel
dialogue: I'll have you know that I can haul up just as much iron as you in a day and still manage to clean up my messes.

speaker: Grogmar
dialogue: You think so, huh? Maybe you'd like to put some Septims behind that boast.

speaker: Odfel
dialogue: You have yourself a bet.

speaker: Odfel
dialogue: {{sicblock|Grelka|Sylgja}}, do you fancy a walk tomorrow?

speaker: Sylgja
dialogue: Odfel, I've told you time and time again. I'm not interested in a relationship with you.

speaker: Odfel
dialogue: And why not? I'm handsome, strong and smart. What else could you possibly need?

speaker: Sylgja
dialogue: I need someone that cares about me more than they care about themselves. That person isn't you.

speaker: Oengul War-Anvil
dialogue: Everyone says Eorlund Gray-Mane is the best smith in Skyrim. I plan to change a few minds about that.

speaker: Oengul
dialogue: No, I want to take my time with it.

speaker: Hermir
dialogue: Can I help with it? Maybe just the cuirass?

speaker: Oengul
dialogue: This is more delicate work than you're used to.

speaker: Hermir
dialogue: I did that engraved piece just last month!

speaker: Oengul
dialogue: This is the royal armor, lass. Maybe in a few years.

speaker: Oengul
dialogue: Did you use my good hammer?

speaker: Oengul
dialogue: Blast, girl, I told you to leave my tools alone. You have yours, and I have mine.

speaker: Hermir
dialogue: I didn't touch it!

speaker: Oengul
dialogue: Hammers don't have legs.

speaker: Hermir
dialogue: Did you look behind the forge? I think I saw it there.

speaker: Oengul
dialogue: Oh... yes. Now that you mention it, I think... sorry about that.

speaker: Oengul
dialogue: Have you been learning your ores?

speaker: Hermir
dialogue: I think I've got a handle on it, but Orichalcum is confusing.

speaker: Oengul
dialogue: Don't even bother with that one. Leave it to the Orcs.

speaker: Hermir
dialogue: Oh, right. That makes sense. Kind of a messy metal, anyway.

speaker: Oglub
dialogue: I serve my chief and my brothers by working in the mines. It's the only place fit for an aging Orc.

speaker: Oglub
dialogue: You could challenge Burguk, my brother. Yours is the stronger swordarm.

speaker: Ghorbash
dialogue: Serving in the Legion taught me to respect leadership. The stronghold needs Burguk.

speaker: Ghorbash
dialogue: It is a fine day to work the mines.

speaker: Oglub
dialogue: This metal will serve the forge well, my brother.

speaker: Ogmund to Kleppr
dialogue: That's a sensible lad. Now fetch me drink.

speaker: Ogol
dialogue: By the Ashpit, we can't go on like this.

speaker: Olaf One-Eye
dialogue: Insolent bard. Die!

speaker: King Olaf One-Eye
dialogue: Insolent bard. Die!

speaker: Olava the Feeble
dialogue: Maybe some other time I'll reveal your destiny, hmm? Tea leaves, palm reading, crystal scrying... Oooh! Maybe trepanning? Ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Olda
dialogue: You're going to try and sell me something? Well, I ain't interested.

speaker: Olfina Gray-Mane
dialogue: There's nothing a man can do that I can't do better, whether it's serving drinks or slaying trolls.

speaker: Olfina
dialogue: Got any sausages? I'm cooking a special breakfast for a friend, and they're his favorite.

speaker: Olfina
dialogue: Best you forget whatever you think you saw, elf. Such idle talk can prove hazardous to one's health.

speaker: Olfina
dialogue: Did you raise your prices, Carlotta?

speaker: Carlotta
dialogue: I had to. The farmers are charging me double for the produce I sell.

speaker: Olfina
dialogue: Let me guess, they're saying it's because of this trouble with the Stormcloaks?

speaker: Carlotta
dialogue: Exactly. Road patrols were cut in half because the Jarl needed soldiers. Now the bandits are bolder than ever. They've been raiding the farms for food, and supplies are scarcer than ever. Maybe I should sell swords and armor, instead.

speaker: Olfina
dialogue: Maybe, but they wouldn't taste as good as a loaf of fresh-baked pumpernickel.

speaker: Jon
dialogue: So I'm, uh... writing a song for you...

speaker: Olfina
dialogue: Why, Jon Battle-Born, you're writing me a song? Does it somehow involve blood, or beheadings, or the honor of my forebears?

speaker: Jon
dialogue: Well, that's where I started. But it turned into something of a ballad.

speaker: Olfina
dialogue: A ballad? Oh, now I know you're joking with me.

speaker: Jon
dialogue: It's all true, I swear it. You can hear it when it's done. I'll just need a year or two to smooth the rough edges.

speaker: Olfina
dialogue: Ha! I thought as much.

speaker: Olfina
dialogue: So have you spoken to that man from the Bards College?

speaker: Jon
dialogue: No, not yet. But I will. I just haven't... gotten around to it yet.

speaker: Olfina
dialogue: Oh Jon, stop dallying. You know you have to go. It's why Mara put you on this earth. You think a few miles can truly keep us apart?

speaker: Jon
dialogue: You mean you won't forget about me the moment I'm out of sight? Get yourself a nice old rich husband, have sixteen babies?

speaker: Olfina
dialogue: Tsk. You've uncovered my master plan. Now I suppose you'll never leave.

speaker: Jon
dialogue: I want to see you when you're done working.

speaker: Jon
dialogue: That's your imagination running wild. Nobody knows how we feel about each other.

speaker: Jon
dialogue: Sing you a special song tonight, beautiful lass?

speaker: Olfina
dialogue: Not now, I'm working.

speaker: Jon
dialogue: Bah. You're always working. Why else would I spend so much time here?

speaker: Olfina
dialogue: Oh Jon, darling. You know you're the only stone-biting, knuckle-dragging Nord for me.

speaker: Jon
dialogue: Ha! That's my girl.

speaker: Olfina
dialogue: And why shouldn't I? Just because I'm a Gray-Mane doesn't mean I can't earn my own keep.

speaker: Ysolda
dialogue: I didn't mean... I'm sorry I asked.

speaker: Olfrid Battle-Born
dialogue: Battle-Born is a name out of legend, sung in the songs of old and heard in deeds of valor for a hundred generations.

speaker: Olfrid
dialogue: Foolish old woman! You know nothing! Nothing of our struggles, our suffering!

speaker: Fralia
dialogue: I will never accept his death! My son still lives. I feel it in my heart. So tell me, Battle-Borns, where is he? Where are you holding my Thorald?

speaker: Idolaf
dialogue: Come on, father. There's nothing more to be said here.

speaker: Olur
dialogue: I work in the forge and the mines. Mother says it pleases her and our people.

speaker: Olur
dialogue: It's simple Orc smithing practice, my chief. Nothing that hasn't been passed down for years.

speaker: Larak
dialogue: I served in the Legion. Perhaps I'll show you some of their technique one of these days.

speaker: Omluag
dialogue: Can't talk. Mulush will beat me if I stop working.

speaker: Omluag
dialogue: Another foul day at the smelter.

speaker: Omluag
dialogue: Sometimes I think we deserve these miserable lives of ours.

speaker: Hathrasil
dialogue: Surprised to see you working. Mulush almost broke your arm yesterday.

speaker: Omluag
dialogue: Does it look like I can afford losing a day's wage? That damn Orc isn't getting the best of me.

speaker: Omluag
dialogue: Divines, I'm tired. This is too much work.

speaker: Hathrasil
dialogue: Just keep at it, or Mulush will beat you.

speaker: Hathrasil
dialogue: Careful of the molten metal. That gets on you, kiss your fingers goodbye.

speaker: Omluag
dialogue: I know what I'm doing. Stop telling me.

speaker: Omluag
dialogue: First war, and now dragons. Everywhere they go, the Nords bring nothing but ruin.

speaker: Hathrasil
dialogue: Ain't nothing for it. They're still in charge.

speaker: Omluag
dialogue: Mulush, we need a break. The heat from the smelter is too much.

speaker: Mulush
dialogue: Are you complaining? Work. If you have strength to whine, you have strength to smelt.

speaker: Mulush
dialogue: Careful. You spill one drop of silver, I'm taking it out of your hide.

speaker: Omluag
dialogue: I'm being as careful as I can.

speaker: Mulush
dialogue: Did you just talk back to me? I'm not paid to listen. I'm paid to keep you working. Now work.

speaker: Ondolemar
dialogue: The Empire exists because we allow it to exist, and I'm here to make sure the Jarl of Markarth remembers that.

speaker: Ondolemar
dialogue: How dare you speak of the Thalmor in such a disgusting manner!

speaker: Razelan
dialogue: What? I didn't... hmm? No, listen, you must have misunderstood... I would never openly insult your... that is to say...

speaker: Ondolemar
dialogue: Your insults and provocations have gone far enough! I'd kill you where you stand if I wasn't bound by my oath as an officer of the Aldmeri Dominion.

speaker: Elenwen
dialogue: Razelan. What is it this time?

speaker: Razelan
dialogue: Madame Ambassador, you know that I would never have behaved... that is to say... well I swear I'm innocent this time!

speaker: Ondolemar
dialogue: Forgive me, Ambassador. I allowed this... fool to provoke me. The fault is mine. There is no need for further disruption on my account.

speaker: Razelan
dialogue: That is absolutely untrue! Uh, that is, yes, of course. What... I don't understand why everyone... never mind.

speaker: Galmar Stone-Fist
dialogue: Not so fast Elf!

speaker: Ondolemar
dialogue: I presume you're talking to me?

speaker: Galmar Stone-Fist
dialogue: On your knees!

speaker: Galmar Stone-Fist
dialogue: I said, on your knees, Elf!

speaker: Ondolemar
dialogue: Enjoy this while you can. Soon you will all be slaves.

speaker: Galmar Stone-Fist
dialogue: Someone get that thing out of here and burn it.

speaker: Onmund
dialogue: My family was convinced that coming here was a death sentence, or worse. It took years of insisting that this is what I'm meant to do.

speaker: Tolfdir
dialogue: Welcome, welcome! We were just beginning. Please, stay and listen. So, as I was saying, the first thing to understand is that magic is, by its very nature, volatile and dangerous. Unless you can control it, it can and will destroy you.

speaker: Brelyna
dialogue: Sir, I think we all understand that fairly well. We wouldn't be here if we couldn't control magic!

speaker: Tolfdir
dialogue: Of course, my dear. Of course. You all certainly possess some inherent natural ability. That much is not being questioned. What I'm talking about is true control, mastery of magic. It takes years, if not decades, of practice and study.

speaker: Tolfdir
dialogue: Please, please! This is exactly what I'm talking about. Eagerness must be tempered with caution, or else disaster is inevitable.

speaker: Onmund
