dialogue: But we've only just arrived here -- you've no idea what any of us are capable of. Why not give use a chance to show you what we can do?

speaker: Onmund
dialogue: We're all pretty new to this, right? Let's just give it a chance. What's the worst that could happen?

speaker: Tolfdir
dialogue: All right, let's settle down. I suppose we can try something practical... In continueing with out theme of safety, we'll start with Wards. Wards are protective spells that block magic. I'll teach you all a ward, and we'll see if you can succesfully use it to block spells, all right?

speaker: Brelyna
dialogue: See? He agrees with us too! Why don't you actually show us something?

speaker: Tolfdir
dialogue: All right, let's settle down. I suppose we can try something practical... In continueing with out theme of safety, we'll start with Wards. Wards are protective spells that block magic. I'll teach you all a ward, and we'll see if you can succesfully use it to block spells, all right?

speaker: Tolfdir
dialogue: All right, let's settle down. I suppose we can try something practical... In continueing with out theme of safety, we'll start with Wards. Wards are protective spells that block magic. I'll teach you all a ward, and we'll see if you can succesfully use it to block spells, all right?

speaker: Peryite
dialogue: One of my monks, the elf Orchendor, was sent to gather these Afflicted. He shepherded them into Bthardamz for me, but has since lost his way.

speaker: Orgnar
dialogue: We got rooms and food. Drink, too. I cook. Ain't much else to tell.

speaker: Delphine
dialogue: Orgnar. [long pause] Orgnar! Are you listening?

speaker: Orgnar
dialogue: Hard not to.

speaker: Delphine
dialogue: The ale's going bad. [pause] Did you hear me?

speaker: Orgnar
dialogue: Yep. Ale's going bad.

speaker: Delphine
dialogue: I guess you don't have potatoes stuck in your ears after all. Just make sure we get a new batch soon.

speaker: Delpine
dialogue: Orgnar. I'm travelling. You've got the inn 'til I get back.

speaker: Orgnar
dialogue: Right. Happy trails.

speaker: Delphine
dialogue: Orgnar, hold down the bar for a minute, will you?

speaker: Orgnar
dialogue: Yeah, sure.

speaker: Delphine
dialogue: Orgnar, this is it. The Inn is yours. I'm probably never coming back here.

speaker: Orgnar
dialogue: Well, now. That's something to think about.

speaker: Delphine
dialogue: Take care of yourself, Orgnar. Goodbye.

speaker: Orgnar
dialogue: Yeah...sure. You too, Delphine. You be safe.

speaker: Orgnar
dialogue: Coming right up.

speaker: Orla
dialogue: What can I do for you?

speaker: Orthorn
dialogue: I uhh... wait, what?

speaker: The Caller
dialogue: He gets the books, I get you. It's very simple.

speaker: Orthorn
dialogue: But why?

speaker: The Caller
dialogue: This little adventure of yours has cost me a number of test subjects. I need more, and you'll do nicely.

speaker: Orthorn
dialogue: You wouldn't do that, would you? You wouldn't leave me here with her!

speaker: The Caller
dialogue: I'm waiting.

speaker: Orthus Endario
dialogue: 'Windhelm's an easy posting!' they said. Guess they didn't count on Ulfric's little uprising.

speaker: Orthus
dialogue: Adelaisa, I'm sorry.

speaker: Adelaisa
dialogue: Sorry isn't good enough, Orthus. There's a lot of gold at stake here, and sniveling isn't going to get it back.

speaker: Orthus
dialogue: I've got a top man on the job right now. He should be returning any moment.

speaker: Adelaisa
dialogue: {{Hide|This|Referring to the Dragonborn}} must be him, then.

speaker: Orthus
dialogue: Vittoria! There's someone I'd like you to meet.

speaker: Vittoria
dialogue: It's very nice to meet you. You'll have to excuse Orthus here. He so rarely gets back to civilization. Stuck in Windhelm, poor fellow. Don't worry, Orthus. I'm doing my best to get you reassigned to Solitude.

speaker: Orthus
dialogue: Oh, don't worry about me. I relish the challenge.

speaker: Paarthurnax
dialogue: But willing or no, they will hear it! Fare thee well, Dovahkiin!

speaker: Pantea Ateia
dialogue: Now you can say you've met the most talented bard in all of Skyrim.

speaker: Pantea
dialogue: You there, have you performed your voice exercises today?

speaker: Aia
dialogue: Always! Perfection takes dedication, after all!

speaker: Pantea
dialogue: Yes, well, see that you keep at it. That is all.

speaker: Pantea
dialogue: Your performance has been excellent lately Aia. You still need training but one day you will make an adequate singer.

speaker: Aia
dialogue: Yes, Dean. Thank you.

speaker: Pantea
dialogue: You there, have you performed your voice exercises today?

speaker: Pantea
dialogue: Yes, well, see that you keep at it. That is all.

speaker: Pantea
dialogue: You there, have you performed your voice exercises today?

speaker: Pantea
dialogue: Yes, well, see that you keep at it. That is all.

speaker: Pantea
dialogue: Passably. Aia is my star pupil; none of the others can hold a candle to her, especially not that wretched Illdi.

speaker: Viarmo
dialogue: Try not to play favorites, Lady Ateia. It does a disservice to the whole class.

speaker: Pantea
dialogue: Yes, Headmaster.

speaker: Pavo Attius
dialogue: The Forsworn have taken Kolskeggr Mine. We're the only ones left.

speaker: Pavo
dialogue: Are you all right, Gat?

speaker: Gat
dialogue: Still shaken from all the fighting, my friend. It's been too long since I had to kill someone.

speaker: Pavo
dialogue: Thank the Divines we survived that.

speaker: Gat
dialogue: Those Forsworn were fierce fighters. Fiercer than I could have imagined.

speaker: Gat
dialogue: I feel like we're mining even more ore than before.

speaker: Pavo
dialogue: It's the rush of good fortune, my friend. It makes you work harder.

speaker: Pavo
dialogue: Are you worried the Forsworn might return?

speaker: Gat
dialogue: I doubt the Forsworn would risk holding this mine a second time. They lost many of their warriors.

speaker: Pavo
dialogue: Do you remember the Legion? Fighting the Thalmor in the Great War?

speaker: Gat
dialogue: There were many good battles, friend. I miss those days.

speaker: Pavo
dialogue: You miss them? I don't know how many times I feared for my life.

speaker: Gat
dialogue: You didn't die. A battle you live through is a great honor.

speaker: Pavo
dialogue: Did you ever want to return to your stronghold? Go back to your family?

speaker: Gat
dialogue: I would need to challenge the chief, and take his head, to return home. I'd rather stay here.

speaker: Pavo
dialogue: Don't tell me you, of all people, are afraid of a battle.

speaker: Gat
dialogue: If you had to kill your own brother to be allowed back home, you'd think twice as well.

speaker: Pavo
dialogue: The Forsworn have taken Kolskeggr Mine. We're the only ones left.

speaker: Skaggi
dialogue: Gods....You head inside and get some rest. I'll send word to the Jarl.

speaker: Sheogorath
dialogue: More tea, Pelly my dear?

speaker: Pelagius
dialogue: Oh, I couldn't. It goes right through me. So many detractors and undesirables, naysayers, buffoons. My...My headsman hasn't slept in three days.

speaker: Pelagius
dialogue: Yes, yes, as you've said countless times before.

speaker: Sheogorath
dialogue: Harumph! Well, if you're going to be like that, I think its best I take my leave. I said a good day to you, sir, I said good day!

speaker: Pelagius
dialogue: Yes. Leave me to my ceaseless responsibilities and burdens.

context: In front of Castle Dour during "To Kill an Empire"
speaker: Agent 2
dialogue: I'm all for diplomacy, but the sooner the Emperor deals with this Civil War mess, the sooner we can get back to Cyrodiil.

context: In front of Castle Dour during "To Kill an Empire"
speaker: Agent 1
dialogue: Lazy and useless, the lot of them, they can't even keep the Stormcloaks in line, no way I trust them with the Emperor's life.

context: In front of Castle Dour during "To Kill an Empire"
speaker: Agent 1
dialogue: All these damn Stormcloaks, they're making me nervous. Never in a million years did I imagine they'd gain control over Solitude.

context: In front of Castle Dour during "To Kill an Empire"
speaker: Agent 2
dialogue: You worry too much, the Emperor's never been safer. You think assassination attempts are planned overnight? We discovered the plot, end of threat.

context: In front of Castle Dour during "To Kill an Empire"
speaker: Agent 1
dialogue: I suppose. But what about the old man? Son killed, family name ruined, and he acts as if nothing even happened. Think he's even fit for duty?

context: In front of Castle Dour during "To Kill an Empire"
speaker: Agent 2
dialogue: I'm going to pretend I didn't hear that. Commander Maro is the best the Penitus Oculatus has ever produced, you should be half the man he is.

context: In front of Castle Dour during "To Kill an Empire"
speaker: Agent 1
dialogue: You misunderstand, it's just, I feel for him is all. To carry a weight like that, it's got to take its toll. That happened to me, I'd be a wreck.

speaker: Penitus Oculatus Agent
dialogue: And the outpost at Dragon Bridge?

speaker: Commander Maro
dialogue: It'll be shuttered by the end of the month.

speaker: Penitus Oculatus Agent
dialogue: Very good. And you'll be returning to... Well, if you don't mind me asking, where exactly will you be going now, sir?

speaker: Commander Maro
dialogue: Hmph. Now there's an excellent question. An excellent question, indeed. Truth is, as soon as the Emperor sets sail, I'm resigning my position.

speaker: Penitus Oculatus Agent
dialogue: Oh... I see. Well then, let me be just say that it's been an honor serving under you Commander Maro.

speaker: Commander Maro
dialogue: The honor has been mine. You should be proud of what we've accomplished here. The Dark Brotherhood is no more. And the Emperor, finally, is safe.

speaker: Penitus Oculatus Agent
dialogue: Yes sir.

speaker: Agent 1
dialogue: Which one was the rat?

speaker: Agent 2
dialogue: Don't know, one of these corpses, does it matter?

speaker: Agent 1
dialogue: Suppose not. What's taking the others so long? The sooner we get out of here *clears throat* the better. Smoke's getting bad, this place will be raging soon.

speaker: Agent 2
dialogue: *coughs three times* Arcturus took some men deeper in *inhales* wanted to be sure. *inhales* Maybe we should *coughs* assist them.

speaker: Agent 1
dialogue: *coughs twice* You assist all you like *inhales* and get roasted for your trouble. I'll guard the exit *coughs*.

speaker: Agent 1
dialogue: It's all over now. Lieutenant said you could see the smoke from Whiterun.

speaker: Agent 2
dialogue: Yeah. I'm glad we can finally stand down- getting tired of looking over my shoulder all the time.

speaker: Agent 1
dialogue: Nothing to do now but sit back, relax, and enjoy the trip home.

speaker: Perth
dialogue: Whoa, there. I don't know where you're going, but stay out of that mine. It isn't safe.

speaker: Perth
dialogue: Steel your nerves. The draugr are gone. Focus on your mining.

speaker: Perth
dialogue: Feels good to be mining again.

speaker: Tuthul
dialogue: How can you say that? This mine was filled with draugr not too long ago.

speaker: Tuthul
dialogue: Those draugr are going to come up and kill us all.

speaker: Perth
dialogue: They haven't moved out of the caves. I think we're safe.

speaker: Tuthul
dialogue: 'We're safe' he says. You'll eat those words when a draugr is tearing into your face.

speaker: Tuthul
dialogue: I don't think it's safe mining a cave on top of that crypt.

speaker: Perth
dialogue: There's a war on. We need every scrap of ore we can get, so we're going to keep digging. Understand?

speaker: Tuthul
dialogue: Fine, but don't say I didn't warn you.

speaker: Tuthul
dialogue: Those draugr are going to be back. I can feel it.

speaker: Perth
dialogue: Don't be such a coward. We haven't seen any draugr since the mine was cleared. Be grateful.

speaker: Plautis Carvain
dialogue: Don't bother me, peasant. I've had a long journey and paid too much coin on these gifts to be late to Vittoria's wedding.

speaker: Salonia
dialogue: Why are we even going to a wedding at this far flung end of the Empire anyway?

speaker: Plautis
dialogue: I told you, it's the wedding of Vittoria Vici, an extremely well connected merchant with the East Empire Company. The Emperor's cousin? Remember? Hopefully these gifts will put us in her good graces, secure that import deal, and lead the way to an audience with the Emperor.

speaker: Salonia
dialogue: I hate it here. Those were my favorite shoes, ruined and for what? We never even made it to the wedding.

speaker: Plautis
dialogue: Wha... Your shoes? We get robbed by bandits, my clothes torn to shreds by some giant cat, our bodyguard eaten by a dragon... And you're worried about your shoes?

speaker: Salonia
dialogue: When we get back to Cyrodiil, I swear I will hire an army of battlemages to come up here and set fire to the whole damned province.

speaker: Ritual Master
dialogue: Wolf Queen. Hear our call and awaken. We summon Potema!

speaker: Ritual Master
dialogue: We summon Potema!

speaker: Necromancer
dialogue: We summon Potema!

speaker: Necromancer 2
dialogue: We summon Potema!

speaker: Ritual Master
dialogue: Long have you slept the dreamless sleep of death, Potema. No longer. Hear us Wolf Queen! We Summon You!

speaker: Ritual Master
dialogue: Summoned with words. Bounds by blood.

speaker: Necromancer
dialogue: We summon Potema!

speaker: Necromancer 2
dialogue: We summon Potema!

speaker: Potema
dialogue: Yes! Yes! Return me to this realm!

speaker: Ritual Master
dialogue: As our voices summon you the blood of the innocent binds you Wolf Queen!

speaker: Ritual Master
dialogue: Summoned with words. Bounds by blood.

speaker: Necromancer
dialogue: Summoned with words. Bounds by blood.

speaker: Necromancer 2
dialogue: Summoned with words. Bounds by blood.

speaker: Potema
dialogue: What! What are you doing?! You fools! You cannot bind me to your wills!

speaker: Ritual Master
dialogue: Summoned with words. Bounds by blood.

speaker: Necromancer
dialogue: Summoned with words. Bounds by blood.

speaker: Necromancer 2
dialogue: Summoned with words. Bounds by blood.

speaker: Potema
dialogue: You ants don't have the power to bind me!

speaker: Priestess of Arkay
dialogue: As we commend your souls to Aetherius, blessings of the Eight Divines upon you, for you are the salt and earth of Nirn, our beloved....

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: What was that?

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: It's nothing. Carry on.

speaker: Captain
dialogue: Yes, General Tullius. Give them their last rites.

speaker: Priestess of Arkay
dialogue: As we commend your souls to Aetherius, blessings of the Eight Divines upon you, for you are the salt and earth of Nirn, our beloved...

speaker: Stormcloak Soldier
dialogue: For the love of Talos, shut up and let's get this over with.

speaker: Priestess of Arkay
dialogue: As you wish.

speaker: Stormcloak
dialogue: You Imperial bastards!

speaker: Ingrid
dialogue: Death to the Stormcloaks!

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: As fearless in death as he was in life.

speaker: Captain
dialogue: Next, the [player race] in the rags!

speaker: Proventus Avenicci
dialogue: Torygg? He simply walked up to the boy and murdered him!

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: My lord. Please. You have to listen. I only counsel caution. We cannot afford to act rashly in times like these. If the news from Helgen is true... well, there's no telling what it means.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: What would you have me do, then? Nothing?

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: My lord. Please. This is no time for rash action. I just think we need more information before we act. I just...

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Who's {{Hide|this|referring to the Dragonborn}}, then?

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: What do you say now, Proventus? Shall we continue to trust in the strength of our walls? Against a dragon?

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: My lord, we should send troops to Riverwood at once. It's in the most immediate danger, if that dragon is lurking in the mountains...

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: The Jarl of Falkreath will view that as a provocation! He'll assume we're preparing to join Ulfric's side and attack him.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Enough! Irileth, send a detachment to Riverwood at once.

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: Yes, my Jarl.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: We should not...

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: I'll not stand idly by while a dragon burns my hold and slaughters my people!

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: If you'll excuse me, I'll return to my duties.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: That would be best.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: Good. You're finally here. The Jarl's been waiting for you.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: You heard the summons. What else could it mean? The Greybeards...

speaker: Hrongar
dialogue: We were just talking about you. My brother needs a word with you.

speaker: Hrongar
dialogue: That was the voice of the Greybeards, summoning you to High Hrothgar! This hasn't happened in ... centuries, at least. Not since Tiber Septim himself was summoned when he was still Talos of Atmora!

speaker: Hrongar
dialogue: Nord nonsense?! Why you puffed-up ignorant... these are our sacred traditions that go back to the founding of the First Empire!

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Hrongar. Don't be so hard on Avenicci.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Back to business, Proventus. We still have a city to defend.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: Yes, my lord.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Proventus, what do you make of all this? If Ulfric were to attack Whiterun...

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: As in all things, lord, caution... I urge us to wait and see.

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: Prey waits.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: I'm of a mind with Irileth. It's time to act.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: You plan to march on Windhelm?

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: I'm not a fool, Proventus. I mean it's time to challenge Ulfric to face me as a man, or march his Stormcloaks up to the gates.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: He'll do no such thing! A dagger in the back is all you could expect!

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: He was rather straightforward with Torygg.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: Torygg? He simply walked up to the boy and murdered him!

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: True. He's already proven his personal strength. Now he seeks to prove his army's.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: Then might I urge you to consider General Tullius' request? I mean, if you are bent on offending Jarl Ulfric...

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: Ulfric is the one who has offended. But, Proventus has a point. Ulfric has made it clear; in his mind, to refuse his claim is to side with the Empire.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: And what harm is there in letting a few Legionnaires die in place of your own men?

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: It seems cowardly.

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: Was it cowardly then to accept the White-Gold Concordat?

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: This again? That was different. Was I given a chance to object to the terms of the treaty? No. The Jarls weren't asked. We were told. And we had to like it.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: The chests of gold didn't hurt.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Damnit! This isn't about gold!

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: It's time to decide.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: Lord, wait. Let us see if Ulfric is serious.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Oh, he's serious. But so am I.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Proventus. Bring me my pen. And the good parchment.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: Are we writing a letter, Lord?

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Yes, to General Tullius. I need to make a few things clear before I accept these Legionnaires of his.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: My lord, our provisions are running dangerously low. Our stores of meat, wine, and grain are all but depleted.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Purchase more supplies, then. That's your job as Steward, isn't it? Why do you trouble me with these details?

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: My lord, since Ulfric Stormcloak's uprising, the cost of goods has doubled. I'll need more coin if I'm to provision us properly.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Our coffers are nearly empty. I can scarcely afford to pay the guards, and we need every one of them in these troubled times. You'll have to make do with what we have, Proventus.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: Yes, my lord.

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: I am concerned about the Jarl's safety. Too many of our guards have been redeployed to fight the Stormcloaks.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: What would you have me do? If we do not send men to fight in the war, you'll find yourself guarding one of Ulfric's men.

speaker: Irileth
dialogue: And if an assassin slips past the night watch, we won't have a Jarl at all. Without Balgruuf's leadership, Whiterun will descend into chaos.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: Nonsense. If Balgruuf falls, someone will take his place, for better or worse. In the meantime, we have a war to win. And win we must.

speaker: Hrongar
dialogue: Proventus, you must help me. We need to convince my brother to do more for the war effort.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: What would you have me do, Hrongar? Your brother is the Jarl. You know I can't question his judgement.

speaker: Hrongar
dialogue: I'm not asking you to defy the Jarl, just to open his eyes. Use subtlety and suggestion to turn his thoughts to the war. You're his steward, he'll listen to you.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: Leave me out of your intrigues, Hrongar. If you have something to say to the Jarl, say it with your own tongue.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: My lord Jarl, if we do not take steps soon, our coffers will be empty.

speaker: Hrongar
dialogue: Raise the taxes, then! Put anyone that refuses to pay in the stocks and make an example of them.

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: As you command, my lord. But, the issue could be solved another way. If we spend less on new arms and armor for the guards, for example...

speaker: Hrongar
dialogue: We're at war, old fool, or have you forgotten? Whiterun is the crown jewel of Skyrim, and you would leave us defenseless?

speaker: Proventus
dialogue: Forgive me, my lord. It was foolish of me to make such a suggestion.

speaker: Savos
dialogue: I'm sorry, were you about to say something?

speaker: Ancano
dialogue: Well, what is the meaning of this?

speaker: Quaranir
dialogue: I'm sorry, I'm afraid I don't understand.

speaker: Ancano
dialogue: Don't play coy. You asked to see a specific member of the College. Here he/she is. Now what is it that you want?

speaker: Quaranir
dialogue: There's been a misunderstanding. Clearly I should not be here. I shall simply take my leave.

speaker: Ancano
dialogue: [angry] What? What trickery is this? You're not going anywhere until I find out what you're up to.

speaker: Quaranir
dialogue: I'm not 'up to' anything. I apologize if I have offended you in any way.

speaker: Ancano
dialogue: [seething] We shall see about this...

speaker: Nurelion
dialogue: I'll be fine.

speaker: Quintus
dialogue: Master, you're far too old for this sort of journey. We don't know what's inside...

speaker: Nurelion
dialogue: I'll...<cough> I can...<cough> just...<cough>

speaker: Quintus
dialogue: You see, you're not well! Have a seat and I'll fetch you some tonic.

speaker: Nurelion
dialogue: Bah, if there was a tonic that could help me, I would have found it by now...

speaker: Nurelion
dialogue: Quintus, could you fetch me a copy of The Firmament? I need to compare the old star charts to today's.

speaker: Quintus
dialogue: Did they really record the star positions from Curalmil's tomb? There's no way it's that precise.

speaker: Nurelion
dialogue: Confound it, boy, I know what I'm doing. It will help me determine the season of his burial, which I can cross-reference.

speaker: Quintus
dialogue: I... I apologize, master.

speaker: Nurelion
dialogue: Don't waste time apologizing, just find the book!

speaker: Quintus
dialogue: Master, I have a question about infusions of arrowroot.

speaker: Nurelion
dialogue: Damn it, child, didn't I tell you to gather my notes on sub-material properties?

speaker: Quintus
dialogue: Yes, and I'm working on it, but I'm also trying to...

speaker: Nurelion
dialogue: When I ask you for something, I expect it to get done.

speaker: Quintus
dialogue: Yes, master, I know. I just want to keep up my own projects as well.

speaker: Nurelion
dialogue: You can waste your own time, not mine. An apprentice obeys his master. A good one does, at least.

speaker: Quintus
dialogue: Yes, master. I'm sorry, I'll get back to those notes straight away.

speaker: Nurelion
dialogue: I'm sorry to always be so hard on you, boy. I just worry I don't have much time left.

speaker: Quintus
dialogue: I know, master. Don't say such things―there is always time.

speaker: Nurelion
dialogue: Don't be so sure. Now, have you finished grinding the dried snowberries?

speaker: Quintus
dialogue: Erm... no. Not yet. I'm sorry, I was reading up on the effects of distillation.

speaker: Nurelion
dialogue: What? You've been lollygagging in idle reading?

speaker: Quintus
dialogue: No... I was trying to...

speaker: Nurelion
dialogue: Out of my sight!

speaker: Raerek
dialogue: I advise Igmund the same way I advised his father. Caution, caution, caution.

speaker: Igmund
dialogue: More settlements have sent riders to say dragons are being spotted throughout Skyrim. The Forsworn ambush our roads and dragons cloud the skies. Is there any good news?

speaker: Raerek
dialogue: Umm.... No, my Jarl. I'm afraid there isn't.

speaker: Raerek
dialogue: It's not that simple, Igmund. There are reports of Forsworn here in the city.

speaker: Igmund
dialogue: It doesn't matter if they're here in the city. We fight them where they live, we won't have to fight them here.

speaker: Raerek
dialogue: They live here, too, my Jarl. That's what I'm telling you.

speaker: Igmund
dialogue: Raerek, how is The Reach faring against this Forsworn menace?

speaker: Raerek
dialogue: Things are bad, Igmund. Our forces are barely able to keep the Forsworn in check. Merchants are reporting the loss of more of their shipments.

speaker: Igmund
dialogue: This is why I say we take the fight to them. Gather the Legion and drive those blasted beasts out of the Reach for good.

speaker: Faleen
dialogue: And what do Legion soldiers know about the hills the Reach? And the caves that make up those hills? The Forsworn can hide and ambush every assault.

speaker: Raerek
dialogue: The safety of the city and our settlements must be our only concern, Igmund. The rest of the Reach is on its own.

speaker: Igmund
dialogue: Cowards, the both of you. My father would not sit idly back and wait while evil men take over his lands. We're done discussing this for now.

speaker: Ragnar
dialogue: Not many Nords would work for a Reachman, but Ainethach is a good man.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Hey, you. You're finally awake. You were trying to cross the border, right? Walked right into that Imperial ambush, same as us, and that thief over there.

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: Damn you Stormcloaks. Skyrim was fine until you came along. Empire was nice and lazy. If they hadn't been looking for you, I could've stolen that horse and been halfway to Hammerfell. You there... You and me, we shouldn't be here. It's these Stormcloaks the Empire wants.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: We're all brothers and sisters in binds now, thief.

speaker: Imperial Soldier
dialogue: Shut up back there!

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: And what's wrong with him, huh?

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Watch your tongue. You're speaking to Ulfric Stormcloak, the true High King.

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: Ulfric? The Jarl of Windhelm? You're the leader of the rebellion. But if they've captured you... Oh gods, where are they taking us?

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: I don't know where we're going, but Sovngarde awaits.

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: No, this can't be happening. This isn't happening.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Hey, what village are you from, horse thief?

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: Why do you care?

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: A Nord's last thoughts should be of home.

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: Rorikstead. I'm... I'm from Rorikstead.

speaker: Imperial
dialogue: General Tullius, sir! The headsman is waiting!

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Good. Let's get this over with.

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: Shor, Mara, Dibella, Kynareth, Akatosh. Divines, please help me.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Look at him, General Tullius, the Military Governor. And it looks like the Thalmor are with him. Damn elves. I bet they had something to do with this. This is Helgen. I used to be sweet on a girl from here. Wonder if Vilod is still making that mead with juniper berries mixed in. Funny, when I was a boy, Imperial walls and towers used to make me feel so safe.

speaker: Haming
dialogue: Who are they, daddy? Where are they going?

speaker: Torolf
dialogue: You need to go inside, little cub.

speaker: Haming
dialogue: Why? I want to watch the soldiers.

speaker: Torolf
dialogue: Inside the house. Now.

speaker: Haming
dialogue: Yes, papa.

speaker: Captain
dialogue: Get these prisoners out of the carts. Move it!

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: Why are we stopping?

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Why do you think? End of the line. Let's go. Shouldn't keep the gods waiting for us.

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: No! Wait! We're not rebels!

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Face your death with some courage, thief.

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: You've got to tell them! We weren't with you! This is a mistake!

speaker: Imperial Captain
dialogue: Step towards the block when we call your name. One at a time.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Empire loves their damn lists.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Ulfric Stormcloak. Jarl of Windhelm.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: It has been an honor, Jarl Ulfric!

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Ralof of Riverwood. Lokir of Rorikstead.

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: You're not going to kill me!

speaker: Captain
dialogue: Anyone else feel like running?

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: By your orders, Captain. I'm sorry. Follow the Captain, prisoner.

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Ulfric Stormcloak. Some here in Helgen call you a hero. But a hero doesn't use a power like The Voice to murder his king and usurp his throne.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: [muffled grunts]

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: You started this war, plunged Skyrim into chaos, and now the Empire is going to put you down, and restore the peace.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: What was that?

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: It's nothing. Carry on.

speaker: Captain
dialogue: Yes, General Tullius. Give them their last rites.

speaker: Priestess of Arkay
dialogue: As we commend your souls to Aetherius, blessings of the Eight Divines upon you, for you are the salt and earth of Nirn, our beloved...

speaker: Stormcloak Soldier
dialogue: For the love of Talos, shut up and let's get this over with.

speaker: Priestess of Arkay
dialogue: As you wish.

speaker: Stormcloak
dialogue: You Imperial bastards!

speaker: Ingrid
dialogue: Death to the Stormcloaks!

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: As fearless in death as he was in life.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: There it is again. Did you hear that?

speaker: Captain
dialogue: I said, next prisoner!

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: To the block, prisoner. Nice and easy.

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: What in Oblivion is that?

speaker: Captain
dialogue: Sentries! What do you see?

speaker: Imperial
dialogue: It's in the clouds!

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Don't just stand there! Kill that thing! Guards, get the townspeople to safety!

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Jarl Ulfric! What is that thing? Could the legends be true?

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Legends don't burn down villages. We need to move. Now!

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Up through the tower, let's go!

speaker: Stormcloak
dialogue: They're hurt, but they'll live. Another second out there with the dragon, and they'd both be dead...

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Let's go! With me, up the tower!

speaker: Stormcloak
dialogue: We just need to move some of these rocks to clear the way!

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: See the inn on the other side? Jump through the roof and keep going! Go! We'll follow when we can!

speaker: Alduin
dialogue: Yol... Toor... Shul!

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Still alive, prisoner? Keep close to me if you want to stay that way. Gunnar, take care of the boy. I have to find General Tullius and join their defense.

speaker: Gunnar
dialogue: Gods guide you, Hadvar.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Stay close to the wall!

speaker: Alduin
dialogue: Yol... Toor... Shul

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Quickly, follow me!

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Hadvar! Into the keep, soldier, we're leaving!

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: It's you and me, prisoner. Stay close! Ralof! You damned traitor. Out of my way!

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: We're escaping, Hadvar. You're not stopping us this time.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Fine. I hope that dragon takes you all to Sovngarde.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: You! Come on, into the keep!

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: It's the Imperials! Take cover!

speaker: Imperial Captain
dialogue: Get this gate open. {{Hide|It's the escaped prisoners!

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: Mara's Mercy, its good to see you! But is it safe for you to be here?

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: We had heard that Ulfric had been captured...

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Gerdur... I'm fine. At least now I am.

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: Are you hurt? What's happened? [looks at player] And who's this? One of your comrades?

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Not a comrade yet...but a friend. I owe him/her my life, in fact. Is there somewhere we can talk? There's no telling when the news from Helgen will reach the Imperials...

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: Helgen? Has something happened...? You're right. Follow me. Hod! Come here a minute. I need your help with something.

speaker: Hod
dialogue: What is it, woman? Sven drunk on the job again?

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: Hod. Just come here.

speaker: Hod
dialogue: Ralof! What are you doing here? Ah...I'll be right down!

speaker: Frodnar
dialogue: Uncle Ralof! Can I see your axe? How many Imperials have you killed? Do you really know Ulfric Stormcloak?

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: Hush, Frodnar. This is no time for your games. Go and watch the south road. Find us if you see any Imperial soldiers coming.

speaker: Frodnar
dialogue: Aw, mama, I want to stay and talk with uncle Ralof!

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Look at you, almost a grown man! Won't be long before you'll be joining the fight yourself!

speaker: Frodnar
dialogue: That's right! Don't worry uncle Ralof, I won't let those soldiers sneak up on you!

speaker: Hod
dialogue: Now, Ralof, what's going on? You two look pretty well done in.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: I can't remember the last time I slept. Where to start? Well, the news you heard about Ulfric was true. The Imperials ambushed us outside Darkwater Crossing. Like they knew exactly where we'd be. That was...two days ago, now. We stopped at Helgen this morning, and I thought it was all over. Had us lined up for the headsman's block and ready to start chopping!

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: The cowards!

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: They wouldn't dare give Ulfric a fair trial. Treason, for fighting for your own people! All of Skyrim would have seen the truth then! But then...out of nowhere...a dragon attacked.

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: You don't mean a real, live...

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: I can hardly believe it myself, and I was there! As strange as it sounds, we'd be dead if not for that dragon. In the confusion, we managed to slip away. Are we really the first to make it to Riverwood?

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: Nobody has come up the south road today, as far as I know.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Good. Maybe we can lay up for a while. I'd hate to put your family in danger, Gerdur, but...

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Thanks, sister. I knew I could count on you.

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: I ought to get back to work before I'm missed, but did anyone else escape? Did Ulfric...

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Don't worry. I'm sure he made it out. It'll take more than a dragon to stop Ulfric Stormcloak!

speaker: Hod
dialogue: I'll let them into the house and, you know, show them where everything is.

speaker: Gerdur
dialogue: Hhmm. Help them drink up our mead, you mean. [to Ralof] Good luck, brother. I'll see you later.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Don't worry about me. I know how to lay low.

speaker: Ranmir
dialogue: Ha! Drink ain't gonna kill me. Not today, anyway.

speaker: Ravam Verethi
dialogue: I could run this ship better than that boy who calls himself a captain. Maybe one day I'll do something about it.

speaker: Razelan
dialogue: Now then. Here's my invitation. I don't have a poisoned dagger strapped to my thigh, et cetera, et cetera.

speaker: Thalmor Soldier
dialogue: I'm just doing my duty, sir. Everything's in order. Welcome back, sir.

speaker: Razelan
dialogue: Yes, yes. Now to find myself a drink.

speaker: Razelan
dialogue: Attention everyone! Could I have your attention, please! I have an announcement to make!  I propose a toast to Elenwen! Our Mistress!

speaker: Elenwen
dialogue: Razelan. What are you doing?

speaker: Razelan
dialogue: I speak figuratively, of course. Nothing could be more unlikely than that someone would actually want her in their bed.

speaker: Razelan
dialogue: Although... most of you are already in bed with her! But again... I speak figuratively, of course!

speaker: Razelan
dialogue: Fine. Fine. Take your hands off me. I'll be a good boy now.

speaker: Razelan
dialogue: Wouldn't want to offend our Thalmor overlords, would we?

speaker: Razelan
dialogue: Someone bring me a drink, quick!

speaker: Reldith
dialogue: City folk might look down on us, but what's wrong with farming? Everything we've got, we had to earn with our own sweat.

speaker: Revyn
dialogue: Niranye, I just have to know―what is your secret?

speaker: Niranye
dialogue: My... my what, now?

speaker: Revyn
dialogue: You know. Where do you get your goods? I am always amazed at how you manage to sell things so cheaply.

speaker: Niranye
dialogue: Oh, just a matter of finding the right suppliers.

speaker: Revyn
dialogue: Well, I'll want to meet them next time they're around. Maybe you can give me an introduction.

speaker: Niranye
dialogue: I'll consider it. Many of the people I deal with are... secretive. You know how it is.

speaker: Revyn
dialogue: Of course! I understand completely. You just put us in a room, and I'll do all the talking. No worries at all.

speaker: Rhiada
dialogue: Sometimes I hear Yngvar singing in his room. He's actually quite good.

speaker: Rhiada
dialogue: I'm sorry, Betrid. I'll clean them right away.

speaker: Betrid
dialogue: No, don't bother. You're useless, as always. I'll get Ildene to do it.

speaker: Rhiada
dialogue: I'm sorry, Betrid. I thought I had cleaned the tables properly.

speaker: Betrid
dialogue: Oh, stop apologizing. It makes you look like an idiot. Learn to talk back a bit, girl! Why, when I was in the temple....

speaker: Rhiada
dialogue: The temple, Betrid? You were one of Dibella's faithful?

speaker: Betrid
dialogue: I misspoke. Never mind what I said. Now get back to work.

speaker: Rhiada
dialogue: You have worked here in the Treasury House for a long time, haven't you Ildene?

speaker: Ildene
dialogue: Yes, child. Nana Ildene has taken care of the Silver-Bloods for many years....

speaker: Rhiada
dialogue: It's just... aren't you worried about the Forsworn? Maybe it's not safe here.

speaker: Ildene
dialogue: Don't you worry Rhiada. If any Forsworn coming knocking on our door, Nana will let you know....

speaker: Rhiada
dialogue: Thanks Nana. I feel better now.

speaker: Rhiada
dialogue: Why, thank you Thonar. I'm flattered.

speaker: Thonar
dialogue: You're married, yes? To that young metal worker?

speaker: Rhiada
dialogue: Eltrys, yes, just last season we were wed.

speaker: Thonar
dialogue: He's a lucky man to have such a beautiful young wife.

speaker: Rhiada
dialogue: Thank you, Thonar. That's generous of you to say.

speaker: Rhorlak
dialogue: I assure you, I have nothing of value. I'm nothing but a poor woodcutter just trying to make ends meet.

speaker: Ri'saad
dialogue: The wise trader finds the best opportunities, even if he must travel far to find them. Skyrim is a ripe opportunity indeed.

speaker: Atahbah
dialogue: My bones ache for the Moonsugar. It has been too long since I tasted it.

speaker: Atahbah
dialogue: My ears hear the truth in your words, and yet my body shakes with the need.

speaker: Atahbah
dialogue: Yes, of course, you are right. Still, I would give much for even a few grains of Moonsugar.

speaker: Atahbah
dialogue: Between the war and the return of the dragons, I wonder if we should not leave Skyrim and ply our trade elsewhere.

speaker: Atahbah
dialogue: That may be, but what of the war? That is not so easy to escape from.

speaker: Atahbah
dialogue: And what makes you think that?

speaker: Ria
dialogue: This is life, brother. The struggle is what reminds us to draw breath.

speaker: Ria
dialogue: Should I be holding the blade further away than a smaller one?

speaker: Ria
dialogue: I guess that comes down to footwork, then.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: Exactly. When you have a big, heavy weight swinging around you upper body, your lower body has to compensate, or you'll fall right over.

speaker: Ria
dialogue: Why can't I train with Aela?

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: Because, you wanted to learn the longer blades. Aela's never used anything bigger than a dagger.

speaker: Ria
dialogue: It's just...I think our fighting styles are similar.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: Well, you can either get better with a bow or try to learn from me.

speaker: Ria
dialogue: It just feels so slow.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: It will feel that way for a while. But eventually you'll get used to it, and then you'll get faster with it. After that, the shortsword will feel like a knitting needle when you pick it up again.

speaker: Ria
dialogue: I've never held a knitting needle.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: Of course not. My mistake.

speaker: Riften Guard Jailor
dialogue: Is it daylight out? Night? I lose track down here.

speaker: Ritual Master
dialogue: Wolf Queen. Hear our call and awaken. We summon Potema!

speaker: Ritual Master
dialogue: We summon Potema!

speaker: Necromancer
dialogue: We summon Potema!

speaker: Necromancer 2
dialogue: We summon Potema!

speaker: Ritual Master
dialogue: Long have you slept the dreamless sleep of death, Potema. No longer. Hear us Wolf Queen! We Summon You!

speaker: Ritual Master
dialogue: Summoned with words. Bounds by blood.

speaker: Necromancer
dialogue: We summon Potema!

speaker: Necromancer 2
dialogue: We summon Potema!

speaker: Potema
dialogue: Yes! Yes! Return me to this realm!

speaker: Ritual Master
dialogue: As our voices summon you the blood of the innocent binds you Wolf Queen!

speaker: Ritual Master
dialogue: Summoned with words. Bounds by blood.

speaker: Necromancer
dialogue: Summoned with words. Bounds by blood.

speaker: Necromancer 2
dialogue: Summoned with words. Bounds by blood.

speaker: Potema
dialogue: What! What are you doing?! You fools! You cannot bind me to your wills!

speaker: Ritual Master
dialogue: Summoned with words. Bounds by blood.

speaker: Necromancer
dialogue: Summoned with words. Bounds by blood.

speaker: Necromancer 2
dialogue: Summoned with words. Bounds by blood.

speaker: Potema
dialogue: You ants don't have the power to bind me!

speaker: Ritual Master
dialogue: Something is wrong. There is an intruder.

speaker: Rogatus Salvius
dialogue: I've been here 50 years, and nothing is going to move me off my land.

speaker: Roggi Knot-Beard
dialogue: I visited the meaderies in Riften once, as a lad. Wish I had their skill.

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: How are the little ones?

speaker: Iddra
dialogue: Oh, you know. Little Kjeld is a handful, and Froa is just so quiet.

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: He takes after his father, and she takes after you.

speaker: Iddra
dialogue: Well, that's the good and the bad of it.

speaker: Iddra
dialogue: If you like mead so much, why not go live in Riften?

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: Oh, I wouldn't be able to help them. Their skills were given by the Divines.

speaker: Iddra
dialogue: Maybe you could be a taster or something.

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: Ah, but I can do that right here. Right now!

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: Have you heard about Goldenglow Meadery?

speaker: Iddra
dialogue: Did something happen to it?

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: All the apiaries... it will take years to get those bees happy again.

speaker: Iddra
dialogue: Do the bees need to be happy?

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: Of course! You can't make good mead without happy honey!

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: You going to be at the inn tonight?

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: What's your wife think of your trips?

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: They're none of her business, and none of yours either.

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: Sweltering in here.

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: I'd like the fresh air better, but this isn't so bad.

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: How do you stay cheery down in these blazes?

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: I don't know. Maybe because it makes the mead taste that much better at night.

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: Again with the mead!

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: Found another one of those vents in back near the scaffold.

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: Does Dravynea know?

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: She hasn't had a chance to look at it yet. Just be careful over there.

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: So, Roggi, when are you going to get yourself a woman?

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: Oh, I'm not sure I could ever settle down like you have, friend.

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: Who says I've settled down?

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: I think this is yet another conversation that wouldn't make your wife happy.

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: That's just it... if she's not happy, there are plenty of other women who will be.

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: Oh, you old charmer.

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: I'm not sure that's a good joke to tell with women present...

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: But don't you get it? She thought he was a troll!

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: I get it. It's funny. It just might upset your wife.

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: Eh, let her get upset. She'll be angry no matter what I say, might as well enjoy myself.

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: How much do you know about the brewing of mead?

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: I know all there is to know about the drinking of it, and that suits me just fine.

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: I've been trying to figure out what makes Riften mead better than the stuff from Whiterun.

speaker: Kjeld
dialogue: Better honey?

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: There has to be more to it than that, though. I wish I knew where the bees got it from.

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: Kjeld bothering you again?

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: Well, you send that blowhard to me if he steps over the line.

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: How's the mine today?

speaker: Dravynea
dialogue: Not too bad. Careful around the more obvious scorchers.

speaker: Roggi
dialogue: As usual. I've always got an eye on the rocks.

speaker: Svari
dialogue: They can't hurt uncle Roggvir. Tell them he didn't do it.

speaker: Addvar
dialogue: Svari, you need to go home. Go home and stay there until your mother comes.

speaker: Sorex
dialogue: Get on with it!

speaker: Jala
dialogue: You've betrayed us!

speaker: Vivienne
dialogue: You should tell her that her uncle is scum that betrayed his High King. Best she know now, Addvar.

speaker: Addvar
dialogue: You're all heart, Vivienne.

speaker: Aldis
dialogue: Roggvir. You helped Ulfric Stormcloak escape this city after he murdered High King Torygg. By opening that gate for Ulfric you betrayed the people of Solitude.

speaker: Sorex
dialogue: He doesn't deserve to speak!

speaker: Roggvir
dialogue: There was no murder! Ulfric challenged Torygg. He beat the High King in fair combat.

speaker: Roggvir
dialogue: Such as our way! Such as the ancient custom of Skyrim, and all Nords!

speaker: Vivienne
dialogue: Cut 'em down!

speaker: Aldis
dialogue: Guard. Prepare the prisoner.

speaker: Roggvir
dialogue: I don't need your help.

speaker: Aldis
dialogue: Very well, Roggvir. Bow your head.

speaker: Roggvir
dialogue: On this day... I go to Sovngarde.

speaker: Rolff Stone-Fist
dialogue: Every night, I walk around the Gray Quarter and let them gray-skins know what I think of 'em.

speaker: Rolff
dialogue: You come here where you're not wanted, you eat our food, you pollute our city with your stink, and you refuse to help the Stormcloaks.

speaker: Suvaris
dialogue: But we haven't taken a side because it's not our fight.

speaker: Angrenor
dialogue: Hey, maybe the reason these gray-skins don't help in the war is because they're Imperial spies!

speaker: Suvaris
dialogue: Imperial spies? You can't be serious!

speaker: Rolff
dialogue: Maybe we'll pay you a visit tonight, little spy. We got ways of finding out what you really are.

speaker: Romlyn Dreth
dialogue: You look like you could use a drink. What do you say to some cheap mead?

speaker: Indaryn
dialogue: Romlyn, I've been meaning to speak to you. I did a count at the meadery and we're four cases short... again.

speaker: Romlyn
dialogue: What are you saying? You think I had something to do with that?

speaker: Indaryn
dialogue: I'm not accusing you of anything. Yet.

speaker: Romlyn
dialogue: The Dreth family doesn't steal, Indaryn.

speaker: Indaryn
dialogue: For your sake, I hope you're right. Because if it is you, and Maven finds out, the Dreth family is going to be one member smaller.

speaker: Romlyn
dialogue: So, what do you think of my plan. You in or out?

speaker: Indaryn
dialogue: If you think I'd would make a move like that without asking Maven, you're out of your mind. Doing that would be a fatal mistake.

speaker: Romlyn
dialogue: Come on, think about it. She'd reward us!

speaker: Indaryn
dialogue: If you want to go out to Whiterun and burn that meadery down, go right ahead. And when the guard traces it back here, and Maven is implicated, I'll be sure to tell her it was your idea.

speaker: Romlyn
dialogue: Have I told you about Valen, my dear?

speaker: Keerava
dialogue: I love when you spin that yarn. Gets better every time you add something new.

speaker: Romlyn
dialogue: He killed six Imperial Guards before they dragged him into the prisons.

speaker: Keerava
dialogue: Was this before or after the Mythic Dawn attacked the Emperor and Valen single-handedly fought them off? Just shut up and drink, Romlyn.

speaker: Niluva
dialogue: Do you know what Indaryn told me? He said that if I'm late one more time, he's going to kick me out the door!

speaker: Romlyn
dialogue: That swit. One day, he'll regret pushing all of us around!

speaker: Niluva
dialogue: What do you mean?

speaker: Romlyn
dialogue: All I'm saying is Indaryn's going to push too far one day and they're going to push back...hard.

speaker: Rondach
dialogue: I have to work, or Anton will rip my head off.

speaker: Rorik
dialogue: I was a different man, once -- strong, commanding, ah, and young. But the Great War was a long time ago.

speaker: Rorlund
dialogue: As high priest of the Eight Divines, I bid you welcome.

speaker: Rorlund
dialogue: Silana, you don't seem yourself. Is something the matter?

speaker: Silana
dialogue: Oh, yes sir. I feel many of Solitude's families are having trouble getting by, and the wealthy do nothing to help them!

speaker: Rorlund
dialogue: Your compassion is admirable, but you see, we cannot help them all. The poor must learn from the examples of the gods and raise themselves up.

speaker: Silana
dialogue: I respectfully disagree, sir. Stendarr and Zenithar may demand strength from them, but Mara and Dibella demand compassion from us.

speaker: Rorlund
dialogue: I see you have meditated on this subject quite thoroughly. I shall not stop you, but please, try to attend to your temple duties as well.

speaker: Rorlund
dialogue: A word, my love?

speaker: Freir
dialogue: What troubles you, darling?

speaker: Rorlund
dialogue: I fear attendance is down. There are so few worshippers coming to see us. Could it be that the war has weakened their faith?

speaker: Freir
dialogue: Nonsense, dear. I've had more visitors than ever seeking the wisdom of the hearth goddesses.

speaker: Rorlund
dialogue: Ah, that must be it. So many of the men are serving in battle. I shall pray to Stendarr that they return victorious.

speaker: Rorlund
dialogue: Ah a few bottles of Spiced Wine should hit the spot.

speaker: Evette
dialogue: Of course. And I'm sure it's mostly for ceremonial purposes.

speaker: Gissur
dialogue: But I need that money, I earned it! I have my own expenses, you know.

speaker: Rulindil
dialogue: Silence! Do not presume, Gissur. You are most useful, but do not presume. We have more informants who are less... offensive.

speaker: Gissur
dialogue: But no one else has brought you such valuable information, have they? [pause] Etienne, he's talked, hasn't he? He knows where that old man you're looking for is, he told me himself.

speaker: Rulindil
dialogue: You'll get your money when he's told the rest of his story, as agreed.

speaker: Gissur
dialogue: So he has talked! I knew it!

speaker: Rulindil
dialogue: Everyone talks, in the end. Now, I have work to do. Leave me to it, if you ever want to see the rest of your payment.

speaker: Gissur
dialogue: Can I... I could help you. He'd talk to me. He trusts me.

speaker: Rulindil
dialogue: You'd like to come downstairs with me, is that it, Gissur? Shall we loose his bonds and put you in a cell together? You can ask him anything you like and see how he answers.

speaker: Gissur
dialogue: No, no. I... I'll wait outside.

speaker: Rulindil
dialogue: That would probably be best. [pause] Now get out!

speaker: Etienne
dialogue: Stop. Please. I don't know anything else. Don't you think I'd have told you already?

speaker: Thalmor guard
dialogue: Silence. You know the rules. Do not speak unless spoken to. Master Rulindil will ask the questions.

speaker: Rulindil
dialogue: Let's begin again.

speaker: Etienne
dialogue: No...for pity's sake...I've already told you everything...

speaker: Rulindil
dialogue: You know the rules.

speaker: Etienne
dialogue: [guard hits him] Nooooo!!!

speaker: Rulindil
dialogue: Start at the beginning, as usual. If you persist in this stubbornness I'll have...

speaker: Etienne
dialogue: No, wait! I was... just catching my breath... why wouldn't I tell you again? I don't even know anything... There's an old man... he lives in Riften. He could be this Esbern you're looking for, but I don't know. He's old and seemed kind of crazy. That's all I know.

speaker: Rulindil
dialogue: And his name is...?

speaker: Etienne
dialogue: I don't know his name. Like I've already told you a hundred- [guard hits him] Ahhh!

speaker: Rulindil
dialogue: You know the rules. Just answer the questions. And where is this nameless old man?

speaker: Etienne
dialogue: Like I said, I don't know. I've seen him down in the Ratway. Maybe he lives down there, but I don't know for sure.

speaker: Rulindil
dialogue: That will be all for now. I must say I continue to be disappointed in your lack of cooperation. I hope next time you will do better.

speaker: Etienne
dialogue: What else do you want from me? I've told you everything. Listen, If you let me go I can take you to Riften, show you where- [guard hits him again] Ghaaa!!!

speaker: Thalmor guard
dialogue: Silence, prisoner!

speaker: Runil
dialogue: Life is far too short, my friend. Don't waste it!

context: Bring one Night Falls on Sentinel to Rustleif
speaker: Rustleif
dialogue: Need a dagger? No? How about a claymore?

speaker: Kematu
dialogue: We meet at last, my dear lady.

speaker: Saadia
dialogue: What is this? What have {{Hide|you|referring to the Dragonborn}} done?

speaker: Kematu
dialogue: Oh, come now. You didn't really expect to manipulate people forever, did you? Your luck had to run out sometime.

speaker: Commander Caius
dialogue: Well, Sabjorn. Now that you've taken care of your little pest problem, how about I get a taste of some of your mead?

speaker: Sabjorn
dialogue: Help yourself, milord. It's my finest brew yet... I call it Honningbrew Reserve. I think you'll find it quite pleasing to your palate.

speaker: Commander Caius
dialogue: Oh come now, this is mead... not some wine to be sipped and savored.

speaker: Commander Caius
dialogue: By the Eight?! What... what's in this?

speaker: Sabjorn
dialogue: I... I don't know. What's wrong?

speaker: Commander Caius
dialogue: You assured me this place was clean! I'll see... see to it that you remain in irons for the rest of your days!

speaker: Sabjorn
dialogue: No, please! I don't understand...

speaker: Commander Caius
dialogue: Silence, idiot! I should have known better... to trust this place after it's been riddled with filth.

speaker: Sabjorn
dialogue: I beg you... please. This is not what it seems!

speaker: Commander Caius
dialogue: You... you're in charge here until I can sort this all out.

speaker: Mallus Maccius
dialogue: It will be my pleasure.

speaker: Commander Caius
dialogue: And you... you're coming with me to Dragonsreach. We'll see how quickly your memory clears in the city's prisons. Now move.

speaker: Sabjorn
dialogue: Look, I assure you, this is all just a huge misunderstanding!

speaker: Commander Caius
dialogue: I said move!

speaker: Mallus Maccius
dialogue: Farewell, Sabjorn.

speaker: Saerlund
dialogue: Because I did something not a soul in this bloodstained house of war has the backbone to do... dared to speak my mind.

speaker: Harrald
dialogue: I see you still have the run of the place, traitor.

speaker: Saerlund
dialogue: Come now brother, don't act all high and mighty. I know you could care less about the war one way or another. The things you say are just an act to please mother.

speaker: Harrald
dialogue: Perhaps. Perhaps not. I'm disappointed in you brother. You had it all. You had it all and your mouth cost you everything.

speaker: Saerlund
dialogue: At least I've chosen a side instead of acting like a spectator. One day, you'll be forced to make a choice. And I hope it's the right one, brother.

speaker: Saerlund
dialogue: So, is this what it's come to? You'd have your own flesh and blood hanged just to solidify your grip as the next Jarl?

speaker: Harrald
dialogue: If that's what it will take then so be it.

speaker: Saerlund
dialogue: What's become of us? We used to be inseparable... always fighting back to back and letting nothing stand in our way. You've changed, brother. And not for the better I'm afraid.

speaker: Harrald
dialogue: I've done what I needed to do keep mother happy. It doesn't matter what I really believe.

speaker: Saerlund
dialogue: You've done what you've had to for yourself, not for mother. Wise up, Harrald. There's a storm on the horizon and it will blow through here with all its fury. It's time to choose a side.

speaker: Saffir
dialogue: Nothing like a good adventure or romance to lose yourself in.

speaker: Saffir
dialogue: I know your family's honor is important to you, but we can't afford it!

speaker: Amren
dialogue: It took me weeks to find that thieves' den. I can't stop now, and I can't get the sword on my own.

speaker: Saffir
dialogue: So you're willing to starve your wife and daughter to reclaim some rusty old sword?

speaker: Amren
dialogue: I just need to hire one, maybe two good men. You won't starve.

speaker: Saffir
dialogue: I'll put it plainly. You can claim your sword, or you can keep your wife. If you set foot outside the gate, I won't be here when you return.

speaker: Amren
dialogue: Saffir! Wait... I....

speaker: Braith
dialogue: Mother? Can I talk to you?

speaker: Saffir
dialogue: Not now, Braith.

speaker: Saffir
dialogue: Not now, Braith.

speaker: Braith
dialogue: I wanted to ask you something. It's about a boy...

speaker: Saffir
dialogue: Not now, Braith. Go... go ask your father.

speaker: Safia
dialogue: I'm a pirate, sweetie. Assassination attempts are an occupational hazard. Now, shall we?

speaker: Alduin
dialogue: {{hide|Sahloknir, ziil gro dovah ulse! Slen Tiid Vo!|Sahloknir, I bind your dragon spirit for eternity! Flesh Time Undo!}}

speaker: Sahloknir
dialogue: {{hide|Alduin, thuri! Boaan tiid vokriiha suleyksejun kruziik?|Alduin, my lord! Has the time come to revive our ancient realm?}}

speaker: Sailor
dialogue: C'mon, let's get something to eat.

speaker: Sailor 2
dialogue: Gods, I'll be glad to see the last of Skyrim. Dragons, murder, rebellion... and we sail right into the middle of it with the Emperor on board.

speaker: Sailor
dialogue: I think we'll all feel better once we're back out at sea. Won't be long now.

speaker: Salma
dialogue: How can you just sit there and wait? We should be in there!

speaker: Beem-Ja
dialogue: We must gather our strength. Who knows what's inside?

speaker: Salma
dialogue: Treasure, that's what! Get off your scaly rump and let's go!

speaker: Beem-Ja
dialogue: [notices player] Hush, Salma. We aren't alone.

speaker: Beem-Ja
dialogue: Don't rush ahead. This is a trap if I ever saw one.

speaker: Salma
dialogue: Would you look at that!

speaker: Beem-Ja
dialogue: This is it! Gathrik awaits us!

speaker: Salma
dialogue: What are you on about? Let's just get the treasure here and go.

speaker: Salonia
dialogue: Why are we even going to a wedding at this far flung end of the Empire anyway?

speaker: Plautis
dialogue: I told you, it's the wedding of Vittoria Vici, an extremely well connected merchant with the East Empire Company. The Emperor's cousin? Remember? Hopefully these gifts will put us in her good graces, secure that import deal, and lead the way to an audience with the Emperor.

speaker: Salonia
dialogue: I hate it here. Those were my favorite shoes, ruined and for what? We never even made it to the wedding.

speaker: Plautis
dialogue: Wha... Your shoes? We get robbed by bandits, my clothes torn to shreds by some giant cat, our bodyguard eaten by a dragon... And you're worried about your shoes?

speaker: Salonia
dialogue: When we get back to Cyrodiil, I swear I will hire an army of battlemages to come up here and set fire to the whole damned province.

speaker: Sapphire
dialogue: I'm really getting tired of your excuses. When you borrowed the money, you said you'd pay it back on time for double the usual fee.

speaker: Sapphire
dialogue: Next time, keep your plans quieter and nothing would have happened to it.

speaker: Shadr
dialogue: What? Are you saying you robbed it? Why? Why are you doing this to me?

speaker: Sapphire
dialogue: Look, Shadr. Last warning. Pay up or else. All I care about is the gold. Everything else is your problem.

speaker: Savos
dialogue: I'm sorry, were you about to say something?

speaker: Ancano
dialogue: Well, what is the meaning of this?

speaker: Ancano
dialogue: Don't play coy. You asked to see a specific member of the College. Here he/she is. Now what is it that you want?

speaker: Quaranir
dialogue: There's been a misunderstanding. Clearly I should not be here. I shall simply take my leave.

speaker: Ancano
dialogue: What? What trickery is this? You're not going anywhere until I find out what you're up to.

speaker: Quaranir
dialogue: I'm not 'up to' anything. I apologize if I have offended you in any way.

speaker: Ancano
dialogue: We shall see about this...

speaker: Mirabelle
dialogue: I continue to hear things about dragon sightings in Skyrim.

speaker: Savos
dialogue: Dragons? Well, that's fascinating. We should have someone look into that.

speaker: Mirabelle
dialogue: Would you like me to send someone? Faralda or Phinis, perhaps?

speaker: Savos
dialogue: I'll think about it.

speaker: Mirabelle
dialogue: Arch-Mage, the Synod have contacted us again, asking if we've any word on their researchers.

speaker: Savos
dialogue: What did you tell them last time?

speaker: Mirabelle
dialogue: That they had arrived, asked for information which was provided to them, and went on their way with no suggestion of further interaction.

speaker: Savos
dialogue: That hasn't changed, has it? Then just tell them again.

speaker: Mirabelle
dialogue: Should we consider investigating the matter?

speaker: Savos
dialogue: No, I don't think so. Respond to their request, and we'll leave it at that.

speaker: Mirabelle
dialogue: Yes, Arch-Mage. Thank you.

speaker: Savos
dialogue: Is there anything new I should be aware of, Mirabelle?

speaker: Mirabelle
dialogue: I'm dealing with a few new research proposals, evaluating the results of three long-term projects, and keeping an eye on our new Apprentices. There were also two items requiring disciplinary action recently.

speaker: Savos
dialogue: Everything's under control, then? Right. Keep up the good work.

speaker: Mirabelle
dialogue: Yes, thank you Arch-Mage.

speaker: Mirabelle
dialogue: Sir, the Imperial Legion has again requested assistance. What shall I tell them?

speaker: Savos
dialogue: The same thing we've told them before, and the same thing we've told these Stormcloaks. It's not our concern.

speaker: Mirabelle
dialogue: Forgive me, but at what point does it become our concern?

speaker: Savos
dialogue: Never. The College cannot become mired in local politics. What happens inside these walls is our worry. What happens outside is theirs.

speaker: Savos
dialogue: Mirabelle, would you please make sure my schedule is clear for the next few days? I'm working on something important.

speaker: Mirabelle
dialogue: Your schedule is always clear, Arch-Mage. I see to that.

speaker: Savos
dialogue: Ah, yes. True. Well, thank you.

speaker: Savos
dialogue: Come on, we're finally here! Let's not waste any more time!

speaker: Savos
dialogue: Don't forget, this whole idea was Atmah's to begin with.

speaker: Savos
dialogue: Can you imagine the looks on their faces when we come back?

speaker: Hafnar
dialogue: You keep talking like you're sure we'll find something useful in here.

speaker: Girduin
dialogue: Given the history of this place, it's more than likely there's still some amount of power here.

speaker: Savos
dialogue: Enchanted weapons, tomes of ancient knowledge, Shalidor's secrets themselves -- who knows what we could find!

speaker: Takes-In-Light
dialogue: And what if... What if there are things guarding this place?

speaker: Atmah
dialogue: Against six College-trained mages? I think we'll be fine.

speaker: Elvali
dialogue: We... we have to go back. We can't leave Girduin...

speaker: Hafnar
dialogue: We barely made it out alive, and you want to go back in?

speaker: Atmah
dialogue: It's too late. There isn't enough of him left to go back in after.

speaker: Takes-In-Light
dialogue: Gods, what have we done?

speaker: Savos
dialogue: We can't go back. Might as well go forward. We can still do this.

speaker: Atmah
dialogue: Savos is right. We can make it if we just stay alert.

speaker: Savos
dialogue: Come on, we can't stop now. We have to keep moving!

speaker: Atmah
dialogue: Where's Elvali? She was right behind me.

speaker: Hafnar
dialogue: Dead. Something grabbed her from behind. Gone before I could do anything.

speaker: Takes-In-Light
dialogue: This is insanity. We never should've come here.

speaker: Atmah
dialogue: You're right. This is all my fault. Should we turn around, head back?

speaker: Hafnar
dialogue: I don't think going back is a good idea.

speaker: Savos
dialogue: Going back would be the end of all of us. We keep pushing forward, and we'll make it. We will!

speaker: Atmah
dialogue: Come on, you can make it. Let's go.

speaker: Atmah
dialogue: We shouldn't have left her there to die!

speaker: Savos
dialogue: What else could we do? Stay there and die with her? She refused to go on, we didn't have a choice!

speaker: Hafnar
dialogue: This is it, you know. Through this door. Can you feel it?

speaker: Atmah
dialogue: We're not going to make it, are we?

speaker: Hafnar
dialogue: We stay together, no matter what. Agreed?

speaker: Atmah
dialogue: I'll be right with you.

speaker: Savos
dialogue: Agreed. We all stay together.

speaker: Savos
dialogue: ...I'm sorry, friends. I'm so sorry! I had no choice! It was the only way to make sure that monster never escaped! I promise you, I'll never let this happen again! I'll seal this whole place away...

speaker: Scouts
dialogue: Why do the Nords bother you so much, Ambarys?

speaker: Ambarys
dialogue: Why do you even need to ask? They treat your people as bad as they do mine.

speaker: Scouts
dialogue: I think that's just their way. The Nords don't like anybody who's not a Nord, but they're not bad people, deep down.

speaker: Ambarys
dialogue: Look around you. Don't you know what their little war is about? They want all non-Nords out of Skyrim. That means you and me.

speaker: Scouts
dialogue: Oh, I doubt that very much. Who would load their ships, then?

speaker: Ambarys
dialogue: Just you wait and see.

speaker: Ambarys
dialogue: How much do they pay you per day?

speaker: Scouts
dialogue: That's really none of your business...

speaker: Ambarys
dialogue: How much?

speaker: Scouts
dialogue: Eight septims per day, plus lodging.

speaker: Ambarys
dialogue: Eight septims for breaking your back, and then you live in squalor. How much is your dignity worth?

speaker: Scouts
dialogue: If it's all the same to you, Scouts-Many-Marshes prefers to eat and drink in peace.

speaker: Ambarys
dialogue: Sorry, my scaly friend, you've come to the wrong place. Around here we don't ignore what's happening in the world.

context: I robbed you, but now I want my money, too
speaker: Sapphire
dialogue: I'm really getting tired of your excuses. When you borrowed the money, you said you'd pay it back on time for double the usual fee.

context: I robbed you, but now I want my money, too
speaker: Shadr
dialogue: I know I did. But how was I supposed to know the shipment would get robbed?

context: I robbed you, but now I want my money, too
speaker: Sapphire
dialogue: Next time, keep your plans quieter and nothing would have happened to it.

context: I robbed you, but now I want my money, too
speaker: Shadr
dialogue: What? Are you saying you robbed it? Why? Why are you doing this to me?

context: I robbed you, but now I want my money, too
speaker: Sapphire
dialogue: Look, Shadr. Last warning. Pay up or else. All I care about is the gold. Everything else is your problem.

speaker: Shadr
dialogue: Here's another septim, Madesi. How much more do I need?

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: Only thirty more and it'll be all yours. If I might ask, who is the lucky woman?

speaker: Shadr
dialogue: It's for Marise, but don't say a word to her!

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: Don't worry, Shadr, your secret is safe with me.

speaker: Shadr
dialogue: Hi, Marise. How are you today?

speaker: Marise
dialogue: I'm well. How are things over at the stables? Old Hofgrir giving you a hard time?

speaker: Shadr
dialogue: Naw... he's fine. Look, I wanted to ask if you'll... um, if you'd like to... well, like to have a drink with me at the Bee and Barb sometime?

speaker: Marise
dialogue: Shadr, that's so sweet... I'd love to.

context: We know about the dragon already
speaker: Shadr
dialogue: Brand-Shei, did you hear about Helgen? It's... it's gone! A dragon burned it to the ground!

context: We know about the dragon already
speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: Yes, I heard. I think all of Skyrim knows by know.

context: We know about the dragon already
speaker: Shadr
dialogue: Do you... do you think that could happen here? I mean, could a dragon come here and burn the city down?

context: We know about the dragon already
speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: I don't know. All we can do is hope the Eight will favor us and have these creatures stay far away from Riften.

speaker: Shadr
dialogue: Yes, Lady Mjoll. If Riften gets attacked, we'll retreat inside the city gates and bar the door just like you said.

speaker: Mjoll
dialogue: Good. You could be our first line of defense since you live outside the city walls, so we're depending on you.

speaker: Shadr
dialogue: Yes. The man came by at noon just like you said. I gave him the package and he gave me this pouch for you. The package was heavy... I needed his help getting it on his horse. What was inside?

speaker: Grelka
dialogue: Hey, I told you not to ask any questions. Now, here. For your trouble.

speaker: Shadr
dialogue: Thanks, Grelka!

speaker: No, sorry
dialogue: Very well. I am poorer of it.

speaker: Sharamph
dialogue: Malacath is pleased with your strength, Larak.

speaker: Larak
dialogue: I am honored.

speaker: Shel
dialogue: My chief, Gharol threatens to have me work in the mines. You won't allow my pretty hands to dirty, will you?

speaker: Burguk
dialogue: No, my wife. You have been given other gifts to please your chief than mine work. I will talk to Gharol and all will be well.

speaker: Shel
dialogue: Oh, thank you my chief!

speaker: Sheogorath
dialogue: Do not believe madness to be a curse, mortal. For some, it is the greatest of blessings. A bitter mercy perhaps, but mercy nonetheless.

speaker: Sheogorath
dialogue: More tea, Pelly my dear?

speaker: Pelagius
dialogue: Oh, I couldn't. It goes right through me. Besides, I have so many things to do. So many detractors and undesirables, naysayers, buffoons. My...My headsman hasn't slept in three days.

speaker: Pelagius
dialogue: Yes, yes, as you've said countless times before.

speaker: Sheogorath
dialogue: Harumph! Well, if you're going to be like that, I think its best I take my leave. A good day to you, sir. I said good day!

speaker: Pelagius
dialogue: Yes. Leave me to my ceaseless responsibilities and burdens.

speaker: Dervenin
dialogue: Master! You've taken me back! Does this mean we're going home? Oh, happy times! I can't wait to...

speaker: Sheogorath
dialogue: Yes, yes, that's quite enough celebration. Let's send you ahead, shall we?

speaker: Larak
dialogue: Your muscles ripple when you work the forge. It's pleasing.

speaker: Shuftharz
dialogue: Thank you, my chief.

speaker: Siddgeir
dialogue: Helvard! The guards are looking sloppy today. I want you to reduce their wages for the month.

speaker: Siddgeir
dialogue: I would think a man of your military training would be able to do with less but so be it.

speaker: Siddgeir
dialogue: Why have taxes not come in from Granite Hill, Nenya? We should send some guards down there.

speaker: Nenya
dialogue: They are only a little late, Jarl. The trade routes are affected by the war, we should give them another day.

speaker: Siddgeir
dialogue: Very well, but when their emissary arrives I want words with him.

speaker: Alvor
dialogue: Sigrid! We have company!

speaker: Sigrid
dialogue: Hadvar! We've been so worried about you! Come, you two must be hungry. Sit down and I'll get you something to eat.

speaker: Alvor
dialogue: Now then, boy, what's the big mystery? What are you doing here looking like you lost an argument with a cave bear?

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: I don't know where to start. You know I was assigned to General Tullius's guard. We were stopped in Helgen when we were attacked by...a dragon.

speaker: Alvor
dialogue: A dragon? That's ridiculous. You aren't drunk, are you boy?

speaker: Sigrid
dialogue: Husband. Let him tell his story.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Not much more to tell. The dragon flew over and just wrecked the whole place. Mass confusion. I don't know if anyone else got out alive. I doubt I'd have made it out if not for my friend here. I need to get back to Solitude and let them know what's happened. I thought you could help us out. Food, supplies, a place to stay.

speaker: Dorthe
dialogue: Hadvar, did you really see a dragon? What did it look like? Did it have big teeth?

speaker: Sigrid
dialogue: Hush, child. Don't pester your cousin.

speaker: Alvor
dialogue: Well, I'd better get back to work. You two make yourselves at home.

speaker: Alvor
dialogue: Good morning, wife.

speaker: Alvor
dialogue: Well, I'd better get to work. I have to fix another saw blade for Gerdur's mill.

speaker: Sigrid
dialogue: Take care, husband.

speaker: Alvor
dialogue: Sigrid! Love of my life! When you get a spare moment, I could use some water.

speaker: Sigrid
dialogue: Don't you sweet talk me, Alvor. Not after last night. I'll bring you water when I'm done with my other chores.

speaker: Alvor
dialogue: Woman, you'll be the death of me yet. Fine, take your time. I'll just die of thirst in the heat of this forge.

speaker: Sigrid
dialogue: Drunk again, Embry? Don't let Alvor hear you talking to me that way. He'll stick your head in his forge.

speaker: Embry
dialogue: So that's a no I take it?

speaker: Sigrid
dialogue: Aye. She's helping me in the house, and even helps her father at the forge.

speaker: Hilde
dialogue: She'll make a fine wife someday.

speaker: Sigrid
dialogue: Thank Shor I have a lot of years before I have to worry about that!

speaker: Silana
dialogue: It should be quite the affair. Nice to have something happy in the midst of the war.

speaker: Evette
dialogue: Vittoria is practically glowing.

speaker: Silana
dialogue: Mistress, a word?

speaker: Silana
dialogue: I know you and father Rorlund have many duties to attend to in the temple, but sometimes I feel that there are more important matters to attend to.

speaker: Freir
dialogue: What could be more important than hearing the prayers of the faithful, and answering the questions of the dedicated?

speaker: Silana
dialogue: Mistress, the people of Solitude are destitute. Many are starving and desperate for work. We need to be more active, to reach out to them.

speaker: Freir
dialogue: We took you in, didn't we? We would be glad to extend our welcome to any other who showed your dedication. What more could we do?

speaker: Silana
dialogue: I know, and I appreciate it dearly. But I can't help but feel we could be doing more...

speaker: Freir
dialogue: Kynareth has blessed you with tremendous compassion, Silana. You will find a way, I'm sure of it.

speaker: Silana
dialogue: Oh, yes sir. I feel many of Solitude's families are having trouble getting by, and the wealthy do nothing to help them!

speaker: Rorlund
dialogue: Your compassion is admirable, but you see, we cannot help them all. The poor must learn from the examples of the gods and raise themselves up.

speaker: Silana
dialogue: I respectfully disagree, sir. Stendarr and Zenithar may demand strength from them, but Mara and Dibella demand compassion from us.

speaker: Rorlund
dialogue: I see you have meditated on this subject quite thoroughly. I shall not stop you, but please, try to attend to your temple duties as well.

speaker: Madena
dialogue: Your ancestors wouldn't want this, Silus!

speaker: Silus
dialogue: Why should I hide from it? This is my family's legacy!

speaker: Madena
dialogue: It's the past! Dead oaths on dead lips. Let it stay there.

speaker: Silus
dialogue: The museum is opening, Madena.

speaker: Ilia
dialogue: Greetings, mother.

speaker: Silvia
dialogue: Daughter. Who is this you have brought me?

speaker: Ilia
dialogue: I found a willing subject for you. Payment has already been discussed, of course.

speaker: Silvia
dialogue: I'll just prepare the subject now...

speaker: Ilia
dialogue: I can't let you do this, mother. You have to die now!

speaker: Jouane
dialogue: Yes, child?

speaker: Sissel
