dialogue: I was just wondering. The next time we meet, do you think maybe you could teach me some fire magic? Nothing dangerous! Maybe a candle lighting spell?

speaker: Jouane
dialogue: By the Eight, keep your voice down! Do you want the entire village to learn our secrets?

speaker: Sissel
dialogue: Oh! I'm... I'm sorry. I didn't mean to upset you.

speaker: Jouane
dialogue: Shh shh. It's fine, child. It's fine. But we must be cautious, hmm? What we do, the things I teach you. The others wouldn't understand.

speaker: Sissel
dialogue: I understand. I'm sorry. I just get so excited thinking about it. So... can we. Do some fire magic?

speaker: Jouane
dialogue: Hmph. Most certainly not. But perhaps I can teach you how to put some candles out. We'll start there.

speaker: Sissel
dialogue: Oooh, wonderful! I can't wait!

speaker: Jouane
dialogue: Today I'll teach you a useful spell that might just save your life. If you should ever fall into a river, you'll be very glad you learned it.

speaker: Sissel
dialogue: Oh! Are you going to teach me how to turn into a mud crab?

speaker: Jouane
dialogue: Oh, it's much better than that. I will teach you how to breathe underwater, with no need to turn into one of those ugly creatures.

speaker: Sissel
dialogue: Wow! Then I could dive into a river and swim so far away that Britte and father could never find me.

speaker: Jouane
dialogue: Now, clear your mind and breathe deeply. Good concentration is very important for spellcasting.

speaker: Skald
dialogue: Your man Horik is wearing his Legion armor. What am I to make of that?

speaker: Brina
dialogue: He's proud of his service, Skald. The Legion taught us loyalty, and we're loyal to Dawnstar.

speaker: Skald
dialogue: This isn't over. I catch you sending one letter to General Tullius, I'll have you both executed.

speaker: Skald
dialogue: You, have a request of me, Bulfrek? [laughter] This should be interesting.

speaker: Bulfrek
dialogue: Well, I was thinking, sir, with the war going on and all. Maybe, I could enlist? Fight the Imperials?

speaker: Skald
dialogue: A servant? Enlisting in the Stormcloaks? [laughter] Ah, Bulfrek, that's why I like having you about. You're always good for a laugh.

speaker: Bulfrek
dialogue: Uh, yes sir. That's me. Your oafish servant.

speaker: Skald
dialogue: Bulfrek, I have an order of swords and armor from the local blacksmith coming here. I need every piece polished to a fine shine.

speaker: Bulfrek
dialogue: Yes, my Jarl. We could hardly waste anyone else's precious time on such a tedious task.

speaker: Skald
dialogue: Exactly, Bulfrek. You always know your place.

speaker: Skald
dialogue: Safety? Don't I have you to handle the town's safety? What is this about, Jod?

speaker: Jod
dialogue: You keep pledging more and more of our guard to the frontlines. The way this is going, we won't be able to defend our own borders.

speaker: Skald
dialogue: Nonsense. The best place for our men is driving the Imperials back. I will ensure that men from Dawnstar get every opportunity for glory.

speaker: Jod
dialogue: Glory is meaningless if they have no home to return to. I urge you to lower our commitments to the front until I'm sure we're safe.

speaker: Skald
dialogue: I won't have you rob our soldiers of their chance to drive out the Empire. I'm done discussing this, Jod.

speaker: Skald
dialogue: We are poised for glory, Jod. The Empire will never take Dawnstar while every last man, woman, and child here draws breathe!

speaker: Jod
dialogue: With respect, Jarl. You can't ask everyone to throw themselves against trained Legionnaires. Let's leave the fighting to the Stormcloaks.

speaker: Skald
dialogue: You're right. Why dilute the glory with too many souls fighting over it? We'll drive out the Empire and be celebrated as heroes when we win.

speaker: Jod
dialogue: If we win. This war is going to drag on for years. I can feel it. We need to prepare for a long struggle ahead.

speaker: Skald
dialogue: Enough of your dire predictions! We will talk about this another time.

speaker: Skald
dialogue: You wish to leave now? In Skyrim's moment of triumph, just before we cast off the yoke of Imperial rule?

speaker: Madena
dialogue: Yes, that's exactly what I'm asking. I'm not a Nord, I'm a Breton, and I have no wish to fight this war.

speaker: Skald
dialogue: I don't think so, Madena. There will be no deserters in this hold, and that's final.

speaker: Skald
dialogue: Madena, can we count on your spells to assist us in this war? The Empire is bound to bring their battlemages against us.

speaker: Madena
dialogue: I told you before, Skald, I have no interest in taking sides in this war. I've no desire to be killed.

speaker: Skald
dialogue: What good is a court mage if she refuses to fight? Where's your sense of duty?

speaker: Madena
dialogue: When I came here, my only duties were to cure crop diseases and occasionally light a bonfire on holidays. I didn't sign up to kill.

speaker: Skald
dialogue: Fine, but this isn't over Madena. We'll talk again.

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: I told you, this is the whelp that Vilkas mentioned.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: Ah, yes. I heard you gave him quite a thrashing.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: Did you call me?

speaker: Aela
dialogue: Of course we did, icebrain. Show this newblood where the rest of the whelps sleep.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: New blood? Oh, hello. I'm Farkas. Come, follow me.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: Brothers and sisters of the Circle, today we welcome a new soul into our mortal fold. This man has endured, has challenged, and has shown his valor. Who will speak for him?

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: I stand witness to the courage of the soul before us.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: Would you raise your shield in his defense?

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: I would stand at his back, that the world might never overtake us.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: And would you raise your sword in his honor?

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: It stands ready to meet the blood of his foes.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: And would you raise a mug in his name?

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: I would lead the song of triumph as our mead hall reveled in his stories.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: Then the judgment of this Circle is complete. His heart beats with fury and courage that have united the Companions since the days of the distant green summers. Let it beat with ours, that the mountains may echo and our enemies may tremble at the call.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: It shall be so.

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: It shall be so.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: It shall be so.

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: All these younglings scampering around.

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: Some of them might try. But that's not what I'm worried about.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: What then?

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: That they might get themselves killed.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: By you?

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: They should be so lucky.

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: Are you prepared for tonight's hunt?

speaker: Aela
dialogue: I've been thinking we need to be more... discreet.

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: There's nothing wrong with what we're doing.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: You know the old man doesn't like it. Let's just not be too obvious.

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: To me as well. I think we don't see the same tradition at play here.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: If you want to lead this pack when I'm gone, you have to see farther. Look closer.

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: Well which is it? Look farther or closer?

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: Come on now, boy, you know what I meant...

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: You speak in riddles sometimes.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: I don't mean to confuse you.

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: It's not confusing... just frustrating.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: You're a strong warrior, Skjor. Your heart is fiery and that serves you well in battle.

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: Thank you, Harbinger.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: But even the bravest of men consider their actions. I want you to survive long enough to take the mantle.

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: Don't worry about me.

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: Heard you had a bit of trouble near Solitude last week.

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: I'm imagining you just standing your ground and letting them tire themselves out.

speaker: Njada
dialogue: I'm telling you, it works. Let them ring their own ears on my shield, then scoop them up off the ground.

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: We all have different means to glory, Stonearm. Well done.

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: I've got a bad grip on my shield, could you take a look at it?

speaker: Njada
dialogue: I'm a warrior, not a blacksmith.

speaker: Skjor
dialogue: Can't you just tell me if the grip is bad?

speaker: Njada
dialogue: If Eorlund made it, it's more likely you're gripping it wrong. Find me tomorrow and we can go over it.

speaker: Skulvar
dialogue: Lookin' forward to it.

speaker: Skulvar
dialogue: Don't suppose there is. But you don't have to be so damned prickly.

speaker: Skulvar
dialogue: Yes, son. We should try to capture it.

speaker: Skulvar
dialogue: Big lizards? By Shor, your mother gave birth to a half-wit. That is the end of this discussion.

speaker: Uthgerd
dialogue: Careful, huh? Thanks, Skulvar. I'll remember that. Ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Katla
dialogue: Another gorgeous gray day, right dear?

speaker: Snilling
dialogue: It's too cold for my bones, but that never seems to stop you, dear.

speaker: Knud
dialogue: I'm gonna go play soldier with a tree!

speaker: Katla
dialogue: That's nice, son. Just don't stomp on the crop like last time!

speaker: Snilling
dialogue: I'll see if I can't get some work done inside, where it's warm.

speaker: Hrefna
dialogue: Sondas, I've heard about Morrowind.

speaker: Sondas
dialogue: Oh? What about it?

speaker: Hrefna
dialogue: That it was black and gross and nobody wanted to live there anymore.

speaker: Sondas
dialogue: I'll have to take your word on that one, my dear.

speaker: Hrefna
dialogue: Do you ever want to go to Morrowind, Sondas?

speaker: Sondas
dialogue: I've been in Skyrim my whole life. Why would I want to leave?

speaker: Hrefna
dialogue: To see the fires!

speaker: Sondas
dialogue: I think I like the lake here just a little more.

speaker: Tormir
dialogue: Sondas, does Hrefna ever mention Meieran to you?

speaker: Sondas
dialogue: She hardly mentions anything else.

speaker: Tormir
dialogue: I'm just worried about what he's teaching her.

speaker: Sondas
dialogue: I wouldn't worry about that. He's a good elf. I trust him.

speaker: Tormir
dialogue: You're probably right.

speaker: Tormir
dialogue: Thanks for looking after Hrefna.

speaker: Sondas
dialogue: Oh, it's no trouble. She's a smart little girl. Might talk your ear off, but she's fun.

speaker: Tormir
dialogue: Well, I know she thinks the world of you.

speaker: Sondas
dialogue: Well, I'll try to be a good influence, then.

speaker: Corpulus
dialogue: Bring up some more mead, my boy. This cask's nearly tapped!

speaker: Sorex
dialogue: Yes, father. Which cask should we open?

speaker: Sorex
dialogue: Good idea, sis. Maybe you ought to be in charge!

speaker: Corpulus
dialogue: Yes, yes, fine. Just hurry! Mustn't keep the customers thirsty!

speaker: Sorex
dialogue: Actually just a bottle for me today. I'm thinking of giving it to Vivienne.

speaker: Evette
dialogue: Sure, Sorex. Just like you did the last one.

speaker: Sorex
dialogue: The last one was warm up.

speaker: Sorex
dialogue: I'm not interested, Jaree. No matter how many times you ask.

speaker: Jaree
dialogue: You might want to rethink that. You're missing out on some opportunities, working in that bar.

speaker: Aldis
dialogue: Lock the city gate.

speaker: Addvar
dialogue: You're all heart, Vivienne.

speaker: Aldis
dialogue: Roggvir. You helped Ulfric Stormcloak escape this city after he murdered High King Torygg. By opening that gate for Ulfric you betrayed the people of Solitude.

speaker: Sorex
dialogue: He doesn't deserve to speak!

speaker: Roggvir
dialogue: There was no murder! Ulfric challenged Torygg. He beat the High King in fair combat.

speaker: Roggvir
dialogue: Such as our way! Such as the ancient custom of Skyrim, and all Nords!

speaker: Vivienne
dialogue: Cut 'em down!

speaker: Aldis
dialogue: Guard. Prepare the prisoner.

speaker: Roggvir
dialogue: I don't need your help.

speaker: Aldis
dialogue: Very well, Roggvir. Bow your head.

speaker: Roggvir
dialogue: On this day... I go to Sovngarde.

speaker: Stig
dialogue: Come now, dearie, surely we aren't all that bad.

speaker: Karita
dialogue: Just... leave me alone! I've brought your mead, now drink it and shut your filthy mouths.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Was Jarl Ulfric with you?

speaker: Stormcloak Soldier
dialogue: No I haven't seen him since the dragon showed up.

speaker: Stormcloak Soldier 1
dialogue: Where in Oblivion are we supposed to go? Where's the way out?

speaker: Stormcloak Soldier 2
dialogue: Just give me a minute. Let me think.

speaker: Stormcloak Soldier 1
dialogue: You hear anything?

speaker: Stormcloak Soldier 2
dialogue: No, but I know they're out there. No other way then can come. Now shut it or you'll ruin our ambush.

speaker: Stormcloak Soldier 1
dialogue: I don't like it. What are they waiting for?

speaker: Stormcloak Soldier 2
dialogue: Maybe they're so scared of you they ran away.

speaker: Stormcloak Soldier 1
dialogue: Hardly likely.

speaker: Stormcloak Soldier 1
dialogue: It's got to be the Imperials! Find them!

speaker: Stormcloak Soldier 1
dialogue: I bet we have rabbit again. I'm getting sick of rabbit.

speaker: Stormcloak Soldier 2
dialogue: Go tell the commander. I'm sure the boot in your arse will take your mind off your troubles.

speaker: Stormcloak Soldier 1
dialogue: How'd you end up here?

speaker: Stormcloak Soldier 2
dialogue: My cousin disappeared one night. Some say the Thalmor grabbed him. It wasn't long before I found myself under Ulfric's banner.

speaker: Stormcloak Soldier 1
dialogue: So why did you join the Stormcloaks?

speaker: Stormcloak Soldier 2
dialogue: I'm a true Nord. Simple as that.

speaker: Stormcloak Soldier 1
dialogue: We're running out of bread. I hope the supplies get here soon.

speaker: Stormcloak Soldier 2
dialogue: Go tell the commander. I'm sure the boot in your arse will take your mind off your troubles.

speaker: Rolff
dialogue: You come here where you're not wanted, you eat our food, you pollute our city with your stink, and you refuse to help the Stormcloaks.

speaker: Suvaris
dialogue: But we haven't taken a side because it's not our fight.

speaker: Angrenor
dialogue: Hey, maybe the reason these gray-skins don't help in the war is because they're Imperial spies!

speaker: Suvaris
dialogue: Imperial spies? You can't be serious!

speaker: Rolff
dialogue: Maybe we'll pay you a visit tonight, little spy. We got ways of finding out what you really are.

speaker: Rolff
dialogue: You come here where you're not wanted, you eat our food, you pollute our city with your stink, and you refuse to help the Stormcloaks.

speaker: Suvaris
dialogue: But we haven't taken a side because it's not our fight.

speaker: Angrenor
dialogue: Hey, maybe the reason these gray-skins don't help in the war is because they're Imperial spies!

speaker: Suvaris
dialogue: Imperial spies? You can't be serious!

speaker: Rolff
dialogue: Maybe we'll pay you a visit tonight, little spy. We got ways of finding out what you really are.

speaker: Ambarys
dialogue: Don't you ever find it demeaning, working for that Nord family?

speaker: Suvaris
dialogue: Look, Ambarys, I just came here for a drink. I don't need any trouble.

speaker: Ambarys
dialogue: Fine, then. I guess some Dunmer are content to be their pets.

speaker: Suvaris
dialogue: Here's what's going to happen. I'm going to pretend I didn't hear that, and you're going to leave me alone. Deal?

speaker: Ambarys
dialogue: What's new with the {{Sic|Cruel-Seas|Shatter-Shields}} Suvaris? Have they given you one of those helmets with the horns on them yet?

speaker: Suvaris
dialogue: What do you want from me? I work for them, okay? We're not friends. They pay me, and I get the job done. That's it.

speaker: Ambarys
dialogue: Touchy. Maybe some Dunmer lives in you yet.

speaker: Suvaris
dialogue: Either pour another drink or keep moving, Ambarys.

speaker: King Olaf One-Eye
dialogue: Insolent bard. Die!

speaker: Svana
dialogue: They say...well, they say he murdered someone. Something to do with Svidi.

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: Come to think of it, I haven't seen Svidi in a while. Wait...he didn't...

speaker: Svana
dialogue: No, it was Svidi's brother, Wulfur. She's in hiding, now. Somewhere far from here, I'd suspect.

speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: If he wasn't a Black-Briar, I'd march right over to the jail and teach Sibbi some manners...but then I'd suspect that I'd end up like Wulfur.

speaker: Svana
dialogue: She said she'll have it soon. She still has her job at the Meadery for now, so she'll be able to pay us.

speaker: Haelga
dialogue: Why do you insist on defending that woman? All she does with her money is spend it on that Dark Elf garbage.

speaker: Svana
dialogue: Just be patient, aunt. She'll have it, I promise.

speaker: Svana
dialogue: Aunt Haelga, why do you...demean yourself with these people you barely know? They show no real love for you.

speaker: Haelga
dialogue: Its only a bit of fun. You're a lovely young thing, you should try it sometime.

speaker: Svana
dialogue: No! I'm saving myself for someone special. Someone who loves me dearly.

speaker: Haelga
dialogue: You mean Sibbi? You must be joking! All he wants to do is bed you and be done with it. You may as well get it over with and let him.

speaker: Svana
dialogue: You're wrong! Sibbi and I are in love and you're just jealous.

speaker: Svana
dialogue: Madesi, why don't you just take a bed here? There's no need to sleep in Beggar's Row.

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: The cold stone...the dampness...it suits me, Svana.

speaker: Svana
dialogue: Are you sure that's the real reason? It wouldn't have anything to do with others making an Argonian unwelcome, because if it is...

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: You have a kind heart, much too kind for Riften. Don't worry about me, I'll be just fine.

speaker: Svana
dialogue: You're an animal, Tythis...keep away from me.

speaker: Tythis
dialogue: Ah, I see that my reputation as a lover has preceded me. Care to reconsider?

speaker: Svana
dialogue: You're disgusting. Don't you ever think of laying a finger on me, or I'll cut off something you can't live without.

speaker: Svana
dialogue: How do you do it, Valindor? How do you work at Black-Briar Meadery and the Fishery without getting exhausted?

speaker: Valindor
dialogue: Oh, it's not so terrible. I actually find the work quite relaxing.

speaker: Svana
dialogue: Relaxing? They must be working you to the bone! You should rest before you do yourself in.

speaker: Valindor
dialogue: Not to worry, dear Svana. I promise you I can handle it, but your concern is quite flattering.

speaker: Svana
dialogue: Wujeeta, you're worrying me. You look so...well, so sad.

speaker: Wujeeta
dialogue: Don't worry about it, Svana. Its my problem...no need for you to get involved.

speaker: Svana
dialogue: If you're in some sort of trouble, I could talk to Haelga.

speaker: Wujeeta
dialogue: No...no. I'm just tired is all. Thank you.

speaker: Svari
dialogue: They can't hurt uncle Roggvir. Tell them he didn't do it.

speaker: Addvar
dialogue: Svari, you need to go home. Go home and stay there until your mother comes.

speaker: Aldis
dialogue: Lock the city gate.

speaker: Vivienne
dialogue: You should tell her that her uncle is scum that betrayed his High King. Best she know now, Addvar.

speaker: Addvar
dialogue: You're all heart, Vivienne.

speaker: Aldis
dialogue: Roggvir. You helped Ulfric Stormcloak escape this city after he murdered High King Torygg. By opening that gate for Ulfric you betrayed the people of Solitude.

speaker: Sorex
dialogue: He doesn't deserve to speak!

speaker: Roggvir
dialogue: There was no murder! Ulfric challenged Torygg. He beat the High King in fair combat.

speaker: Roggvir
dialogue: Such as our way! Such as the ancient custom of Skyrim, and all Nords!

speaker: Vivienne
dialogue: Cut 'em down!

speaker: Aldis
dialogue: Guard. Prepare the prisoner.

speaker: Roggvir
dialogue: I don't need your help.

speaker: Aldis
dialogue: Very well, Roggvir. Bow your head.

speaker: Roggvir
dialogue: On this day... I go to Sovngarde.

speaker: Addvar
dialogue: Svari, Jala said you stole an apple from her cart yesterday. Is this true?

speaker: Svari
dialogue: Just a little one! I was hungry!

speaker: Greta
dialogue: I'll talk with Jala, dear. I'm sure she'll accept a potato as repayment.

speaker: Addvar
dialogue: I suppose. But Svari, we don't steal. We're better than that. Understand?

speaker: Svari
dialogue: Yes, papa.

speaker: Greta
dialogue: Eat up, Svari.

speaker: Addvar
dialogue: It's all we've got for today. Don't be greedy.

speaker: Greta
dialogue: Maybe we'll have better luck tomorrow.

speaker: Addvar
dialogue: We'll make it, Greta. We always have so far...

speaker: Swanhvir
dialogue: Yes sir, of course.

speaker: Gestur
dialogue: All right. Keep up the good work.

speaker: Varnius
dialogue: Th... thank you, my Jarl. Thank you.

speaker: Sybille
dialogue: Your eminence, my scrying has suggested nothing in the area. Dragon Bridge is under imperial control. This is likely superstitious nonsense.

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: Oh. Yes, of course you are right. Falk, tell Captain Aldis I said to assign a few extra soldiers to Dragon Bridge.

speaker: Varnius
dialogue: Thank you, Jarl Elisif. But about the cave...

speaker: Falk
dialogue: I will have someone take care of the cave as well Varnius, you can rest easy. You're dismissed.

speaker: Sybille
dialogue: Steward, I will need the following reagents for my studies. Please see to them.

speaker: Falk
dialogue: Miss Stentor, these are quite expensive. I trust you know how limited the Hold's funds are at this time?

speaker: Sybille
dialogue: Yes, and I'm also aware of how necessary my divinations and wards have been in the city's defense. My experiments are all I ask for in return.

speaker: Falk
dialogue: Very well. But I suspect her grace will not be pleased.

speaker: Sybille
dialogue: And? I've seen Jarls come and go. This one only became Jarl because her husband died. She'll be replaced in a matter of months.

speaker: Falk
dialogue: Miss Stentor, watch your tongue in the Jarl's court!

speaker: Sybille
dialogue: On threat of what, exactly? This city wouldn't run without me! Now if you'll excuse me, my work awaits.

speaker: Falk
dialogue: It's nearly time to collect taxes on your properties here in the city, Bryling. We'll need to visit each home for an assessment.

speaker: Sybille
dialogue: Oh, well done. Very subtle.

speaker: Bryling
dialogue: I beg your pardon?

speaker: Sybille
dialogue: Oh, I'm sorry, did I imply that you'd be meeting for purposes other than court business? You must forgive me.

speaker: Falk
dialogue: Hold your tongue, wizard, or you're likely to lose it.

speaker: Sybille
dialogue: I should very much like to see you try it, my dear steward.

speaker: Bryling
dialogue: Stop it, both of you. You're acting like children.

speaker: Sylgja
dialogue: I owe it all to my father who started me swinging the pickaxe when I was a barefoot little girl.

speaker: Grogmar
dialogue: Well, it shows. Your skill rivals some of the greatest miners I've known.

speaker: Sylgja
dialogue: Thank you. It's nice to know someone admires me for more than just my appearance.

speaker: Odfel
dialogue: {{sicblock|Grelka|Sylgja}}, do you fancy a walk tomorrow?

speaker: Sylgja
dialogue: Odfel, I've told you time and time again. I'm not interested in a relationship with you.

speaker: Odfel
dialogue: And why not? I'm handsome, strong and smart. What else could you possibly need?

speaker: Sylgja
dialogue: I need someone that cares about me more than they care about themselves. That person isn't you.

speaker: Taarie
dialogue: Sister dear, could you try sewing those sleeves a little tighter? We can't have our customers looking sloppy because of your work.

speaker: Endarie
dialogue: Oh certainly, dear sister. We couldn't afford to have our customers look like the simple pigs they are, now could we?

speaker: Taarie
dialogue: Good. And while you're at it, perhaps you should sew your mouth shut when our fine customers are within earshot, hmm?

speaker: Svari
dialogue: They can't hurt uncle Roggvir. Tell them he didn't do it.

speaker: Addvar
dialogue: Svari, you need to go home. Go home and stay there until your mother comes.

speaker: Aldis
dialogue: Lock the city gate.

speaker: Vivienne
dialogue: You should tell her that her uncle is scum that betrayed his High King. Best she know now, Addvar.

speaker: Addvar
dialogue: You're all heart, Vivienne.

speaker: Aldis
dialogue: Roggvir. You helped Ulfric Stormcloak escape this city after he murdered High King Torygg. By opening that gate for Ulfric you betrayed the people of Solitude.

speaker: Sorex
dialogue: He doesn't deserve to speak!

speaker: Roggvir
dialogue: There was no murder! Ulfric challenged Torygg. He beat the High King in fair combat.

speaker: Roggvir
dialogue: Such as our way! Such as the ancient custom of Skyrim, and all Nords!

speaker: Vivienne
dialogue: Cut 'em down!

speaker: Aldis
dialogue: Guard. Prepare the prisoner.

speaker: Roggvir
dialogue: I don't need your help.

speaker: Aldis
dialogue: Very well, Roggvir. Bow your head.

speaker: Roggvir
dialogue: On this day... I go to Sovngarde.

speaker: Elvali
dialogue: I can't believe we're doing this.

speaker: Savos
dialogue: Can you imagine the looks on their faces when we come back?

speaker: Hafnar
dialogue: You keep talking like you're sure we'll find something useful in here.

speaker: Girduin
dialogue: Given the history of this place, it's more than likely there's still some amount of power here.

speaker: Savos
dialogue: Enchanted weapons, tomes of ancient knowledge, Shalidor's secrets themselves -- who knows what we could find!

speaker: Takes-In-Light
dialogue: And what if... What if there are things guarding this place?

speaker: Atmah
dialogue: Against six College-trained mages? I think we'll be fine.

speaker: Elvali
dialogue: We... we have to go back. We can't leave Girduin...

speaker: Hafnar
dialogue: We barely made it out alive, and you want to go back in?

speaker: Atmah
dialogue: It's too late. There isn't enough of him left to go back in after.

speaker: Takes-In-Light
dialogue: Gods, what have we done?

speaker: Savos
dialogue: We can't go back. Might as well go forward. We can still do this.

speaker: Atmah
dialogue: Savos is right. We can make it if we just stay alert.

speaker: Savos
dialogue: Come on, we can't stop now. We have to keep moving!

speaker: Atmah
dialogue: Where's Elvali? She was right behind me.

speaker: Hafnar
dialogue: Dead. Something grabbed her from behind. Gone before I could do anything.

speaker: Takes-In-Light
dialogue: This is insanity. We never should've come here.

speaker: Atmah
dialogue: You're right. This is all my fault. Should we turn around, head back?

speaker: Hafnar
dialogue: I don't think going back is a good idea.

speaker: Savos
dialogue: Going back would be the end of all of us. We keep pushing forward, and we'll make it. We will!

speaker: Atmah
dialogue: Come on, you can make it. Let's go.

speaker: Talen
dialogue: I don't know Bolli. It's getting dangerous outside the walls.

speaker: Bolli
dialogue: Oh come now, what's a dragon or two compared to a day full of fishing!

speaker: Talen
dialogue: That's not funny, Bolli. People are scared.

speaker: Talen
dialogue: Keerava, we're running low on Black-Briar Mead.

speaker: Talen
dialogue: We could always look for another brand.

speaker: Keerava
dialogue: That isn't an option. Maven sees me serve a competitor's brand here and we may as well dig our own graves.

speaker: Keerava
dialogue: Don't worry, the time will come when we can walk away from here.

speaker: Talen
dialogue: I hope so. I can't stand this city anymore.

speaker: Keerava
dialogue: Damn it, Talen. We still don't have enough this year to get out of Riften.

speaker: Keerava
dialogue: Talen, do you believe what they're saying? Do you really think the dragons have returned?

speaker: Talen
dialogue: I don't know what to believe. If it's true, then dark times may be upon us.

speaker: Keerava
dialogue: What should we do?

speaker: Talen
dialogue: We hold each other close and hope that all of this ends well.

speaker: Keerava
dialogue: No, no, Maramal...We talked about this...Talen...

speaker: Maramal
dialogue: Keerava, certainly we can come to some sort of understanding? These people must be made aware of the chaos they've sown.

speaker: Talen
dialogue: Enough, Maramal. We've all heard of the dragons and their return. There's no need to use them as an excuse to harrass our customers.

speaker: Maramal
dialogue: Very well, Talen. I'll remove myself from this den of iniquity.

speaker: Talen
dialogue: We're not kicking you out, just keep the sermons at the temple and let us all sin in peace.

speaker: Talen
dialogue: Sorry Hemming, I've no interest in becoming your valet.

speaker: Hemming
dialogue: What's the matter, I thought you people were used to indentured servitude.

speaker: Talen
dialogue: Xhuth! Black-Briar or not, say that again and so help me you're going to need more than your mother to protect you from me.

speaker: Talen
dialogue: I think you've had plenty, Vulwulf. Maybe you should head on home.

speaker: Vulwulf
dialogue: You stupid lizard! I said give me some more drink, or I'll have your head on a pike!

speaker: Talen
dialogue: Suit yourself.

speaker: Talib
dialogue: I'm fine, father. Work is fine.

speaker: Gestur
dialogue: Good, good. It's honest work, son. No shame in that.

speaker: Talib
dialogue: Of course not. I never thought otherwise.

speaker: Gestur
dialogue: Right. Well, you let me know if you need anything.

speaker: Teeba-Ei
dialogue: Teeba-Ei is cold, but Teeba-Ei works hard as always.

speaker: Gestur
dialogue: Yes, well... That's all we ask of you. Carry on.

speaker: Teeba-Ei
dialogue: Yes sir.

speaker: Orthorn
dialogue: I uhh... wait, what?

speaker: The Caller
dialogue: He gets the books, I get you. It's very simple.

speaker: Orthorn
dialogue: But why?

speaker: The Caller
dialogue: This little adventure of yours has cost me a number of test subjects. I need more, and you'll do nicely.

speaker: Orthorn
dialogue: You wouldn't do that, would you? You wouldn't leave me here with her!

speaker: The Caller
dialogue: I'm waiting.

speaker: Thonar
dialogue: I am busy keeping this family in coin and your pretty little head adorned with jewels, so I'll thank you not to question where I go at night, wife.

speaker: Betrid
dialogue: Well maybe if you would finally convince Thongvor to put you in charge of the family, I wouldn't need to question you anymore.

speaker: Thonar
dialogue: I'll take control of the family on my own time, Betrid. Until then, my brother remains in charge and you'll keep your mouth shut.

speaker: Betrid
dialogue: Oh dear, whatever is a girl to do with such fearful brutes about her?

speaker: Betrid
dialogue: Did I hear correctly, Thonar? Is your brother really asking you to settle another dispute between Mulush and Nepos?

speaker: Thonar
dialogue: Someone has to keep the silver production running, Betrid, and that means keeping Mulush and Nepos in line once in a while.

speaker: Betrid
dialogue: Humph. Who's running the Silver-Bloods? You or your brother? You need to tell Thongvor that he should settle this himself or step down.

speaker: Thonar
dialogue: The only thing I need to do, dear wife, is make sure profits are up, no matter what. If Thongvor won't do the dirty work, I will.

speaker: Betrid
dialogue: You'll never be in charge of this family with that attitude, loving husband.

speaker: Thonar
dialogue: Ah, Nana Ildene, whatever would my family do without you?

speaker: Ildene
dialogue: Ah, Thonar, don't you worry. Nana Ildene isn't going anywhere.

speaker: Thonar
dialogue: Um, good. We reward loyalty, you know.

speaker: Ildene
dialogue: Oh, I know, Thonar. Only a mad woman would ever betray the Silver-Blood family.

speaker: Thonar
dialogue: Uh, yes. Quite.

speaker: Thonar
dialogue: You're a very pretty young woman, Rhiada.

speaker: Rhiada
dialogue: Why, thank you Thonar. I'm flattered.

speaker: Thonar
dialogue: You're married, yes? To that young metal worker?

speaker: Rhiada
dialogue: Eltrys, yes, just last season we were wed.

speaker: Thonar
dialogue: He's a lucky man to have such a beautiful young wife.

speaker: Rhiada
dialogue: Thank you, Thonar. That's generous of you to say.

speaker: Thongvor
dialogue: Jarl can refuse to see me all he likes. He can't ignore us forever.

speaker: Thongvor
dialogue: You there. You another Imperial puppet? Answer me.

speaker: Thongvor
dialogue: How's the forge today?

speaker: Moth
dialogue: It's fine. Much better than the rickety tools I had in the Legion.

speaker: Thongvor
dialogue: Remember that old rusty sword I had? Damn thing must have had over a hundred chips in it.

speaker: Moth
dialogue: Well, if you had learned to swing it correctly. A sword is an extension of the arm, not a meat cleaver.

speaker: Thongvor
dialogue: I was about to say how impressed I was that you always managed to put it back together.

speaker: Moth
dialogue: Flattery doesn't suit you, Thongvor.

speaker: Moth
dialogue: Hello, my friend. Come to visit the forge?

speaker: Thongvor
dialogue: I grow tired of counting coin all day. Put steel in my hand, not gold.

speaker: Moth
dialogue: Your family's success burdens you, does it?

speaker: Thongvor
dialogue: Sometimes I miss the Legion, back when the Empire stood up for Skyrim.

speaker: Moth
dialogue: No politics, Thongvor. I told you before.

speaker: Thongvor
dialogue: I want soldiers sent to deal with these dragons. Every able-bodied man and woman who can carry a bow.

speaker: Reburrus
dialogue: We can't do that. Every soldier we send to hunt dragons is one more man that can't defend the Reach.

speaker: Thongvor
dialogue: Killing dragons isn't defending the Reach?

speaker: Reburrus
dialogue: Our men know how to kill Forsworn and Legionnaires, not dragons.

speaker: Thongvor
dialogue: I want word on our campaign against the Imperials.

speaker: Reburrus
dialogue: I have a few very detailed missives from border patrols, beginning with Fifth Irregulars' reports on the movements of....

speaker: Yngvar
dialogue: Oh, Talos's breath, Reburrus. Skip ahead to the good part.

speaker: Reburrus
dialogue: Oh, right. Oh, well, things are going well enough. At least, as well as we can hope.

speaker: Thongvor
dialogue: What does that mean Reburrus? Are we winning or aren't we?

speaker: Reburrus
dialogue: I, uh, I can't tell Thongvor. It's anyone's guess.

speaker: Thongvor
dialogue: I see. Well, let's continue this discussion later then.

speaker: Thongvor
dialogue: How goes the trade in and out of the city?

speaker: Reburrus
dialogue: Very well, Thongvor. With the Stormcloaks here to help, the Silver-Blood family control nearly every route in and out of the city.

speaker: Yngvar
dialogue: Except the ones attacked by Forsworn.

speaker: Reburrus
dialogue: Well yes, of course you had to go and mention that.

speaker: Thongvor
dialogue: The Forsworn aren't our real concern, defeating the Imperials and making sure we keep control of this city is.

speaker: Reburrus
dialogue: Yes, Thongvor.

speaker: Thongvor
dialogue: Reburrus, I need you to draft a letter to Ulfric requesting more men.

speaker: Yngvar
dialogue: Ha! About time we got some more muscle in this city.

speaker: Reburrus
dialogue: Thongvor, do you really think that's wise? I mean, King Ulfric is such a busy man, and there are so many areas of Skyrim to protect.

speaker: Thongvor
dialogue: Whose side are you on, Reburrus? I'm not worried about Skyrim, I'm worried about the Reach. Specifically, the part of the Reach we're standing on.

speaker: Reburrus
dialogue: Yes, Thongvor. I'll draft the letter immediately.

speaker: Reburrus
dialogue: Thongvor, I have the latest reports from Cidhna Mine and the smelter. We should go over them immediately.

speaker: Thongvor
dialogue: Reburrus, there is a war being fought across all of Skyrim, and you bother me with the usual mundane reports about silver?

speaker: Reburrus
dialogue: Look at these figures, Thongvor! Ore yield is down by half, and the amount of silver bars being smelted is slipping even more than that.

speaker: Thongvor
dialogue: Oh, very well. I'll send my brother. He'll straighten this out.

speaker: Reburrus
dialogue: Very good, Thongvor. It relieves me to hear you say that.

speaker: Kraldar
dialogue: So, what's the latest exciting news about goings-on in Winterhold?

speaker: Thonjolf
dialogue: There is no news, I'm afraid.

speaker: Kraldar
dialogue: None? Nothing at all? Nothing from the College, even?

speaker: Thonjolf
dialogue: I shall inform you the moment something noteworthy happens.

speaker: Kraldar
dialogue: Yes, that will be fine. Thank you.

speaker: Thonjolf
dialogue: Will you be needing anything special today?

speaker: Kraldar
dialogue: Why don't you see if Arch-Mage Aren is interested in joining me for a meal?

speaker: Thonjolf
dialogue: Again? Are you sure? He still hasn't answered your last several requests.

speaker: Kraldar
dialogue: Well, he's been very busy. Perhaps today he'll have some free time.

speaker: Thonjolf
dialogue: As you wish.

speaker: Thonjolf
dialogue: Malur, I need you to take care of something.

speaker: Thonjolf
dialogue: I haven't even said what it is.

speaker: Malur
dialogue: Doesn't really matter. Thanks, but no.

speaker: Thonnir
dialogue: How are we supposed to feel safe in our own homes?

speaker: Jorgen
dialogue: We have no need for wizards in our midst!

speaker: Thonnir
dialogue: Morthal has enough problems as it is!

speaker: Jorgen
dialogue: Bah, its no use. Let's get back to it then.

speaker: Jorgen
dialogue: And it looks creepy, too.

speaker: Thorek
dialogue: The orcs have breached the inner sanctum, Brother Veren.

speaker: Veren Duleri
dialogue: We must hold. We can't allow the Skull to fall into their hands.

speaker: Thorek
dialogue: But... no more than a handful of us remain, brother.

speaker: Veren Duleri
dialogue: Then we have no choice. The Miasma must be released.

speaker: Thorek
dialogue: The Miasma? But, brother...

speaker: Veren Duleri
dialogue: We have no alternative. It's the will of Vaermina.

speaker: Veren Duleri
dialogue: Brother Thorek, we must remain here and guard this Skull with our lives if necessary.

speaker: Thorek
dialogue: Agreed. To the death.

speaker: Veren Duleri
dialogue: Then let it be done. Farewell, my brothers!

speaker: Titus Mede II
dialogue: But of course. You and I have a date with destiny. But so it is with assassins and emperors, hmm?

speaker: Noblewoman
dialogue: But aren't you the least bit nervous? After everything that's happened?

speaker: Emperor Titus Mede II
dialogue: You mean the wedding? My cousin's apparent murder? An unfortunate misunderstanding, no more. Cold mead, hot tempers... these things happen.

speaker: Nobleman
dialogue: Quite. Yet that recent business with the young officer. Maro, was it? How dreadful. The son of your commander, plotting your assassination.

speaker: Emperor Titus Mede II
dialogue: Aha! Here we are. Honored guests, I present to you - the Gourmet! Ah, the Potage le Magnifique. So delicious. My friends, as emperor, I of course reserve the right of first taste.

speaker: Emperor Titus Mede II
dialogue: Oh... Oh how marvelous. Just delicious. It is everything I had hoped it would be. Please, everyone. Enjoy.

speaker: Noblewoman
dialogue: But aren't you the least bit nervous? After everything that's happened?

speaker: Emperor Titus Mede II
dialogue: You mean the wedding? My cousin's apparent murder? An unfortunate misunderstanding, no more. Cold mead, hot tempers... these things happen.

speaker: Nobleman
dialogue: Quite. Yet that recent business with the young officer. Maro, was it? How dreadful. The son of your commander, plotting your assassination.

speaker: Emperor Titus Mede II

speaker: Emperor Titus Mede II
dialogue: Oh... Oh how marvelous. Just delicious. It is everything I had hoped it would be. It.... I.... I think something's... wrong... I... Hunh...

speaker: Penitus Oculatus Agent
dialogue: By the gods! The Gourmet and the chef have poisoned the Emperor! Get them!

speaker: Gianna
dialogue: What? No! No, you don't understand! There's been some kind of mistake! I... Aggghhh!

speaker: Tolfdir
dialogue: Welcome, welcome! We were just beginning. Please, stay and listen. So, as I was saying, the first thing to understand is that magic is, by its very nature, volatile and dangerous. Unless you can control it, it can and will destroy you.

speaker: Brelyna
dialogue: Sir, I think we all understand that fairly well. We wouldn't be here if we couldn't control magic!

speaker: Tolfdir
dialogue: Of course, my dear. Of course. You all certainly possess some inherent natural ability. That much is not being questioned. What I'm talking about is true control, mastery of magic. It takes years, if not decades, of practice and study.

speaker: Tolfdir
dialogue: Please, please! This is exactly what I'm talking about. Eagerness must be tempered with caution, or else disaster is inevitable.

speaker: Onmund
dialogue: But we've only just arrived here -- you've no idea what any of us are capable of. Why not give us a chance to show you what we can do?

speaker: Onmund
dialogue: We're all pretty new to this, right? Let's just give it a chance. What's the worst that could happen?

speaker: Tolfdir
dialogue: All right, let's settle down. I suppose we can try something practical... In continuing with our theme of safety, we'll start with Wards. Wards are protective spells that block magic. I'll teach you all a ward, and we'll see if you can successfully use it to block spells, all right?

speaker: Brelyna
dialogue: See? He agrees with us too! Why don't you actually show us something?

speaker: Tolfdir
dialogue: All right, let's settle down. I suppose we can try something practical... In continuing with our theme of safety, we'll start with Wards. Wards are protective spells that block magic. I'll teach you all a ward, and we'll see if you can successfully use it to block spells, all right?

speaker: Tolfdir
dialogue: All right, let's settle down. I suppose we can try something practical... In continuing with our theme of safety, we'll start with Wards. Wards are protective spells that block magic. I'll teach you all a ward, and we'll see if you can successfully use it to block spells, all right?

speaker: Tolfdir
dialogue: Now, let's see. What shall we have the rest of you do? Brelyna, my dear, why don't you search for warding magics. Anything designed to keep people out. Don't interact with them, just identify them. All right, everyone. Let's be careful, but have fun!

speaker: Tolfdir
dialogue: Well, this is highly unusual. And very interesting.

speaker: Ancano
dialogue: I'm afraid I must intrude. I need to speak to your associate immediately.

speaker: Tolfdir
dialogue: This is most inappropriate! We are involved in serious research here!

speaker: Ancano
dialogue: [condescending] Yes, I've no doubt of its gravity. This, however, is a matter that cannot wait.

speaker: Tolfdir
dialogue: Well, I'm quite sure I've never been interrupted like this before...the audacity!...[to player] I suppose we'll have to continue this at some later time, when we can avoid interruptions.

speaker: Ancano
dialogue: You've come for me, have you? You think I don't know what you're up to? You think I can't destroy you? The power to unmake the world at my fingertips, and you think you can do anything about it?

speaker: Tolfdir
dialogue: Spells have no effect!

speaker: Ancano
dialogue: I am beyond your pathetic attempts at magic. You cannot touch me.

speaker: Tolfdir
dialogue: The staff! Use it on the Eye!

speaker: Ancano
dialogue: Enough! Still you persist? Very well. Come then. See what I can do now.

speaker: Torbjorn
dialogue: The eyes of the law are everywhere these days. The guards are looking for a killer, but who knows what else they might turn up? Good day.

speaker: Torbjorn
dialogue: You've done more than enough already. You've been a good friend in a time of need, and we won't forget that. I'm sorry I lost myself for a moment there. I just need some time to get over the loss.

speaker: Tormir
dialogue: Sondas, does Hrefna ever mention Meieran to you?

speaker: Sondas
dialogue: She hardly mentions anything else.

speaker: Tormir
dialogue: I'm just worried about what he's teaching her.

speaker: Sondas
dialogue: I wouldn't worry about that. He's a good elf. I trust him.

speaker: Tormir
dialogue: You're probably right.

speaker: Hrefna
dialogue: And Meieran thinks we should go there!

speaker: Tormir
dialogue: I don't want to hear another word about what you're learning from the elf! It's high time you learned to be a Nord, too!

speaker: Hrefna
dialogue: But mama...

speaker: Tormir
dialogue: He's a half-decent farmer. Ask him to teach you to farm!

speaker: Tormir
dialogue: Thanks for looking after Hrefna.

speaker: Sondas
dialogue: Oh, it's no trouble. She's a smart little girl. Might talk your ear off, but she's fun.

speaker: Tormir
dialogue: Well, I know she thinks the world of you.

speaker: Sondas
dialogue: Well, I'll try to be a good influence, then.

speaker: Haming
dialogue: Who are they, daddy? Where are they going?

speaker: Torolf
dialogue: You need to go inside, little cub.

speaker: Haming
dialogue: Why? I want to watch the soldiers.

speaker: Torolf
dialogue: Inside the house. Now.

speaker: Haming
dialogue: Yes, papa.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: See the inn on the other side? Jump through the roof and keep going! Go! We'll follow when we can!

speaker: Alduin
dialogue: Yol... Toor... Shul!

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Still alive, prisoner? Keep close to me if you want to stay that way. Gunnar, take care of the {{hide|boy|Referring to Haming.}}. I have to find General Tullius and join their defense.

speaker: Gunnar
dialogue: Gods guide you, Hadvar.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Stay close to the wall!

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: I'm still not sure I understand what you're asking.

speaker: Torsten
dialogue: A navy, my lord. We could stop the influx of Imperial troops to Solitude, and choke their northern lines.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: But most of their supply routes come south, from Cyrodiil.

speaker: Torsten
dialogue: But imagine—fleets of ships sailing from Windhelm, all bearing the Stormcloak flag! It would be glorious!

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: And I suppose the Cruel-Seas would be just the clan to provide ships and men?

speaker: Torsten
dialogue: You need but ask.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: I'll think on this, but I make no promises.

speaker: Torsten
dialogue: I can ask no more. Thank you, my lord!

speaker: Tulvur
dialogue: Sir, I'm going to need some better equipment if you want me plowing the frost.

speaker: Torsten
dialogue: Like what?

speaker: Tulvur
dialogue: Well, some tools that aren't rusted through would be a start.

speaker: Torsten
dialogue: I'll provide you wood and timber to make whatever riggings you'll need.

speaker: Tulvur
dialogue: I'm not building a ship, sir. I'm trying to make things grow.

speaker: Torsten
dialogue: Tulvur! I've just completed inspection of the farmhouse.

speaker: Torsten
dialogue: It's filthy in there! Dirt everywhere, and it looks like the dogs have the run of the place.

speaker: Tulvur
dialogue: Well, sir, it's a farmhouse. It's not going to be as clean as your house in the city.

speaker: Torsten
dialogue: I just know that our sailors are able to keep their ship quarters clean, and I expect the same of you.

speaker: Tulvur
dialogue: I'll do my best, sir.

speaker: Torsten
dialogue: How's business today?

speaker: Hillevi
dialogue: Well enough, I suppose. Nilsine bought up most of the tomatoes, and was asking if we could get more.

speaker: Torsten
dialogue: We've got another dozen ripening on the vine. They should be ready in a few days.

speaker: Hillevi
dialogue: I'll be sure to tell her.

speaker: Torturer
dialogue: You fellows happened along just in time. These boys seemed a bit upset at how I've been entertaining their comrades.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Don't you even know what's going on? A dragon is attacking Helgen!

speaker: Torturer
dialogue: A dragon? Please. Don't make up nonsense. Although, come to think of it, I did hear some odd noises coming from over there.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Come with us. We need to get out of here.

speaker: Torturer
dialogue: You have no authority over me, boy.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Didn't you hear me? I said the keep is under attack!

speaker: Torturer
dialogue: There's no way out that way, you know...

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Wait a second. Looks like there's something in this cage.

speaker: Torturer
dialogue: Don't bother with that. Lost the key ages ago. Poor fellow screamed for weeks.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: See if {{Hide|you|Referring to the Last Dragonborn.}} can get it open with some picks. We'll need everything we can get.

speaker: Torturer
dialogue: Sure, take all my things. Please.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Grab what you can and let's go.

speaker: Torturer
dialogue: You fellows happened along just in time. These boys seemed a bit upset at how I've been entertaining their comrades.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Don't you even know what's going on? A dragon is attacking Helgen!

speaker: Torturer
dialogue: A dragon? Please. Don't make up nonsense. Although, come to think of it, I did hear some odd noises coming from over there.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Come with us. We need to get out of here.

speaker: Torturer
dialogue: You have no authority over me, boy.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Didn't you hear me? I said the keep is under attack!

speaker: Torturer
dialogue: There's no way out that way, you know...

speaker: Torvar
dialogue: Yes. You're quite fond of saying that. You know I like hammers and axes.

speaker: Athis
dialogue: Aren't they slow? I can get in and out before you can have one swing.

speaker: Torvar
dialogue: Let's test that out sometime.

speaker: Torvar
dialogue: I've been hunting on my own for years.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: Fighting people is different. Smarter.

speaker: Torvar
dialogue: Some of 'em, anyway.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: Time to train.

speaker: Torvar
dialogue: Enough with the training, I want to go fight something.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: No fighting, not just yet. Not 'till Skjor says so. You train now.

speaker: Torvar
dialogue: Easy enough for you to say. You get to fight.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: But before I fought, I had to train.

speaker: Torvar
dialogue: One day, when you and I are on the Circle, we can change the way things are run around here.

speaker: Athis
dialogue: I don't think that's how the Circle works.

speaker: Torvar
dialogue: They're lording it over us all the time, though.

speaker: Athis
dialogue: Young warriors are smart to listen to older ones. They've lived.

speaker: Torvar
dialogue: Master, I...

speaker: Torvar
dialogue: Forgive me. You're just the one in charge, and it's what I'm used to.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: No one is in charge here. Each Shield-Brother is his own man, each Shield-Sister her own woman.

speaker: Torvar
dialogue: Well why do I have to listen to Skjor, then?

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: Skjor has been a warrior for a long time. You would be wise to listen to him. Any warrior that gets to be old is either fearsome or a coward. I'll let you find out which Skjor is.

speaker: Torvar
dialogue: Do you think I could be a member of the Circle? Some day? If I work hard?

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: Don't worry about such things. Just focus on your own honor. Bring glory to the Companions, and that glory will return upon you.

speaker: Torvar
dialogue: I just want to make sure I'm moving up.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: This isn't the military, son. There are no ranks.

speaker: Torvar
dialogue: But aren't the Circle in charge? And don't you lead them?

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: I guide the Companions. The Circle advises me. But we are all free warriors. Only our honor binds us together.

speaker: Tova
dialogue: I understand you purchase used goods, as well as sell them?

speaker: Aval
dialogue: Yes, that's right. Whether or not I'm interested depends on what you've got, of course.

speaker: Tova
dialogue: I have some things that belonged to my daughter, Friga. She... she won't be needing them any more.

speaker: Aval
dialogue: Oh, I see. Yes, yes of course I'll take a look. Just bring them by whenever it's convenient for you.

speaker: Tsavani
dialogue: Who comes, Malborn? You know I don't like strange smells in my kitchen.

speaker: Malborn
dialogue: A guest, feeling ill. Leave the poor wretch be.

speaker: Tsavani
dialogue: A guest? In the kitchens? You know this is against the rules...

speaker: Malborn
dialogue: Rules, is it, Tsavani? I didn't realize that eating Moon Sugar was permitted. Perhaps I should ask the Ambassador...

speaker: Tsavani
dialogue: Tss! Get out of here; I saw nothing.

speaker: Tulvur
dialogue: Sir, I'm going to need some better equipment if you want me plowing the frost.

speaker: Torsten
dialogue: Like what?

speaker: Tulvur
dialogue: Well, some tools that aren't rusted through would be a start.

speaker: Torsten
dialogue: I'll provide you wood and timber to make whatever riggings you'll need.

speaker: Tulvur
dialogue: I'm not building a ship, sir. I'm trying to make things grow.

speaker: Torsten
dialogue: Tulvur! I've just completed inspection of the farmhouse.

speaker: Torsten
dialogue: It's filthy in there! Dirt everywhere, and it looks like the dogs have the run of the place.

speaker: Tulvur
dialogue: Well, sir, it's a farmhouse. It's not going to be as clean as your house in the city.

speaker: Torsten
dialogue: I just know that our sailors are able to keep their ship quarters clean, and I expect the same of you.

speaker: Tulvur
dialogue: I'll do my best, sir.

speaker: Hillevi
dialogue: How have things been with you?

speaker: Tulvur
dialogue: I got another harangue from Torsten yesterday.

speaker: Hillevi
dialogue: Don't worry about him. I know you work hard, and I'm the one who gets you your money.

speaker: Tulvur
dialogue: Thank you, miss, I appreciate that.

speaker: Hillevi
dialogue: And what about the dogs? How are those precious little angels?

speaker: Tullvur
dialogue: Healthy and strong. Ysgramor's coat's gotten so thick, he looks fat!

speaker: Hillevi
dialogue: Oh, that's just adorable.

speaker: Tuthul
dialogue: I feel like any moment, a draugr is going to come and chop my head off.

speaker: Perth
dialogue: Steel your nerves. The draugr are gone. Focus on your mining.

speaker: Perth
dialogue: Feels good to be mining again.

speaker: Tuthul
dialogue: How can you say that? This mine was filled with draugr not too long ago.

speaker: Tuthul
dialogue: Those draugr are going to come up and kill us all.

speaker: Perth
dialogue: They haven't moved out of the caves. I think we're safe.

speaker: Tuthul
dialogue: 'We're safe' he says. You'll eat those words when a draugr is tearing into your face.

speaker: Tuthul
dialogue: I don't think it's safe mining a cave on top of that crypt.

speaker: Perth
dialogue: There's a war on. We need every scrap of ore we can get, so we're going to keep digging. Understand?

speaker: Tuthul
dialogue: Fine, but don't say I didn't warn you.

speaker: Tuthul
dialogue: Those draugr are going to be back. I can feel it.

speaker: Perth
dialogue: Don't be such a coward. We haven't seen any draugr since the mine was cleared. Be grateful.

speaker: Tythis
dialogue: Hey, Svana...I hear you like Dark Elves. Perhaps I can show you what a real Dark Elf can do to you.

speaker: Svana
dialogue: You're an animal, Tythis...keep away from me.

speaker: Tythis
dialogue: Ah, I see that my reputation as a lover has preceded me. Care to reconsider?

speaker: Svana
dialogue: You're disgusting. Don't you ever think of laying a finger on me, or I'll cut off something you can't live without.

speaker: Tythis
dialogue: Niluva, you promised you'd pay me back yesterday. So what's the story?

speaker: Niluva
dialogue: Just give me a few more days and I promise I'll come up with it.

speaker: Tythis
dialogue: If you'd stop wasting your coin on that Skooma, you'd have enough gold to live on!

speaker: Niluva
dialogue: Sorry, Tythis. I'll get it to you somehow.

speaker: Tythis
dialogue: Maybe its time to quit, then.

speaker: Ungrien
dialogue: And do what? Losing a job from the Black-Briar family would make me a made man! No one would ever take me on anywhere else.

speaker: Tythis
dialogue: Don't let it get you down. Indaryn will eventually tire of picking on you and move on to someone else.

speaker: Tythis
dialogue: Marise, I've come to warn you that the Thieves Guild has been harassing shopkeepers again.

speaker: Marise
dialogue: I've heard. Bolli and Keerava were speaking of it just a little while ago.

speaker: Tythis
dialogue: I hope that doesn't mean things are going to get worse around here.

speaker: Tythis
dialogue: Madesi, have you heard the Imperials might be headed this way? What would we do?

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: They aren't invading, milord... it's simply a response to Ulfric and his Stormcloaks. I assure you everything will be fine.

speaker: Tythis
dialogue: But I've heard from the Snow-Shods that they intend to burn this place to the ground!

speaker: Madesi
dialogue: Tythis, please. The Snow-Shods are good people, but tend to exaggerate. Try and stay calm for your own sake.

context: What are you doing with all these clothes?
speaker: Tythis
dialogue: Brand-Shei... have you managed to find those boots for me?

context: What are you doing with all these clothes?
speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: What's with all the boots and shoes you keep buying? You must have bought twenty pairs in the last two years.

context: What are you doing with all these clothes?
speaker: Tythis
dialogue: Always be prepared. You never know if you might get a split in one, or lose one, then where would you be? No sir, that's not happening to me.

context: What are you doing with all these clothes?
speaker: Brand-Shei
dialogue: Um... okay. Well, the boots aren't here yet. Hopefully on the next Khajiit caravan.

speaker: Tythis
dialogue: Wujeeta, you can't keep showing up here late. Bolli's just going to get someone to replace you.

speaker: Wujeeta
dialogue: No, no, no. I need this job! This is the last place in town to have work.

speaker: Tythis
dialogue: There's always the Thieves Guild.

speaker: Wujeeta
dialogue: What was that?

speaker: Tythis
dialogue: Nothing, nothing. Just straighten yourself out before you find yourself headed back to Black Marsh.

speaker: Tythis
dialogue: Of course. I rented a bed there. Where else would I sleep?

speaker: Haelga
dialogue: I have plenty of room in my bed.

speaker: Tythis
dialogue: Good, that must be very comfortable for you. I think mine's a bit too small. Perhaps we could trade?

speaker: Tythis
dialogue: Grelka, can you repair boots?

speaker: Grelka
dialogue: Leather? If they're armored, you should talk to Balimund over at The Scorched Hammer.

speaker: Tythis
dialogue: Horker skin, actually.

speaker: Grelka
dialogue: Why in goodness name would you have... oh never mind, just bring them by my house later and I'll see what I can do.

speaker: Ugor
dialogue: Halt! {{Hide|You|Referring to the Dragonborn}} have no business here, outsider. Leave at once.

speaker: Ugor
dialogue: We need nothing from outsiders! Yamarz will provide for us.

speaker: Atub
dialogue: We cannot carry on this way! You know we are doomed if we do not do something!

speaker: Ugor
dialogue: Yamarz charged me with keeping outsiders away from Largashbur. You would have me disobey him?

speaker: Atub
dialogue: You were charged with keeping us inside the walls. Have faith, Ugor. I only wish the best for our tribe.

speaker: Ugor
dialogue: Fine, it's your neck.

speaker: Ulfric Stormcloak
dialogue: I fight for the men I've held in my arms, dying on foreign soil! I fight for their wives and children, whose names I heard whispered in their last breath. I fight for we few who did come home, only to find our country full of strangers wearing familiar faces. I fight for my people impoverished to pay the debts of an Empire too weak to rule them, yet brands them criminals for wanting to rule themselves! I fight so that all the fighting I've already done hasn't been for nothing! I fight... because I must.

speaker: General Tullius
dialogue: Ulfric Stormcloak. Some here in Helgen call you a hero. But a hero doesn't use a power like the Voice to murder his king and usurp his throne. You started this war, plunged Skyrim into chaos, and now the Empire is going to put you down, and restore the peace.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Hey, you. You're finally awake. You were trying to cross the border, right? Walked right into that Imperial ambush, same as us, and that thief over there.

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: Damn you Stormcloaks. Skyrim was fine until you came along. Empire was nice and lazy. If they hadn't been looking for you, I could've stolen that horse and been halfway to Hammerfell. You there... You and me, we shouldn't be here. It's these Stormcloaks the Empire wants.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: We're all brothers and sisters in binds now, thief.

speaker: Imperial Soldier
dialogue: Shut up back there!

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: And what's wrong with him, huh?

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Watch your tongue. You're speaking to Ulfric Stormcloak, the true High King.

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: Ulfric? The Jarl of Windhelm? You're the leader of the rebellion. But if they've captured you... Oh gods, where are they taking us?

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: I don't know where we're going, but Sovngarde awaits.

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: No, this can't be happening. This isn't happening.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Hey, what village are you from, horse thief?

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: Why do you care?

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: A Nord's last thoughts should be of home.

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: Rorikstead. I'm... I'm from Rorikstead.

speaker: Imperial
dialogue: General Tullius, sir! The headsman is waiting!

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Good. Let's get this over with.

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: Shor, Mara, Dibella, Kynareth, Akatosh. Divines, please help me.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Look at him, General Tullius, the Military Governor. And it looks like the Thalmor are with him. Damn elves. I bet they had something to do with this. This is Helgen. I used to be sweet on a girl from here. Wonder if Vilod is still making that mead with juniper berries mixed in. Funny, when I was a boy, Imperial walls and towers used to make me feel so safe.

speaker: Haming
dialogue: Who are they, daddy? Where are they going?

speaker: Torolf
dialogue: You need to go inside, little cub.

speaker: Haming
dialogue: Why? I want to watch the soldiers.

speaker: Torolf
dialogue: Inside the house. Now.

speaker: Haming
dialogue: Yes, papa.

speaker: Captain
dialogue: Get these prisoners out of the carts. Move it!

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: Why are we stopping?

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Why do you think? End of the line. Let's go. Shouldn't keep the gods waiting for us.

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: No! Wait! We're not rebels!

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Face your death with some courage, thief.

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: You've got to tell them! We weren't with you! This is a mistake!

speaker: Imperial Captain
dialogue: Step towards the block when we call your name. One at a time.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Empire loves their damn lists.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Ulfric Stormcloak. Jarl of Windhelm.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: It has been an honor, Jarl Ulfric!

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Ralof of Riverwood. Lokir of Rorikstead.

speaker: Lokir
dialogue: You're not going to kill me!

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Wait. You there. Step forward. Who are you?

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: Captain. What should we do? He/She's not on the list.

speaker: Captain
dialogue: Forget the list. He/She goes to the block.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: By your orders, Captain. Follow the Captain, prisoner.

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Ulfric Stormcloak. Some here in Helgen call you a hero. But a hero doesn't use a power like The Voice to murder his king and usurp his throne.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: [muffled grunts]

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: You started this war, plunged Skyrim into chaos, and now the Empire is going to put you down, and restore the peace.

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Jarl Ulfric! What is that thing? Could the legends be true?

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Legends don't burn down villages. We need to move. Now!

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Up through the tower, let's go!

speaker: Stormcloak
dialogue: They're hurt, but they'll live. Another second out there with the dragon, and they'd both be dead...

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: Let's go! With me, up the tower!

speaker: Stormcloak
dialogue: We just need to move some of these rocks to clear the way!

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Balgruuf won't give us a straight answer.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: He's a true Nord. He'll come around.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Don't be so sure of that. We've intercepted couriers from Solitude. The Empire's putting a great deal of pressure on Whiterun.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: And what would you have me do?

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: If he's not with us, he's against us.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: He knows that. They all know that.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: How long are you going to wait?

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: You think I need to send Balgruuf a stronger message.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: If by message you mean shoving a sword through his gullet.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Taking his city and leaving him in disgrace would make a more powerful statement, don't you think?

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: So we're ready to start this war in earnest then?

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: I still say you should take them all out like you did Deadking Torygg.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Torygg was merely a message to the other Jarls. Whoever we replace them with will need the support of our armies.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: We're ready when you are.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Things hinge on Whiterun. If we can take the city without bloodshed all the better. But if not...

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: The people are behind you.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Many I fear still need convincing.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Then let them die with their false kings.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: We've been soldiers a long time. We know the price of freedom. The people are still weighing things in their hearts.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: What's left of Skyrim to wager?

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: They have families to think of.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: How many of their sons and daughters follow your banner? We are their families.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Well put, friend. Tell me, Galmar, why do you fight for me?

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: I'd follow you into the depths of Oblivion, you know that.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Yes, but why do you fight? If not for me, what then?

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: I'll die before elves dictate the fates of men. Are we not one in this?

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Your words give voice to what we all feel, Ulfric. And that's why you will be High King. But the day words are enough, will be the day when soldiers like us are no longer needed.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: I would gladly retire from the world were such a day to dawn.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Aye. But in the meantime, we have a war to plan.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Tell me again why we're wasting time and dwindling resources chasing a legend. We don't even know it exists!

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: The Jarls are upset. They don't all support you.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Damn the Jarls.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: They demand the Moot.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: And damn the Moot! We should risk letting those milkdrinkers put Torygg's woman on the throne? She'll hand Skyrim over to the elves on a silver plate.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: All the more reason then. The crown would legitimize your claim.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: A crown doesn't make a king.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: No, but this one...

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: If it even exists.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: It exists. And it'll be the symbol of the righteousness of our cause. Think about it. The Jagged Crown! It heralds back to a time before Jarls and Moots. Back to the time when a king was a king because his enemies fell before him, and his people rose because they loved him. Skyrim needs that king. You will be that king, Ulfric. You must be.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: You're certain you've found it?

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: When have I ever been false with you?

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Fine. I'll send the Unblooded here with you. Fancy a crawl through a moldering dungeon to see if you can't stir up Galmar's Jagged Crown?

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: It'll be there. You'll see.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: You were right, Galmar.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: I'm in no mood to joke.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Give the word, my lord, and Whiterun is yours.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Whiterun is only a means to an end.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: I've toured our camps. We're ready, Ulfric... Whenever you are.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Is any man ever ready to give the order that will mean the deaths of many?

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: No. But neither is every man able to give that order when he must. But you are that man, Ulfric. You've been that man before, and you'll be him again. And these men and women―they call themselves Stormcloaks because they believe in you. They are the meanest, toughest sons of bitches Skyrim has to offer. And they want this. They want this as much as you do. Perhaps, they want it more.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: We are ready. And I might be old myself, but I'll kick those damn walls down with my bare feet―if you would only ask me to do it!

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Ha. And I'm sure you could do it, too. Alright. This is it.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Aye, and the sons of Skyrim will greet that dawn, teeth and swords flashing.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: So it begins.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Secure the door.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Already done.

speaker: Rikke
dialogue: Ulfric. Stop.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Stop what? Taking Skyrim back from those who'd leave her to rot?

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: You were there with us. You saw it. The day the Empire signed that damn treaty was the day the Empire died.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: The Empire is weak, obsolete. Look at how far we've come and with so little. When we're done rooting out Imperial influence here at home, then we will take our war to the Aldmeri Dominion.

speaker: Rikke
dialogue: You're a damn fool.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Stand aside woman. We've come for the General.

speaker: Rikke
dialogue: He has given up. But I have not.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Rikke. Go. You're free to leave.

speaker: Rikke
dialogue: I'm also free to stay and fight for what I believe in.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: You're also free to die for it.

speaker: Rikke
dialogue: This is what you wanted? Shield brothers and sisters killing each other? Families torn apart? This is the Skyrim you want?!

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Damnit woman, stand aside.

speaker: Rikke
dialogue: That's not the Skyrim I want to live in.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Rikke. You don't have to do this.

speaker: Rikke
dialogue: You've left me no choice... Talos preserve us.

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Enough... enough...

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: This is it for you. Any last words before I send you to Oblivion?

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: You realize this is exactly what they wanted.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: What who wanted?

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: The Thalmor. They stirred up trouble here. Forced us to divert needed resources and throw away good soldiers quelling this rebellion.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: It's a little more than a rebellion, don't you think?

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: We aren't the bad guys you know.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Maybe not, but you certainly aren't the good guys.

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Perhaps you're right. But then what does that make you?

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: You just said it yourself.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: It makes us right.

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: And if I surrender?

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: The Empire I remember never surrendered.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: That Empire is dead. And so are you.

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: So be it.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Just kill him and let's be done with it already.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Come, Galmar. Where's your sense of the dramatic moment?

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: By the gods! If it's a good ending to some damn story you're after - perhaps the Dragonborn should be the one to do it.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Good point.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Good. It's done.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Well, I suppose some kind of speech is in order.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: I'll go gather the men in the courtyard.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: And Elisif?

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Don't you worry about her. I've sent my best men to round her up.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: And now, I present to you, Ulfric Stormcloak, hero of the people, liberator and High King of Skyrim!

speaker: Soldier
dialogue: And what about Jarl Elisif?

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: I do!

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: How'd I do?

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Eh, not so bad. Nice touch about the High King.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Thank you, I thought so, too.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: It's a foregone conclusion, you know.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Oh, I know.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: The Imperials aren't going to leave us alone. They still have camps in the hills. They'll continue to strike out at us, whenever and wherever they can.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: I'm not afraid of the remnants of the Legion, in time they'll all give up and go home. What I fear, is that the Thalmor will see our victory here and turn greater attention to our shores. We must be prepared to face them.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: May the gods preserve us all.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Come, Galmar. We've still much work to do.

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Secure the door.

speaker: Rikke
dialogue: Already done, sir.

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Ulfric Stormcloak! You are guilty of insurrection, murder of Imperial citizens, the assassination of King Torygg, and high treason against the Empire. It's over.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Not while I'm still breathing, it's not.

speaker: Rikke
dialogue: Step aside Galmar. We're here to accept Ulfric's surrender.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: I'll never surrender Skyrim into the hands of a corrupt and dying Empire.

speaker: Rikke
dialogue: Skyrim doesn't belong to you, Ulfric.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: No... But I belong to her.

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Enough! You are traitors and will die traitors' deaths. Stand down and face public execution, or advance and face summary execution by my hands. It matters little to me. Either way I'll be sending your heads back to Cyrodiil.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Well? What are we waiting for?

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Well Ulfric, you can't escape from me this time. Any last requests before I send you to... to wherever you people go when you die.

speaker: Rikke
dialogue: Sovngarde... sir.

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Right. Well?

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Let the Dragonborn be the one to do it. It'll make for a better song.

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Song or not, I just want it done.

speaker: Rikke
dialogue: Talos be with you...

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: What was that, Legate?

speaker: Rikke
dialogue: Nothing. Just saying goodbye.

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: Well, the men will be expecting some kind of speech. And we'll need to hand the city over to that Free-Winter fellow.

speaker: Rikke
dialogue: Brunwulf. Yes, I've sent men to protect him and bring him here. Windhelm will need a government quickly if we are to prevent more violence.

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: The Legion will be staying here for quite some time. I don't expect there to be any further violence.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Galmar thinks we should double our men in the Reach.

speaker: Jorleif
dialogue: A reasonable strategy.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: And you, Jorleif?

speaker: Jorleif
dialogue: Well, sir, the hold of Falkreath is fairly vulnerable, and blocks the only road from Cyrodiil.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: A good point, old friend.

speaker: Jorleif
dialogue: To be sure, my lord, I am not skilled in the arts of war or military tactics.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: But you're able to see the whole in the parts, and for that I'm grateful.

speaker: Jorleif
dialogue: As you wish, sir.

speaker: Jorleif
dialogue: Sir, there continues to be unrest in the Gray Quarter.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Blasted dark elves. I don't suppose you could tell them that I presently have larger concerns? Such as all of Skyrim?

speaker: Jorleif
dialogue: They don't seem to be very sympathetic to our cause, sir.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Let me know if you hear anything more substantial.

speaker: Jorleif
dialogue: Of course, my lord.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Jorleif, I want you to send a messenger to our western camps.

speaker: Jorleif
dialogue: And the message, sir?

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: I'm diverting Gar and Haddring's men to join him.

speaker: Jorleif
dialogue: Is that wise, sir?

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: It will work if we can pull Hran's men from the south. And find a bit of luck.

speaker: Jorleif
dialogue: Of course. Something that seems to be in short supply these days.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: I'm not seeking advice right now, friend. Just send the message.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Is there any news from High Rock?

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Not a peep. Those prissy Bretons can't be made to lift a finger to help their neighbors.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: I suppose we shouldn't be surprised. They've never had many problems with the Empire.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Those milk-drinkers? Might as well be elves. Think they're better than us.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Regardless, it appears Skyrim must stand alone, again.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: Calm yourself, Galmar. Save it for the battlefield.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Our men are getting massacred out there. Damn Imperials.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: We can't march on Solitude. Not yet. One thing at a time.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: We need to move faster. Keep them off balance.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: It's working, Galmar. Our patience has won us friends and allies. And our armies are systematically taking care of the rest.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Do you think we could persuade one of the dragons to join our side?

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: I'm fairly sure that the dragons don't care about our matters one way or the other.

speaker: Galmar
