dialogue: But just think of the advantage.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: I'm not saying it wouldn't be useful. But there are better uses of our resources right now.

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: I don't suppose we would ever really trust the thing anyway.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: I'm still not sure I understand what you're asking.

speaker: Torsten
dialogue: A navy, my lord. We could stop the influx of Imperial troops to Solitude, and choke their northern lines.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: But most of their supply routes come south, from Cyrodiil.

speaker: Torsten
dialogue: But imagine—fleets of ships sailing from Windhelm, all bearing the Stormcloak flag! It would be glorious!

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: And I suppose the Cruel-Seas would be just the clan to provide ships and men?

speaker: Torsten
dialogue: You need but ask.

speaker: Ulfric
dialogue: I'll think on this, but I make no promises.

speaker: Torsten
dialogue: I can ask no more. Thank you, my lord!

speaker: Gharol
dialogue: Imagine the heads of your enemies as you forge. Let your hatred work the steel.

speaker: Umurn
dialogue: Yes, mother.

speaker: Umurn
dialogue: The metal has been stubborn today. It refuses to bend.

speaker: Gharol
dialogue: Save your anger for the forge. The steel cannot hear your whining.

speaker: Umurn
dialogue: Sorry, mother. I'll focus on my work.

speaker: Gharol
dialogue: Ah, is there any weapon finer than an Orc blade?

speaker: Umurn
dialogue: No, mother. It's no wonder our enemies fear the sight of an Orc warrior.

speaker: Una
dialogue: I keep coming out here thinking I'll see what others see in this... frivolity.

speaker: Una
dialogue: I'm pleased when the palace is clean, I'm pleased when the beds are made on time, I'm pleased when Erdi isn't around. Most of those don't happen very often.

speaker: Ungrien
dialogue: I can't take it anymore, Tythis. Indaryn keeps pushing me around and I'm not even doing anything wrong.

speaker: Tythis
dialogue: Maybe its time to quit, then.

speaker: Ungrien
dialogue: And do what? Losing a job from the Black-Briar family would make me a made man! No one would ever take me on anywhere else.

speaker: Tythis
dialogue: Don't let it get you down. Indaryn will eventually tire of picking on you and move on to someone else.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: Unmid, I wish to travel about the city. Prepare an escort please.

speaker: Unmid
dialogue: Begging your pardon my lady, but I strongly recommend against it.

speaker: Laila
dialogue: Anuriel seems to think that seeing me on the streets might bolster the city's morale.

speaker: Unmid
dialogue: My lady, there could be agents of the Empire looking for an opportunity like that to have you killed. Are you willing to take that risk?

speaker: Laila
dialogue: No. Of course you're right, Unmid. I'll stay here for now.

speaker: Unmid
dialogue: Anuriel, would you please stop declaring that the city is safe for the Jarl to roam? You and I both know that isn't true.

speaker: Anuriel
dialogue: I would never knowingly place Laila in danger, you know that too. Why do you always question my judgment? You don't trust me.

speaker: Unmid
dialogue: I trust you, I'm just concerned about her safety. That's all. Don't be angry with me.

speaker: Anuriel
dialogue: I'm not angry with you. Tell you what, lover. Meet me in my chambers later and we can discuss the situation in private.

speaker: Anuriel
dialogue: Unmid, my sweet. Are we still meeting later for... combat training?

speaker: Unmid
dialogue: Of course. Your training isn't complete yet.

speaker: Anuriel
dialogue: I look forward to it then.

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: How is your hunting with Yatul?

speaker: Urog
dialogue: We are strong. We get the job done.

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: I'm proud of you for helping provide for us.

speaker: Urog
dialogue: Well someone has to provide around here.

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: What is that supposed to mean?

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: I don't know what your aunts told you, but...

speaker: Urog
dialogue: They're not my aunts. They're your aunts. And they told me enough.

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: What are you talking about?

speaker: Urog
dialogue: About how the Divines cursed you. What horrible thing did you do to deserve it?

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: Nothing! I... it's ill fortune. That's all.

speaker: Urog
dialogue: Well, your ill fortune means I have no mother.

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: I... I'm sorry.

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: Haven't I always been a good father? A good chief?

speaker: Urog
dialogue: Yatul and I do all the hunting. Mul and Gadba do all the mining. It seems like all you do is find more wives to get killed.

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: That's not fair, now.

speaker: Urog
dialogue: Just... try and keep out of our way.

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: Come, child, I will tell you how to track a snow cat.

speaker: Urog
dialogue: But you said that was impossible.

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: No, just very difficult. You have to look for shift in various shades of white.

speaker: Urog
dialogue: My eyes are sharp.

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: They are, but your mind has to be sharp, too.

speaker: Urog
dialogue: What's the most dangerous beast you've ever killed?

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: Oh, probably a troll.

speaker: Urog
dialogue: They're fearsome!

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: They are indeed. Nothing like your mother, though!

speaker: Urog
dialogue: That's what everyone keeps saying. But you didn't kill her. That's what I was asking.

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: Oh of course. My mistake.

speaker: Urog
dialogue: What about my father? Was he a good hunter?

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: Oh, you've seen your father just trying to chase a skeever from his house. He's a bit soft.

speaker: Urog
dialogue: Sometimes I'm surprised he's still the chief.

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: We all are, my dear, but sometimes the Divines reward those who don't seem to deserve it. Call it dumb luck.

speaker: Uthgerd
dialogue: Careful, huh? Thanks, Skulvar. I'll remember that. Ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Valindor
dialogue: Oh, it's not so terrible. I actually find the work quite relaxing.

speaker: Svana
dialogue: Relaxing? They must be working you to the bone! You should rest before you do yourself in.

speaker: Valindor
dialogue: Not to worry, dear Svana. I promise you I can handle it, but your concern is quite flattering.

speaker: Vals
dialogue: The dead should be made to serve the living, not the other way around!

speaker: Golldir
dialogue: I'll return my ancestors to Sovngarde, and you with them!

speaker: Vals
dialogue: Sovngarde is a myth, you s'wit! And now you can join your ancestors in service to me.

speaker: Vampire
dialogue: And who is this?

speaker: Vighar
dialogue: It is no matter, this fool will be the next act of the show.

speaker: Vampire
dialogue: These Vigilants never know when to give up. I thought we'd taught them enough of a lesson at their hall.

speaker: Vampire 2
dialogue: To come in here alone.... a fool like all the rest of them.

speaker: Vampire
dialogue: He fought well though. Jeron and Bresoth were no match for him.

speaker: Vampire 2
dialogue: Ha. Those two deserved what they got. Their arrogance had become insufferable.

speaker: Vampire
dialogue: All this talk is making me thirsty. Perhaps another Vigilant will wander in soon.

speaker: Vampire 2
dialogue: I wish Lokil would hurry it up. I have half a mind to return to the castle and tell Harkon what a fool he's entrusted this mission to.

speaker: Vampire
dialogue: And I have half a mind to tell Lokil of your disloyalty.

speaker: Vampire 2
dialogue: You wouldn't dare. Now shut up and keep on watch.

speaker: Adalvald
dialogue: I'll never tell you anything, vampire. My oath to Stendarr is stronger than any suffering you can inflict on me.

speaker: Lokil
dialogue: I believe you, Vigilant. And I don't think you even know what you've found here. So go and meet your beloved Stendarr.

speaker: Vampire
dialogue: Are you sure that was wise, Lokil? He still might have told us something. We haven't gotten anywhere ourselves with...

speaker: Lokil
dialogue: He knew nothing. He served his purpose by leading us to this place. Now it is up to us to bring Harkon the prize. And we will not return without it. Vingalmo and Orthjolf will make way for me after this.

speaker: Vampire
dialogue: Yes, of course Lokil. Do not forget who brought you news of the Vigilants' discovery.

speaker: Lokil
dialogue: I never forget who my friends are. Or my enemies.

speaker: Curwe
dialogue: I had a look at that boneyard the other day, Vantus. The one to the Northwest.

speaker: Vantus
dialogue: I told you I don't like you going there. I've seen scavengers picking at the mammoths. They could be dangerous.

speaker: Curwe
dialogue: You know, I was thinking of expanding the herb garden. Make room for some new plants I'm planning.

speaker: Vantus
dialogue: That should be all right. How much space were you planning?

speaker: Curwe
dialogue: Oh, half the field should do.

speaker: Vantus
dialogue: Half the field? What could need half the field?

speaker: Curwe
dialogue: I just think pollinating would be easier if I could do a lot of plants at once.

speaker: Vantus
dialogue: Uh... why don't we talk about this later?

speaker: Varnius
dialogue: I swear to you, unnatural magics are coming from that cave! There are strange noises and lights! We need someone to investigate!

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: Then we will immediately send out a legion to scour the cave and secure the town. Haafingar's people will always be safe under my rule.

speaker: Varnius
dialogue: Th... thank you, my Jarl. Thank you.

speaker: Sybille
dialogue: Your eminence, my scrying has suggested nothing in the area. Dragon Bridge is under imperial control. This is likely superstitious nonsense.

speaker: Falk
dialogue: Perhaps a more... tempered reaction... might be called for?

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: Oh. Yes, of course you are right. Falk, tell Captain Aldis I said to assign a few extra soldiers to Dragon Bridge.

speaker: Varnius
dialogue: Thank you, Jarl Elisif. But about the cave...

speaker: Falk
dialogue: I will have someone take care of the cave as well Varnius, you can rest easy. You're dismissed.

speaker: Arnbjorn
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Veezara
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha! Again! Again! Do the part where he tries to buy you some candy.

speaker: Gabriella
dialogue: Oh Babette, but you are so wicked.

speaker: Nazir
dialogue: What about you, Festus? How did that last contract turn out?

speaker: Arnbjorn
dialogue: Oh, yes, please, old man. Regale us with your tales of wizardry...

speaker: Gabriella
dialogue: And what of your latest, Arnbjorn. Something about a Khajiit? Merchant was it?

speaker: Babette
dialogue: Oh, a big doggy chasing a little kitty! How adorable!

speaker: Nazir
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Festus
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Veezara
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Arnbjorn
dialogue: I am not adorable, it was not funny, and he wasn't a merchant. He was a Khajiit monk, a master of the Whispering Fang style. But now he's dead... and I have a new loincloth.

speaker: Nazir
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Festus
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Veezara
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Babette
dialogue: Ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha ha!

speaker: Veezara
dialogue: Tell me, sister. Are the stories true?

speaker: Babette
dialogue: You must be talking about the caravan job...

speaker: Veezara
dialogue: You infiltrated the position, eliminated the target, and made it look like an accident. Impressive. I'd say you earned your bonus on that one!

speaker: Babette
dialogue: In truth? It was so easy, I feel a bit guilty. Once again, the sweet, innocent child earned more trust than was wise.

speaker: Veezara
dialogue: Tell me, brother. Are the stories true?

speaker: Festus Krex
dialogue: You must be talking about the caravan job...

speaker: Veezara
dialogue: You infiltrated the position, eliminated the target, and made it look like an accident. Impressive. I'd say you earned your bonus on that one!

speaker: Festus Krex
dialogue: What? You think me too old, too feeble? There is more knowledge in me than in two of you pups together. And knowledge... knowledge is my weapon.

speaker: Babette
dialogue: Just try to relax, Veezara. Let the elixir do its work. You'll feel better, shortly.

speaker: Veezara
dialogue: Achh... Thank you, dear. You are most kind. The jester's cut feels as bad as it looks, I'm afraid.

speaker: Astrid
dialogue: Damn it, this never should have happened! We knew better. We knew better, and still we let our guards down. Agh!

speaker: Festus Krex
dialogue: It's true, I'm afraid, Cicero was a little whirlwind, slashing this way and all that. It would have been funny, if he weren't trying to murder us all.

speaker: Veezara
dialogue: Bested by a fool. Who's the fool now, hmm?

speaker: Babette
dialogue: Hush, Veezara. You were very brave. Astrid may well be dead if not for you.

speaker: Astrid
dialogue: She's right. I'll be forever in your debt, dearest brother. Now be quiet. Just... just rest.

speaker: Thorek
dialogue: The orcs have breached the inner sanctum, Brother Veren.

speaker: Veren Duleri
dialogue: We must hold. We can't allow the Skull to fall into their hands.

speaker: Thorek
dialogue: But... no more than a handful of us remain, brother.

speaker: Veren Duleri
dialogue: Then we have no choice. The Miasma must be released.

speaker: Thorek
dialogue: The Miasma? But, brother...

speaker: Veren Duleri
dialogue: Brother Thorek, we must remain here and guard this Skull with our lives if necessary.

speaker: Thorek
dialogue: Agreed. To the death.

speaker: Veren Duleri
dialogue: Then let it be done. Farewell, my brothers!

speaker: Erandur
dialogue: Wait... Veren... Thorek... you're alive!

speaker: Veren Duleri
dialogue: No thanks to you, Casimir.

speaker: Erandur
dialogue: I no longer use that name. I'm Erandur, Priest of Mara.

speaker: Veren Duleri
dialogue: You're a traitor. You left us to die and then ran before the Miasma took you.

speaker: Erandur
dialogue: No. I... I was scared. I wasn't ready to sleep.

speaker: Veren Duleri
dialogue: Enough of your lies! I can't allow you to destroy the Skull, Priest of Mara.

speaker: Erandur
dialogue: Then you leave me no choice!

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: You better have a damn good reason to be here with that murderer.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: Please, lower your weapons so we can speak. I have proof that you've all been misled!

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: No tricks, Karliah or I'll cut you down where you stand. Now what's this so-called proof you speak of?

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: I have Gallus' journal. I think you'll find its contents disturbing.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Let me see. No, it... it can't be. This can't be true. I've known Mercer too long...

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: It's true, Brynjolf. Every word. Mercer's been stealing from the Guild for years, right under your noses.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: There's only one way to find out if what the lass says is true. Delvin, I'll need you to open the Vault.

speaker: Delvin
dialogue: Wait just a blessed moment, Bryn. What's in that book? What did it say?

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: It says Mercer's been stealing from our vault for years. Gallus was looking into it before he was murdered.

speaker: Delvin
dialogue: How can Mercer open up a vault that needs two keys? It's impossible. Could he pick his way in?

speaker: Vex
dialogue: That door has the best puzzle locks money can buy. There's no way it can be picked open.

speaker: Karliah
dialogue: He didn't need to pick the lock.

speaker: Delvin
dialogue: What's she on about?

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Use your key on the vault, Delvin. We'll open it up and find out the truth.

speaker: Delvin
dialogue: I've used my key, but the vault's still locked up tighter than a drum. Now use yours.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: By the Eight! It's gone, everything's gone! Get in here, all of you!

speaker: Delvin
dialogue: The gold, the jewels... it's all gone.

speaker: Vex
dialogue: That son-of-a-bitch! I'll kill him!

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Vex! Put it away... right now. We can't afford to lose our heads... we need to calm down and focus.

speaker: Delvin
dialogue: Do what he says, Vex. This isn't helpin' right now.

speaker: Vex
dialogue: Fine. We do it your way. For now.

speaker: Brynjolf
dialogue: Delvin, Vex... watch the Flagon. If you see Mercer, come tell me right away.

speaker: Vex
dialogue: Delvin, that last shipment we heisted on the Cyrodiil frontier was worthless!

speaker: Delvin
dialogue: That's impossible. I distinctly heard that lout in the tavern say it was a full shipment of furs. They should be worth a fortune.

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: Ah, Viarmo. I assume you are here to petition for the reinstatement of the Burning of King Olaf Festival.

speaker: Viarmo
dialogue: I am, Jarl. I wish to present King Olaf's verse from the Poetic Edda. Recovered this very day from the Bards Tomb.

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: Ah, you mentioned something that would convince us the festival should take place but I didn't expect King Olaf's lost verse. Please proceed.

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: You have proven your point, Viarmo. The festival is truly a celebration of Solitude and a condemnation of false kings.

speaker: Viarmo
dialogue: I thank you and the college thanks you, Jarl.

speaker: Elisif
dialogue: Furthermore, I believe that such a fine poem deserves some payment of Patronage. The college will be generously rewarded.

speaker: Viarmo
dialogue: Thank you yet again. I will make sure our applicant, who was instrumental in... recovering the poem will be well rewarded.

speaker: Viarmo
dialogue: How are your students coming along?

speaker: Inge
dialogue: Some of them have a long way to go, but they're mostly passable. Don't let them hear I said that, though!

speaker: Viarmo
dialogue: Of course not! Complacency is the bane of art. They're in good hands with you, Inge.

speaker: Inge
dialogue: Yes, Headmaster.

speaker: Viarmo
dialogue: How are your students coming along?

speaker: Giraud
dialogue: Bunch of distractions, if you ask me. They just interrupt the rest of my work.

speaker: Viarmo
dialogue: I'm sorry to break it to you, Giraud, but students are an unfortunate necessity of a college. Do try to persevere.

speaker: Giraud
dialogue: Yes, Headmaster.

speaker: Viarmo
dialogue: How are your students coming along?

speaker: Pantea
dialogue: Passably. Aia is my star pupil; none of the others can hold a candle to her, especially not that wretched Illdi.

speaker: Viarmo
dialogue: Try not to play favorites, Lady Ateia. It does a disservice to the whole class.

speaker: Pantea
dialogue: Yes, Headmaster.

speaker: Vampire
dialogue: And who is this?

speaker: Vighar
dialogue: It is no matter, this fool will be the next act of the show.

speaker: Tyranus
dialogue: So you don't know anything about this house?

speaker: Tyranus
dialogue: Anyone seen entering or leaving? Any strange lights or unusual noises?

speaker: Yngvar
dialogue: It's abandoned and it's always been abandoned.

speaker: Tyranus
dialogue: Get out of my head, Daedra!

speaker: Molag Bal
dialogue: You will kill. You will kill, or you will die!

speaker: Tyranus
dialogue: I don't want to die. I can't die here! The Daedra has us. It's you or me!

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Vignar Gray-Mane! Your family was noticeably absent from the walls. Now I know why. Wouldn't a dagger in the back have sufficed?

speaker: Vignar
dialogue: You think this is personal? The Empire has no place in Skyrim... not any more. And you? You have no place in Whiterun anymore.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: A convenient position to hold now. But mark my words, old man, in the days to come, Ulfric will spread his rebellion thin. And what then? We need the Empire, as much as it needs us. We Nords are the Empire! Our blood built it. Our blood sustains it! You of all people should know that.

speaker: Vignar
dialogue: If this was my Empire, I'd be able to worship whoever I damned well pleased. You wish to see an Empire without Talos? Without its soul? We should be fighting those witch-elves, not bending knee to them. The Emperor is nothing more than a puppet of the Thalmor. Skyrim needs a High King who will fight for her, and Whiterun needs a Jarl who will do the same.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: Tell me, Vignar. Was all this worth it? How many of those corpses lining our streets wear the faces of men who once called you friend? What about their families?

speaker: Galmar
dialogue: Enough! Both of you! There is a burning city out there that needs a government.

speaker: Vignar
dialogue: He's right. Galmar, come, let us restore order.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: This isn't over. You hear me you old fool! This isn't over! {{hide|And you. A Stormcloak? I'd thought better of you.|Referring to the Dragonborn.}} You'll all come to regret this day.

speaker: Vignar
dialogue: There's a chill in the air. Ysmir's beard, it gets colder in here every day.

speaker: Brill
dialogue: That's just you getting skinnier every day, old man. You're losing your padding. You need to eat more.

speaker: Vignar
dialogue: Well, if my layabout manservant fed me more, that wouldn't be a problem.

speaker: Brill
dialogue: Oho! Manservant? Is that what I am now?

speaker: Vignar
dialogue: My mistake. A manservant wouldn't let me starve or freeze. I let you live here, and now I'm two steps closer to the grave.

speaker: Brill
dialogue: Old man, without me, you would have withered away a long time ago.

speaker: Vignar
dialogue: Hmph. Damn you for being right.

speaker: Vignar
dialogue: You ain't made me that stew in a long time.

speaker: Brill
dialogue: Which, the mutton or the vegetable?

speaker: Brill
dialogue: Hmm, so I haven't. All right, I'll buy the ingredients tomorrow and we can have it for dinner.

speaker: Brill
dialogue: Fancy a game of Iron Hearts later?

speaker: Vignar
dialogue: You going to lose horribly, and then say you let me win?

speaker: Vignar
dialogue: Then you're on.

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: I won't say it again, Vignar; Talos worship is forbidden. It's the Empire's law, and we're still a part of the Empire.

speaker: Vignar
dialogue: A law made at the tip of an Aldmeri sword, aye. A sword stained red with Nord blood. Is this what our people fought and died for? To forsake our most beloved ancestor and divine?

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: I'm no happier about this than you are, but I don't want {{sicquote|the|to}} see the Thalmor rounding up people in the streets and throwing them in prison.

speaker: Vignar
dialogue: Do your loyalties lie with the Thalmor, then?

speaker: Balgruuf
dialogue: I warn you, Gray-Mane, you are treading on dangerous ground.

speaker: Vignar
dialogue: Don't threaten me, boy. You're either a Nord who respects our traditions, or you're not. If not, it isn't me you'll have to answer to, but the people of this city and this Hold.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: Come to me with questions. I know our history almost as well as Vignar by now. Except I can remember it.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: But I still hear the call of the blood.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: You have my brother and I, obviously. But I don't know if the rest will go along quite so easily.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: Leave that to me.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: Master, you're not truly considering accepting him?

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: I am nobody's master, Vilkas. And last I checked, we had some empty beds in Jorrvaskr for those with a fire burning in their hearts.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: Apologies. But perhaps this isn't the time. I've never even heard of this outsider.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: Sometimes the famous come to us. Sometimes men and women come to us to seek their fame. It makes no difference. What matters is their heart.

speaker: Kodlak
dialogue: Vilkas, take him out to the yard and see what he can do.

speaker: Eorlund
dialogue: Who will start?

speaker: Aela
dialogue: I'll do it. Before the ancient flame... We grieve.

speaker: Eorlund
dialogue: We grieve.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: We grieve.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: We grieve.

speaker: Eorlund
dialogue: At this loss... We weep.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: We weep.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: We weep.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: We weep.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: For the fallen... We shout.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: We shout.

speaker: Eorlund
dialogue: We shout.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: We shout.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: And for ourselves... We take our leave.

speaker: Eorlund
dialogue: We take our leave.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: We take our leave.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: We take our leave.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: His spirit is departed. Members of the Circle, let us withdraw to the Underforge, to grieve our last together.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: The old man had one wish before he died. And he didn't get it. It's as simple as that.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: Being moon-born is not so much of a curse as you might think, Vilkas.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: That's fine for you. But he wanted to be clean. He wanted to meet Ysgramor and know the glories of Sovngarde. But all that was taken from him.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: And you avenged him.

speaker: Farkas
dialogue: Kodlak did not care for vengeance.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: No, Farkas, he didn't. And that's not what this is about. We should be honoring Kodlak, no matter our own thoughts on the blood.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: You're right. It's what he wanted, and he deserved to have it.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: Kodlak used to speak of a way to cleanse his soul, even in death. You know the legends of the Tomb of Ysgramor.

speaker: Aela
dialogue: There the souls of Harbingers will heed the call of northern steel. We can't even enter the tomb without Wuuthrad, and it's in pieces, like it has been for a thousand years.

speaker: Eorlund
dialogue: And dragons were just stories. And the elves once ruled Skyrim. Just because something is, doesn't mean it must be. The blade is a weapon. A tool. Tools are meant to be broken. And repaired.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: Is that? Did you repair the blade?

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: It will feel that way for a while. But eventually you'll get used to it, and then you'll get faster with it. After that, the shortsword will feel like a knitting needle when you pick it up again.

speaker: Ria
dialogue: I've never held a knitting needle.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: Of course not. My mistake.

speaker: Ria
dialogue: Should I be holding the blade further away than a smaller one?

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: If you keep it in close, you'll have more control, but it can be harder to balance a strike.

speaker: Ria
dialogue: I guess that comes down to footwork, then.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: Exactly. When you have a big, heavy weight swinging around your upper body, your lower body has to compensate, or you'll fall right over.

speaker: Ria
dialogue: Why can't I train with Aela?

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: Because, you wanted to learn the longer blades. Aela's never used anything bigger than a dagger.

speaker: Ria
dialogue: It's just...I think our fighting styles are similar.

speaker: Vilkas
dialogue: Well, you can either get better with a bow or try to learn from me.

speaker: Hadvar
dialogue: What was that?

speaker: Tullius
dialogue: It's nothing. Carry on.

speaker: Captain
dialogue: Yes, General Tullius. Give them their last rites.

speaker: Priestess of Arkay
dialogue: As we commend your souls to Aetherius, blessings of the Eight Divines upon you, for you are the salt and earth of Nirn, our beloved...

speaker: Stormcloak Soldier
dialogue: For the love of Talos, shut up and let's get this over with.

speaker: Priestess of Arkay
dialogue: As you wish.

speaker: Stormcloak
dialogue: You Imperial bastards!

speaker: Ingrid
dialogue: Death to the Stormcloaks!

speaker: Ralof
dialogue: As fearless in death as he was in life.

speaker: Captain
dialogue: Next, the [player race description]!

speaker: Viola
dialogue: Hello! Captain, can you spare a moment? I heard something the other day I wanted to share with you.

speaker: Lonely-Gale
dialogue: What did you hear?

speaker: Viola
dialogue: It was an old Nord proverb. It said the best way to get over the loss of a lover is to find a new one.

speaker: Lonely-Gale
dialogue: I didn't lose a lover, Viola; I lost my wife. It's not the same thing.

speaker: Viola
dialogue: Well, if it works in the one case, why not the other? Don't you want to at least give it a try?

speaker: Lonely-Gale
dialogue: No, I really don't. It'll be a while before I'm ready for that. I'll be on my way now.

speaker: Viola
dialogue: Captain Lonely-Gale, I-I've been looking for you everywhere!

speaker: Lonely-Gale
dialogue: And now you've found me. Can I help you?

speaker: Viola
dialogue: Have you thought about my invitation?

speaker: Lonely-Gale
dialogue: I've thought about it, but I'm not sure it's such a good idea.

speaker: Viola
dialogue: Oh, I see. Is it still too soon?

speaker: Lonely-Gale
dialogue: Yes, I think that must be it. My wife hasn't been gone that long, after all. Ask me again on another day.

speaker: Viola
dialogue: I'm sorry to be such a bother. We'll talk another time.

speaker: Viola
dialogue: Captain. Captain!

speaker: Lonely-Gale
dialogue: What is it now, Viola?

speaker: Viola
dialogue: Did you notice that the snow settles in a different direction near the murder sites?

speaker: Lonely-Gale
dialogue: Don't you think all your tramping around there investigating might have something to do with it?

speaker: Viola
dialogue: I... well... perhaps. But still, it's curious.

speaker: Viola
dialogue: Do you think those Dark Elves had anything to do with the murders? The attacks all happened at night, after all.

speaker: Lonely-Gale
dialogue: Viola, Dark Elves sleep, just like the rest of us.

speaker: Viola
dialogue: You wouldn't think it from the racket that Cornerclub makes.

speaker: Lonely-Gale
dialogue: I'm sure the guards have the matter well in hand. Now, if you'll excuse me.

speaker: Svari
dialogue: They can't hurt uncle Roggvir. Tell them he didn't do it.

speaker: Addvar
dialogue: Svari, you need to go home. Go home and stay there until your mother comes.

speaker: Aldis
dialogue: Lock the city gate.

speaker: Vivienne
dialogue: You should tell her that her uncle is scum that betrayed his High King. Best she know now, Addvar.

speaker: Addvar
dialogue: You're all heart, Vivienne.

speaker: Aldis
dialogue: Roggvir. You helped Ulfric Stormcloak escape this city after he murdered High King Torygg. By opening that gate for Ulfric you betrayed the people of Solitude.

speaker: Sorex
dialogue: He doesn't deserve to speak!

speaker: Roggvir
dialogue: There was no murder! Ulfric challenged Torygg. He beat the High King in fair combat.

speaker: Roggvir
dialogue: Such as our way! Such as the ancient custom of Skyrim, and all Nords!

speaker: Vivienne
dialogue: Cut 'em down!

speaker: Aldis
dialogue: Guard. Prepare the prisoner.

speaker: Roggvir
dialogue: I don't need your help.

speaker: Aldis
dialogue: Very well, Roggvir. Bow your head.

speaker: Roggvir
dialogue: On this day... I go to Sovngarde.

speaker: Angeline
dialogue: Vivienne, could you check out supplies of mandrake root?

speaker: Vivienne
dialogue: Which one is that again?

speaker: Angeline
dialogue: It's the root that looks like an ugly little man.

speaker: Vivienne
dialogue: In that case, I'm pretty sure it tried to buy me a drink last night.

speaker: Vivienne
dialogue: Do you miss your days training at the College?

speaker: Lisette
dialogue: Absolutely not. I prefer to be near enough to come visit but free to come and go as I please.

speaker: Vivienne
dialogue: I could listen to him/her play all day.

speaker: Lisette
dialogue: He's/She's okay. A little breathy and a little harsh on the notes.

speaker: Vivienne
dialogue: Speaking of harsh, you Bards don't cut each other any slack, do you?

speaker: Lisette
dialogue: Not in our nature.

speaker: Vulwulf
dialogue: Typical Imperial rot. You speak of Skyrim like you know the land, know its people. You're from Cyrodiil! You know nothing about us! Nothing!

speaker: Alexia
dialogue: Oh, I know enough. I know those trouble-making Stormcloaks refuse to submit to Imperial authority. Such seditious behavior. Why it's treason!

speaker: Vulwulf
dialogue: And when the elves marched into your beloved Cyrodiil, and everyone took up arms against them, wasn't that treason? Against the Dominion? Huh?

speaker: Alexia
dialogue: Why that's not the same thing at all. The Dominion were invaders. Conquerors. We had to fight them, to preserve our own way of life.

speaker: Vulwulf
dialogue: My point exactly.

speaker: Vulwulf
dialogue: Drink up, my boy! Drink to those who have fallen! May their souls find their way to Sovngarde!

speaker: Asgeir
dialogue: Take it easy, father. You're making a scene.

speaker: Vulwulf
dialogue: I'll rest easy when we've driven every last Imperial pig back across the Jerall Mountains!

speaker: Vulwulf
dialogue: Now, do me the honor I deserve as your father and drink up!

speaker: Asgeir
dialogue: Yes... father.

speaker: Asgeir
dialogue: I'm sorry you disapprove, father. But I've made up my mind. I'm not a warrior, I'm a businessman.

speaker: Vulwulf
dialogue: The only reason you have the gold for your 'business' is because I gave it to you.

speaker: Asgeir
dialogue: I'll pay you back, if it means that much.

speaker: Vulwulf
dialogue: It's not about the coin, it's about honoring your legacy by picking up arms and keeping this land free. The sooner you remember that, the better.

speaker: Vulwulf
dialogue: Maven! So good to see you again. Hoist a flagon and celebrate with me!

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Vulwulf, it's always a pleasure. When you're standing downwind of me.

speaker: Vulwulf
dialogue: Sorry, what was that?

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Nothing Vulwulf.... cheers.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: I'm telling you, Vulwulf, it's the investment you've been waiting for.

speaker: Vulwulf
dialogue: So I pay for the weapon shipments and you oversee their distribution to the Stormcloaks?

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Exactly. What better way to help the cause than to put weapons into the hands of young Nord warriors dying for their homeland?

speaker: Vulwulf
dialogue: Shor's Beard! You're right! I'll do it... provided you supervise the shipments personally.

speaker: Maven
dialogue: Don't worry, I'll treat those shipments as if I owned them myself.

speaker: Nura
dialogue: You need to be easier on Asgeir. All he wants to do is please you.

speaker: Vulwulf
dialogue: It would please me if he'd take up arms and fight to save his homeland. Is that too much to ask my own son?

speaker: Nura
dialogue: That's right. He is your son. He has his own hopes and dreams and we have no right to tell him otherwise.

speaker: Vulwulf
dialogue: You can't deny the fact that he needs to give back to his people, to fight to keep us free. You healed the wounded, Nura. You saw their life's blood spilling into the mud, giving back to the land. No, I'm sorry, I've worked too damn hard to let his life go to waste.

speaker: Nura
dialogue: How are things at the Meadery, my dear?

speaker: Vulwulf
dialogue: Not this again...

speaker: Nura
dialogue: Hush, Vulwulf... let the boy speak.

speaker: Asgeir
dialogue: It's going very well, actually. The war hasn't even slowed down our production or shipping at all.

speaker: Vulwulf
dialogue: Of course it is. That's what happens when you're partners with a corrupt Imperial whore like Maven.

speaker: Nura
dialogue: Vulwulf! The Empire may be our enemy, but Asgeir is still our son and we're a long way from Cyrodiil.

speaker: Asgeir
dialogue: Father, I promise you, this has nothing to do with Empires or politics. It's just business.

speaker: Vulwulf
dialogue: It has everything to do with politics. Asgeir my son, you have so much to learn.

speaker: Vulwulf
dialogue: Talen! Another round!

speaker: Talen-Jei
dialogue: I think you've had plenty, Vulwulf. Maybe you should head on home.

speaker: Vulwulf
dialogue: You stupid lizard! I said give me some more drink, or I'll have your head on a pike!

speaker: Talen-Jei
dialogue: Suit yourself.

speaker: Drennen
dialogue: I don't like this place. It feels like we're being...watched.

speaker: Breya
dialogue: Its a simple job, Drennen. We get in, we steal the Lexicon, we leave. Don't get jumpy.

speaker: Fathoms
dialogue: If you two cannot handle this, we can find others to hire.

speaker: Roots
dialogue: Enough. Their services will be more than adequate. Let us continue.

speaker: Drennen
dialogue: This place is unbelievable.

speaker: Roots
dialogue: Indeed. Avanchnzel is as much a library as it is a city. Built to hold the vast memories of the Dwemer.

speaker: Breya
dialogue: Why are all these...things...ignoring us?

speaker: Roots
dialogue: Avanchnzel is waiting.

speaker: Breya
dialogue: Waiting for what?

speaker: Roots
dialogue: No one seems to know. Perhaps the return of the Dwemer. Perhaps the ending of the world.

speaker: Breya
dialogue: Best get rid of the ones we see. Just in case.

speaker: Drennen
dialogue: This place is huge.

speaker: Roots
dialogue: It is large, indeed. I did not anticipate Avanchnzel's size or the time needed to uncover the entrance. A few hours sleep and we should be ready to continue through.

speaker: Drennen
dialogue: Maybe we should turn back. I don't want to sleep here.

speaker: Roots
dialogue: Drennen, do you understand that the Lexicon at the bottom of this place holds the accumulated memories of centuries of Dwemer.

speaker: Breya
dialogue: Not to mention our pay.

speaker: Fathoms
dialogue: So we're not turning back, you fool.

speaker: Breya
dialogue: Besides, you're not afraid of a few sleeping metal men. Are you, Drennen?

speaker: Breya
dialogue: I thought you said these things were 'sleeping'?

speaker: Roots
dialogue: You said they were sleeping. I said they were waiting. It seems a few of them were 'waiting' for someone to try and take the Lexicon.

speaker: Drennen
dialogue: I can't do this. We shouldn't be here. I'm sorry.

speaker: Fathoms
dialogue: Let the field mouse run. Your pay will be double.

speaker: Breya
dialogue: My pay will be nothing if we die in here!

speaker: Roots
dialogue: Calm yourself, Breya. We are close to the Lexicon. I can feel it calling. We can do it without Drennen.

speaker: Roots
dialogue: We are close now. Can you feel the Lexicon calling out?

speaker: Fathoms
dialogue: [sarcastic] Sure.

speaker: Breya
dialogue: So we get it and get out, right?

speaker: Roots
dialogue: Once we have the Lexicon, we need to take it to its podium. I know what to do from there. Soon the Lexicon's knowledge will be mine.

speaker: Fathoms
dialogue: Ours. Soon the Lexicon's knowledge will be ours.

speaker: Roots
dialogue: Of course.

speaker: Roots
dialogue: We're almost there. I can hear the Lexicon. Come on, quickly!

speaker: Breya
dialogue: Something doesn't feel right. [pause] Wait!

speaker: Bolli
dialogue: Wujeeta, we need to talk.

speaker: Wujeeta
dialogue: I know, I was late. I'm sorry.

speaker: Bolli
dialogue: I don't know what I'm going to do with you. I can't just let this go unpunished.

speaker: Wujeeta
dialogue: Please, don't get rid of me! I need the coin. I... I'll work for free for the rest of this week. Please!

speaker: Bolli
dialogue: Sigh. Very well. You're lucky Maramal has placed me in a very forgiving mood.

speaker: Wujeeta
dialogue: Don't worry about it, Svana. Its my problem...no need for you to get involved.

speaker: Svana
dialogue: If you're in some sort of trouble, I could talk to Haelga.

speaker: Wujeeta
dialogue: No...no. I'm just tired is all. Thank you.

speaker: Wujeeta
dialogue: No, no, no. I need this job! This is the last place in town to have work.

speaker: Tythis
dialogue: There's always the Thieves Guild.

speaker: Wujeeta
dialogue: What was that?

speaker: Tythis
dialogue: Nothing, nothing. Just straighten yourself out before you find yourself headed back to Black Marsh.

speaker: Wuunferth
dialogue: What is the meaning of this?

speaker: Jorleif
dialogue: You're under {{Sicblock|the arrest|arrest}}, for the Murder of Susanne of Candlehearth Hall. And Friga Shatter-Shield. And all the rest. We're wise to your scheming, you coward.

speaker: Wuunferth
dialogue: Has the whole city lost their brains? I've been scrying and auguring to find the murderer myself.

speaker: Jorleif
dialogue: Make your excuses from the Bloodworks, wizard. Get him out of my sight.

speaker: Windhelm Guard
dialogue: Yes, sir! I'm sorry, sir. But you'll have to come with me.

speaker: Wuunferth
dialogue: This isn't over, Jorleif!

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: I hear Mauhulakh is wandering again. He's after a new woman.

speaker: Bolar
dialogue: He's lonely. What do you expect?

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: No matter. You'll take care of things like you always have.

speaker: Bolar
dialogue: Please, let's not have it come to that.

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: True... we could simply make sure she never reaches Narzulbur.

speaker: Bolar
dialogue: That wasn't what I meant.

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: If he does show up with a bride, we'll have to move quickly.

speaker: Bolar
dialogue: Once she's with child, I will not harm her.

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: Yes, you've made that quite clear in the past. And now we have Urog and Dushnamub because of your weakness.

speaker: Bolar
dialogue: They are good, loyal children.

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: Have you scried anything new in the entrails?

speaker: Bolar
dialogue: Very little. It's an uncertain time.

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: Not for us, it isn't.

speaker: Bolar
dialogue: For all of us.

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: Come back to me when you have something useful.

speaker: Bolar
dialogue: He's been spending a lot of time at the graves again.

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: Good. The more time he pines for the dead wives, the less time he spends finding a new one.

speaker: Bolar
dialogue: Be careful. The spirits can speak to the living if there's a strong connection.

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: Bah. He never had a connection with any of them beyond what his loins told him.

speaker: Bolar
dialogue: Maybe, but...

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: We're the ones he loves. Me, and you.

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: You wanted to see me?

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: Bolar said you had been looking for a new wife?

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: Well, I...

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: I don't think you're quite ready yet.

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: How will I know when I'm ready?

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: Bolar and I will tell you.

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: Bolar has been in a bad mood for weeks, now.

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: Oh? I hadn't noticed.

speaker: Mauhulakh
dialogue: Since Galka was taken from us. She's been... sad, I guess.

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: She's just worried about you. We all are. We just want you to be happy. We want to make you happy.

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: Come, child, I will tell you how to track a snow cat.

speaker: Urog
dialogue: But you said that was impossible.

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: No, just very difficult. You have to look for shift in various shades of white.

speaker: Urog
dialogue: My eyes are sharp.

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: They are, but your mind has to be sharp, too.

speaker: Urog
dialogue: What's the most dangerous beast you've ever killed?

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: Oh, probably a troll.

speaker: Urog
dialogue: They're fearsome!

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: They are indeed. Nothing like your mother, though!

speaker: Urog
dialogue: That's what everyone keeps saying. But you didn't kill her. That's what I was asking.

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: Oh of course. My mistake.

speaker: Urog
dialogue: What about my father? Was he a good hunter?

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: Oh, you've seen your father just trying to chase a skeever from his house. He's a bit soft.

speaker: Urog
dialogue: Sometimes I'm surprised he's still the chief.

speaker: Yatul
dialogue: We all are, my dear, but sometimes the Divines reward those who don't seem to deserve it. Call it dumb luck.

speaker: Ysolda
dialogue: I've got a recipe for venison stew that I want to try out. Will you have venison anytime soon?

speaker: Ysolda
dialogue: Make it quick, and there might be a bowl of hot stew in it for you.

speaker: Ysolda
dialogue: So you can spend it on drinks at the Bannered Mare? If it's food you need, ask for that instead.

speaker: Brenuin
dialogue: Never mind you, then. I'll find a more charitable soul.

speaker: Ysolda
dialogue: That's what I thought.

speaker: Ysolda
dialogue: Those green apples you sold me the other day were delicious.

speaker: Ysolda
dialogue: I'm sure you could charge double for those and still sell them all within a week.

speaker: Carlotta
dialogue: You're right. I'll have to remember that the next time I get a shipment in.

speaker: Ysolda
dialogue: Fralia, do you ever deal with the Khajiit at all? I'm sure they would love to trade in your husband's steel.

speaker: Fralia
dialogue: Plenty of people here that need Eorlund's craftsmanship, my dear. We've never had any reason to deal with those caravans of theirs.

speaker: Ysolda
dialogue: I'm here to buy food, Nazeem. I suppose you don't need to worry about that.

speaker: Nazeem
dialogue: Owning a farm does have its advantages.

speaker: Ysolda
dialogue: Are you still working at the Bannered Mare in the evenings, Olfina?

speaker: Olfina
dialogue: And why shouldn't I? Just because I'm a Gray-Mane doesn't mean I can't earn my own keep.

speaker: Ysolda
dialogue: I didn't mean... I'm sorry I asked.
